name: GMB Lead-Gen Arbitrage System
definition: Create Google My Business profiles in underserved local markets, rank them in the top-3 organic results, capture inbound calls, and monetize either by selling leads directly to existing advertisers, splitting jobs with subcontractors 60/40, or charging a flat monthly retainer — all with zero ad spend.

name: Niche-Volume Trade-off Matrix
definition: A two-axis selection framework pairing job-value against search-volume across service categories: car detailing (high volume, low job value ~$200), house cleaning (mid volume, mid value), skilled trades like plumbing/HVAC (lower volume, high job value $700+), and specialty trades like roofing/pest control (low volume, high value).

name: Deliberate Pairing Framework
definition: Branding is the deliberate pairing of a product/brand with people, experiences, or outcomes that the ideal customer associates positively with, creating conditioned purchasing behavior; good branding maximizes the percentage of the ideal audience who experience a positive outcome from the pairing.

name: Brand Strength Measurement Triad
definition: Brand strength is measured on three axes: (1) Influence — likelihood the brand changes someone's behavior upon recognition; (2) Direction — whether behavior change moves toward or away from the brand; (3) Reach — how many people the brand changes behavior for.

name: Brand-to-Premium-Product Flywheel
definition: A four-step sequence: weak brand + deliberate pairing with things customers like → strong brand → strong brand applied to commodity product → customers buy to acquire the association, paying premium price.

name: Four Types of Trust
definition: A 2x2 framework mapping trust by (1) who bears the risk and (2) who does the punishing, yielding four trust types: self-risk-other-punishes, other-risk-self-punishes, self-risk-environment-punishes, other-risk-environment-punishes.

name: Skill Stacking Framework
definition: A sequence where foundational skills (math, accounting) compound into specialized capabilities (tax, insurance, CFO readiness), enabling faster wealth creation than starting from scratch.

name: Long-Term Greed Principle
definition: Decision-making discipline where a founder assumes permanent ownership and evaluates every cost-cutting decision through a 10+ year lens, avoiding false savings that introduce long-term risk.

name: Time Allocation Matrix
definition: Classifying all work as either earning (work whose income is material to current cash needs) or learning (work whose knowledge gain is material to future earning power), ensuring all time falls into one of these two categories.

name: Three Methods for Calculating Customer LTV
definition: Three back-of-napkin approaches to estimating customer lifetime value: (1) Lifetime Revenue divided by total customers, (2) Average monthly price divided by monthly churn rate, (3) Sales velocity method using stable monthly revenue divided by monthly new sales count.

name: Revenue Asymptote Model
definition: A business with fixed new-sales rate, price, and churn will converge toward a maximum monthly revenue ceiling equal to (new sales per month x price) / churn rate; businesses above that ceiling shrink toward it, businesses below it grow toward it.

name: Three Levers to Break a Revenue Plateau
definition: When a recurring-revenue business is stagnant, exactly three variables can change its asymptote: (1) increase new-sales volume, (2) raise price, or (3) reduce churn — and reducing churn first multiplies the impact of the other two.

name: Three Affiliate Integration Modes
definition: Alex Hormozi's ranked list of three ways to integrate an affiliate into your revenue: (1) give away your lead magnet free so they distribute it, (2) let them sell your lead magnet at 100% margin while you capture the customer relationship for upsell, (3) commission-based kickback on referred sales — ordered easiest to hardest to execute.

name: Guarantee Formula
definition: A structured template for any guarantee: 'If you don't X in Y time, we will Z.' The goal is to maximize net conversions (new sales minus refunds), not to offer the most extreme terms; the guaranteed element should address the customer's biggest fears.

name: Launch-to-Integration Affiliate Activation
definition: A two-phase model for converting a trial-referral affiliate into a fully activated partner: Phase 1 (Launch) — propose a big coordinated campaign to their customer base after the trial succeeds; Phase 2 (Integration) — embed the referral into the affiliate's standard sales process so it happens automatically without reminders.

name: Core Four Advertising Methods
definition: The only four ways a person can let others know about what they sell, derived from combining two audience types (warm/cold) with two communication modes (one-to-one/one-to-many): warm outreach, posting free content, cold outreach, and paid ads.

name: Lead Getter Hierarchy
definition: Four types of external parties who advertise on your behalf in ascending order of leverage: customers (referrals), employees, agencies, and affiliates; each multiplies lead flow beyond what a single founder can generate.

name: More Better New
definition: A three-stage framework for scaling any advertising channel: first maximize volume (more), then improve conversion rates at the biggest drop-off constraint (better), then expand to new placements, platforms, or core four activities (new).

name: Document-Demonstrate-Duplicate
definition: A three-step employee training model: document every step of the task as a checklist while performing it, demonstrate the checklist step-by-step in front of the trainee, then have the trainee duplicate the process while being observed.

name: Whisper-Tease-Shout Launch Method
definition: A three-phase product and affiliate launch sequence: whisper (create curiosity months out with behind-the-scenes hints), tease (reveal value elements and date weeks out), shout (issue specific CTAs with urgency and scarcity in the final days).

name: What-Who-When Ad Framework
definition: An advertising copywriting structure that combines the eight value elements (dream outcome, perceived likelihood, time delay, effort) with multiple stakeholder perspectives (prospect, spouse, colleagues, rivals) and three time horizons (past, present, future) to generate compelling ad angles.

name: Seven-Step Lead Magnet Creation
definition: A sequential process for building a high-converting lead magnet: identify the narrow problem and right avatar, select solution type (reveal problem / sample / one step of multi-step), choose delivery mechanism (software / information / service / physical product), test naming, maximize ease of consumption, maximize quality, and add a clear CTA.

name: Generate Flow, Monetize Flow, Add Friction
definition: A three-stage acquisition sequencing model: start with the highest-volume (free or deeply discounted) front end to generate lead flow, monetize that flow, then progressively add friction to raise lead quality over time.

name: Four Ways to Display Discounts
definition: A framework for structuring discount offers across four display formats (dollar off, percentage off, buy-X-get-Y, limited-time unit price) so businesses can test which representation drives the highest response rate for a given price point.

name: Five Friction Levers
definition: Five controllable mechanisms for raising free-offer lead quality while reducing volume: increased qualifications, information requirements and question types, number of steps, forced consumption of sales material, and advertisement length.

name: Two-Step Sale
definition: A sales architecture that splits the close into two appointments: a low-cost or discounted first transaction that captures card-on-file and builds trust, followed by a second appointment where the core high-ticket offer is sold as an upsell.

name: Four Offer Types Money Model
definition: A sequenced offer stack combining Attraction Offers (strangers to customers), Upsell Offers (spend more), Downsell Offers (yes when they would say no), and Continuity Offers (keep buying) to maximize 30-day profit and recurring revenue.

name: Payment Plan Downsell Process
definition: A seven-step funnel shifting from full prepayment to free trial: (1) reward prepay with discount, (2) 3rd-party financing/credit card/layaway, (3) half now half later, (4) desire check 1-10 scale, (5) three-payment split, (6) evenly spread payments, (7) free trial with card.

name: Menu Upsell Four-Tactic Process
definition: A structured upsell sequence combining Unselling (cross out what they don't need), Prescription Upselling (tell them exactly what they do need), A/B Upselling (ask preference between two options), and Card On File (make payment frictionless).

name: Anchor Upsell Framework
definition: A five-step premium-first pricing process: present anchor (5-10x premium), get the gasp, come to the rescue by asking what makes the premium matter to them, present core offer, ask how they want to pay.

name: Win Your Money Back Offer
definition: An attraction offer where customers pay upfront and earn their money back as cash or store credit if they meet defined results, actions, or both criteria; the real profit comes from the upsell made to successful customers.

name: Grand Slam Offer
definition: An offer combining an attractive promotion, unmatchable value proposition, premium price, and unbeatable guarantee with a money model that lets you get paid to acquire customers, creating a category of one with no direct price comparison.

name: The Value Equation
definition: A four-variable formula for perceived value: (Dream Outcome x Perceived Likelihood of Achievement) divided by (Time Delay x Effort & Sacrifice). Maximizing the numerators and minimizing the denominators increases willingness to pay.

name: M-A-G-I-C Naming Formula
definition: A five-component offer naming framework: Magnetic reason why + Avatar announcement + Goal statement + Interval (time duration) + Container word (bundle descriptor). Applies 3-5 components to create a name that attracts the target avatar and signals unique value.

name: Sales-to-Fulfillment Continuum
definition: A trade-off axis between ease of selling (high fulfillment burden) and ease of fulfillment (harder to sell); the optimal sweet spot is a highly sellable offer that is also operationally manageable. Start by over-delivering, then systematize.

name: Virtuous Cycle of Price
definition: A causal loop in which premium pricing increases client emotional investment, perceived value, and results, attracting better clients and generating margin to reinvest in service quality, which sustains premium pricing. The inverse vicious cycle applies when prices are cut.

name: Ad Assembly Line Process
definition: Decompose ad creation into three interchangeable components (hook, meat, CTA) produced in bulk separately, then assembled combinatorially to generate 150-750 unique ads per week from a single recording session.

name: Five Ad Meat Formats
definition: Five proven content formats for the body of an ad: Demonstration, Testimonial, Education, Story, and Faceless; these formats work across all industries and can be mixed and matched.

name: Audience Awareness Ladder (adapted from Eugene Schwartz)
definition: A five-level model mapping ad hook style to audience knowledge state: Most Aware (offer-driven), Product-Aware (proof-driven), Solution-Aware (promise-driven), Problem-Aware (pain-driven), Completely Unaware (curiosity-driven).

name: Four Pillars of Lead Nurture
definition: A four-part framework (Availability, Speed, Personalization, Volume) derived from analysis of 4,000+ daily appointments in ALAN software that identifies the primary drivers of show rates for scheduled sales appointments.

name: BAMFAM
definition: Book-A-Meeting-From-A-Meeting: always schedule the next appointment during the current appointment rather than following up later, to prevent leads from going cold between calls.

name: Lead Nurture Throughput Math
definition: Three-metric model: Schedule Rate (engaged leads who schedule) x Show Rate (scheduled leads who show) = Throughput (total engaged leads who show). Optimizing any variable compounds the others.

name: 10 Different Ways to Make a Million Dollars
definition: A structured breakdown of ten distinct paths to generate a million dollars of value, each demonstrating value-creation or arbitrage mechanics that work at any revenue scale.

name: The Big Three Partnership Inputs
definition: A partnership creates value only when at least one partner contributes something the other lacks: knowledge, money, or time. If both partners have identical inputs on all three axes, one partner is unnecessary.

name: Mission-Values-Interests Alignment
definition: A durable partnership requires alignment on three levels: where the business goes (mission), how it gets there (values), and whether lifestyle/interests are compatible. Misalignment on any axis creates persistent conflict.

name: Assume-Close Supplement Upsell Sequence
definition: A two-stage upsell where a nutrition consult is booked 48 hours after the initial sale, then supplements are baked into the habit plan via assumed close ("I need you to take this at this time"), with billing charged to card on file.

name: Insult vs. Criticism Distinction
definition: An insult attacks someone's character; a criticism states the gap between what was said and what happened. Using this distinction converts performance conflicts into actionable observable-reality statements.

name: Vendor-First Channel Cracking Playbook
definition: When entering any new acquisition channel, buy agency expertise first, use the agency period to train an in-house person, then transition to consulting relationship until in-house performance exceeds agency baseline.

name: GMB City Selection Framework
definition: A two-factor evaluation system that scores candidate cities by (1) monthly search volume for the target service and (2) competition quality in the top-three GMB rankings, combining both scores to prioritize which cities to enter.
concept: Market Selection Criteria: Growth + Pain + Targeting

name: Search-Volume-to-Profit Formula
definition: A four-variable formula (search volume / 1000 / close rate x 30 x avg profit per job) that converts monthly search volume into a projected monthly profit figure for any city-service combination.

name: Diagnostic Sales Process
definition: A 7-8 step sales framework that replaces transactional one-off selling with a goal-anchored, personalized presentation: pre-sale questionnaire, credit card collection, current state elicitation, desired state elicitation, obstacle identification, price presentation tied to the goal, prepayment incentive, and recurring/continuity transition.

name: Sales Step-Downs
definition: A cascading offer sequence presented after the goal-price is established: (1) prepay in full for largest discount, (2) third-party financing, (3) partial payment with smaller discount, (4) payment plan continuity, (5) book next appointment — ensuring every customer buys something.

name: Transactional vs. Custom Sale Spectrum
definition: A two-pole model of sales: transactional (high velocity, low ticket, customer fit to product) vs. enterprise/relational (custom, high touch, stakeholder-driven); the diagnostic sale occupies the profitable middle by delivering a product-level operation while feeling custom to the buyer.

name: Six Steps to Brand Building
definition: A sequential framework: (1) understand what branding is (deliberate pairing), (2) understand why it matters (LTV:CAC economics), (3) identify the who (growing, moneyed, findable, in pain), (4) map what they like, (5) associate/advertise to pair yourself with those things, (6) keep your promise with the product.

name: Three Influence Levels Framework
definition: A hierarchy of persuasion power: (1) what you tell people yourself (least influential), (2) what others say about you (far more influential), (3) what customers experience themselves (completes the loop and creates the virtuous cycle).

name: Virtuous Cycle of Branding
definition: A self-reinforcing loop: make a promise -> keep that promise -> customers tell others you kept it -> new customers try you -> you keep your promise to them -> cycle repeats and the audience that vouches for you compounds.

name: Four Who Qualifications
definition: Screen target audiences against four criteria before committing: (1) growing market, (2) can afford your price, (3) easy to find/target, (4) actively in pain (want the solution). All four must be satisfied.

name: Five Phases of Content Marketing
definition: A five-stage progression from first post to full-scale creation-and-capture operation: (1) post once, (2) post consistently on one platform, (3) post reliably on all platforms, (4) maximize volume on each platform simultaneously, (5) actively create and capture content for distribution at scale.

name: 13 Ways to Legally Destroy Your Competition
definition: A structured taxonomy of thirteen moat-building strategies businesses can embed into their DNA to achieve durable competitive dominance: (1) network effects, (2) exclusive resource/technology control, (3) government regulation/licensing, (4) economies of scale, (5) vertical integration, (6) brand identity and customer loyalty, (7) strategic pricing, (8) exclusive contracts, (9) capital requirements as barrier, (10) intellectual property, (11) acquisitions and mergers, (12) innovative business model, (13) distribution channel control.

name: Freemium Disruption Model
definition: Give away for free what competitors charge for, fund the free offering from an alternative revenue stream, and let word-of-mouth drive demand; CAC equals cost-to-service-free-user divided by conversion rate to paid.

name: Top-Down Talent Market Entry
definition: Start at the most expensive market tier and work down; sell to rich customers first to fund the infrastructure needed to eventually sell at volume to lower-income segments.

name: Talent ROI Ladder
definition: Each successive level of hire (50k, 300k, 1M/yr) generates a higher return multiple (5x, 14x, 50x), demonstrating that talent arbitrage improves as the compensation level rises.

name: Better-Not-Bigger Growth Model
definition: Relentless pursuit of product and service quality generates customer demand that forces organic expansion; growth as a self-imposed objective produces bloat and mission drift.

name: Coats-of-Paint Iteration
definition: A sequential editing process in which each pass focuses on a single class of issue (punctuation, data, typos, content, transitions), producing compounding quality improvements that a single review cannot achieve.

name: Brand-as-Compounding-Investment
definition: Direct response advertising functions like a paycheck (stop spending, stop earning); brand investment functions like an IRA (slow to compound, but eventually generates returns that outperform any single ad campaign).

name: More, Better, New Scaling Framework
definition: A three-phase advertising and marketing scaling sequence: exhaust volume first (more), then optimize conversion (better), then add new channels only when more and better are exhausted.

name: Core Four Advertising Methods
definition: The four and only four ways to let people know about a product or service: warm outreach (1:1 to people who know you), cold outreach (1:1 to strangers), content (1:many to people who know you), and paid ads (1:many to strangers).

name: Value Equation
definition: A four-variable model of perceived value: Dream Outcome x Perceived Likelihood of Achievement / Time Delay x Effort and Sacrifice. Increasing numerator variables or decreasing denominator variables raises the value of any offer.

name: Five Levels of Awareness
definition: Eugene Schwartz's model of audience awareness states: Unaware, Problem Aware, Solution Aware, Product Aware, Most Aware. Each level outward requires progressively more sophisticated ad creative to convert.

name: Kaleidoscope Process
definition: Ten variation techniques applied to a single winning ad (background change, props, re-record, reorder, visual filters, visual effects, font/caption change, pacing change, music addition, same hook with new back half) to multiply reach without creating new creative from scratch.

name: CLOSER Framework
definition: A six-step sales call structure: Clarify why the prospect is there, Label the problem, Overview past experiences (pain cycle), Sell the vacation (outcome), Explain away concerns, Reinforce the decision post-close.

name: Core Four Methods
definition: The four and only four ways one person can let others know about their product: warm outreach (one-to-one), cold outreach (one-to-one), content creation (one-to-many), paid advertising (one-to-many).

name: Three Legs of the Stool
definition: Every business requires exactly three functional leaders: one for customer acquisition, one for delivery, and one for internal operations; these three roles correspond to the only three levers that increase enterprise value.

name: Five Reasons Framework
definition: A diagnostic for why a team member is not executing a desired task: (1) did not know you wanted it, (2) did not know how, (3) did not know the deadline, (4) not motivated, (5) has a blocking constraint.

name: Sawdust Revenue Model
definition: Identify existing assets (people, space, data, relationships) that are already paid for and combine them into additional product lines that generate revenue without adding operational drag.
concept: Fast Cash Plays via Underutilized Assets

name: Failure-Learning-Success-Complacency Cycle
definition: A cyclical model describing the entrepreneurial arc: failure generates learning, learning generates success, success generates complacency, and complacency regenerates failure; the cycle is inevitable and non-linear.

name: Ignorance Tax / Ignorance Debt
definition: The cost of operating with a less accurate model of reality, framed as a recurring debt payment; the gap between current knowledge and optimal knowledge is paid via lost revenue every year it persists.

name: 14 Money Mistakes Framework
definition: A structured list of 14 specific financial errors that young people commonly make in their 20s that compound into long-term constraints; each mistake has an observable correction pattern.

name: Money Allocation Prioritization
definition: A system where income is allocated to competing priorities (learning, necessities, discretionary) by explicit decision before any spending occurs, ensuring intentional capital deployment rather than reactive spending.

name: Time-Wage Cost Accounting
definition: A decision framework where every purchase is converted to the number of hours of work required to earn it (accounting for taxes), making the true cost of spending viscerally apparent.

name: 12 Internal Copy Hacks
definition: Alex Hormozi's internal checklist of 12 (plus one bonus) principles applied to every piece of advertising copy, covering headlines, specificity, proof, trust, urgency, authority, CTAs, and readability.

name: How to Yay Without Boo Headline Template
definition: A headline formula structured as: 'How to [desired outcome] without [feared obstacle], even if [biggest insecurity].' Combines benefit, objection preemption, and empathy in one clause.

name: What-Who-When Status Framework
definition: A copy-writing framework (documented in Hormozi's Leads book, p.140) that dimensions status by: What the benefit is, Who awards the status (family, rivals, colleagues), and When (past, present, future).

name: Five-Stage Awareness Stack
definition: Eugene Schwartz's customer awareness ladder applied to ad targeting: Unaware (hook with curiosity) -> Problem Aware (name the symptom) -> Solution Aware (prior failed attempts) -> Product Aware (category comparison) -> Most Aware (direct offer). Each level requires a different hook.

name: Three Methods for Google Business Profile Verification
definition: Three distinct verification pathways for listing and maintaining Google Business profiles: email/phone code verification, instant verification, and video verification, each with different suspension risk profiles and category applicability.

name: Multi-Profile Geographic Coverage System
definition: Spread three to ten independently verified Google Business Profile listings across a service area (roughly one per 10-mile radius) so each profile captures local search traffic without competing against the others.

name: Suffering as Fixed Cost
definition: Suffering is an invariant cost incurred on any life path; the variable is the return you choose to demand for that suffering.
concept: All Life Paths Have Equal Suffering; Outcome Differs by Choice

name: Perceived Lack of Options Model
definition: Sadness is operationally defined as a perceived lack of options; options are expanded not by changing circumstances but by changing the trades one is willing to make.

name: Three-Variable Lead Viability Math
definition: A channel's economic viability is determined by exactly three numbers: cost per lead, close rate (% of leads converted), and average deal size. Their product determines CAC and whether the channel is profitable.

name: Funnel Friction Stacking
definition: When a funnel generates too many unqualified leads, add qualification gates in sequence — first in ad copy, then in opt-in fields (scored questions), then by gating the scheduler behind a score threshold — until the unqualified volume is filtered out.

name: Automated Service Business (Call-Capture Arbitrage)
definition: A three-role system: Google Business profiles generate inbound calls, a Philippines-based VA answers and books appointments, and a local contractor fulfills the job; operator collects the spread.

name: Four Pillars of Influencer Marketing
definition: A CPG brand influencer program structured into four execution pillars: paid influencer (CPM-negotiated), gifting (micro-influencer seeding), TikTok Shop affiliates, and product placement (reach without mention).

name: TikTok Shop Launch Velocity Framework
definition: A coordinated launch approach for CPG on TikTok Shop: seed top affiliates 10 days pre-launch, coordinate simultaneous posting in a 24-hour window at launch, and sustain momentum via a Discord-managed affiliate community with weekly calls.

name: Single-Behavior Leverage Framework
definition: Identify one behavior or skill with the highest number of positive downstream impacts; high leverage means one input produces many large outcomes.

name: Six Decisions That Set the Entrepreneur's Ceiling
definition: Greg LaVecchia's six-decision framework: (1) leave comfortable 7/10 situations, (2) refuse to become cautious after failure, (3) build reputation as primary leverage, (4) skip networking and build instead, (5) exploit youth as an underused asset, (6) refuse early optimization and scale the unscalable.

name: Four TikTok Shop Launch Actions
definition: Joel's four-step framework for brands entering TikTok Shop: (1) authentic content creation, (2) budget for creator sampling, (3) Discord community hub for affiliates, (4) letting creators create without brand-identity constraints.

name: Four Layers of Google Review Legitimacy
definition: A set of four criteria Google uses to detect and filter illegitimate reviews: account history and locality, device and network fingerprinting, behavioral patterns (volume spikes, same-day clusters), and account diversity.

name: Reciprocal Review Exchange Outreach
definition: A structured outreach sequence targeting local business owners in adjacent niches, offering to exchange reviews as mutual support.

name: Zero-Capital Drop-Servicing Launch Sequence
definition: A four-step organic launch for a local-service middleman business requiring $0 upfront: (1) pick a low-barrier service (auto detailing or cleaning), (2) create a Google Business Profile with a made-up company name, (3) accumulate 15-20 reviews from personal network, (4) find a cheap contractor on Facebook Marketplace and mark up their rate 30-40%.

name: GMB Lead Generation Stack
definition: A four-step system for generating organic residential cleaning leads at zero ad cost: (1) identify low-competition, high-search cities using SEMrush keyword volume data; (2) create a Google My Business profile listed at a commercial address in that city; (3) load the profile with reviews matching the third-ranked competitor; (4) apply keyword-based GMB SEO across title, description, services, and Q&A sections to outrank incumbents.

name: Remote Cleaning Arbitrage Model
definition: A business model where the operator generates leads via GMB, outsources all physical cleaning to independent contractors who supply their own vehicle and equipment, quotes jobs by mirroring local competitor pricing, collects payment from the customer, pays the contractor, and retains the spread — targeting 60%+ gross margin with no on-site involvement.

name: Drop-Servicing Lead Arbitrage Model
definition: Generate local-service leads via Google Business Profile ranking in low-competition cities, then fulfill via subcontractor on a 50/60-40 revenue split with zero inventory.

name: City Selection Criteria (Two-Filter Rule)
definition: A market qualifies when two out of the top three Google Map Pack results have under 100 reviews AND the target keyword has at least 600 monthly searches.

name: Revenue Reverse-Engineering from Search Volume
definition: Calculate required monthly searches by chaining: (target monthly profit) / (avg ticket) / (margin%) / (conversion rate) = daily jobs needed; then multiply by empirical searches-per-job ratio to set minimum search volume target.

name: Half-Step Frame Repackaging
definition: Keep existing content substance (hooks, stories, topics) unchanged but shift the narrative frame from end-user perspective to practitioner-facing case-study perspective, changing the audience attracted without rebuilding the content library.

name: Four-Component Mental Toughness Model
definition: Mental toughness has four measurable variables: (1) threshold — how much adversity before behavior changes; (2) magnitude — how much behavior changes once it does; (3) resilience — how fast behavior returns to baseline; (4) adaptation — whether the rebound lands above, at, or below the original baseline.

name: Five Levels of Friendship
definition: A hierarchy for evaluating friendship depth: Level 1 = talk about the past; Level 2 = talk about other people; Level 3 = talk about ideas; Level 4 = can do things together; Level 5 = can make, lose, and spend money together.

name: Two-Question Decision Razor
definition: Before acting on an impulse, ask (1) what do I want to have happen? and (2) what action increases the odds of that happening? The initial gut reaction is usually antithetical to both answers.

name: More, Better, New Scaling Hierarchy
definition: Three categories of business moves in descending risk-adjusted return order: More (repeat what works), Better (small variation on what works), New (wholly different action). New is highest resource cost and lowest probability of success; most businesses should limit themselves to one New per year.

name: Three-Step Organic Local Lead System
definition: A sequential framework for building a service business with zero ad spend: (1) Setup — create and optimize Google Business Profiles with keyword-matched names; (2) Lead Generation — rank in the local top-three map pack via keyword optimization and review parity; (3) Fulfillment — convert inbound calls via on-site quote, deposit collection, and contractor execution.

name: Two Signs of Future Wealth
definition: A framework identifying wealth trajectory through two measurable indicators: monetary measuring units (base unit size for money-denominated decisions) and time horizon (speed of execution and duration of goal commitment).

name: Measuring Sticks
definition: The cognitive shorthand units (e.g., Chipotle burritos, $1K, $10K, $1M) that people use to mentally chunk and evaluate financial decisions; larger units correlate with wealth and determine participation in opportunities.

name: Time Perspective Axis (Micro and Macro)
definition: Two dimensions of time-based decision-making: micro (daily execution speed and communication turnaround) and macro (time horizon in years/decades for goal achievement).

name: Two-Risk Business Taxonomy
definition: All business risk falls into two categories: idea risk (does the market want this?) and execution risk (can this be done well?); choosing to attack only execution risk is a deliberate strategy, not a limitation.

name: Risk-Adjusted Return Compounding
definition: A framework for achieving outsized returns by stringing together high-probability moderate-upside bets and letting compounding do the work, rather than swinging for a single 100x bet with a low probability of success.

name: Google Business Profile Lead Gen Framework
definition: A three-step local-services lead generation system: (1) verify and rank a Google Business Profile with reviews, (2) answer inbound calls with a scripted close, (3) outsource fulfillment to a subcontractor on a 60-40 revenue split.

name: Inspection-Fee Close Sequence
definition: A two-step close for local service calls: first close the inspection appointment with a nominal fee ($60) to create skin-in-the-game commitment; let the on-site subcontractor close the full job — eliminating the need for the call-taker to know anything about the service.

name: Remote Service Arbitrage Model
definition: A three-step arbitrage loop: (1) rank a Google Business Profile for a high-demand local service in a low-competition area, (2) receive inbound leads from organic search, (3) subcontract the work to a local contractor at ~60% of the job price and pocket ~40%.

name: GBP Market Research Filter
definition: Two-variable screen to select target markets before listing a Google Business Profile: minimum 1,000 monthly keyword searches for the target service+city combination (via Semrush Keyword Overview), AND at least two of the top-three organic competitors holding under 100 reviews.

name: Anchor Upsell with Downsell Fallback
definition: Present the premium tier (e.g., $100K) as the primary offer and sell it fully before offering a stripped-down version at a lower price; the buyer who declines the premium has already mentally justified its value, making the downsell feel like a bargain.

name: Qualified Questionnaire Funnel
definition: Replace a generic request-for-quote form with a multi-question quiz that captures budget and fit signals; route qualified leads directly to a booking calendar while disqualified leads receive a PDF or no-book outcome.

name: Four Business Levers
definition: A growth model with exactly four variables: traffic (volume entering the top), conversion (percentage who pay), price (revenue per customer), and churn (rate of loss); growing the business requires moving at least one lever while keeping the others stable or improving.

name: More-Better-New Prioritization
definition: A sequenced decision framework for growth investments: first ask whether you can do more of what already works, then whether you can do it better, and only when both are exhausted should you try something new.

name: One-Time vs. Ongoing Value Split
definition: A pricing architecture that separates education-type value (one-time skill transfer, charged as upfront) from community-type value (calls, coaching, ads, tools - consumed monthly, charged as recurring); combining them into a single payment causes churn when the one-time value is consumed.

name: Guru Model vs. Network Model
definition: Two community structures: Guru Model (hub-and-spoke, every member tied only to the creator) and Network Model (mesh, members tied to multiple other members); the Network Model produces dramatically lower churn because losing one connection does not trigger departure.

name: Theory of Constraints for Business Growth
definition: A business grows until it hits its constraint, then stops; entrepreneurs must identify and focus on the binding constraint rather than working on preferred tasks.

name: Three-Path Framework for Capturing Value
definition: When you have a high-leverage capability, choose between: partnering with a larger business, buying the business yourself, or licensing your capability to others.

name: Building for Scale Foundation Decision
definition: The foundation built for a $10M business differs from one for $100M; attempting to scale a 10-story foundation to 100 stories fails.

name: Three Entrepreneurial Paths
definition: Three distinct career trajectories available to entrepreneurs: the Pure Artist (scaling through excellence in a craft), the Pure Entrepreneur (scaling through business systems across multiple ventures), and the Hybrid Path (combining craft mastery with business delegation to maintain personal involvement in the core activity).

name: Artist Progression Model
definition: A pricing and reputation path for pure artists, advancing from commoditized pricing (equal to competitors) to premium pricing (higher quality, faster execution, trusted reputation) to luxury pricing (rare, highly specialized, exclusive market).

name: Advisor Hierarchy
definition: Five levels of advisor quality ranked by experience and track record: (1) founder who achieved it themselves and repeatedly helped others reach the same goal; (2) operator who has repeatedly helped others reach the goal without achieving it themselves; (3) founder who achieved it but hasn't helped others; (4) observer who has seen multiple people achieve it; (5) untrained observer with no domain experience.

name: Product, Marketing, Sales Hierarchy
definition: Three core business skills ranked by ultimate business impact: exceptional product creates word-of-mouth and scales indefinitely; marketing amplifies an existing product to a ceiling; sales closes individual deals but cannot overcome poor product quality.

name: Multi-Stage Business Scaling Roadmap
definition: A 10-stage progression across 8 business functions (product, marketing, sales, customer success, recruiting, IT, human resources, finance) mapped from zero to $100M+, derived from reviewing all Acquisition.com portfolio companies and where they got stuck.

name: Capital Stack Diversification
definition: Diversifying investments not only across asset classes (stocks, crypto, real estate) but also vertically by position in the capital stack (preferred creditor vs. equity holder), so that in a downturn the investor is among the first to be repaid.

name: Earning Power Formula
definition: Pay = Value Created x Negotiation Skill / Replaceability. Three variables determine income: how much value you create, how well you negotiate, and how hard you are to replace.

name: Rank-and-Rent Google Business Profile Model
definition: Create and optimize a Google Business Profile for a service niche in a low-competition city, rank it to the top three results via keyword-matched business name and reviews, then rent traffic access to a local contractor on a monthly retainer.

name: Four Business Growth Levers
definition: Every lever that can grow a business maps to one of four variables: traffic, conversion, price, or churn. Any activity that does not ladder up to one of these four levers should be eliminated.

name: More, Better, New Scaling Sequence
definition: Before exploring new growth channels, first maximize volume on current channels (More), then improve quality within those channels (Better); only pursue New tactics when More and Better are genuinely exhausted.

name: What Good Looks Like Pattern Recognition
definition: The central compounding advantage in entrepreneurship is calibrating what excellent talent, excellent processes, and excellent operations actually look like at each revenue stage; this recognition is only acquired through repeated direct exposure to high-caliber examples.

name: Drop-Servicing Niche Selection Filter
definition: Three criteria that make a niche viable for a remote drop-servicing business: (1) high average ticket (targeting ~$7,500/job), (2) low Google Map Pack competition (few reviews, no keyword-optimized names), (3) strong local search volume sufficient to generate required lead flow.

name: Keyword-Optimized Google Business Profile Ranking Method
definition: A two-factor ranking formula for Google Map Pack: (1) include the service keyword and city name verbatim in the business profile name, and (2) accumulate more high-star reviews than competitors. Whichever profile best matches the search query's exact terms ranks first regardless of age.

name: Four Vectors of Competitive Advantage
definition: A business can win on one of four strategic dimensions: speed (faster delivery), risk (reliability/consistency/reputation), cost (cheaper than competitors), or ease (reduced effort/friction for the customer); winning one is sufficient, winning multiple creates dominance.

name: Value Equation Mapping
definition: The four competitive vectors map directly to the four components of the value equation: speed = time delay, risk = perceived likelihood of achievement, ease = effort and sacrifice, cost = dream outcome price.

name: Three Speed Sub-Vectors
definition: Speed competitive advantage is operationalized through three sub-vectors: templates (remove decision-making), pre-made (anticipate demand), and availability (minimize booking latency).

name: Four Guarantee Types
definition: Risk mitigation for customers is structured across four guarantee types: unconditional (best for new businesses), conditional (if-then terms), implied/performance-based (skin-in-the-game), and anti-guarantee (for established reputation).

name: Solo-Operator Partnership Model
definition: A three-stage contracting process for drop-servicing: source a small or solo trade contractor via Google My Business, Facebook Marketplace, or Nextdoor; qualify them on availability, revenue split openness, and communication quality; then formally onboard with documented rules, a communication system, a payment structure, and backup contractors.

name: Core Four Acquisition Channels
definition: Four mutually exclusive methods for getting customers: paid ads, organic content, cold outreach, and affiliate/partner referral. Every business should map which of the four it currently uses before deciding what to add.

name: Golden Ratio of Passive Growth
definition: The ratio of monthly referral percentage to monthly churn percentage that determines whether a business grows, stays flat, or declines without paid acquisition.

name: Lollapalooza Effect
definition: Charlie Munger's term for explosive growth outcomes caused by multiple independent reinforcing factors multiplying together, rather than a single silver bullet.

name: School Games
definition: A 30-day competition on the School.com platform where community creators compete for new recurring revenue added, with the top 10 flying to headquarters; designed to make business-building fun and measurable.

name: Unicorn Decomposition
definition: Replace a key-man whose value comes from combining multiple skills by identifying each component skill separately and hiring specialists who are individually best-in-class at each chunk.

name: Bootstrap Debt Ladder
definition: Every business incurs debt from inception; bootstrap companies incur leadership/management/technical debt while VC-backed companies incur financial debt — the type of debt chosen determines growth speed, dilution risk, and long-term soundness.

name: Test Cost-Output Ordering
definition: Rank every candidate business test by lowest guaranteed cost versus highest potential output, and execute them in that order to maximize expected return on experimentation.

name: Mass Google Business Profile Takeover
definition: A multi-profile local SEO strategy that lists 10+ Google Business Profile locations spread across a service area so that every proximity-based search returns at least one profile near the searcher, generating inbound calls without paid ads.

name: Reoccurring vs Recurring Revenue
definition: Revenue that reliably repeats through customer re-purchase behavior (reoccurring) without requiring a subscription or membership contract (recurring); demonstrating a high percentage of past customers return to buy again makes a business valuable even without formal subscriptions.

name: Best-Version Business Modeling
definition: Identify the largest existing business in your category, analyze what they did to get there, map the steps between your current state and theirs, and identify skill gaps that become your prioritized learning agenda.

name: Customer Avatar Reverse-Engineering
definition: Identify the highest-spending retained customers by examining four lenses (psychographics, demographics, geographics, activities), then reorient ads and messaging to attract more of those specific people while excluding others.

name: Missionary vs. Mercenary Founder Frame
definition: A founder driven by mission (what the business represents) outlasts and outperforms one driven by money, because mission resists shiny distractions while mercenary focus succumbs to any easy short-term win.

name: Essential Few Menu Discipline
definition: Constrain the product line to the smallest number of items that covers the majority of demand; each added item splits sales from existing items and adds operational complexity, so the discipline is to refuse additions even when individually profitable.

name: Gift Card Referral Play
definition: A holiday-timed referral tactic where existing customers pay a deeply discounted price (90%+ off) for gift cards equal to one base unit of service, which they give to others — generating paid referral leads and new customer acquisition.

name: Discount-for-Names Exchange
definition: When a prospect asks for a discount, exchange it for three names of friends who might benefit — tying the discount to an immediate introduction obligation rather than giving it away freely.

name: Free Referral Incentive Close
definition: After closing a sale, offer the new customer a cash reward (e.g., $100 per referred buyer) as an immediate post-sale pitch, framed as a way to get the purchase for free.

name: Success-Moment Three-Way Text
definition: At the moment a client achieves a visible result, take their phone, photograph the outcome together, and send a three-way text introduction to someone they know — converting transformation momentum into a warm referral lead.

name: Handwritten Card Event Referral
definition: Mail handwritten invitations to existing customers for an appreciation event with a P.S. instruction to text the letter to a friend as a guest pass, generating warm walk-ins and follow-up appointment bookings.
concept: Conferences and Events as High-Leverage Channels

name: Spouse Enrollment Strategy
definition: Proactively pre-empt the spouse-as-obstacle objection by pitching a paired spouse program with a stat showing higher success rates for couples, framing it as an expected norm rather than an upsell.

name: Seven Retention Levers
definition: A prioritized sequence of seven churn-reduction tactics derived from top-1% gym operators: onboarding, unlockables, exit interviews, attendance tracking, reach-outs, events, and handwritten cards.

name: Unlockables and Milestones
definition: A reward structure where bonuses (content, access, perks) are released on customer activity milestones (activation, testimonial, referral, ascension) or tenure milestones (month 3, 6, 8, 15), creating forward-looking incentives to stay.

name: Angry Boat Technique
definition: An exit-interview de-escalation method where the service provider expresses greater anger at the problem than the canceling customer, which causes the customer to feel validated and self-soothe, enabling a save or upsell.

name: Remote Auto Detailing Model
definition: A three-part arbitrage system: (1) list Google Business profiles for a mobile car detailing service, (2) receive inbound calls from nearby searchers, (3) dispatch a contracted detailer at roughly half the customer price and pocket the spread — all managed remotely without performing any physical labor.

name: Brand as Association Bundle
definition: A brand is a bundle of associations between the known (positive referents) and the unknown (company/logo); adding a rotten association degrades the entire bundle, just as one dead flower ruins a bouquet.

name: Four Market Position Matrix
definition: Four pricing-position tiers -- luxury (Veblen good: price itself is the value), premium (utility + above-average quality), mid-tier (commoditized), and low-cost leader (efficiency-driven) -- with distinct buyer psychology and competitive dynamics at each level.

name: Reward-Punish-Extinguish Training Model
definition: Three and only three levers for shaping behavior: reward (carrot immediately post-behavior), punishment (aversive stimulus immediately post-behavior), or extinction (no response). Reward changes behavior longer; punishment changes behavior faster but requires escalating intensity as the person desensitizes.

name: Lead Nurture Checklist (17-Point)
definition: A multi-item show-rate optimization checklist covering response speed, pre-call information delivery, personalized video, gift-card incentives, open loops, and pre-built deliverables; each item adds roughly 2-5% to show rate, compounding from 30-40% baseline to 85%+.
concept: Show-Up Rate and Lead Nurture Optimization

name: Fix Back to Front
definition: Sequence business improvements from offer (what you sell) to sales process (how you sell) to targeting (who to sell to) to traffic (how they find you); always repair downstream before upstream.

name: Seed of Doubt Framework
definition: When selling against commodity competitors on price, enumerate risk, speed, and ease dimensions the competitor fails on; surfacing these variables in a sales call shifts the buyer's comparison frame from price to value.

name: VIP + Standard Tier Architecture
definition: Lead every sales conversation at the premium tier (VIP); move prospects down to standard only when they self-identify as budget-constrained, preserving margin from high-willingness-to-pay buyers while retaining volume.

name: Six Pillars of Self-Work
definition: Alex Hormozi's summary of personal development reduced to six interdependent principles: thoughts are not inherently true, feelings do not mandate action, events have no inherent good or bad nature, ignorance is the primary enemy, changing surroundings changes behavior, and actions (not past) define identity.

name: Yeti Can Vacuum Model
definition: A mental model for separating internal emotional state from behavioral output, analogous to a double-walled vacuum insulated can: feelings are on one side, actions on the other, with deliberate space (time) as the insulating layer between them.

name: Opportunity Valuation Formula
definition: Evaluate any monetization opportunity as: (number of units sold) x (gross profit per unit) / (competitive moat difficulty). The product of the first two terms is the revenue ceiling; the denominator penalizes saturated or hard-to-defend markets.

name: Media Marketing-Fulfillment Identity
definition: In media businesses, the marketing activity and the fulfillment activity are the same act — creating and distributing content simultaneously markets and delivers the product. No other business category shares this property.

name: Three Foundation Steps for Escaping Poverty
definition: A sequential three-layer model: (1) accept full personal responsibility ('my fault'), (2) use what you actually have rather than what you wish you had, (3) protect self-approval against social pressure from people whose lives you do not want.

name: Glass Timeline Metaphor
definition: Life's effort curve is visualized as a rope of glass pulled toward you: early stages are bloody and painful, gradually becoming smoother and then sweet; progress requires consuming today's pain to pre-empt tomorrow's.

name: Experience Points Model
definition: Failed bets and failed experiments do not return you to zero; each one adds an experience point. Accumulating enough experience points causes a level-up, as in video games. The cost of each successive level's experience points rises.

name: Value Equation for Affiliate Activation
definition: Three levers for getting affiliates to act: reduce risk (testimonials, ongoing payments), increase speed (urgency window), and increase ease (pre-built emails, landing pages, CRM setup).

name: 3A Reframing Framework
definition: A three-step sales objection-handling sequence: Acknowledge (restate the prospect's concern to build rapport and buy thinking time), Associate (link the prospect's question or objection to behaviors of the best-performing customers), then Ask (redirect with a targeted question rather than answering the original objection directly).

name: Straw Man Association
definition: A technique for delivering a harsh truth in a sales call without insulting the prospect directly: create a third-party foil (a recent customer, a named success story, or an authority figure like the CEO) whose situation mirrors the prospect's, then address the tough truth to the foil rather than to the prospect.

name: Minimum Effective Dose Optimization
definition: For each life goal (work, marriage, health), identify the minimum input that sustains it, then stack goals so the highest-ROI activities dominate the schedule; the last hour of work often yields lower ROI than the first hour of relationship investment.

name: Text-Then-Step-Away Conflict Resolution
definition: When in conflict, both parties physically change environments and communicate via text rather than verbal exchange; removes real-time emotional escalation and creates deliberative space between stimulus and response.

name: Document-Demonstrate-Duplicate
definition: A three-step training method: (1) document the exact checklist of steps while performing the task; (2) demonstrate it step-by-step to the employee; (3) have the employee duplicate it in front of you, iterating the checklist until replication is perfect.

name: Stop-Start-Keep Feedback Frame
definition: A behavior-change feedback structure: tell a person what behavior to stop doing, what new behavior to start doing, and what current behavior to keep doing — in that order — to give actionable specificity rather than vague trait labels.

name: Value Equation (100M Offers Framework)
definition: Four variables that drive perceived value and purchasing decisions: Dream Outcome, Perceived Likelihood of Achievement, Time Delay (speed of delivery), and Effort and Sacrifice (friction of use). Maximize Dream Outcome and Likelihood; minimize Time Delay and Effort.

name: Value Enhancers (Urgency, Scarcity, Guarantees, Bonuses, Naming)
definition: Five offer-design levers that sit on top of the core Value Equation to further increase purchasing propensity; each lever independently raises perceived value or lowers perceived risk.

name: System 1 / System 2 Decision Framework
definition: Daniel Kahneman's distinction between fast, automatic, unconscious mental processes (System 1) and slow, deliberative, conscious processes (System 2); Sutherland treats advertising and politics as System 1 businesses.

name: Choice Architecture
definition: Changing the structural framing of a decision — order of options, default presentation, group vs. individual selection — to alter outcomes without changing underlying preferences or using coercion.

name: Costly Signalling Theory
definition: Biological concept in which a signal derives credibility precisely from its expense or difficulty; in marketing, costly advertising is a commitment device that signals the brand has a reputation at stake.

name: Hybrid GMB Method
definition: A two-phase Google Business Profile strategy: first maximize one optimized profile (keywords, reviews, completeness), then scale by deploying 20 additional profiles across different geographic pins — all forwarding leads to the same booking page via call-tracking numbers and duplicate websites.

name: VA Business Automation Stack
definition: A four-component operational handoff system for drop-servicing businesses: (1) inbound call answering via scripted VA, (2) calendar and tracking-sheet booking, (3) technician dispatch and negotiation, (4) payment collection and follow-up — designed to remove the founder from all day-to-day operations.

name: Depth-Plus-Breadth Skill Architecture
definition: A career model requiring deep mastery in one discipline combined with breadth across related fields; depth alone is insufficient for high-value roles in fast-changing industries.

name: Passion Attacking the Market
definition: A competitive strategy where founders apply genuine personal passion to a market niche, enabling them to out-compete data-driven corporate competitors who lack that passion; the passion provides resilience and differentiation that purely analytic market-followers cannot replicate.

name: Small Battles Compounding Framework
definition: A progressive confidence-building method where a founder takes on one small winnable battle, then compounds those wins weekly until the battles themselves snowball in scale relative to the founder's growing capability; the mechanism is repeated small wins building identity and capability.

name: One of Zero Content Standard
definition: A content bar above one-of-one (saying only what only you can say) requiring that every deliverable also has no comparables — nothing anyone else does — used to set team ambition during the 100M Leads launch.

name: One Idea Per Slide Presentation Design
definition: A presentation-design discipline, derived from watching a TED talk titled Death by PowerPoint, that pairs a single idea with a supporting visual on each slide, replacing bulleted text walls.

name: Offer Stack Build-Then-Reveal
definition: A direct-response sales tactic in which value components are stacked visibly for roughly 17 minutes before a price reveal, creating emotional tension and a villain-to-hero arc when the price is lower than expected.

name: Bezos Regret Minimization Framework
definition: Project yourself to age 80 and identify which choices you would regret not making; use regret asymmetry to overcome short-term fear of leaving a stable path.

name: Incremental Talent Partnership Test
definition: A business partner passes the bar only if they add skill sets and perspectives the existing team genuinely lacks; duplicating existing strengths creates tension without value.

name: Remote Service Arbitrage Niche Tier List
definition: A five-tier ranking system (Goated, Amazing, Good, Shit, Retarded) for evaluating remote service arbitrage niches along three axes: barrier to entry (Google Business Profile verification difficulty), ticket size per job, and competitive density on Google Maps.
concept: Market Selection Criteria: Growth + Pain + Targeting

name: Three Margin-Compression Eventualities
definition: Three structural forces that compress margins in every mass-market business at scale: rising CPMs, declining conversion as audiences get colder, and increasing fixed-cost infrastructure.

name: Expectation-Delivery Gap Model
definition: A model in which word-of-mouth valence is determined by the gap between customer expectations (set by marketing) and actual delivery; over-promising compresses or inverts this gap, generating negative word-of-mouth that compounds against paid acquisition.

name: Knowledge-Aligned Capital Deployment
definition: Deploy capital only into opportunities where your accumulated knowledge and expertise exceed 80% of the required skill domain, enabling an unfair advantage over competitors.

name: Barbell Investment Strategy
definition: A two-pole capital structure with positions in high-confidence domains and alternative assets, maintaining minimal exposure to mid-tier opportunities where competitive advantage is unclear.

name: Three-Phase Personal Investment Path
definition: Sequential capital allocation: phase 1 invest in yourself (skills, access, coaching), phase 2 index the excess (S&P 500), phase 3 deploy stockpiled capital into private deals within your expertise domain.

name: StageGate (Bloom Accelerated Version)
definition: A condensed product-concept-to-market validation process that tests new ideas in a controlled internal environment (cafeteria placement) before committing to production, running in weeks rather than the years corporate StageGate typically requires.

name: Strategic Partner vs. Capital-Only Investor
definition: A two-option framework for evaluating potential investors: (1) private equity with capital only and no operating experience, or (2) a strategic partner with direct domain experience who contributes network, wisdom, and sweat equity beyond the check.

name: Front-End / Back-End Split
definition: Front-end covers controllable inputs (industry selection, service-type targeting, urgency positioning); back-end covers the sales process and contractor incentive alignment that converts leads into high-ticket jobs.

name: Service Type / Urgency Level / Customer Type Triage
definition: Three filters applied within a niche to surface higher-ticket jobs: (1) service type sub-niche, (2) urgency of the customer's need, (3) commercial vs. residential customer type.

name: Fix vs. Solution Offer
definition: Present two tiers to the customer: a cheap temporary fix and a permanent solution priced 5-10x higher; the solution framing reframes cost as long-term savings and drives higher-ticket closes.

name: VSL Pre-Frame Close System
definition: A three-part cold-outbound close architecture: (1) VSL that pre-frames the prospect before the call, (2) scripted qualification and pre-frame on the call, (3) training cadence ensuring reps follow the process — designed to move close rates from 6% to 20%+ on cold leads.

name: Quality + Quantity Offer Bifurcation
definition: Split a project-based service into two distinct offer tracks: a high-ticket upfront quality package capturing representative ICPs, and a lower-cost recurring quantity package providing fresh, ongoing UGC-style assets — enabling continuity revenue that project-only pricing cannot sustain.

name: Software Valuation Components
definition: Three features that make software economically valuable at exit: near-zero marginal cost for additional customers (high gross margin), viral growth, and revenue retention (ideally net negative churn via account expansion).

name: Whisper-Tease-Shout Launch Framework
definition: A three-phase product launch sequence: Whisper (mysterious pre-launch curiosity), Tease (building anticipation and excitement), Shout (explicit CTA and live availability).

name: Grand Slam Membership Offer
definition: A membership offer engineered using the value equation (dream outcome, perceived likelihood, time delay, effort/sacrifice) with layered bonuses, skip mechanics, personalization, and credit-based billing to convert a low-recurrence product into a high-retention subscription.

name: Market Selection Four-Factor Test
definition: A four-question filter for evaluating a market: (1) Are they in pain? (2) Do they have purchasing power? (3) Are they easy to target? (4) Is the market growing?
concept: Market Selection Criteria: Growth + Pain + Targeting

name: Persuasion vs. Legislation vs. Economics Hierarchy
definition: A three-tier policy toolkit (legislation, economic incentives, voluntary persuasion) where persuasion uniquely preserves individual optionality and enables distributed adaptation that centralized tools cannot achieve.

name: Placebo Libertarianism
definition: Offering a structured menu of behaviorally equivalent options (e.g., choose any 3 of 5 actions) so individuals feel autonomous choice, increasing adoption and evangelism relative to mandated single behaviors.

name: Model Distortion Cycle
definition: When a model or metric becomes widely used, behavior optimizes toward the metric rather than the underlying reality the metric was designed to measure, progressively distorting the domain it was meant to describe.

name: Learn Season vs Earn Season
definition: Career has two distinct modes: seasons of learning (prioritize skill acquisition over income) and seasons of earning (collect on accrued skill equity); switching to earn mode prematurely permanently caps growth potential.

name: Brand as Garden of Association
definition: A brand is a curated garden where anything not aligned with the target association is a weed; even good things dilute the intended association if they are off-brand.

name: Product vs. Marketing Time Allocation
definition: Two-year product + zero-effort marketing permanently outperforms two-month product + two-year marketing because exceptional product quality unlocks compounding word-of-mouth leverage.

name: Seven Levels of Advice Weighting
definition: A ranked hierarchy for evaluating whose advice to weight, from comments by strangers at level 7 down to someone who has taken multiple people identical to you exactly where you want to go at level 1.

name: Slot Machine Opportunity Framework
definition: A mental model for choosing between opportunities by holding effort cost constant and varying payout magnitude and payout timeline; reveals that most people choose low-payout-fast machines over high-payout-slow machines even when effort is equal.

name: Short Pain / Long Gain Trade Matrix
definition: A 2x2 framework mapping temporal trade types: short pain yields long gain (the optimal trade); short gain yields long pain (the guaranteed loss); comfort is short gain at the cost of long pain; fear-facing is short pain for long gain (fulfillment).

name: Ladder-to-Wall Focus Model
definition: A visual model where four rungs (concurrent projects) stacked across four separate walls never reach critical height on any single wall, but four rungs concentrated on one wall clears the top; illustrates why focused single-project commitment outperforms parallel effort.

name: Four-Component Mental Toughness Model
definition: Mental toughness decomposed into four measurable behavioral dimensions: tolerance (how much hardship before behavior changes), fortitude (how severe the behavior change is), resilience (how quickly one returns to baseline), and adaptability (whether the new baseline is higher or lower than the old one).

name: Trauma as Permanent Behavior Change
definition: Trauma defined operationally as a permanent change of behavior resulting from an aversive stimulus, removing the valence assumption; trauma can be positive (new baseline higher) or negative (new baseline lower).

name: One-Time Value vs. Consumable Value Framework
definition: A two-column decomposition of any education or service offer: Column A (one-time value — skills a buyer uses once, after which the provider adds no further value) vs. Column B (consumables — ongoing outputs buyers must re-consume monthly, enabling recurring revenue).

name: Harvard Differentiation Framework
definition: Three criteria that distinguish durable education brands: (1) high admission standards that exclude most applicants, (2) no outcome promises to students, (3) not everyone passes — creating scarcity, brand value, and pricing power.

name: Three Marshmallow Problem
definition: A reframe of the classic delayed-gratification marshmallow test arguing that indefinitely delaying reward (waiting for the third marshmallow that may never come) is distinct from optimally timed gratification; strivers who always delay often end up with stale first marshmallows and no second.

name: BANT Qualification
definition: Four-variable lead-scoring framework: Budget, Authority, Need, Timing — used to score inbound leads and prioritize the highest-close-probability calls.

name: Good Friction vs. Bad Friction
definition: Good friction (e.g., income question, budget pre-qual) filters out unqualified leads while letting qualified leads through; bad friction (e.g., slow page load, photo upload) repels everyone including qualified leads.

name: Document-Demonstrate-Duplicate
definition: A three-stage training process: (1) Document the script and steps, (2) Demonstrate execution in front of the trainee, (3) Duplicate by watching the trainee perform and giving immediate feedback.

name: AB Offer Architecture (Anchor + Core)
definition: A two-tier offer structure with a high-commitment annual tier (anchor) and a shorter-term core offer; the anchor is taken by ~20% of buyers and subsidizes the blended average cash collected per door.

name: One Avatar, One Channel, One Product
definition: Until reaching $1M+ in revenue, a business should have exactly one customer avatar, one acquisition channel, and one core product to avoid the performance dilution of multi-front effort.

name: Demand Unlock Decision Tree
definition: A three-branch diagnostic for demand-constrained businesses: (1) open a new channel, (2) lower CAC via CRO or better creative/offer, or (3) simply spend more on existing channel.

name: UGC Content Loop
definition: A decentralized content engine in which customers are incentivized to post trip montages in exchange for gated content, generating 20-30 videos per week that are tested organically and the winners are scaled as paid ads.

name: Kaleidoscope Creative Variation
definition: Take one winning creative and generate 20-30 visual variations via AI filters, color treatments, cartoonization, and motion conversion, then blast all variants to find new winners without changing the underlying offer or copy.

name: Lead Scoring by Dual Qualifier
definition: Score and prioritize inbound leads by two qualifying variables (e.g., credit card spend and vacation spend), calling two-for-two matches first, one-for-one matches second, and zero-for-two last.

name: Damaging Admissions Front-Load
definition: Open a sales call by proactively listing every limitation and reason the product will not work for the prospect, before stating benefits, so the prospect self-qualifies and believes the benefits when stated.

name: Custom-Order Sales Flow
definition: A four-stage sequential funnel for converting DIY railing browsers into custom-order buyers: (1) form opt-in, (2) pre-call VSL with price anchoring and BANT qualification via SMS, (3) consultative phone close with on-call discount incentive, (4) card capture on the call.

name: Long-Term Email Nurture Structure
definition: A recurring two-to-three-times-per-week email cadence rotating three content themes: (1) before/after transformation photos, (2) cool project showcases, (3) FAQ objection-breakers — each email structured as subject line, immediate visual reward, CTA link, and PS.
concept: 2x Weekly Email Cadence with Rotating Themes

name: ICE Prioritization Framework
definition: A three-variable scoring model (Impact, Confidence, Ease) used to rank business initiatives by expected return per resource allocated; maps to Hormozi's four-element value equation (dream outcome, perceived likelihood, time to achieve, effort required).

name: BAMFAM (Book A Meeting From A Meeting)
definition: A scheduling method where a rebooking appointment is made at the moment the customer completes their current appointment, rather than relying on the customer to self-schedule later.

name: Shotgun Offer Partnership Exit
definition: A buy-sell mechanism where one partner proposes a price at which they will either buy the other out or be bought out themselves, creating a fair market-clearing price without negotiation asymmetry.

name: Six-Title Career Ladder for Technicians
definition: A compensation and titling progression (Junior Technician -> Technician -> Senior Technician -> Junior Artist -> Artist -> Senior Artist) with pay bumps every three months and skill unlocks at each level, designed to retain service staff for two-plus years.

name: Virtuous Cycle of Pricing
definition: Raising price increases emotional investment, which increases perceived value, which improves results, which decreases customer demandingness and generates more revenue to fund delivery — a self-reinforcing loop.

name: Demand-Constrained vs Supply-Constrained Diagnosis
definition: Before investing in lead generation, determine whether doubling lead flow would be absorbed (demand-constrained) or collapse fulfillment (supply-constrained); only demand-constrained businesses should invest in more leads.

name: Affiliate Offer Architecture (Lead-Magnet Upsell)
definition: Structure affiliate deals so the partner sells or gives away the lower-ticket service, keeps all that revenue, and the affiliate business upsells into its core higher-ticket offer on the back end — converting the partner's cost of acquisition into the affiliate's effective CAC.

name: What-Who-When Copy Framework
definition: A multi-angle copywriting structure derived from the value equation: address dream outcomes (speed, likelihood, ease) and nightmare scenarios (pain, fear) to produce varied ad copy that reaches the broadest set of qualified avatars.

name: Front-End / Back-End Offer Ladder
definition: A two-stage offer architecture where a low-friction front-end product (~$5k) closes fast on one call, converts prospects to customers, and funds the cash outlay while seeding the upsell into the core high-ticket back-end product ($30k+).

name: Milestone Upsell Sequence
definition: Three timed upsell attempts during a short engagement window: (1) at the first measurable win, (2) one week later, (3) last-chance before the window closes; each attempt is easier because the client is now a paying customer experiencing results.

name: Waive-Fee Close
definition: An offer structure in which the seller waives the upfront implementation fee in exchange for a multi-quarter commitment; the buyer chooses between paying the fee and staying month-to-month or committing long-term and getting the fee waived.

name: ICE Prioritization
definition: Rank initiatives by Impact (how big a difference it makes), Confidence (how likely it is to work), and Ease (how hard it is to execute); highest-scoring items execute first.

name: Value Acceleration Method
definition: Acquisition.com scorecard that simultaneously maximizes business value and minimizes risk; flags key-man dependency and customer concentration as primary red flags.

name: Cost-Plus vs. Value-Based Pricing
definition: Two pricing models: cost-plus anchors price to input cost, limiting upside; value-based anchors price to buyer willingness-to-pay, which is uncapped and decoupled from vendor cost changes.

name: Nail It Then Scale It
definition: Solidify unit economics, grand opening process, hiring, and culture in one location before replicating; rushing to expand before the model is proven adds time to reaching the 10th location even while shortening time to the second.

name: Peak-End Memory Rule
definition: Customers remember exactly two moments of any experience: the peak emotional high and how it ended; engineering a strong ending (e.g., a surprise free dessert) is the highest-leverage moment for driving return visits.

name: Four-Skit Training Method
definition: Staff training broken into four scripted behavioral rules (greeting, drink special pitch, food pairing upsell, review/comeback close) practiced as skit repetitions before each shift; repetition volume cements the behavior into automatic execution.

name: Document-Demonstrate-Duplicate
definition: Three-step skill transfer method: make a checklist (document), execute it in front of the learner (demonstrate), then have the learner execute it in front of you (duplicate).

name: Sell at the Point of Greatest Pain
definition: The optimal moment to close a sale is when the prospect experiences peak deprivation or pain, not after the initial value has been delivered and relief achieved.

name: Value Equation (Dream Outcome, Perceived Likelihood, Time, Effort)
definition: Four levers that determine perceived value: dream outcome, perceived likelihood of achievement, time delay, and effort/sacrifice required; lowering the latter three raises perceived value.

name: Core Four Lead Generation Methods
definition: Four primary lead generation activities: paid ads, organic posting/free content, outreach, and referrals; a business should maximize one before adding new channels.

name: Promise-Proof-Path Framework
definition: A three-element video intro structure: Promise (what the viewer will gain), Proof (why they should trust the speaker), and Path (the structure of what will be covered) — derived by Alex Hormozi from analyzing the intros of his top 35 YouTube videos.

name: Content Topics Quadrant
definition: Four temporal buckets for generating content topics: Real-Time (tweet/note dumps as things happen), Recent Past (calendar review of the week), Far Past (big belief-shifting lessons), and Manufactured (staged experiences like 'I lived on $100 for a month').

name: Brand Strength Three-Factor Model
definition: A brand's value is a function of three factors: Influence strength (does seeing it change behavior?), Directionality (does that behavior move toward or away from the brand?), and Reach (how many people have the association at all?).

name: Long-Form Content Three Formats
definition: All long-form content reduces to three formats that can be intermixed: Lists, Steps, and Stories — with each format serving different depth and engagement functions.

name: Self-Serve Pricing by Weight
definition: A retail pricing model in which customers fill their own container and pay per ounce, shifting price accountability from the store to the consumer and raising average ticket without visible upselling.

name: High-Margin-First Display Order
definition: Arranging a self-serve product line so customers encounter the highest-margin items first, filling capacity before reaching lower-margin or perishable items at the end.

name: Level Up Before Plateau
definition: Identify when you have maxed out a market or venture, then transition 95% of focus to the next larger challenge while keeping the prior on autopilot at 5% effort.

name: Stay Ready So You Don't Need to Get Ready
definition: Maintain daily cognitive, physical, emotional, and social readiness so you can capitalize on unplannable opportunities (regulatory shifts, new platforms, cultural movements) the moment they appear.

name: Warm Process on Cold Leads Inversion
definition: Cold acquisition processes work on both cold and warm leads; warm-only processes fail on cold leads. The safe default is always the cold process because running warm leads through a cold process does not hurt conversion, but the reverse leaves cold leads unsold.

name: Soft Handoff Transition Model
definition: Instead of a 100% immediate transfer of clients to a new practitioner, the founder remains nominally in the loop (via shared notes, occasional messages, no live calls) while the new hire handles day-to-day delivery, reducing churn risk and theft risk during the transition.

name: Customer Profitability Analysis
definition: A three-axis diagnostic that segments customers by (1) demographics, (2) behaviors at entry, and (3) actions taken after joining, to isolate the 20% most profitable customer archetype for replication.

name: Bad Customer Red Flag Checklist
definition: Six observable warning signs that a customer segment is structurally unprofitable: short lifespan, excessive support demands, scope creep, dissatisfaction despite above-and-beyond service, pressure to overpromise, and knowingly selling customers you expect will fail.

name: Transition Sequencing for Avatar Upgrade
