definition: A phased approach to migrating away from low-quality customers: (1) conduct profitability analysis, (2) redefine ICP, (3) realign all messaging and offers top-to-bottom, (4) implement sales qualification gates, (5) cap the percentage of low-quality customers sold per period, (6) gradually decrease low-quality share until elimination.

name: Four-Step Business Monetization Process
definition: A linear customer conversion system consisting of: (1) get the ad, (2) capture the opt-in via lead magnet, (3) warm via video sales letter, (4) qualify via BANT before the sales call.

name: Four-Step Persuasion Framework
definition: A copywriting model that covers all emotional angles of any call to action: gain good (positive future), lose bad (negative removal), keep bad (negative continuation if no action), lose good (positive forfeited if no action).

name: Five-P VSL Structure
definition: A video sales letter outline with five sequential sections: Proof, Promise, Pain, Plan, Picture (visual), followed by an FAQ block and a closing proof stack.
concept: VSL as Qualification and Pre-Frame Gate

name: Three Lead Magnet Types
definition: A taxonomy of lead magnets: (1) Reveal-a-problem (expose a root cause), (2) One step of a multi-step solution (solve one small loop completely), (3) Free trial of one step in a multi-step process.

name: Organic Plus CTA Ad Format
definition: A paid-ad creation method: produce organic content, identify high-engagement pieces via the platform algorithm, add a call to action at the end, then pay to promote, turning validated organic winners into performance ads.

name: Hook-Meat-CTA Ad Structure
definition: A direct-response ad assembly framework: (1) Hook drawn from best-performing cross-industry organic and ads, (2) Meat built using the four-step persuasion framework plus audience-status extensions, (3) Call to action that is both stated and visually demonstrated in the ad.

name: Volume times Leverage Output Model
definition: Business output equals the amount of actions taken multiplied by the return per action; both variables must be grown together, and high volume compounds leverage by accelerating skill development.

name: Need-to-Believes Confidence Score
definition: Every new venture has a set of discrete assumptions (need-to-believes) that must be validated before committing resources; tracking which have been proven converts optimism to confidence score.

name: Ignorance Debt Framework
definition: Founders incur a debt of ignorance for every role or capability they do not yet understand; this debt is paid through time, failed hires, and lost revenue until the founder has seen what good looks like.

name: LTV to CAC Ratio (LTGP:CAC)
definition: A ratio between lifetime gross profit (total revenue from a customer minus cost of delivery) and customer acquisition cost (all marketing and sales spend divided by customers acquired); the single number that predicts how far a business can scale advertising and how profitable it can become.

name: LTV Stack Architecture (back-to-front)
definition: Building lifetime gross profit by designing from the most expensive back-end offer first, then working forward so each front-end customer can be ascended through cross-sells and upsells, increasing average LTV without changing CAC.

name: CAC Funnel Optimization (front-to-back)
definition: Improving cost-to-acquire by working from the earliest funnel stage (ad creative and offer) toward later stages (show rate, close rate), because early-stage improvements affect the largest percentage of prospects and yield the highest order-of-magnitude impact.

name: Volume Negates Luck
definition: Outcompeting structurally disadvantaged conditions (bias, inexperience) by doing multiples of the volume the incumbent best performer does, until skill closes the gap.

name: What Would It Take Framework
definition: When facing a bias or structural disadvantage, ask the gatekeeper explicitly what objective proof would change their mind, then over-deliver on exactly that standard.

name: Four Business Sticking Points
definition: A sequential framework of the four structural constraints every scaling business must resolve: (1) wrong customer mix, (2) mispriced compensation or undercharging, (3) premature overexpansion, (4) lack of focus.

name: Ideal Customer Quadrant Filter
definition: A four-column customer-ranking method (love working with / highest spend / highest operational profit / easiest to deliver) used to identify the ideal customer archetype from existing customer history.

name: Commitment as Elimination of Alternatives
definition: Commitment is operationally defined as the active removal of competing options; focus is measured by the number and quality of opportunities declined.

name: Three Cash-Flow Pull-Forward Levers
definition: A three-part sequence for a capital-constrained product business to accelerate cash collection before acquiring a major asset: (1) renegotiate supplier payment terms to net 30/60/90, (2) use pre-orders to collect revenue before production, (3) maximize existing volume capacity to generate operating cash flow.

name: Attention-to-Perception Bridge
definition: Changing what you focus attention on (the frame or narrative) restructures how you perceive a situation, which restructures your emotional and behavioral response.

name: Unique-Expensive-Sticky-Air-Owner (UESAO) Business Framework
definition: Charlie Munger and Warren Buffett's five-attribute filter for the ideal business: Unique (brand moat others cannot copy), Expensive (high gross margin — buy for a penny, sell for a dollar), Sticky (recurring or reoccurring demand), Air (low capital expenditure required to stay competitive), and managed by an Owner-minded operator who treats 100% of their net worth as if it is in the business forever.

name: Inverted Thinking (Invert, Always Invert)
definition: A problem-solving method attributed to Albert Einstein and popularized by Charlie Munger: instead of asking how to achieve a goal, ask how to guarantee its opposite outcome, then invert those answers. Used because humans are biologically stronger at detecting threats and negatives than finding positives.

name: Three-Channel Contractor Sourcing Framework
definition: A ranked hierarchy of three platforms for sourcing cheap labor contractors (Google My Business low-review listings, Facebook Marketplace, Nextdoor), plus an SMS-blast mega-channel that outperforms all three on speed and volume.

name: Appointment-First Phone System
definition: A structured inbound call protocol for local service businesses that prioritizes booking an in-person appointment over any phone-based quoting, using inspection fees and two-choice scheduling to prevent customer defection.

name: Inspection Fee Waiver Close
definition: A close mechanic that charges a flat inspection/diagnostic fee (e.g. $60) upfront, then waives it against the job total if the customer proceeds, locking in commitment and removing the competitor-shopping window.

name: GMB Drop-Servicing Model
definition: Create and optimize Google My Business listings in high-demand service niches, generate leads organically via local map-pack ranking, then fulfill jobs via subcontractors at a 25-45% profit margin — requiring no trade skills and minimal upfront capital.

name: Energy Drink Review Method
definition: A specific organic review-generation tactic referenced in Eric's course that generates 20-40 five-star GMB reviews per day that stick, enabling rapid map-pack ranking without paid advertising.

name: GBP Ranking Factor Hierarchy
definition: An ordered set of Google Business Profile ranking signals ranked by impact: title (keyword + city) > description (keyword density) > reviews (count + rating + replies) > service areas + zip codes > services/products/updates > website.

name: GBP Keyword Placement Map
definition: A structured map of the seven locations within a Google Business Profile where keywords can be embedded: title, description, review replies, products, services (with descriptions), Q&A, and service areas.

name: Two-Tiered Affiliate Incentive Structure
definition: A layered affiliate reward system with unscalable premium prizes for top performers (e.g., top 10, top 50) and accessible prizes for the long tail (anyone who hits a minimum activation threshold), so both whales and small promoters have meaningful incentive to participate.

name: Affiliate Machine: Offer-Page-Promote-Support Loop
definition: A four-stage affiliate program build: (1) design the affiliate offer (money, free stuff, or both), (2) build an affiliate sales page explaining prizes and mechanics, (3) promote the program through existing channels, (4) support affiliates with onboarding, attribution tracking, leaderboards, and pre-written collateral.

name: Mental Accounting and Prepaid Cost Absorption
definition: Costs that are paid upfront and mentally committed (stored value cards, advance hotel/airline payments) feel like sunk costs, making subsequent expenditures feel smaller than their absolute price.

name: Abductive Inference Framework
definition: A problem-solving method (named by Charles Sanders Peirce) that begins from a strange observed fact and asks: what would have to be true for this to occur? Requires imagination and hypothesis, unlike induction (data to rule) or deduction (rule to conclusion). Used in detective work, Darwin's theory of evolution, and Fleming's discovery of penicillin.

name: Post-Rationalization Asymmetry
definition: The observation that the set of ideas that can be validated after discovery (post-rationalized) is substantially larger than the set that can be generated through logical pre-reasoning alone; creativity expands the viable solution space beyond what deduction can reach.

name: Bee Waggle Dance Exploration Model
definition: Bees use a waggle dance to communicate known food sources, but a significant fraction (~20%) of bees ignore the dance and explore independently. Evolutionary modeling showed this inefficiency is adaptive: exploratory bees prevent the colony from becoming trapped in a local maximum and enable adaptation to changing environments.

name: Four Sources of Money
definition: Four buckets from which purchases can be financed: debt (consumer credit), savings (past self), cash flow (current income), and new opportunities (created income). The fourth — new opportunities — is the only one that preserves all existing financial flows while adding new capital.

name: SME 500 Investment Thesis
definition: Invest in the SME 500 (yourself: skills, mindset, execution) rather than the S&P 500 in early career. A $500 certification can triple lifetime hourly earnings versus turning $1,000 into $1,100 via index funds.

name: Time Liberation Stack
definition: A specific $1,500/month spending allocation that eliminates 96 hours of low-skill personal labor monthly: ~$800 for food/meal service (~50 hrs), ~$500 for house cleaning (~25 hrs), ~$200 for laundry (~16 hrs). The recovered hours are then reallocated to higher-earning activity.

name: Brand as Bouquet of Associations
definition: A brand is not a single thing but a collection of deliberately cultivated intangible associations (values, personality signals, recurring themes) that an audience links to a company or person; removing even one negative association degrades the whole bouquet.

name: Season of Learning vs. Season of Earning
definition: Early career is a season of learning in which the optimal trade is time and labor at below-market wage in exchange for skill equity that compounds; earning mode only becomes rational once that skill base is established.

name: Two Ways to Sell a Product
definition: All product selling reduces to two poles: mass social normalisation (everybody buys this, so it must be good — the Coca-Cola model) or exclusivity signalling (very few people buy this, so it must be good — the French luxury goods model). Television excels at the former; precision direct marketing excels at the latter.

name: Targeting-Communication Cancellation Trap
definition: Combining high precision targeting with low-impact communication format cancels the benefit of each: precision targeting creates value by enabling expensive, high-impact outreach to a small qualified audience; cheap digital delivery destroys that value by making the outreach feel mass-market and easy-to-ignore.

name: Industry Belief Inertia
definition: Systems of false or questionable beliefs persist in industries when consensus makes dissent socially/professionally costly, not because evidence supports them.

name: Direct Response Doom Loop
definition: A named cycle in paid-media e-commerce where revenue scales until CAC rises and gross margins compress until the business is a high-liability, low-margin operation that requires perpetual revenue just to sustain the team.

name: Brand Loop
definition: The virtuous cycle in which a strong brand promise attracts true believers (influencers, affiliates), the product reinforces that promise on delivery, and each satisfied customer deepens the brand rather than diluting it — enabling exits at premium multiples rather than product-arbitrage multiples.

name: Design for Extremes, Not Average
definition: Products and solutions designed for extreme or unusual consumer segments often achieve mainstream adoption; designing for a single representative average person creates dead ends.

name: Lateral Category Analysis
definition: A problem-solving approach that recognizes most complex problems have already been solved in different domains, requiring transfer of solutions across category boundaries.

name: TRIZ Problem Definition Linkage
definition: A framework for identifying how poor problem definitions create false constraints that prevent recognition of solutions already existing in other domains.

name: Obedient Bee vs. Rogue Bee Allocation
definition: Organizations should split employee effort between exploitation (obedient bees following known directions) and exploration (rogue bees taking random journeys), with separate ROI thresholds for each, because over-compliance traps the system in a local maximum and starves it of new discoveries.

name: Time-Average vs. Ensemble-Average Growth
definition: In multiplicative systems (finance, life, business), consistent low-variance growth compounds to a higher terminal value than high-variance growth with the same arithmetic mean, because a single catastrophic loss in a multiplicative chain destroys all prior gains. Formalized by Ole Peters and Murray Gell-Mann.

name: Lateral Category Transfer (TRIZ)
definition: Most complex problems have already been solved in a different domain; the innovation move is to identify the solved version in the adjacent domain and transfer it, rather than reinvent within the current domain. Named practice from Soviet TRIZ methodology.

name: Blue Mountain Paths Framework
definition: A decision model in which multiple distinct routes all reach the same destination (the prize); the mistake is spending time at the base choosing rather than climbing any of them.

name: Remote Service Arbitrage
definition: Build Google My Business (GMB) profiles for service niches, capture inbound leads, and subcontract fulfillment to local tradespeople, keeping the margin spread as profit.

name: Placebo-Plus-Drug Optimization Framework
definition: Rather than subtracting the placebo effect from drug efficacy in trials, medical and commercial value creation should maximize both the intrinsic effect and the perceptual/contextual effect simultaneously, as they may multiply rather than merely add.

name: Austrian School Value Definition
definition: Value is whatever someone is prepared to pay for, regardless of whether it originates in intrinsic product properties or psychological/contextual framing; the distinction between manufacturing value and marketing value is meaningless from the standpoint of economic outcomes.

name: McNamara Fallacy (Quantitative Bias)
definition: Measuring only what is objectively quantifiable (SI units: weight, time, speed) while discounting subjective improvements systematically distorts strategy; named for Robert McNamara's use of kill counts in the Vietnam War.

name: Meaning-Emotion-Behavior Chain
definition: Human decision-making follows a fixed sequence: context changes meaning, meaning triggers emotion, emotion drives behavior, behavior is followed by post-hoc rationalization. People do not respond to things; they respond to things-in-context.

name: Costly Signaling Theory
definition: A signal is only reliable — and therefore persuasive — when it consumes a resource that is in short supply (money, creativity, effort, skill), making it too costly to fake. The framework, derived from Amotz Zahavi's handicap principle in evolutionary biology, explains why expensive or difficult communication is trusted and cheap communication is discounted.

name: Rider-and-Elephant Dual-Process Model
definition: Jonathan Haidt's model in which conscious reasoning (the rider) sits atop unconscious instinct (the elephant). The rider generates post-hoc rationalizations; the elephant actually drives behavior. Effective communication must be written for the elephant, not just the rider.

name: Faith-in-Futurity Signaling
definition: Upfront expenditure on communication or physical commitment (advertising spend, premium print, engagement rings, bank architecture) functions as a credible proof of long-term intent because a short-term actor would never pay such costs voluntarily.

name: Paid Inspection Appointment Funnel
definition: A four-stage sales flow for high-ticket home services: (1) answer phone instantly, (2) close a paid inspection appointment, (3) send confirmation and reminders, (4) have contractor upsell on-site and close same-day.

name: Tamagotchi Microbiome Frame
definition: A mental model for understanding diet: the gut microbiome is treated as a living creature (like a Tamagotchi) that must be actively fed the right inputs; this reframes eating from deprivation-avoidance to additive caretaking.

name: Good Bugs / Bad Bugs Spectrum
definition: ZOE's working taxonomy that classifies gut bacteria into approximately 50 beneficial and 50 harmful species, providing a simplified vocabulary for communicating the microbiome's role in health outcomes.
concept: Undefined Words Create Mythology and Prevent Clear Thinking

name: Parallel Funnel Structure
definition: A mirror of the demand-generation funnel built for talent: app-gen, app-nurture, interviewing, onboarding, and retention/ascension for salespeople, running concurrently with the lead-gen funnel.

name: Uninformed Optimism to Breakthrough Arc
definition: A four-stage emotional arc in any hard endeavor: (1) uninformed optimism, (2) informed pessimism, (3) valley of despair (where most quit), (4) upside and goal achievement. Most people exit at stage 3 by starting a new cycle at stage 1.

name: Declarative vs Procedural Knowledge
definition: Two distinct knowledge types: declarative (knowing about — facts, concepts, how something works) versus procedural (knowing how — the embodied ability to execute). Declarative knowledge is commonly mistaken for procedural, causing false confidence.

name: Three Outcomes of Difficulty
definition: Every hard endeavor resolves in exactly one of three ways: (1) you quit, (2) external circumstances improve (it gets easier), or (3) you develop internally (you get harder). No fourth outcome exists; difficulty always ends.

name: Brand Bounce vs Brand Extension
definition: A brand extension stays within the same category (e.g., a light variant); a brand bounce moves into a completely different category and uses the brand as instant credentials in that new space.

name: Peak-End Rule Applied to Customer Experience
definition: How an experience ends has a disproportionate effect on the memory of the entire experience; excellence at the close point (e.g., coffee at meal end) carries outsized weight relative to the preceding sequence.
concept: Brand Effect on Customer Behavior and WTP

name: Minority Rule in Product and Menu Design
definition: When one group will only accept option A and another group accepts either A or B, the entire system defaults to A regardless of majority preference — meaning intransigent minorities set the standard for the whole.

name: Commercial Innovation Framework
definition: A class of innovation distinct from product innovation: changing how something is sold, priced, packaged, or bundled (e.g., Amazon Prime, Persil rail tickets) to unlock value without altering the product itself.

name: Step Back to Go Forward Scaling Sequence
definition: When graduating from solo operator to team-based delivery, early VA or hire performance dips temporarily before enabling the next revenue step; accepting short-term regression is the price of permanent capacity expansion.

name: Pick Your Price
definition: A three-stage offer structure: (1) market the offer as free, (2) at checkout present three donation/payment tiers (small/medium/large) with escalating bonuses, (3) end with a payment method question and silence. The framing attributes bonuses to staff, not the business, to exploit the consumer preference for paying employees over businesses.

name: Remote Service Arbitrage Setup Sequence
definition: A five-step launch sequence for a remote service arbitrage business: (1) choose a niche by evaluating local competition, (2) create Google Business Profile listings, (3) acquire reviews in volume (~60-100 per profile), (4) recruit 3-5 subcontractors in the niche, (5) answer inbound calls and dispatch contractors.

name: Desperation-Driven Business Creation
definition: The best businesses emerge from desperation because founders have no choice but to take massive action and accept unacceptable personal costs.

name: Three-Component Remote Service Scaling Framework
definition: A structured breakdown of the three operational areas that determine whether a remote home-service arbitrage business reaches $10k-$30k/month: (1) Setup, (2) Marketing/Ranking, and (3) Fulfillment.

name: Scenting the Soap
definition: Attach a selfish individual benefit (vanity, social fear) to a prosocial behavior so people adopt the behavior for private reasons and the social benefit emerges as a byproduct.

name: Kano Excitement Attribute
definition: Norio Kano's model distinguishing threshold functional attributes (must-haves) from excitement attributes (delighters) that disproportionately determine purchase choice even when functionally trivial.

name: Benign Bullshit
definition: A reframing device that attaches an emotionally resonant but functionally irrelevant superlative or story to a product or place, converting it from a utilitarian object into a destination or desirable identity.

name: Local Service Arbitrage
definition: A three-step model: create Google Business Profile listings for in-person local services, rank in the top three via keyword optimization and reviews, then route inbound calls to a subcontractor who does the work while the operator keeps ~40% of gross profit after materials.

name: Profile-Rank-Convert Sequence
definition: Sequential steps for local service arbitrage: (1) select low-competition, high-demand service and city using keyword volume tools; (2) list and verify a Google Business Profile with service+city in the name; (3) acquire enough reviews to match the #3 ranked competitor; (4) fill all profile sections with keyword-optimized copy; (5) answer calls professionally and pre-book paid inspections for high-ticket services.

name: Epiphany Bridge Testimonial Template
definition: A structured interview format capturing before/after results along two axes (internal and external) at three stages (before, decision moment, after) to produce testimonial content that doubles as lifecycle ads.

name: Willingness-to-Pay Feature Buckets
definition: A four-bucket framework for recurring community offers identifying the features with highest observed willingness to pay: exclusive access, exclusive content, exclusive events, and exclusive newsletter/publication.

name: Bonus Rent Test
definition: Each bonus in an offer must independently justify the full price of the offer on its own; any bonus that fails this test is cut, forcing consolidation to only the highest-value items.

name: AI Productivity Levels
definition: Two-tier framework for AI leverage: Level 1 is using AI as a filter to consume 10x information and produce 10x output; Level 2 (expert level) is redirecting 90% of prior generation time toward QA and validation, becoming more valuable by spending human effort where machines cannot replace judgment.

name: AI Evolution Stages
definition: Five sequential stages of AI development: (1) language/text generation via large language models; (2) image and video generation; (3) physical-world robots; (4) superintelligence (AI smarter than all humans combined); (5) the Singularity, where AI self-directs beyond human foresight.

name: Four Types of Leverage
definition: Naval Ravikant's hierarchy of leverage: labor (other people's effort), capital (other people's money), code (software that scales infinitely), and media (content that reaches unlimited audiences with one-time creation cost).

name: Capture-Hold-Multiply Attention Framework
definition: Alex Hormozi's three-part model for attention-based wealth creation: (1) capture attention from audiences, (2) hold it over time by remaining loyal to brand and giving without asking, and (3) multiply it by layering additional audience pools through multi-dimensional interests.

name: Remote Service Arbitrage Model
definition: A three-step business model: (1) create a Google Business Profile for a high-demand, low-competition local service; (2) rank it in the top three organic results by keyword-matching the business name and accumulating reviews; (3) forward inbound calls to an independent contractor who performs the work, keeping 40% of job revenue as the operator margin.

name: City-Service Selection Criteria
definition: Evaluate any city-service combination using two filters from SEMrush and Google Maps: at least 1,000 monthly searches for the service-plus-city keyword, and at least two of the top three Google Business competitors having fewer than 100 reviews.
concept: Market Selection Criteria: Growth + Pain + Targeting

name: 24 Investing Rules Framework
definition: A structured set of decision-making principles for capital deployment, framed as if-then conditional rules that preserve decision-making quality over time.

name: High-Commitment / Low-Expectations Pairing
definition: Two-variable pairing for durable life satisfaction: commitment defined as the elimination of all alternatives, paired with expectations deliberately held below reality so that actual outcomes consistently exceed them.

name: Three Stages of Dissatisfaction Progression
definition: A developmental arc in which individuals move through (1) blaming others for unmet wants, (2) learning to acquire things but envying parallel paths, and (3) consciously accepting trades and tolerating chosen paths.

name: Seven Time-Buying Investments
definition: A sequenced set of seven outsourcing decisions (meals, laundry, house cleaning, sleep optimization, landscaping, transportation, semi-private flying) ordered by cost-efficiency and number of hours reclaimed per dollar spent.

name: Four Business Risk Categories
definition: The four structural risks that prevent small businesses (under $10M revenue) from being sellable assets: key man risk, single channel risk, key customer risk, and single vendor risk.

name: Document-Demonstrate-Duplicate Training
definition: A three-step process for transferring any skill: (1) document the checklist of steps while performing, (2) demonstrate the checklist in front of the trainee, (3) have the trainee duplicate it in front of you. Checklist granularity scales inversely with trainee skill level.

name: Supply Constraint Resolution Sequence
definition: Three ordered tactics for supply-constrained businesses: first raise prices (highest ROI for least effort), second increase service ratio (more clients per unit of capacity), third hire people to do the work (eliminates key man risk but requires the most effort).

name: Key Vendor Protection Stack
definition: Three layered tactics to reduce vendor concentration risk: (1) redundancy (backup providers spun up and approved), (2) mutually insured destruction (become a large enough percentage of vendor revenue that they cannot afford to lose you), (3) covenants and terms (notice periods, breakup fees, SLA fines).
concept: Platform Choice and Backup Channel Resilience

name: Seven-Step Lead Magnet Creation Framework
definition: A sequential checklist for designing lead magnets: (1) define the problem and audience, (2) choose how to solve it, (3) choose delivery mechanism, (4) package/name it, (5) make it fast and easy to consume, (6) make it genuinely excellent, (7) make the next step easy and clear.

name: Complete Solution to Narrow Problem
definition: A lead magnet is a fully complete solution to one narrowly defined micro-step problem within the customer journey, not a partial solution gated behind a paywall; solving it completely opens the prospect to the next sequential problem, which becomes the paid offer.

name: GMB Three-Pack Ranking Blueprint
definition: A five-element system for ranking a Google Business Profile into the local three-pack: (1) strategic placement in low-competition, high-search-volume areas, (2) review quantity matching or exceeding the third-place profile, (3) profile metric superiority on rating and completeness, (4) title-and-description SEO with primary keyword, (5) sustained human activity signals.

name: Expectation-Experience Alignment
definition: The quality of an experience is determined not by objective properties but by the congruence between advance expectations and actual delivery.

name: 10-Chessboard Leverage Principle
definition: Every marketing action, dollar, or resource deployed should simultaneously generate content or reach across at least 10 channels, so each move compounds rather than spending once.

name: Consumer-Feels-Like-Robbing-You Offer Design
definition: Bundle near-zero-COGS digital assets (PDF guides, private social access) onto a physical product so the perceived value overwhelms the price point, making the tangible product feel like a bonus rather than the core purchase.

name: Stay Ready Framework
definition: Greg LaVecchia's operational definition of discipline: maintaining a state of ongoing readiness so that preparation is continuous rather than reactive to opportunity.

name: Brand vs. Product Distinction
definition: A product sells units; a brand commands household awareness, cultural relevance, and community loyalty — achieved by reinvesting in community, content, and product innovation rather than performance advertising alone.

name: Rule of One
definition: Launch with one product, one social channel, one marketing channel, and one sales channel; when revenue plateaus, add exactly one increment to exactly one of those categories before expanding further.

name: Authoritative-Figure-as-Brand-Nucleus
definition: Position an authoritative figure (e.g., a founder or influencer with an existing following) as the identity core of a platform brand, but name the brand around a transformation theme rather than the person's name to eliminate key-man risk while retaining the emotional and reputational pull of the individual.

name: Day-Zero TikTok Shop Launch Framework
definition: Four-step launch sequence for a brand entering TikTok Shop from day zero: (1) authentic raw content, (2) creator seeding budget, (3) creator community hub (Discord), (4) creator autonomy over content creation.

name: Brand vs. Product Reinvestment Split
definition: A capital allocation model where incremental revenue is directed toward community-building assets (events, podcasts, product innovation) rather than performance marketing spend, to cross the ceiling from product to brand.

name: Winning Lottery Ticket Metaphor
definition: Asking a successful entrepreneur what their winning playbook was is like asking someone what their winning lottery ticket numbers were — the numbers are now obsolete and irrelevant to future plays.

name: Open-Gate Product Selection Framework
definition: Choose the next product by identifying where your unique asset stack (relationships, capital, team capabilities) makes an apparently impossible barrier into an open gate that competitors cannot walk through.

name: Sequential Small Battle Method
definition: A progression where a founder wins one small battle, then one per month, then one per week, then one per day — each stage compounding relative magnitude until the founder has transformed their identity.

name: DTC-to-Amazon-to-Retail Launch Sequence
definition: A three-stage distribution expansion path for consumer products: validate product-market fit on direct-to-consumer, prove demand at scale on Amazon, then use that proof to secure retail shelf space where competitors are absent.

name: Passion-Angle White Space Framework
definition: Identify all existing passions, then find the larger adjacent market where that passion-angle has no passionate competitor — rather than limiting yourself to the market you are already passionate about.

name: Output-as-Real-Estate Mental Model
definition: Every unit of content, ad, or listing is treated as a piece of real estate stacked on the world; more output means higher probability that one unit converts, regardless of individual quality.

name: Remote Service Arbitrage (RSA)
definition: A three-part system: (1) create a Google Business Profile for a local service in a low-competition city, (2) rank it in the top-3 via keyword-matched name and review volume, (3) book inbound calls as appointments and forward jobs to a sub-contracted service provider at a 60/40 split — keeping 40% as commission.

name: City Selection Matrix
definition: A two-axis evaluation framework — monthly search volume (minimum 1,000/mo via SEMrush) versus competitor review count in the top 3 (target under 100 reviews) — used to identify cities where ranking in the top-3 Google Maps position is achievable without a physical address.
concept: Market Selection Criteria: Growth + Pain + Targeting

name: C-L-O-S-E-R Formula
definition: A six-step in-person sales framework: Clarify why they are there, Label them with the problem, Overview their past pains, Sell the vacation (outcome), Explain away concerns, and Reinforce their decision.

name: Wedding Cake Gym Profit Model
definition: A three-tier revenue architecture (large-group training, semi-privates, supplements) where each tier carries both icing (front-end cash) and cake (recurring EFT), designed to accommodate the full customer buying curve and capture multiple spending wallets.

name: Gym Profit Levers
definition: Three macro levers that together transform gym profitability: Price Levers (membership price, billing cycle, membership levels), Capacity Levers (session duration, membership limits, attendance spread, physical space, exercise selection), and Overhead Levers (number of sessions, trainer hours, trainer pay).

name: Five Horsemen of Retention
definition: Five evidence-based retention tactics for membership businesses: Reach-Outs (personal touch every 14 days), Attendance Tracking (weekly red-flag identification), Handwritten Cards (at sign-up, referral requests, milestones), Member Events (every 21 days), and Exit Interviews (re-sell using C-L-O-S-E-R).

name: Client-Financed Acquisition
definition: A growth model in which a high-ticket front-end offer generates more cash on Day 1 than the cost of the leads that produced it, creating a negative acquisition cost and eliminating the need for a marketing budget.

name: Ideal Customer Life Cycle
definition: Four sequential customer milestones gym owners should deliberately engineer: Connect (form a relationship quickly), Refer/Testify (earn social proof and referrals), Testify/Refer (order may flip), and Ascend (upsell to higher-tier service or adjacent product).

name: The Four Functions of Business
definition: Every business requires four specialized roles: marketer (promotion and brand), salesperson (conversion), product person (design and experience), and operator/customer success (implementation and retention).

name: Three Levels of Entrepreneurial Evolution
definition: Players progress from individual contributor (doing the work), to specialist/executive (managing a function), to coach (recruiting, building culture, and delegating decisions).

name: Output Formula
definition: Total output is determined by two variables: volume of activity (hours of work) multiplied by leverage of activity (impact per unit of work).

name: Angry Customer De-escalation
definition: When a customer is upset, validate their anger and take ownership immediately; downplaying creates discrepancy and escalates emotion, while empathy and action reduce tension.

name: Insurance Product Architecture
definition: Transform a service (storage, maintenance, conditioning) into a perceived insurance product by anchoring it to a familiar comparison (e.g., car insurance) and framing ongoing value preservation.

name: No-Based Close Framework
definition: Structure upsells by embedding the base offer in the close question (e.g., 'We'll store and condition the coat—you don't want anything else, do you?') so a no-response confirms yes on the base offer.

name: Scarcity and Demand Perception
definition: Create artificial scarcity via limits (e.g., two coats per customer), multiple price strikes, final-sale language, and single-file queuing to trigger urgency and perception of high demand.

name: Content Graph vs. Social Graph
definition: A two-axis model distinguishing platforms that serve content based on your social network (social graph) from platforms that serve content based on interest signals regardless of social connections (content graph); TikTok operates on the content graph, which enables discovery of content the user did not know they would want.
concept: Platform Choice and Backup Channel Resilience

name: Single-Highest-Leverage Activity Framework
definition: Identify the one activity that, if done alone, accomplishes all other objectives; hire people for everything else and concentrate founder time entirely on that activity.

name: Four Acquisition Channels
definition: Four non-referral channels for getting clients: paid ads, organic content, cold outreach, and affiliate/partner networks.

name: Sales God to Sales Training God Identity Shift
definition: A two-phase identity reframe for founder-dependent sales businesses: Phase 1 (sales god) — founder closes deals personally and maximizes individual output; Phase 2 (sales training god) — founder codifies their winning behaviors into teachable scripts and systems, and judges themselves by how well they can replicate their performance in others rather than by their own closing numbers.

name: Dollars Per Box Focus
definition: A unit-economics operating discipline in which every employee and decision is anchored to the net profit generated per box shipped, including all variable costs (meat, packaging, dry ice, shipping, credit card fees), rather than top-line revenue.

name: Barbell Hiring Strategy
definition: A talent acquisition model that recruits at two extremes: recent graduates or early-career workers (hungry, high learning velocity) and experienced retirees (domain expertise, legacy-driven), deliberately avoiding mid-career professionals who optimize for title and resume advancement over output.

name: For Life Offer Stack
definition: A retention architecture in which subscribers accumulate multiple ongoing product perks (e.g., free bacon for life, free ground beef for life) tied to continuous subscription, making cancellation progressively costlier as perk count grows.

name: Trojan Horse Influencer Outreach
definition: An influencer acquisition tactic in which the brand leads with a genuine value exchange (featuring the influencer's recipes in shipped boxes) to earn a reply, then converts the conversation into a promotional partnership, paying the influencer in currency they prefer (fame/reach) rather than upfront cash.

name: Guaranteed Path + Fast Path Market Entry
definition: A two-track strategy for entering a new local market: one track is the reliable organic/outreach playbook (guaranteed path); the other is paid ads at low daily budget ($100-200/day) to accelerate learning (fast path). Both run concurrently.

name: CPA Channel Expansion Model
definition: Replace dependence on 3-4 high-value referral partners by expanding to 30-40 CPAs, converting each into an independent pipeline that collectively 10x lead flow without changing the core offer.

name: Sales Director Role Definition
definition: A sales director's primary function is culture maintenance and daily sales training — not closing deals or carrying specialized domain knowledge about the product being sold.

name: Scientific Attribution Model
definition: A hybrid attribution rule: if conversion happens within 30 days of a touchpoint, credit goes to last touch; if more than 30 days, credit goes to first touch. Designed to avoid over-indexing on direct response (last-touch only) or brand (first-touch only).

name: Delivery-Change Moral High Ground Pitch
definition: A three-part reframe for announcing a delivery reduction: (1) acknowledge you have been falling short of a stated promise, (2) position the change as restoring integrity rather than cutting service, (3) list reasons the new format benefits clients, making it socially costly for any client to object.

name: Big Head Long Tail Pricing
definition: Charge a large upfront fee for the primary value (skill or transformation), then price the continuity component much lower as a near-free network access fee, separating one-time value from consumable recurring value.

name: Five-Part Sales Training Rotation
definition: Break sales team training into five rotating daily segments: intro, discovery, offer, objections, looping, and a fifth wild-card slot for the current high-priority skill gap; rotate through all segments to keep every part of the script sharp.
concept: Daily Sales Role-Play as Training Cadence

name: Three-Bucket Avatar Segmentation
definition: Segment prospects by three independent axes: demographics (who they look like), quantifiables (business size and financials), and behaviors (actions correlated with activation and retention); only sell to avatars that score well on all three.

name: Management Diamond
definition: A diagnostic model for identifying why a person is not executing: they don't know they need to do it, don't know how, don't know when, have something blocking them, or lack motivation.

name: Inbound/Outbound Separation
definition: Inbound and outbound sales must be structurally separate teams; inbound is a reward earned by top closers, not a starting point for new salespeople.

name: Recruiting as Volume Game
definition: When talent is the binding constraint, the primary lever is 3-10x outreach volume and recruiter headcount, not recruiter quality alone — treated identically to a sales volume problem.

name: Talent Investment ROI Math
definition: A three-variable calculation (cost of hire, gross profit per hire, number of hires needed) that frames a recruiting budget as a capital-allocation decision with a stated payback multiple.

name: 20% Guaranteed Cost of Change
definition: Every change to a running business incurs a guaranteed ~20% performance decrement before any gains accrue; this floor means a change requires 50%+ upside to justify the certain downside.

name: Defend-the-Perimeter Scaling Metaphor
definition: A spatial analogy mapping business scope to physical defense area: the larger the territory a single person tries to defend, the less effective their defense becomes; a founder spreading across multiple business layers is analogous to guarding an entire city block solo.

name: Creative Agency Pivot: Volume Over Premium
definition: A two-pole strategic choice for AI ad production businesses: pursue true enterprise at $500K with the AI kept hidden, OR pursue mid-market clients spending $100K+/month in ads by replacing their entire creative team with high-volume AI-generated ads at a monthly retainer.

name: Four-Problem Upstream Diagnosis
definition: A four-part diagnostic for revenue-plateau businesses: avatar clarity, offer structure, positioning, and messaging — in that order of fix priority.

name: Map Clients to Product Suite (Not Product to Clients)
definition: Rather than customizing every offer to each client's venue, templatize a product suite (e.g., three core configurations) and map inbound clients to the nearest template.

name: Global vs. Local Positioning Frame
definition: For corporate or B2B buyers who will try to commoditize the offer, reframe the value conversation from line-item cost to total business cost (time, switching costs, headcount waste), so that price comparison becomes impossible.

name: Two-Path Exit Decision
definition: When a service business has both an operator-facing education or coaching arm and a corporate/studio arm, the founder must choose between path A (information/coaching = higher annual income, very hard to sell) and path B (corporate brand = lower annual income, easier to sell at exit); there is no viable third path.

name: Equity Decomposition Framework (Cash Flow, Sale, Risk, Control)
definition: A four-part breakdown of what equity actually consists of (cash flow, sale upside, risk, and control) used to identify which components an employee actually wants so non-dilutive alternatives can be offered in their place.

name: OTE Reverse-Engineering for Profit Share
definition: A compensation design process that starts from desired on-target earnings for a role, then back-calculates the profit-share percentage required to hit that OTE at expected profit levels, rather than picking an arbitrary percentage.

name: The Swamp
definition: A 1-3M revenue band where thin margins (10-20%) make hiring an operator impossible without absorbing the majority of available profit, trapping founders in a double-bind of either working two full-time roles or taking a large bet that destroys profitability.

name: Sales Motion Fix Before Pricing Fix
definition: A two-step repair sequence: fix the in-person close process first (order 1), then raise prices (order 2); reversing the sequence is ineffective because a broken sales motion causes the founder to attribute low conversion to price, when the real driver is process.

name: Direct Response Doom Loop
definition: A compressing cycle in which e-commerce revenue scales via paid media while margins simultaneously shrink until the business becomes a high-liability, low-margin operation that must keep selling just to sustain its cost base.

name: Eugene Schwartz Awareness Pyramid
definition: A five-level customer awareness hierarchy (Unaware, Problem Aware, Solution Aware, Product Aware, Most Aware) that determines what hook and click journey a prospect requires; bridge pages convert colder audiences by stepping them up through levels before reaching a sales page.

name: Brand Completion Loop
definition: A virtuous cycle in which a strong brand promise attracts customers, the product experience either reinforces or destroys that promise, and reinforcement deepens brand equity, enabling premium pricing and affiliate recruitment.

name: Pre-Job / Post-Job Contractor Vetting Framework
definition: A two-phase contractor evaluation system: pre-job checks (availability, split agreement, communication quality) and post-job verification (invoice confirmation, customer callback, willingness-to-return test) to assess reliability and trustworthiness before committing to ongoing use.

name: Marketing as Filtration System
definition: Marketing finds ideal buyers who already exist rather than educating or converting beginners into ideal buyers; the message and medium select for the avatar, not transform them.

name: Nail It Then Scale It
definition: A sequencing rule for brick-and-mortar expansion: prove that a single unit operates at sustained performance without the founder before committing capital to a second location.

name: Founder-Absence Test (Three-to-Six Month)
definition: A three-to-six month period in which the founder fully withdraws from day-to-day operations to confirm the GM can sustain or grow the business independently; failure during this window blocks expansion.

name: ACQ Universe Framework
definition: A layered monetization architecture: free media generates attention, low-ticket conversions (books, email list, School) capture contact info, a tiered advisory practice converts business owners to high-ticket, and excess capital redeploys into real estate, ventures, and private equity — all anchored by one brand credibility promise.

name: Disney Analogy for B2B Media Company
definition: Maps Acquisition.com revenue streams to Disney properties: brand = Disney Studios, ACQ Network = Disney+, Advisory Practice = theme parks, School = Star Wars/Marvel franchise investments, insurance/sales AI/lending = future spokes — illustrating how a single brand supports multiple distinct monetization arms.

name: Billionaire Wealth Construction Phases
definition: Three phases of misunderstanding how billionaire wealth accumulates: phase one (make $1B yearly), phase two (take home $1-2B lifetime), phase three (own assets worth $1B+ that appreciate tax-free).

name: Billionaire Reversal-Engineering Framework
definition: Four required properties of billionaire-scale opportunities: not limited by founder time, serve a massive marketplace, have very high gross margins, and operate on a very long time horizon.

name: Leverage and Acquisition Returns
definition: The mechanics of acquisition financing: write check for fraction of purchase price (e.g., $15M down on $50M deal), take loan for remainder (e.g., $35M), use cash flows to pay back debt during hold period, then realize full appreciation multiple on the original equity.

name: One-Level-Up Channel Strategy
definition: Instead of acquiring end customers directly, acquire the intermediary (agency, guru, mentor) who already has those customers, capturing higher LTV via onboarding fees, per-customer fees, and recurring top-line percentage.

name: Logic-First vs. Empirical Testing Tradeoff
definition: When decisions are constrained to only those that make sense in advance, high-value solutions are systematically missed because their value proposition is counterintuitive.

name: Five-Step Content Growth Process
definition: A content production and distribution system with five sequential steps: (1) test ideas on Twitter/TikTok, (2) record long or short videos from winning ideas, (3) add varied call-to-actions, (4) contextualize content to each platform, (5) dramatically increase distribution volume.

name: Concentric Circles Objection Framework
definition: A sales close model that peels objections from the outside in: first circumstances (time/money/fit), then other people (spouse/partner), then avoidance (need to think) — each layer requiring its own overcome before the next is revealed.

name: Past-Present-Future Close
definition: A three-stage close sequence used once a prospect is in the avoidance layer: past (neutralize prior failures as non-predictive), present (teach a three-criteria decision framework), future (surface and resolve specific fears).

name: Three-Component Sales Team System
definition: A sales team scaling model composed of three interdependent subsystems: (1) recruiting the right talent by matching personality to sales type, (2) training reps on the prospect's pain rather than product features, (3) managing toward conviction by refreshing testimonials and success stories.

name: Choose Your Regrets Framework
definition: Christopher Hitchens' principle that because opportunity cost is structurally unavoidable in all human choices, regrets are inevitable rather than the result of bad decisions; the only agency available is choosing which regrets to accept.

name: Local Service Arbitrage Framework
definition: A business model where the operator sources low-cost service providers (typically immigrants or older workers without marketing skills), acquires clients via free Google Maps marketing, and captures the 2x+ spread between client pricing and provider cost.

name: Proof-Promise-Plan Introduction Framework
definition: A three-part intro structure for educational video content: (1) Proof — establish credibility with evidence you can deliver; (2) Promise — state what viewers will get or learn; (3) Plan — preview the structure of how the promise will be fulfilled. Order is flexible; lead with whichever element is most load-bearing for that piece.

name: Three Content Bucket Model
definition: A taxonomy dividing all content into Entertainment (goal: get people to watch/consume), Education (goal: change behavior), and Edutainment (goal: both simultaneously). The most common audience outcome — not creator intent — defines which bucket the content falls in.

name: Six Shifts Framework
definition: Alex Hormozi's six strategic pivots derived from 40 months and $4M in content production: (1) Edutainment to Education, (2) For Us to For You, (3) Wide to Narrow topics, (4) Views to Revenue (RPM) as primary metric, (5) Shorts to Longs, (6) Assume More to Assume Nothing about audience familiarity.

name: The Grandfather Frame
definition: A perspective-shifting practice that imagines viewing your current life through the eyes of your 85-year-old self, enabling gratitude for present circumstances by recognizing their irreplaceable nature.

name: Trust-Conviction Sales Framework
definition: Two necessary and sufficient conditions for any sale: the salesperson must have conviction (belief in the product) and must establish trust with the prospect; conviction transfers through trust.

name: Childlike Curiosity Objection Handling
definition: Handle objections by responding with genuine curiosity and follow-up questions rather than counter-argument; neutralizes the adversarial dynamic that prevents closing.

name: No-Based Close
definition: Ask for permission or frame the close as a low-stakes request so the prospect can say no without feeling pressured; natural persuaders use this instinctively.

name: Close-Rate Pricing Gap Framework
definition: A five-tier scale mapping close-rate ranges to the implied pricing multiple still available; 80%+ close rate = 3-4x multiple remaining; 30-40% = appropriately priced; below 30% = execution problem.

name: Service Pricing Virtuous Cycle
definition: A closed loop in which higher price enables higher gross margins, which fund better talent, which deliver better service, which improve reputation, which drive demand, which justify higher price.

name: LTV:CAC Automation Ratio Framework
definition: The minimum acceptable ratio of lifetime gross profit to customer acquisition cost varies by the number of business functions (lead gen, conversion, delivery) that are automated vs. manual: all three automated = 3:1 minimum; two automated = 6:1; one automated = 9:1; none automated = 12:1+.

name: 30-Day Cash Black Box
definition: A presale model in which ad spend is made on day 0, leads close within 24 hours, and total cash collected from those customers within 30 days exceeds the ad spend, creating a self-financing loop that funds the business build-out before the doors open.

name: S&ME Investment Framework
definition: Allocate 100% of excess income to education (courses, coaching, mentorships, workshops) that increases earning capacity rather than passive assets, because earning capacity compounds faster than 10% annual returns.

name: Skills Stack Exponential Growth
definition: Each additional skill multiplies return on existing skills: videography + editing + social media + copywriting + branding + operations + leadership creates a CMO-level asset that compounds earning capacity 10x faster than base skills alone.

name: Bridge-Building Discipline
definition: Completing one skill stack fully (all 30 bricks to first dollar) is superior to building many half-finished bridges; speed of mastery depends on identifying which brick is missing and focusing there.

name: Seven Newsworthiness Factors for Storytelling
definition: A seven-component framework identifying what makes stories compelling: recency, impact, prominence, proximity, conflict, unusualness, and update frequency. More components present = more interesting story.

name: Story Arc Elements
definition: Six structural elements of a story: setting, character, desire, struggle, eureka moment, victory, and resolution. Effective stories weave both the external (observable) and internal (emotional) journey.

name: Framework Validity Test
definition: A two-criterion test for any mental model: it must be (1) useful in practice and (2) valid across multiple different circumstances. A framework is tested by applying it to novel situations and adjusting until no falsifying case can be found.

name: Learning to Try Framework
definition: A meta-skill built by committing all discretionary effort, money, and time to one domain for an extended daily period; once internalized, the skill of sustained commitment transfers across domains (saxophone, tennis, content creation) because skill acquisition follows the same pattern everywhere.

name: Tolerance as First Component of Mental Toughness
definition: A model of mental toughness whose first component, tolerance, measures how long a person maintains their intended behavior before hardship causes a behavioral change (the fuse length), distinct from pain tolerance or pain ignorance.

name: Felix Dennis Eleven Levels of Wealth
definition: Felix Dennis's framework from his book on wealth breaks affluence into 11 tiers, asserting that only at $400M+ liquid does a person achieve true financial freedom where they can do whatever they want without constraint.
concept: Wealth Tiers and Diminishing Marginal Returns

name: Four Pillars of Millionaire Thinking
definition: Greg Lavecchia's four-part framework for what separates successful entrepreneurs: (1) opportunities reward execution not ideas; (2) knowing exactly who you build for makes everything work; (3) environment determines ceiling; (4) the goal is who you become, not external success.
concept: Execution and Rapid Adjustment Over Planning

name: Inspired Internet Pledge (Three-Principle Framework)
definition: A three-part industry commitment: (1) Create for Well-Being — understand what content attributes correlate with well-being; (2) Listen and Act — gather experiential data from users who have experienced online harm; (3) Commit to Openness — share safety learnings across the industry rather than treating user well-being as a competitive differentiator.

name: Inspiration-to-Realization Funnel
definition: Pinterest's platform design moves users from open-ended inspiration (unbranded search, mood boards) through narrowing intent to final purchase action — a full-funnel trajectory unique among digital platforms because it begins before the user has formed a specific product intent.

name: Three-Category Drop-Servicing Pricing Framework
definition: A decision tree for structuring drop-servicing margins across three service types: (1) phone-priceable low-ticket services at 50% markup, (2) on-site contractor-priced trade services at a 60/40 split, and (3) high-ticket multi-visit services at 20% markup.

name: BSL Tripod (Build, Sell, Lead)
definition: Three mutually required skill categories — building (mechanical), selling (verbal), and leading (social) — that together constitute all value-generating activity; removal of any one leg collapses the whole structure.

name: BSL x R Formula
definition: Wealth output is the product of Build, Sell, and Lead skill levels multiplied by the amount of Risk the individual is willing to assume; risk is a scalar multiplier on all three skill categories.

name: Delivery Cube
definition: A multi-axis product-design tool that explores how to solve one customer problem by varying: (1) level of personal attention, (2) customer effort expected, (3) environment/medium, (4) consumption format, (5) response speed, (6) a 10x-priced version, and (7) a 1/10th-priced same-outcome version.

name: Problem-Solution Cycle
definition: Solving a customer's presenting problem invariably generates the next problem; a mature product ecosystem anticipates this chain and pre-builds the sequence of solutions.

name: Three Paths for Multiplying Capital
definition: Money generated by BSL can be: (1) wasted, (2) stored (e.g., gold — speculative, zero yield), or (3) multiplied via buying assets or lending; only buying and lending compound over time.

name: Four-Strategy Compounding Framework
definition: Alex Hormozi's four-part personal finance strategy: (1) increase income, (2) reduce spending, (3) invest faster/earlier, (4) invest in income-earning skills as the highest-ROI lever.

name: Skill Bridge Metaphor
definition: Skills are individual bridge segments; missing links prevent income from crossing to the other side. Each purchase adds a segment, and no single skill alone spans the gap — the full chain compounds.

name: Learning Budget Model
definition: Allocate a fixed monthly percentage of income (1–10%) as a mandatory spending budget for skill experiments and education; the mechanism is forced experimentation, not optional learning.

name: SCALE Value Creation Framework
definition: Five levers that increase a business's enterprise value: (S) debt capacity from cash flow, (C) organic growth rate, (A) business categorization / tech enablement, (L) size premium, (E) age / longevity.

name: Three Ways to Make a Business More Valuable
definition: Every value-creation initiative in a business maps to one of three outputs: increase number of customers, increase lifetime value (LTV/LTGP) per customer, or decrease risk / increase reliability of future earnings.

name: Four Market Positions
definition: A marketplace contains four distinct value positions arrayed by price and experience: bargain (cheapest, poor quality), best value (better quality per dollar), premium (high-end with consistent quality), and luxury (price-insensitive status-driven).

name: Rich Customer Service Model
definition: Five principles for serving wealthy customers: deliver dream outcome with high confidence, prioritize speed and convenience over price, require minimal effort and sacrifice, accept multiple contact channels for ease, and reinvest margin to exceed promises.

name: Five Benefits of Premium Pricing
definition: Raising prices generates five customer-side benefits: increased emotional investment, higher perceived value (independent of product quality), better actual results, lower-demand customer base, and higher margin to reinvest in delivery.

name: Three-Step Super Influencer Process
definition: A three-step structured approach to leveraging influencer partnerships: (1) pick the right influencer using audience-size comparison, (2) get them to respond using verification, a magic message, and the Rule of 100, (3) close the deal using Proof-Promise-Plan-Offer preparation.

name: Proof-Promise-Plan-Offer Presentation
definition: A four-part influencer pitch structure: Promise (the upside they will receive), Proof (evidence via case studies or comparable stats), Plan (next steps and expected effort from each party), Offer (economics structured so the influencer clearly gets the better side of the deal).

name: Influencer Outreach Circle Method
definition: A layered outreach sequence for identifying and reaching influencers: (1) influencers known personally, (2) second-degree introductions from own network, (3) influencers followed or heard of via multi-channel direct outreach, (4) formal agent or website contact channels.

name: Audience-Size Partnership Model
definition: A decision rule for structuring influencer partnerships: if your brand's audience is larger than the influencer's, have them promote your brand; if their audience is larger, deliver under their brand. The relative size of audiences determines who promotes and who delivers.

name: Do Epic Then Talk Framework
definition: Two-step sequence for building credibility and providing value: (1) achieve something notable or accumulate effort-proof, then (2) talk about what you learned from it.

name: Logic-Evidence-Utility Framework
definition: A three-step analytical framework (from Dr. Cashy) for dissolving vague self-narratives: (1) Logic — define the problem in observable behavioral terms; (2) Evidence — demand actual data for the claim; (3) Utility — ask whether it matters relative to your goals.

name: Patient Outputs, Impatient Inputs
definition: A behavioral framework separating controllable inputs (actions taken) from uncontrollable outputs (results); patience means finding productive action in the meantime, while impatience drives increasing input volume.

name: Management Diamond
definition: A five-reason diagnostic for why an employee fails to complete a task: (1) did not know what was wanted, (2) did not know how to do it, (3) did not know the deadline, (4) lacked motivation/incentive, (5) was blocked by an impediment. Each node is addressed with a distinct fix: communication, training, deadline-setting, reinforcement, or blocker removal.
concept: The Execution Gap: Knowledge Without Action

name: Bundling and Unbundling Terms
definition: A communication discipline that replaces abstract bundled labels (e.g., 'be charismatic,' 'stop being a dick') with specific observable micro-behaviors so that instructions are actionable and behavior change is trainable.

name: Logic-Evidence-Utility (LEU) Framework
definition: A three-question filter for evaluating claims: (1) What does this mean? (logic/definition), (2) How do you know? (evidence), (3) So what? (utility/actionability). Used to detect bullshit and sharpen thinking.
concept: Undefined Words Create Mythology and Prevent Clear Thinking

name: Four Paths to Ultra-Wealth
definition: A taxonomy of four capital structures for wealth accumulation: (1) other people's money in your business (VC-backed founder), (2) your money in your business (bootstrapped founder), (3) your money in other people's businesses (investor), (4) other people's money in other people's businesses (fund manager).

name: Two and Twenty Fund Structure
definition: The standard private equity and venture capital fee structure: 2% annual management fee on funds raised, plus 20% carried interest on profits at fund conclusion; carried interest is taxed at capital gains rates.

name: Compounding Vehicle Test
definition: A business must have one of two compounding mechanisms to generate inevitable growth: customers who never stop buying (recurring/reoccurring revenue) or a distribution base of people who never stop selling.

name: V-Shape Rebound Toolkit
definition: A named collection of cognitive tools (cosmic relevance, veteran frame) whose shared purpose is to compress the time from an aversive event back to baseline behavior, making recovery as rapid and V-shaped as possible.

name: Veteran Frame
definition: A perspective tool: imagine the same inconvenience occurring one thousand times in a row; identify how you would feel on the thousandth occurrence; then recognize that feeling is available on the first occurrence because the circumstance itself has not changed.

name: Cosmic Relevance Frame
definition: A perspective tool that situates a personal setback within its astronomical context (planet orbiting a sun inside a galaxy inside an ever-expanding universe) to instantly reduce the perceived magnitude of the setback to near zero.

name: Four Pillars of Legitimate Education
definition: A four-part framework distinguishing legitimate education businesses from scams: selective customer admission, data-backed outcomes (not income promises), free content paired with paid implementation, and willingness to fail students to protect brand.

name: Goose and Eggs Framework
definition: Distinguishes the asset that generates value (the goose) from the sellable outputs that asset produces (the eggs); advises founders to hold the goose and sell the eggs rather than liquidating the generative asset itself.

name: Franchise Law Three-Part Test
definition: A business becomes a legally defined franchise when it combines three elements: a shared name, a shared system, and a fee. Any two of the three elements alone avoids franchise classification; all three without registration creates an illegal franchise.

name: Roll-Up Arbitrage Model
definition: Aggregating fragmented businesses into a single entity to sell at a higher earnings multiple than any individual unit would command; the orchestrator earns a percentage of the upside from the multiple expansion while all participants benefit.

name: C-L-O-S-E-R Sales Script Framework
definition: A question-based call structure: Clarify why the prospect is there, Label them with their problem, Overview their past experiences and pains, Sell by invitation (get invited to pitch), Explain solutions to 2-3 of their stated problems, then address concerns and Reinforce the decision.

name: Sales Manager Daily Feedback Loop
definition: A structured 60-minute per-rep weekly cadence: 30 minutes reviewing 1-2 recorded calls at 2x speed with written notes, 5 minutes communicating the top 1-2 highest-impact improvements, 25 minutes role-playing those specific improvements with the rep.

name: Sales Team Culture Triad
definition: Three levers for maintaining sales team culture and performance: (1) a live visual leaderboard, (2) KPI-linked competitions every 4-6 weeks, (3) mandatory bottom-10% quarterly cuts.

name: Behavioral Change Intensity Scale
definition: A two-pole axis measuring how much behavior changes after a person's tolerance threshold is exceeded: high fortitude = minimal behavior change; low fortitude = severe, life-disrupting behavior change.

name: Four Money Source Types
definition: A taxonomy of four categories from which any purchase can be funded: past money (savings), income money (current earnings), debt money (future earnings borrowed), and new money (incremental income generated specifically for the purchase using underutilized existing resources).
concept: Fast Cash Plays via Underutilized Assets

name: Sawdust Money Framework
definition: A personal purchasing philosophy in which a discretionary purchase is funded exclusively by activating currently underutilized resources (time, assets, skills) to generate incremental revenue dedicated to that specific purchase, leaving existing income flows, savings, and debt position untouched.
concept: Fast Cash Plays via Underutilized Assets

name: Six Principles for Building Capacity Before Knowing What to Do
definition: A six-part framework for ambitious people who lack direction: (1) build physical and financial capacity, (2) save money to buy optionality, (3) add and practice skills, (4) build an audience without a product, (5) build a waitlist before building the thing, (6) expand luck surface area via networking and geographic proximity.

name: Skill Stacking Multiplier
definition: Each new skill acquired multiplies the value of all previously held skills; the portfolio grows super-linearly because each layer has the prior layers as prerequisites.

name: Conscious Trade Accounting Framework
definition: Every life outcome requires a conscious trade of something valued (time, safety, experience); the framework asks two questions: what am I trading, and what am I trading it for.

name: Upside-Downside Asymmetry Frame
definition: Downside is bounded (survivable worst-case) while upside is unbounded; therefore rational action tilts toward taking bets rather than avoiding them.

name: Wallet Objection Handling Framework
definition: A structured five-step process to address wallet/payment objections during closing by confirming payment method availability upfront and providing alternative payment paths (ACH, Apple Wallet, delayed payment).

name: RFP Frame + Value Frame Stack
definition: Every B2B sales conversation operates on two simultaneous layers: the RFP frame (commodity, price-comparison, minimum viable compliance) and the value frame (holistic business impact, ROI, total cost of risk). Winning requires satisfying the RFP floor while differentiating on the value ceiling.

name: Case Study Close
definition: In procurement-driven (RFP) sales contexts, attach a peer-company case study to every bid that demonstrates the most analogous client's outcome on the exact value drivers (speed, risk reduction, total cost) the buyer cares about; the prior client's voice displaces price-only comparison.

name: Flip to Motivated Buyer Framework
definition: When sellers are structurally reluctant (frozen market), redirect sourcing effort toward buyers with forced timelines (e.g., 1031 exchange deadlines) who must transact regardless of market conditions, and use their urgency to extract seller-side deals.

name: Community-as-CRM Asset Framework
definition: Build a gated community of your exact target avatar (e.g., multifamily owners in one metro), position yourself as the gating function, and over time create a proprietary CRM that is both an ongoing deal-flow engine and a sellable business asset.

name: Commission-to-Consulting Revenue Conversion
definition: Replace variable transaction-based commission income with a fixed annual consulting retainer; subsidize the retainer with a deeply discounted commission rate so the recurring income is pulled forward while clients perceive total cost as lower.

name: Many-Sided Die Framework
definition: A mental model in which business success is represented as a die roll: each attempt converts a red side to green when it succeeds; the number of sides (difficulty) is unknown; the only guarantee is that continued rolling eventually produces a green streak, and quitting guarantees loss.

name: Infinite Game of Business
definition: Business is an infinite game with no terminal winner; the only distinction is between players (those still in the game) and quitters; staying in the game is the sole winning condition.

name: Four Types of Leverage (4Cs)
definition: Four categories of leverage that multiply output relative to input: Collaboration (people working for you), Capital (other people's money deployed on their behalf), Code (software that scales without incremental labor), and Content (media that reaches many without repeated effort).

name: Document-Demonstrate-Duplicate
definition: A three-step skill transfer framework: (1) the teacher documents the skill as a step-by-step reference, (2) demonstrates it live in front of the learner, and (3) the learner duplicates it in front of the teacher for feedback.

name: Earn-to-Learn Transition Sequence
definition: A four-phase career transition: (1) live below your means to stack cash, (2) start a side hustle and sustain it until it matches current income, (3) sustain the match for six months to confirm it is not a seasonal spike, then (4) cut the employment cord.

name: Business Video Verification Framework
definition: Three-component video submission process for Google Business Profile verification: location proof via street signage, business proof via company vehicle and tools, and ownership proof via vehicle access.

name: Service Area Business Listing Strategy
definition: An operational model for listing and ranking plumbing, HVAC, and trade-service businesses in target geographies without requiring a physical address, using only service area designations.

name: Three-Tier Google Business Profile Reinstatement Strategy
definition: A categorization of suspended profile recovery difficulty into low-barrier niches (high success, minimal evidence), service-area profiles (moderate difficulty, documentation helpful), and spammy-category+address profiles (high difficulty, substantial documentation required).

name: STAR System
definition: A five-step diagnostic framework for why a person did not do what was asked: (1) did they not know I wanted it done, (2) did they not know what I wanted done, (3) did they not know how to do it, (4) did they not know when it was due, (5) were they blocked by circumstances.

name: Document-Demonstrate-Duplicate
definition: A three-step skill-transfer protocol: write the steps (document), perform the steps in front of the trainee (demonstrate), have the trainee perform the steps in front of you (duplicate).

name: Need-to-Believes Minimization
definition: Reduce the number of distinct beliefs a customer must hold before purchasing; fewer required beliefs means faster, higher-volume conversion.

name: Pre Greater Than Post
definition: Invest effort in idea and concept development before execution; pre-production leverage dwarfs post-production editing for educational and advertising content.

name: Sell in a Vacuum
definition: Two paths to eliminate price competition: sell where no one else sells (location advantage) or sell something no one else sells (product advantage).

name: Damaging Admissions Formula
definition: Acknowledge a genuine negative before stating a compelling positive; the admission amplifies belief in the positive claim and neutralizes objections the prospect was already holding.

name: Three-Step Business Scaling Framework
definition: Sequential model: (1) Promote to acquire customers, (2) Improve product through customer feedback loops, (3) Scale marketing spend once retention and LTV are proven.

name: Reoccurring vs Recurring Revenue Model
definition: Distinction between subscription-based recurring revenue (Netflix, utilities) and transactional reoccurring revenue (Facebook ads, one-time purchases that repeat).

name: Conviction-Trust Sales Framework
definition: Two necessary conditions for any sale: (1) the seller must have near-total conviction in their product, and (2) the prospect must develop enough trust in the seller that the seller's conviction transfers to the prospect.

name: Consultative Sales Sequence
definition: A structured conversation sequence: (1) why are they there / what is the problem, (2) what have they tried and failed, (3) why your product is different from what failed, (4) ask permission to explain the product, (5) explain through experiences (not features), using analogies, (6) close.

name: No-Based Close
definition: Framing the close as a soft opt-out question (e.g., 'Would you mind?') rather than a hard yes-demand, exploiting natural communication dynamics where 'I don't mind' is easier to say than 'yes'.

name: Three-Factor Instant Verification Trust Model
definition: Google trusts established Gmail accounts, devices, and previous activity; instant verification requires a combination of all three factors working in alignment.

name: GMB Optimization Maturity Model
definition: Three tiers of GMB profile completeness determine ranking speed and call volume: abandoned (no optimization), minimally optimized (basic profile work), and fully optimized (reviews, photos, description, citations, backlinks).

name: Content-First to Paid Ads Sequencing
definition: A three-step acquisition sequence: (1) post organic before/after content, (2) identify the best-performing piece, (3) attach a CTA and run it as a paid ad.

name: Risk-Adjusted Debt Analysis
