definition: A financial analysis framework that applies beta-style volatility adjustment (as used in mutual fund comparison) to business and real estate debt, making the true risk cost of leverage mathematically comparable to unleveraged alternatives.

name: Calibrated Cannonballs
definition: Jim Collins-coined framework Dave Ramsey adopted: test ideas at small scale (cannonball) before committing full resources, as opposed to firing full cannonballs blind (unfocused hustle).

name: Loss Leader Splinter
definition: Itemize all components of your offer, peel off one high-perceived-value component, price it at 80-90% off to drive traffic, then upsell the full bundle at standard margin.

name: Gift Card Referral Strategy
definition: Sell heavily discounted gift cards (80-90% off face value) limited to 2 per existing customer, restricted to use by friends and family only, capturing referral contact info at point of sale for follow-up and conversion to higher-ticket upsell.

name: High-Ticket Scarcity Drop
definition: Create a premium offer priced 10-100x the standard offer, limit availability to 5% of your customer base (the top 20% of the top 20% by spend), build advance hype, then publicly count down remaining units to amplify FOMO.

name: Buy X Get Y Free (Prepay)
definition: Set a differentiated service tier at 2x the standard price, add 1-2 features unavailable in the standard tier to justify the price difference, then offer additional units free (buy 1 get 2, buy 4 get 8) to front-load cash and accelerate customer acquisition.

name: MAGIC Offer Wrapper
definition: A five-element naming and positioning frame applied to any promotion: Magnetic reason why (M), Avatar specificity (A), Goal/dream outcome (G), time Interval (I), Container word/bucket label (C). Combines to produce an offer name that calls out the right buyer and sets expectation of a specific transformation.

name: Work = Outputs = Volume x Leverage
definition: A redefinition of work as outputs (enterprise value created) rather than time or effort; work rate is outputs divided by time, making leverage — the multiplier on each unit of activity — the primary variable to optimize.

name: Stages of Change / Uninformed Optimism Cycle
definition: A five-stage arc (uninformed optimism -> informed pessimism -> crisis of meaning -> informed optimism -> achievement) that most entrepreneurs abort at the crisis of meaning, re-entering at uninformed optimism with a new venture instead of completing the arc.

name: Woman in the Red Dress Discipline
definition: A named discipline for saying no to attractive-but-distracting opportunities; capacity to decline scales with the dollar value of the opportunity, requiring deliberate practice at each level.

name: Four Brand Economics
definition: Brand translates to four compounding business benefits: (1) conversion rate lift (more people buy when presented with an offer), (2) click-through rate lift (more people take the first action in the funnel), (3) price point premium (customers pay more for trusted brands), (4) repurchases (existing customers buy again and again).
concept: Brand Effect on Customer Behavior and WTP

name: Four Levels of Lead Getter Leverage
definition: Four levels of customer acquisition leverage, ranked by output per unit of founder effort: (1) solo founder doing outreach directly (1:1 ratio, fully capped), (2) employees or agencies doing outreach on the founder's behalf (centralized multiplier), (3) affiliates or independent businesses sending referrals (decentralized multiplier), (4) existing customers referring new customers organically (compounding decentralized multiplier).

name: Input-Output Money-Making System
definition: Every business has a set of granular input activities that directly drive two outputs: number of customers and lifetime value per customer. Scaling requires (a) identifying the actual input activities (not amorphous descriptors), (b) eliminating non-contributing activities, and (c) scaling inputs via automation, other people, or one-to-many leverage.

name: Four-Step Google Review Generation via Facebook Marketplace
definition: A systematic process for generating local Google reviews by offering monetary incentives through Facebook Marketplace, managing reviewer locations, and verifying legitimacy.

name: Six Persuasion Tools (Cialdini-Applied)
definition: Alex Hormozi's application of Robert Cialdini's influence research to his own businesses: reciprocity, consistency, social proof, liking, authority, and scarcity/urgency — each operationalized with concrete business tactics.

name: ACA Framework
definition: A three-step conversational rapport sequence: Acknowledge what the other person said, Compliment what it reveals about them, then Ask the next question to move the conversation forward.

name: BATNA (Best Alternative to a Negotiated Agreement)
definition: A negotiator's best alternative if the current deal fails; serves as the psychological floor below which no agreement should be accepted, and as a source of leverage that enables more aggressive initial offers.

name: MESO (Multiple Equivalent Simultaneous Offers)
definition: Presenting two or three structurally different but economically equivalent offers simultaneously to reveal the counterpart's hidden priorities and embed reciprocity without a concession.

name: Deal Variable Expansion
definition: Decomposing a negotiation into as many independent variables as possible (price, speed, risk allocation, ease, terms, furnishings, financing) so that horse-trading preserves anchor price while appearing cooperative.

name: Leaky Bucket Retention Diagnosis
definition: Track monthly joins versus cancels to classify a recurring-revenue business as growing, flat, or declining; MRR grows only when new members exceed churned members.

name: Day-90 / Month-6 Retention Milestones
definition: Two tactical milestones that predict long-term retention: surviving day 90 cuts monthly churn roughly in half; surviving month 6 cuts it by ~5x again, because churn drops from 20%+ in months 1-3 to ~10% at day 90, then to ~2% by month 6.

name: Snakes and Ladders Onboarding
definition: Remove snakes (friction, confusion, overwhelm) and front-load ladders (the stickiest value moments) in onboarding; new members should hit a fast win within the first 24 hours.

name: Lead-with-Free Client Acquisition Framework
definition: A three-stage approach for zero-track-record service founders: (1) offer free engagement (e.g., five calls) to eliminate the proof barrier, (2) win on service quality and aligned incentive signaling, (3) convert to paid or collect testimonial for future paid prospects.

name: Four Business Shapes
definition: All businesses belong to one of four structural types (e-commerce, service, education/info-media, SaaS) each with a characteristic growth curve, dominant scaling constraint, and competitive moat requirement.

name: Big Head, Long Tail
definition: In education businesses, charge a high one-time price for the core knowledge (big head) and a much lower recurring price for consumable ongoing elements such as community, updated resources, or continued education (long tail); the mismatch in value is what drives churn when the ratio is reversed.

name: Attraction-Conversion-Delivery
definition: Every business has three structural layers: attraction (getting leads), conversion (closing sales), and delivery (fulfilling the service or product); the layer that requires human labor is the scaling constraint.

name: Core Four Methods
definition: The four and only four advertising methods available to any business: warm outreach (1-to-1, known), cold outreach (1-to-1, unknown), paid ads (1-to-many, unknown), and content posting (1-to-many, known). Growth requires going all-in on one before adding others.

name: More, Better, New Growth Framework
definition: Three and only three primary growth strategies: do more of what already works (highest risk-adjusted return), do what you are doing better (incremental improvement), or do something entirely new (highest risk, lowest return probability). Most entrepreneurs default to New when More is almost always the correct answer.

name: Proof, Promise, Plan Hook Formula
definition: Alex Hormozi's top-performing YouTube hook structure, derived from reviewing highest-view videos: lead with proof (demonstrate the result exists), follow with promise (what the viewer will get), close with plan (how they will get it). Applies to content, cold outbound, and paid ads.

name: 70-20-10 Effort Allocation Rule
definition: Allocate 70% of advertising and content effort to direct carbon copies of proven winning hooks and formats; 20% to adjacent variations one degree removed from the proven core; 10% to entirely new experiments. Hormozi cites this ratio as grounded in work by Sergey Brin / Larry Page and asserts most entrepreneurs have it exactly inverted.

name: Five Levels of Customer Awareness
definition: Eugene Schwartz's framework: Unaware (no knowledge of problem or solution) -> Problem Aware (knows they have pain) -> Solution Aware (knows solutions exist) -> Product Aware (knows specific products) -> Most Aware (existing customer, ready for offer). Advertising message complexity and offer-directness must match the awareness level of the target audience. Direct response captures only the Most Aware slice; brand building moves the larger unaware/problem-aware population toward purchase.

name: Supply vs. Demand Triage
definition: A binary diagnostic framework that classifies every business growth problem as either supply-constrained (too few capacity to serve existing demand) or demand-constrained (too few customers for existing capacity) before prescribing any intervention.

name: Three Supply Levers
definition: For supply-constrained businesses, three ordered levers: (1) raise prices substantially to reduce load and increase margin, (2) change the service-to-delivery ratio from one-on-one to one-to-many, (3) hire and train additional staff to parallel the founder's capacity.

name: Accordion Constraint Cycle
definition: The natural business dynamic where solving a demand constraint creates a supply constraint and vice versa; growth stalls when founders fail to recognize which constraint is currently binding and keep working on the one they already solved.

name: Network-vs-Headhunter Role Routing
definition: Hire within your own network for roles where you have domain expertise to evaluate candidates; use a paid headhunter for roles where you lack that expertise (e.g., finance, tech, HR at leadership level).

name: City Selection Framework for Google Business Profiles
definition: A two-axis evaluation model for selecting service-area cities: balance high search volume with low-to-medium competition, verify contractor availability, and filter for profitable demographics.

name: Search Volume and Competition Threshold Matrix
definition: Quantified guidance for minimum searches and maximum competitor review counts, varying by service ticket price and delivery model (service-area vs. address-based).

name: Value Equation
definition: A four-component model for pricing based on perceived value: Dream Outcome x Perceived Likelihood of Achievement, divided by Time Delay x Effort and Sacrifice. Raising the numerator or lowering the denominator increases what the market will pay.

name: Customer Finance Acquisition
definition: A cash-flow structure in which the first customer transaction is priced to cover CAC + COGS + next-customer CAC within 30 days, making the customer base self-financing and removing capital as a growth constraint.

name: Wealth Alchemy
definition: The mechanism by which customer acquisition cost, annual recurring revenue, and enterprise value multiples compound: spending $X on permanent-customer CAC creates $Y in annual revenue that is worth $10Y+ in tax-free enterprise value at sale.

name: Cringe-as-Status-Play Reframe
definition: A three-part disambiguation of cringe, shame, and guilt that exposes cringe as a defensive status signal from the observer, not evidence of wrongdoing by the actor.
concept: Shame vs. Guilt: Navigating Social Signals

name: Three Strategic Objectives Filter
definition: Every initiative must map to one of three objectives: (1) get more customers, (2) increase LTGP (make customers worth more), or (3) reduce risk that those two things stop happening (increase enterprise value). Anything not mapping to one of these is cut.

name: More, Better, New Sequencing
definition: Before adding any new initiative, first maximize volume of the best existing activity (More), then optimize its quality and efficiency (Better); only after exhausting both steps should new channels or initiatives be added (New). Most businesses skip straight to New.

name: Eight Ways to Get Customers (Core Four + OOP Four)
definition: Only four direct acquisition methods exist: warm outreach, cold outreach, paid ads, and content. All four can also be executed by Other People (OOP): customers (referrals), affiliates, employees, and agencies. Every lead strategy maps to one of these eight cells.

name: Rule of 100
definition: Daily minimum lead-generation activity standard: spend $100 on ads, OR make 100 cold outreaches, OR make 100 warm outreaches, OR produce 100 minutes of content. Volume done consistently at this floor compounds results.

name: Impact-Ease Prioritization Matrix
definition: Rank all initiatives by two dimensions: impact (revenue or risk effect) and ease (effort required). Execute high-impact/easy tasks first, work down the quadrants, and discard low-impact/hard tasks regardless of how appealing they feel.

name: What-Who-How Planning
definition: Strategy sessions produce a list of Whats (objectives). Each What must be assigned a Who (person responsible). If the same Who has held the same What for three or more quarters without completing it, the Who is the problem, not the What.

name: Volume and Time Frame Recontextualization
definition: A two-lever mental model using volume (frequency normalization) and time horizon (existential perspective) to reframe negative circumstances as neutral or positive.

name: Seven-Step Outlearning Process
definition: A sequential learning framework: (1) define learning as same-condition behavior change, (2) deconstruct the skill into sub-behaviors, (3) define measurable success criteria, (4) ignore causal explanations and focus on observable inputs/outputs, (5) model top performers by observing what they do, (6) analyze differences between your top 10% attempts and the rest and iterate, (7) repeat with increasing volume.

name: Skill Deconstruction Hierarchy
definition: Skills are nested from broad domain labels (business, basketball) down through sub-skills (marketing, dribbling) to atomic observable behaviors that can be tracked and changed; learning requires chunking down to the observable behavioral unit.

name: Start-Stop-Keep Feedback Format
definition: A three-part feedback structure: identify behaviors you want someone to start (not currently doing), stop (currently doing but unwanted), and keep (currently doing and valuable). Translates culture into observable behavioral directives.

name: Culture-Talent-Training Execution Triad
definition: Three-part diagnostic for why execution fails: (1) Culture — the rules governing what gets rewarded and punished; (2) Talent — the quality of people doing the behaviors; (3) Training — translating abstract goals into observable, repeatable behaviors.

name: Four Investor Acquisition Channels
definition: Four discrete paths to reach accredited investors without relying on a personal network: (1) affiliate model (leverage someone else's existing investor audience), (2) paid ads (targeted to accredited investors), (3) content marketing (thought leadership that attracts inbound investor interest), (4) outbound direct contact.

name: Three Levels of Salesmanship
definition: A progression from solo selling (Level 1) to recruiting individual salespeople (Level 2) to building and leading a team of salespeople (Level 3); each level requires a distinct identity and skill set.

name: Bad Google Review Removal Framework
definition: A systematic three-tiered escalation process: report from the owner account, recruit 3+ separate accounts to report (prioritizing local guide accounts), and if unsuccessful, escalate to daily reports across multiple accounts over a week.

name: Downside Tolerance Decision Filter
definition: A four-question sequence for evaluating any new opportunity: (1) What is the upside? (2) What is the downside? (3) Can I live with the downside? (4) How likely is the downside? If the downside is not livable, do not proceed regardless of upside.

name: Licensing Approval Gate
definition: A single prerequisite criterion before permitting expansion into a licensing model: the existing core business must be able to open a new location every quarter using a team that does not include the founder, with zero founder involvement required.

name: Ham and Garlic Framework
definition: Wrap the thing customers need (garlic: continuity) inside the thing they want (ham: a defined short program); the front-end defined offer is a sales vehicle, not the end product.

name: Two-Pronged Distribution Layer Strategy
definition: When building a distribution layer, combine (1) a launch campaign for immediate value for affiliates/distributors who have no initial trust, and (2) a long-term retention journey that treats distributors as customers with their own customer journey.

name: Observable Universe Definitions Framework
definition: Define every abstract concept in terms of observable, court-admissible behaviors so that all parties share a common referent and communication becomes precise rather than amorphous.

name: Behavior-Ladder Decomposition
definition: Break abstract trait labels (confident, lazy, patient) into the discrete observable micro-behaviors that cause observers to apply those labels, then address those micro-behaviors directly.

name: Traffic-Volume Funnel Routing
definition: Route cold traffic to live call (small volume) or webinar with post-webinar 1-on-1 solicitation (larger volume); funnel structure scales with traffic quantity.

name: C-L-O-S-E-R Framework
definition: A six-stage question-based sales call structure: Clarify (why they are on the call), Label (restate the problem back to them), Overview (past pains and failed solutions), Sell (the vacation / the outcome), Explain (away objections), Reinforce (the decision post-yes). Works for B2C and B2B from $500 to $100,000+ ticket prices.

name: Three Distortions of Reality (Ellis Framework)
definition: From cognitive behavioral therapy, Albert Ellis reduced sales objections to three root distortions: Circumstances (I must get what I want when I want it), Others (other people must treat me fairly or be condemned), and Self (I must do well or I am no good). All sales objections map to one of these three buckets.

name: Six Cs Scaling Framework
definition: A system for duplicating sales skill across a team: Closure sequence (question-based script), Consistent daily training and conviction, Call recordings (game tape review), Communication cycles (daily wrap-up + weekly one-on-ones), Cuts (remove bottom performers fast), Competition and career path (six-week cycles, milestone-based pay increments).

name: Five Objection Buckets
definition: All sales objections resolve to five surface manifestations of three core distortions: Time (busy / no time in day / when-then fallacy), Value/Price (too expensive / can't afford), Fit (not sure it's for me / won't change habits), Authority (must talk to partner/spouse), and Avoidance/Stall (need to think about it). Peeling each layer moves the prospect from external blame toward self-ownership.

name: Unit Economics as North Star for Franchising
definition: Every franchise-demand problem traces back to a single root cause: the unit economics of each individual restaurant. Fix per-location profitability first; franchise interest is a downstream symptom.

name: Five-Element Sales Tone Framework
definition: A model decomposing vocal sales delivery into three fixed constants (volume, speed, articulation) and two variable elements (pauses, pitch direction) that together govern comprehension and call-to-action compliance.

name: Word-Blackout Script Memorization Method
definition: A script-internalization technique where the salesperson reads the full script aloud, then progressively blacks out one word per pass until the entire script is delivered from memory against a blank page.

name: Pulling-Teeth Discovery Loop
definition: A discovery questioning technique that alternates between requests for examples and requests for specifics until the prospect produces a concrete, actionable problem statement that can be chunked up to a solvable category.

name: TEAM Partnership Acronym
definition: A partner is worth adding only if they contribute at least one of four things: Time, Expertise, Assets, or Money that the founder genuinely lacks.

name: C-L-O-S-E-R Sales Framework
definition: A seven-step closing sequence: Clarify why they are here, Label them with a problem, Overview past experience and pain, Sell the vacation (outcome), make the Offer, handle concerns (Explain), Reinforce the decision after buying.

name: Best-Case Worst-Case Close
definition: A risk-reversal closing technique that explicitly names the best outcome (transformation) and worst outcome (work out for free and get refund) to eliminate perceived downside and accelerate commitment.

name: Results Flywheel
definition: A three-step self-reinforcing loop: acquire customers, get them results, use those results (proof) to acquire more customers.

name: Four-Part Profit Optimization Sequence
definition: A sequential four-step plan to triple EBITDA without growing revenue: (1) fix the sales motion, (2) optimize pricing and packaging per service line, (3) generate sufficient cash flow, (4) acquire the talent needed to shore up infrastructure.

name: Cloud-to-Dirt Knowledge Stack
definition: Vertical integration of knowledge from high-level strategy and people management down to granular API-level technical execution; enables a business owner to see cross-functional AI applications that pure technologists cannot.

name: AI as Tool, Not Business
definition: Businesses should use AI as one of many operational tools (analogous to the internet) rather than repositioning themselves as AI companies; the goal is better outcomes, not AI as identity.

name: Inversion Method for Goal Clarity
definition: A two-step process: list every action that would guarantee failure, then flip each item to its opposite to produce the winning action list.

name: Five Stages of Opportunity Hopping
definition: The named arc of any new endeavor: (1) Uninformed Optimism, (2) Informed Pessimism, (3) Valley of Despair, (4) Informed Optimism, (5) Winning; most people exit at stage 3 and restart the cycle in a new domain.

name: Operationalized Trait Decomposition
definition: Breaking a high-level personality trait (e.g., charismatic) into its constituent observable micro-behaviors so any person can practice and be measured on them individually.

name: Barbell AI Strategy
definition: Position on two extremes simultaneously: high-risk AI-first operations on one pole, and bets on timeless human needs (health, food, entertainment) on the other; avoid the unprotected middle.

name: Workflow-First Org Design
definition: Replace role-based org thinking with workflow-based thinking: decompose every role into four to ten granular tasks, then ask which tasks can live inside an automated workflow instead of headcount.

name: BYOS / BYOA Model
definition: Bring Your Own Software or Bring Your Own Agent: employees and contractors who arrive with pre-built AI agents that replace entire department outputs become disproportionately valuable as labor markets shift.

name: Five-Stage Script Rotation
definition: A weekly cycle of daily role-play sessions covering five discrete script stages: intro, discovery, offer, objections/looping, and a rotating hot-topic day based on team need.
concept: Daily Sales Role-Play as Training Cadence

name: Three-Bucket Avatar Segmentation
definition: Segment prospects into three classification buckets before selling: demographics (who they look like), quantifiables (business size, revenue), and behaviors (actions taken by activated vs. churned look-alikes).

name: Elephant and Rider Model
definition: Dual model of the brain in which the conscious mind (rider) sits atop the subconscious mind (elephant); the rider cannot force the elephant to do anything it does not want to do.

name: Rider-Elephant Model
definition: A mental model dividing human decision-making into the rational rider (which generates reasons and justifications) and the emotional elephant (which generates emotions and determines actual behavior through instinctive responses).

name: Post-Rationalization Model
definition: The brain constructs plausible-sounding justifications for decisions already made instinctively; conscious reasoning acts as post-hoc narrative building rather than actual decision mechanism.

name: Uncertainty and Delay as Upside Filter
definition: All the upside worth having in life sits behind exactly two prices people refuse to pay: uncertainty (not knowing the outcome) and delay (not knowing how long to wait). Because most people are unwilling to bear these two costs, they remain the primary arbitrage opportunities.

name: One-One-One Rule
definition: Sell one product to one avatar through one channel until reaching $1M annual revenue; any expansion before that threshold dilutes focus and delays the first scaling milestone.

name: BANT Qualification
definition: Four-axis prospect filter originating at IBM in the 1960s: Budget (can they afford it?), Authority (can they make the decision?), Need (does the problem require solving now?), and Timing (are they willing to act today?).

name: CLOSER Framework
definition: Six-stage sales call structure: Clarify where the prospect is, Label them with their problem, Overview their past experiences, Sell the vacation (outcome), Explain away concerns, Reinforce the decision post-close.

name: Plus-Plus-Minus-Minus Persuasion
definition: Four-angle value articulation used during the sell phase: working with provider gets more good things AND less bad things; not working with provider gets more bad things AND less good things.

name: BANT Qualification
definition: A four-criteria lead qualification filter — Budget, Authority, Need, Timing — used to determine whether a prospect should receive time or a lead magnet before a sales conversation.

name: Lead Magnet Quality Framework
definition: Four attributes that make a lead magnet effective: fast, easy, narrow, solves one complete problem — the solution reveals the next problem that the paid offer solves.

name: Three Ps of Acquisition Process
definition: Product, Prospect, Process — the three variables that determine VSL length and sales approach design before building any conversion asset.

name: More, Better, New Scaling Sequence
definition: Before opening a new acquisition channel, do more of what already works, then make it better; only pursue new channels after existing ones are maximized.

name: Client-Financed Acquisition
definition: A growth model where the revenue from each sale covers both the fulfillment cost of that customer AND the acquisition and fulfillment cost of the next customer, eliminating capital as a growth constraint.

name: Trial-to-Activation Rebate Structure
definition: Two-step activation incentive: charge upfront, then rebate or waive the next billing period if the user completes a defined first-value action within the trial window.

name: Scale or Fail Competition Structure
definition: A competitive selection framework where multiple business owners pitch their operations to a mentor, who provides scaled guidance to the winner; outcomes are binary (scale or failure within 90 days).

name: Nine-Tool AI Replacement Framework
definition: A systematic approach to replacing human labor across nine functional areas (sales, content, training, recruiting, operations) using specific AI tools, resulting in measurable productivity gains of 25-40%.

name: Personalization-at-Scale Architecture
definition: Using AI voice cloning and video deepfakes to create personalized outreach (videos, voicemails, emails) that appear hand-made but scale to thousands of prospects.

name: Six Big Mistakes of Small Business Owners
definition: A diagnostic checklist of six recurring errors: selling to too many avatars (over-focus), overexpansion, wrong compensation structure, mispricing, single-product (no front/back end), and disorganized offer architecture.

name: BANT Qualification
definition: A four-variable lead-qualification framework: Budget (can they pay?), Authority (can they decide alone?), Need (how important is this?), Timing (how quickly do they want to act?).

name: Education vs. Traditional Business Comparison
definition: A two-axis decision framework comparing digital education/coaching businesses against traditional service businesses on speed-to-income, exit potential, capital requirements, and key-man risk to guide founders choosing a business model.

name: Three Key Man Risks in Education Businesses
definition: Three simultaneous personal-brand dependencies in education businesses: the founder is (1) the customer-acquisition engine (ads/personal brand), (2) the product creator and updater, and (3) the cultural anchor for the entire team.

name: Five Sales Metrics Dashboard
definition: A five-variable sales diagnostic: show rate, offer rate, close rate, cash collected percentage, and units sold. Multiplying through the chain reveals where the largest leverage opportunities lie.

name: Zombie Objection Handling
definition: Surface and resolve common objections (the zombie) during discovery or before the close, rather than waiting for them to materialize at price presentation; named as killing zombies while they are far away rather than on top of you.

name: Looping Close Method
definition: When a prospect raises an objection: resolve the specific concern, then re-ask for the sale. Repeat until either a genuine blocking issue is uncovered or the prospect commits. The number of sales made is directly proportional to the number of times you ask.

name: 85-Year-Old Decision Framework
definition: Simulate advice from your 85-year-old self to cut through fear and short-term noise; the older self consistently counsels enjoyment over sacrifice and reveals how few decisions truly matter.

name: Four Cs of Leverage
definition: Naval Ravikant's four leverage types renamed by Hormozi as Collaboration (people), Capital (money), Code (software), and Content (media); each multiplies output per unit of effort at near-zero marginal cost.

name: Inverted Problem Solving
definition: Charlie Munger's inversion method: instead of asking how to achieve a goal, list everything that would destroy it, then reverse those items to derive strategic anchors.

name: 40-for-2 Management Trade
definition: A founder trades 40 hours of direct selling for 2 hours of managing a salesperson; repeating this trade accumulates until the founder does 40 hours of management and zero selling, then can trade management hours to a manager in turn.

name: Agency Learning and Internalization Playbook
definition: A three-phase framework for using external agencies to acquire skills and then internalizing them: Phase 1 (Basic Agency) forces execution cadence on fundamentals; Phase 2 (Advanced Agency) teaches nuanced platform expertise through documented decision-making; Phase 3 (Internal Team + Consulting) builds in-house capability while maintaining support relationship.

name: The Agency Trap Cycle
definition: A predictable 11-step degradation pattern where agencies assign senior talent initially, move that talent to newer customers, replace with junior reps, and create a churn loop that ends in account cancellation.

name: Skill Stacking Order: Have It, Promote It, Convert It, Lead It
definition: Alex Hormozi's four-phase sequence for building a business skill portfolio: (1) acquire a base skill to sell, (2) learn advertising/promotion, (3) learn conversion/persuasion, (4) learn leadership and operations.

name: Lead Source Testing Protocol
definition: For cold outreach, run samples of 100-500 leads from each of multiple lead sources simultaneously, measure response rate per source, then double down on the highest-throughput source.

name: Give Until They Ask Conversion Sequence
definition: Provide free value without asking for money until prospects spontaneously request more or ask how to buy; then make the offer. The sequence: give value -> build trust -> prospect signals demand -> offer paid product.

name: Process-Goal Reframe
definition: Replace outcome goals (sell X copies) with process goals (four hours of promotion per day); judge success by adherence to committed actions, not external results.

name: Give in Public, Sell in Private
definition: Maintain high-value public content to build goodwill and audience growth; reserve direct commercial asks for private DM conversations when a prospect has already signaled interest.

name: ICE Framework
definition: A prioritization method borrowed from the investing world with three axes: Impact (magnitude of expected business improvement), Confidence (probability the change works), and Ease (resource and timeline cost). The composite score determines which changes are worth the guaranteed cost of change.

name: Cost of Change Principle
definition: Any modification to a people-dependent business process incurs an approximately 20% guaranteed short-term performance decrement; changes are only worth making when the expected upside exceeds that decrement, and doing nothing typically yields a free ~5% annual improvement from natural learning.

name: LTV:CAC Leverage Ladder
definition: A tiered target for the lifetime gross profit-to-customer acquisition cost ratio, calibrated to the automation level of acquisition, conversion, and delivery: fully automated businesses can sustain 3:1; fully manual service businesses require 20:1 or higher to absorb lumpiness during scaling.

name: Income-to-Expense Ratio as Wealth Accumulation Engine
definition: Wealth accumulates at the rate of the gap between income and expenses; peace of mind scales with the multiple of income over expenses, not absolute income level.

name: Season Model of Founder Spending
definition: Alex Hormozi frames his financial history as distinct seasons, each defined by an income level, an expense profile, and a reinvestment decision; each season's constraints shaped the next season's capacity.

name: Sphere of Competence Investing Filter
definition: A decision rule (attributed by Hormozi to Warren Buffett and Charlie Munger) that restricts investment activity to domains where the investor has deep, practiced expertise; outside those domains, capital losses are predictable.

name: Push vs. Pivot Dichotomy
definition: A two-branch decision framework for hard entrepreneurial moments: push means intensify effort on the current path because the fundamentals are sound; pivot means change direction because the original assumption was wrong. The critical failure mode is doing neither.

name: Partner Contribution Screen
definition: A three-criterion test for evaluating potential business partners: the partner must bring time, money, or skills that the founder genuinely lacks. If none of the three is present, the partner is not needed and should not receive equity.

name: Backyard Football Fundamentals
definition: A strategic heuristic (shared with Hormozi by a private-equity CEO) that warns against complex, clever strategies in favor of relentless execution of a few core basics: acquire customers, deliver excellently, repeat.

name: Free Trial Plus Penalty Model
definition: A client-acquisition model where prospects receive service at no charge in exchange for behaving as required; failure to complete specified behaviors triggers a billing event. Designed to fill a proof pipeline when testimonials are absent.

name: Two End-States Framework for Client-Acquisition Agencies
definition: Client-acquisition agencies for small businesses inevitably converge on one of two viable long-run business models: ultra-low-cost high-volume automation or high-ticket whale/upmarket positioning. The mid-market is structurally unviable.

name: Click-to-Close Vertical Integration
definition: The strategic goal of owning every stage of the deal pipeline from lead sourcing through close, eliminating external gatekeepers and capturing full margin at each stage.
concept: Vertical Integration to Capture Full Margin

name: Defend the Perimeter Metaphor
definition: A spatial analogy comparing business focus to a single soldier guarding progressively larger areas: one room (easy), one building (hard), one block (nearly impossible) — illustrating that spreading attention across multiple business lines is like a single defender guarding an entire city block alone.

name: Moral High Ground Delivery Change Pitch
definition: A reframing technique for announcing service delivery reductions: position the change as fulfilling a prior promise (integrity), enumerate reasons it benefits clients, and make any objection equivalent to attacking your integrity.

name: Six Content Shifts Framework
definition: A six-part content strategy overhaul Alex Hormozi executed: (1) edutainment to education, (2) for-us to for-you, (3) wide to narrow topics, (4) views to ad revenue as primary metric, (5) shorts to long-form emphasis, (6) assuming familiarity to assuming nothing about viewer identity.

name: Paired KPIs Method
definition: A management heuristic pairing a volume metric with a quality metric for any business function so that neither metric can be gamed independently; e.g. views paired with RPM, speed of resolution paired with quality score.

name: Ad Effectiveness Six-Factor Scorecard
definition: Alex Hormozi's framework for evaluating ads across six dimensions: (1) did it grab attention, (2) did it make you care, (3) did it sell the dream, (4) did it create urgency, (5) did it show social proof, and (6) did it tell you what to do next.

name: Brand Equation Formula
definition: A branding structure where the brand is explicitly equated to a value (e.g., Jeep = Freedom), that value is then equated to things the target demo already likes, creating a chain of association that transfers sentiment to the brand.

name: Value Acceleration Method
definition: A ten-part framework developed at Acquisition.com for transforming a cash-generating business into a high-value institutional-grade asset by optimizing three enterprise-value variables: number of customers, lifetime gross profit per customer, and risk (continuity likelihood).

name: Nine C's of Recurring Revenue
definition: Nine levers that increase subscription stickiness: Consumption, Collateral, Cost of Switching, Choice, Control (money flow), Cause, Community, Contracts, and Communication.

name: One-One-One Rule
definition: Until a business reaches $1M/year in revenue, focus on one offer, one avatar, and one acquisition channel before adding complexity.

name: Theory of Constraints Applied to Sales Metrics
definition: Identify the single lowest-performing metric in the sales funnel (show rate, close rate, offer percentage, cash collected) and attack it first, because a 5% improvement in the binding constraint yields the highest throughput increase.

name: Business Sale Phase Framework
definition: A four-phase sequence for selling a business at institutional scale: Phase 0 prerequisites (deal-killer checklist), Phase 1 prep (banker selection and materials), Phase 2 marketing (teaser, NDA, data room, IOIs), Phase 3 close (LOIs, diligence, purchase agreement, escrow).

name: Enterprise Value Equation
definition: Enterprise value equals a discount applied to all future sales; the discount rate reflects the probability those sales will actually occur, meaning high enterprise value requires both large projected sales and high certainty of execution.

name: Problem-Solution Cycle
definition: Solving any business problem creates a new adjacent problem; the cycle repeats indefinitely, and sophisticated operators use this to intentionally introduce and sell the next problem.

name: Three Backend Metrics Framework
definition: The three metrics that determine backend health for a recurring-revenue service business: time to first value, customer satisfaction score, and ascension rate (upsell conversion).

name: Leading vs. Lagging Indicator Distinction
definition: Churn is a lagging indicator (a result you cannot directly fix); the behavioral signals that predict churn (e.g., login frequency, missed sessions) are leading indicators that can be driven before churn occurs.

name: Want Less or Trade More
definition: A two-option resolution to the dissatisfaction of wanting two incompatible things: either reduce your desire for the thing you say you want, or pay the cost required to get it. There is no third path.

name: Active Active, Passive Passive
definition: A capital management rule: keep passive investments managed by partners so they consume no founder attention, and deploy active effort only in the core business where ROI on time is highest.

name: Generational Teaching Framework
definition: A multi-generational model where each generation forges further than the last by standing on the shoulders of predecessors, each mentor helping the next generation clear obstacles faster.

name: Mentor-Student Progression Hierarchy
definition: A structured view of learning where students move through sequential stages (basics, intermediate, advanced) without needing to deprecate earlier teachers when surpassing them.

name: Copy-Test-Repeat Loop
definition: A three-step content and business growth loop: (1) find a proven operator doing well, (2) copy their strategy or content format exactly, (3) repeat whatever works while running small experiments on new formats in parallel.

name: Remote Service Lead-Arbitrage Model
definition: A business model where the operator captures inbound service leads (via Google Maps listings and reviews), presents as a company, dispatches a subcontractor to do the work, and retains a margin percentage (e.g., 40%) without possessing the underlying trade skill.

name: Rule of 300 (Warm Outreach Breakdown)
definition: A three-step decomposition of the Rule of 100 for warm outreach: (1) post one piece of content on one platform, (2) leave 100 high-quality comments inside a community of your target audience, (3) do one-on-one outreach to the warm list generated by step 2 (post likers, post commenters, comment likers, comment repliers).

name: Four-Stage Customer Acquisition Sequence (Homies to Paid)
definition: Alex Hormozi's personal framework for getting first customers: Stage 1 (Homies) - train friends for free to collect before/afters; Stage 2 (Referrals) - ask those friends to refer others; Stage 3 (Charitable Bridge) - accept donations-to-charity in lieu of cash to overcome pricing fear; Stage 4 (Paid Launch) - convert existing network to paid using accumulated proof.

name: 13 Instructions for Starting Entrepreneurs
definition: Alex Hormozi's Slack message (seen by ~4 million people) listing 13 operating rules for new entrepreneurs: follow instructions, Google before asking, share what you learn, do the Rule of 100 daily, expect excitement to fade before real work starts, recognize you are the product being built, accept that everything is unscalable at first, understand pain forces improvement, eliminate complaining, repeat proven actions, write down your reasons, accept that hard = consistency not complexity, and just win once to get addicted.
concept: The Execution Gap: Knowledge Without Action

name: Three Value-Creation Frames for Premium Offers
definition: Three intellectual attack vectors for designing a premium one-on-one offer: (1) 10x/100x price thought-experiment to identify low-cost high-value inclusions; (2) word-of-mouth-only constraint to identify what a perfect customer experience requires; (3) remove-unscalable-but-keep-10x-value to engineer a scalable high-value tier.

name: Premium Tier Anchor Model
definition: A two-tier offer structure where an expensive unscalable one-on-one tier is listed alongside a scalable lower-priced tier; the premium tier anchors perceived value for the scalable tier via price contrast and brand narrative even if few or no premium buyers convert.

name: Value Equation
definition: A four-variable model for offer value: (Dream Outcome x Perceived Likelihood of Achievement) / (Time Delay + Effort and Sacrifice). Increasing numerator variables and decreasing denominator variables produces a more valuable offer.

name: One Avatar One Product One Channel
definition: The minimum viable growth formula for reaching $1M: choose one specific customer type, one product, and one advertising channel — maximize each before adding complexity.

name: Core Four Advertising Methods
definition: Four foundational advertising actions a founder can execute personally: warm outreach (1-to-1 to known contacts), content posting (1-to-many to known audience), paid ads (1-to-many to strangers), cold outreach (1-to-1 to strangers). All advertising ultimately reduces to combinations of these four.

name: Quad Marketing Calendar
definition: A four-direction marketing model requiring simultaneous advertising to: prospects (convert to customers), customers (convert to repeat buyers), candidates (convert to employees), and employees (keep engaged and ascending). Neglecting any quadrant creates a growth ceiling.

name: Five-Phase Entrepreneur Cycle
definition: Sequential phases when pursuing any new opportunity: (1) Uninformed Optimism, (2) Informed Pessimism, (3) Valley of Despair, (4) Informed Optimism, (5) Achievement. Most newcomers quit during phase 3 and cycle back to phase 1 on a new opportunity, never reaching phase 5.

name: Rule of 100
definition: Doing 100 primary actions over 100 days reliably produces the first meaningful result; the 100-unit count is the atomic activity goal rather than any outcome metric.

name: CLOSER Framework
definition: A six-stage sales close acronym: Clarify why the prospect is there, Label them with the problem, Overview past pain, Sell the vacation (three-pillar pitch), Explain away concerns, Reinforce the decision.

name: Management Diamond
definition: A five-factor diagnostic for employee non-performance: did they not know what, how, when, why, or are they blocked? Each factor has a specific remediation path.

name: Three Business Pillars (Acquisition, Delivery, Operations)
definition: Every business rests on three functions: acquisition (marketing + sales), delivery (product + fulfillment + customer success), and operations (IT, legal, finance, HR) which supports the first two.

name: Document-Demonstrate-Duplicate (3D Training)
definition: Three-step skill transfer method: document the process as a checklist, demonstrate it in front of the trainee following the checklist, then have the trainee duplicate it using the same checklist to verify they achieve the same outcome.

name: Three Ps (Pain, Passion, Profession)
definition: Three origin categories for choosing who to serve: a pain you overcame, something you are passionate about, or a professional skill you developed in the marketplace.

name: Eight LTV Levers
definition: Eight ways to increase customer lifetime value: raise price, decrease cost, increase purchase frequency, add complementary products, increase quantity per purchase, upgrade quality, decrease quantity (downsell), or decrease quality (economy tier).

name: Red-Yellow-Green Delegation Inventory
definition: A color-coded categorization system applied to every founder task: green = delegate immediately to existing team; yellow = install a process or one-time project first, then delegate; red = requires a hire or new capability not yet present in the organization.

name: Shadow-Supervise-Support Training Sequence
definition: A three-stage employee handoff protocol: (1) Shadow — employee watches founder execute; (2) Supervise — founder watches employee execute and provides corrections; (3) Support — founder is available but not involved, and the employee owns the work independently.

name: Frustrated Fred vs. Wealthy William Wealth Model
definition: A comparative financial model contrasting two $10M-revenue/$2M-profit businesses: one requiring 80 hours/week of founder time (valued at personal income only) versus one fully founder-independent (valued at 6x profit multiple), demonstrating that business independence multiplies net worth non-linearly.

name: SPCL Influence Framework
definition: Four stacked components that determine a creator's influence over an audience: Status (controls scarce resources), Power (say-do correspondence reinforcement history), Credibility (third-party verifiable proof), Likeness (demographic or values similarity).

name: Proof-Promise-Plan Introduction Structure
definition: A three-part educational video introduction: Proof (demonstrate you can do what you claim), Promise (state what the viewer will get or learn), Plan (set expectations for what happens next). Order is flexible; lead with whichever element matters most for the specific content.

name: Four Audience Monetization Paths
definition: Four ways to monetize an existing audience arranged on a continuum from low-risk/low-value to high-risk/high-value: (1) Affiliates — paid after sales on standard terms; (2) Sponsorships — paid upfront as a traffic source via CPM or whitelisting; (3) Partnerships — equity deals ranging from minority to majority; (4) Own brand — start your own product from scratch.

name: Bouquet Brand Assembly Model
definition: A brand is built by deliberately pairing your product or name with people, experiences, and values your ideal customer already likes. Each pairing is a flower; repeated positive pairings form a bouquet (the brand). Narrowing means clustering similar flowers; expanding means adding adjacent ones. A single bad pairing is one rotten flower that mars the whole bouquet.

name: Six-Step First $100K Roadmap
definition: A sequential six-step plan to earn and bank $100K: (1) cut all costs, (2) save time, (3) research skills people already pay for, (4) spend time learning through iteration, (5) spend money on tools/implementation/attempts, (6) do not increase lifestyle.

name: 4-4-4 Time Split
definition: For people without a 9-to-5 job, divide 12 active hours into three four-hour blocks: promotion (letting people know about your offer), delivery (fulfilling what you promised), and building (researching opportunities and prioritizing next actions).

name: First-Party Data Learning Loop
definition: A five-step skill-acquisition cycle: (1) do high volume, (2) analyze the top 10% of outputs, (3) identify what differentiates the top 10% from the bottom 90%, (4) isolate the most important variable, (5) avoid the mistakes the bottom 90% keeps making, then repeat 100 more times.

name: 1-1-1 Rule
definition: Sell one product or service to one avatar on one channel until you reach $1 million in revenue; do not diversify until that milestone is hit.

name: Four Audience Monetization Pathways
definition: A continuum of four methods for monetizing an audience — affiliates, sponsorships, partnerships (equity), and own brand — ordered from lowest risk/value to highest risk/value, with distinct compensation structures and exit value implications.

name: Exit Value–Risk–Work–Cash Framework
definition: A four-variable deal evaluation framework: assess exit value, cash in/out, amount of work required, and risk exposure; balance these four variables to find the right deal position on the affiliate-to-own-brand continuum.

name: Equity Vesting Split for Partnership Deals
definition: A three-bucket equity structure for influencer partnerships: a fixed upfront grant (for association transfer), a performance tranche (for results delivered), and a time-vested tranche (for sustained promotion); example split is 25% upfront, 25% performance, 50% over time.

name: Trim and Stack Offer Design
definition: A two-phase offer redesign process: first list all current deliverables, then cut and recombine them to retain only what clients most value, eliminating everything else to reduce delivery load while maintaining perceived value.

name: Supply Constraint Resolution Matrix
definition: Four-lever framework for resolving capacity bottlenecks in service businesses: (1) raise price so fewer people buy, (2) change delivery ratio from 1:1 to 1:N, (3) productize the delivery, or (4) hire additional staff to absorb load.

name: Novelty-Loyalty-Exploration-Trust-Chase-Journey Trade
definition: A three-part framework for understanding monogamy: committing to one partner means trading novelty for loyalty, exploration for trust, and the chase for a shared journey toward a common goal.

name: Downside-First Matching (Realtor Analogy)
definition: A mate-selection approach in which candidates lead with their genuine negatives rather than positives, enabling prospective partners to self-select based on compatibility with those downsides, producing stronger matches where a partner's objections become the other's indifferences.

name: Four-Component Mental Toughness Model
definition: Mental toughness is a four-part measurable skill (tolerance, fortitude, resilience, adaptability) that determines how much a bad event changes goal-aligned behavior, how severely, how long, and to what new baseline.

name: Six-Step Wealth-Building Sequence
definition: A staged personal finance process: (1) emergency seed fund $1k-$5k, (2) pay off consumer debt smallest-balance-first, (3) expand emergency fund to 3-6 months expenses, (4) eliminate risky/discretionary spending and downgrade depreciating assets, (5) invest 15% pre-tax income automatically, (6) pay off mortgage to achieve zero fixed costs.

name: 30 by 12 Working Challenge
definition: Work 30 consecutive days, 12 hours per day with no weekends off, to simultaneously eliminate spending and maximize income, compressing the savings curve and recalibrating perception of sustainable work capacity.

name: Interests-Proficiency-Tolerance Arc
definition: Three sequential drivers of entrepreneurial endurance: interests get you started, proficiency keeps you going, and pain tolerance helps you finish.

name: Reinforcing Event Reframe
definition: A framework for sustaining difficult behaviors by identifying the reinforcing event (the why that makes the pain worth taking), distinguishing reinforcement from reward.

name: Four Steps to Your Best Year
definition: A sequential framework for achieving major life and business goals: (1) Eliminate distractions, (2) Get started, (3) Get better, (4) Never stop.

name: Difficulty Curve
definition: The four-phase emotional arc of any hard endeavor: uninformed optimism -> informed pessimism -> valley of despair -> breakthrough; most people quit at despair and restart a new uninformed optimism cycle, never reaching the upside.

name: Rule of 100
definition: A daily output standard for early-stage entrepreneurs: reach out to 100 people, make one post that took at least 100 minutes, spend $100+ on ads, and spend at least 100 minutes improving ads and researching — sustained daily until results appear.

name: Declarative vs Procedural Knowledge
definition: Two distinct types of learning: declarative knowledge is knowing about something (e.g., reading about cold outbound), while procedural knowledge is knowing how to do it (gained only through repetition). Mistaking declarative for procedural is the primary reason people stall after consuming information.

name: Logic-Evidence-Utility Framework
definition: A three-step framework for dismantling limiting self-narratives: (1) Logic - define the claim in observable behavior terms, (2) Evidence - examine how many data points actually support it, (3) Utility - ask whether maintaining the belief serves your goals.

name: Short-Pain Long-Gain Trade Matrix
definition: A two-axis matrix mapping short/long pain and short/long gain: the optimal trade is short pain for long gain (courage, hard conversations); the worst trade is short gain for long pain (comfort, avoidance). Comfort is short gain + long pain; fulfillment is short pain + long gain.

name: Document-Demonstrate-Duplicate Skill Acquisition
definition: A three-stage method for acquiring any skill from an expert: (1) have the expert document each step as a checklist while performing it, (2) watch them demonstrate while explaining each step, (3) replicate in front of them until you can do it without correction across multiple attempts.

name: Three Growth Vectors (Shopify)
definition: Shopify's three primary growth levers: (1) referral ecosystem with generous rev-share, (2) a competitive event to cross the chasm from early adopters to mainstream, (3) economies-of-scale aggregation passed back to merchants.

name: Crafter Track vs. Manager Track
definition: A dual career-ladder system where employees choose either an individual-contributor (crafter) path or a management path, preventing forced promotion-to-management for high performers.

name: Merchant Obsession Heuristic
definition: A single-question decision filter used at Shopify: when facing two options, always choose the one that is better for the merchant; replaces ad-hoc judgment with a centralized mission-aligned litmus test.

name: What Does This Change Framework
definition: When a bad event occurs, ask: does this change my job, my food, my housing, my relationships? If the answer is no, the suffering is voluntary and can be opted out of.

name: Sword of Gryffindor Filter
definition: A mental frame in which every adversity is evaluated only for what it adds — mirroring the goblin-made sword that absorbs only that which strengthens it — and the rest is discarded.

name: Exploration-to-Exploitation Lifecycle
definition: A two-phase career structure where early years are spent broad exploration (trying many things) before locking into deep exploitation (one skill, all-in); Naval Ravikant's framing applied to ambition in your 20s and 30s.

name: Infinite Game Frame
definition: Business (and health, marriage) are infinite games where the only objective is to stay in the game; therefore success is defined by choosing to continue, not by any single outcome.

name: Bridge-Building Success Model
definition: Success is not a single leap across a chasm but incremental brick-laying: each failure installs a brick, and the accumulated path eventually spans the gap; the outcome appears binary but the construction is linear.

name: Interests-Proficiency-Pain Tolerance Arc
definition: A three-stage model of what sustains a long-horizon pursuit: interests get you started, proficiency keeps you going, and pain tolerance is what determines whether you finish.

name: Reinforcing vs. Rewarding Event Distinction
definition: Behavior is sustained by reinforcing events (outcomes that make the actor more likely to repeat the action) not rewarding ones; a painful shock can be reinforcing if it protects something valued, while a monetary reward can lose reinforcing power through variety-saturation.

name: Maximizer vs. Optimizer Frame
definition: Maximizers ask how to get as much as possible (absolute returns); optimizers ask how to get as much as possible from as little as possible (relative returns). Maximizers win at the top of competitive distributions because diminishing returns still produce positive returns.

name: ICE Prioritization for Change Bets
definition: Evaluate any proposed change using three axes: Impact (how large is the upside?), Confidence (how likely is success?), and Ease (what resources are required?). Only pursue changes that score high on all three, given the guaranteed 20% output decrement from switching costs.

name: Core Four Scaling Sequence
definition: The four customer acquisition channels (warm outreach, cold outreach, content, paid ads) should each be scaled via a sequenced more-first approach: first increase creative volume, then increase spend, then expand to new platforms. Risk increases at each stage.

name: Four Business Growth Levers
definition: A business grows by exactly two paths (more customers or higher customer value), each decomposable into two sub-levers: more traffic + better conversion, and higher price + lower churn.

name: Three Brand-Building Inputs
definition: Brand is built exclusively through three channels: what you say, what others say, and what customers experience directly; the third channel (product experience) is the only non-advertising input.

name: Double-Time Job Framework
definition: Spend half the day working tomorrow's job (building what comes next) and half on today's job; this allows a business owner to move at twice the speed and compound over time.

name: Preparation Scaled by Audience Size
definition: The principle that preparation effort should scale proportionally (or as an order of magnitude) with audience size relative to a known baseline; 100x audience implies 100x preparation.

name: Moseyverse Book Series Architecture
definition: A multi-book business-content series where each successive book builds on the prior audience and deepens brand equity, analogous to Harry Potter's compounding first-day sales across sequels.

name: Three P's Framework
definition: Three origin buckets for business ideas: Pain (personal problem overcome), Profession (day-job skill), and Passion (deep personal interest).

name: Mosey Money Mad Lib
definition: A sentence-completion template for articulating a business offer: 'I help [who] get [good stuff] without [bad stuff] through [unique mechanism].'

name: Unique Mechanism
definition: A proprietary named process or system (checklist or sequential steps) that differentiates a solution from competitors and anchors a prospect's hope of success.

name: Warm Outreach First-Five-Customers System
definition: A structured cold-to-warm contact script: greet, give specific compliment, state one-sentence offer, ask if they know anyone who needs it; repeat for four hours per day or 100 contacts per day.

name: Seven Sellable Categories
definition: A taxonomy of value types that can be monetized: products (physical/digital), services (physical/digital), access (physical/digital), attention (physical/digital), risk (physical/digital), money (physical/digital), and endorsement/brand (physical/digital).

name: Delivery Cube
definition: A six-dimensional framework for scaling delivery: audience scale (one-to-one, small group, one-to-many), delivery model (DIY, DWI, done-for-you), support medium (chat, email, phone, Zoom), consumption format (visual, audio, live, recorded, text), speed and convenience (24/7 vs. scheduled, response time), and price-value testing (10x and 1/10th scenarios).

name: 10x Litmus Test for Opportunity Attention
definition: A heuristic for filtering which opportunities deserve a founder's dedicated time: the projected outcome must be at least 10x the current business size; below that threshold, the opportunity cost of attention is not justified.

name: No Half Measures Commitment Framework
definition: A decision doctrine stating that partial commitment is functionally equivalent to no commitment; when pursuing any meaningful goal, all alternatives must be eliminated to guarantee full effort.

name: Irreversibility Filter
definition: A pre-decision screening step that identifies which categories of action are irreversible (reputation damage, capital loss above a threshold, time lost) and excludes them from risk-taking, reserving bets only for domains with recoverable downside.

name: SCARF Model (Status, Certainty, Autonomy, Relatedness, Fairness)
definition: Five psychological dimensions (Status, Certainty, Autonomy, Relatedness, Fairness) that humans care about deeply and that economists systematically ignore; boosting any one of these drives adoption, satisfaction, or behavior change independent of the product's functional attributes.

name: Messaging vs. Signaling Distinction
definition: Two fundamentally different communication modes: Messaging (efficient information transfer when sender is trusted) and Signaling (costly, broadcast communication that functions as proof of sincerity and quality when trust is absent). Optimizing for messaging efficiency in a signaling context destroys trust.

name: Psycho-logic / Alchemy of Second-Order Sense
definition: A design philosophy that looks for solutions in non-obvious psychological dimensions rather than logical-functional ones; the best innovations make second-order sense (they work through perception, status, context-framing) rather than first-order logical sense, because first-order solutions are already competed away.

name: Systemic vs. Segment Market Diagnosis
definition: Before committing to a business model pivot, determine whether the revenue decline is systemic (affecting all carriers/markets nationwide) or segment-specific (one state or carrier class); only a systemic verdict justifies model-level change.

name: Back-End Continuity Test
definition: Before replacing a transactional model with a subscription model, first test whether existing emergency/transactional customers can be converted to a recurring offer at point of service completion; inability to close that upsell is decisive evidence against switching the entire model.

name: Reframing as Value Creation
definition: A two-move innovation model: (1) find what people want and devise a way to provide it, or (2) find what you can provide and devise a way to make people want it — both require reframing, not just delivery.

name: Sat-Nav Thinking Critique
definition: A decision-making failure mode where an optimizer maximizes one metric (e.g., speed) while ignoring others the person actually values (e.g., variance reduction, scenic quality), leading to systematically suboptimal outcomes.

name: Choice Architecture Analysis
definition: The discipline of examining how the ordering, framing, and availability of options drives behavior independently of stated preferences — and redesigning those structures to unlock better outcomes.

name: Missing First Diamond
definition: A mandatory period of open, exploratory messiness at the start of every brief — asking 'what is really going on?' before any assumption about tools or solutions is made — that precedes both divergent and convergent thinking phases.

name: Backward Reasoning (Thinking Backwards)
definition: Inverting the standard forward-reasoning mode (data leads to conclusion) to ask instead: 'What would have to be true if we want more people to do X?' — sacrificing clarity for vastly greater surface area of creative opportunity.

name: Top-Down vs. Bottom-Up Thinking
definition: Top-down thinking imposes legibility from above using available aggregate data and pre-rationalised arguments; bottom-up thinking starts from ground-level observation and asks what data is actually needed, revealing problems invisible to top-down analysis.

name: Passion Etymology Reframe
definition: Reframes passion from doing what you love to finding something meaningful enough to suffer for, rooted in the Latin root passio (suffering) and its first usage in the Passion of Christ.

name: Fixed-Cost Suffering Model
definition: All life paths (employment, entrepreneurship, wealth, poverty, marriage, singlehood) carry equivalent suffering; the variable is what you receive in return, not whether you suffer.
concept: All Life Paths Have Equal Suffering; Outcome Differs by Choice

name: Prioritize-Urgency-Eliminate Loop
definition: A three-step repeating cycle for business focus: (1) Prioritize the single highest-leverage constraint, (2) Create urgency via shortened meeting cadence and explicit deadlines, (3) Eliminate all competing work from the team's plate until the constraint is solved, then reassess and repeat.

name: Tree-Pruning Business Model
definition: Metaphor equating business resources to tree sap: side projects and B-plus problems draw resources from the trunk (primary growth path), slowing revenue growth; pruning these offshoots channels all resources into the main trunk and accelerates growth.

name: Theory of Constraints Applied to Business
definition: Every business has exactly one binding constraint limiting growth at any moment; removing it causes natural growth until the next constraint surfaces; strategy is the discipline of identifying and attacking only that single constraint.

name: Profile Volume as Revenue Engine
definition: In drop-servicing (remote service arbitrage via Google LSA profiles), total revenue is a direct function of number of active, optimized business profiles; revenue scales roughly linearly with verified profile count until automation becomes the binding constraint.

name: Verify-First, Scale-Second Sequence
definition: In Google LSA drop-servicing, the critical bottleneck before revenue is verification of the business profile; until at least one profile is verified, no leads arrive regardless of niche selection or area quality — verification unlocks the entire revenue loop.
concept: Execution and Rapid Adjustment Over Planning

name: Client-Financed Acquisition (CFA)
definition: A model where 30-day gross profit from one new customer exceeds the cost of acquiring and fulfilling two customers, enabling unlimited growth with no external capital.

name: Never Go Hungry Framework (Six Traffic Sources)
definition: Six always-available pools for new customers: paid media, earned media, owned media, outbound, affiliates/partners, and referrals; each individually capable of generating $20M+ in revenue.

name: Grand Slam Offer (Seven Components)
definition: A seven-element offer construction system: promotion type (free/discount/premium), core offer, bonuses, scarcity, urgency, guarantees, and magic naming formula; designed to make offers so compelling prospects feel foolish declining.

name: Six Levers of Lifetime Gross Profit
definition: Six levers to maximize revenue per customer: (1) increase price, (2) reduce cost of fulfillment, (3) increase purchase frequency, (4) upsell (more or better), (5) downsell, (6) cross-sell adjacent needs.

name: Value Equation (Four Drivers)
definition: A four-variable formula for perceived value: (dream outcome x perceived likelihood of achievement) / (time delay x effort and sacrifice). Increasing the numerator or decreasing the denominator increases willingness to pay.

name: Drop-Servicing via Google Business Profile Stack
definition: A zero-capital local service business model where an operator creates multiple Google Business Profile listings across sub-areas of a city, generates inbound calls organically, and outsources fulfillment to licensed contractors at a 40-60% revenue split while keeping the remainder as profit.

name: Three-Phase Contractor Onboarding
definition: A contractor vetting sequence of: (1) brief qualifying call to assess license and fit, (2) first trial job to verify honesty and quality, (3) second trial job to confirm, then (4) a 30-40 minute onboarding meeting to formalize expectations, payment process, and communication norms.

name: Physical Product Brand Launch Framework
definition: A structured approach to launching a physical product brand: (1) identify a high-margin product with sticky recurring usage tied to unavoidable daily behavior, (2) design premium pricing supported by brand narrative (aspirational identity over features), (3) build manufacturing capability for differentiation (customization moat), (4) scale through multi-channel distribution (founder + influencer affiliates), (5) target avatar segments with identity-specific messaging.

name: Nose Strip Business Model
definition: A recurring consumer product with $20/month price point, 80% gross margins, 10% monthly churn reaching 5,000 equilibrium users ($80k/month net), scaled via influencer partnerships (40% commission) to multi-channel distribution.

name: Variables of Validity and Comfort
definition: A launch framework that substitutes a missing influencer following by embedding pre-trusted cultural artifacts (nostalgic flavors, recognizable reference points) directly into the product or offer to provide consumer comfort on first encounter.

name: Media House First Model
definition: A brand-building model in which the company operates primarily as a content production engine, generating audience trust and demand before optimizing distribution or retail placement.

name: Mosey Money Minute Email Structure
definition: A repeatable email format consisting of: (1) brand-consistent subject line, (2) immediate-reward opening quote or tweet, (3) one-concept tactical body under 200 words, (4) contextual CTA, (5) PS statement as a secondary engagement hook.

name: Email Behavioral Reward Loop
definition: Frame every element of an email as a reinforcement step: reward the open (immediate value in first glance), reward the read (actionable tactic), reward the click (high-quality destination), so each action increases the probability of the same action on the next email.

name: 70-20-10 Ad Budget Allocation
definition: Allocate 70% of ad resources to proven winners, 20% to adjacent permutations of those winners, and 10% to wild experimental ideas; mirrors how time is spent daily on creative production.

name: Proof Continuum
definition: A spectrum of proof credibility for ads: anonymous text testimonials at the low end; in-person, live, look-alike, specific-result demonstrations at the high end. Each dimension (in-person vs virtual, live vs recorded, similar avatar vs dissimilar, specific desired result vs generic) increases or decreases believability.

name: Four Group Funnel Conversion Mechanisms
definition: Four ways to convert free-group members into paid clients: (1) free onboarding call for every new member that pivots to a sales conversation; (2) five-video series inside the group acting as a broken-up VSL covering opportunity, core story, three belief-breaking stories, and CTA; (3) weekly webinar with soft CTA where setters pull engaged chatters; (4) DM setters engaging anyone who likes, comments, or posts.
concept: Show-Up Rate and Lead Nurture Optimization

name: Friction Calibration Rule
definition: Adjust funnel friction in response to lead volume and quality: add friction when too many unqualified leads opt in; remove friction when opt-in volume is too low; if nearly no friction exists and leads are still bad, the targeting is wrong.

name: Eastern Subtraction Philosophy
definition: Instead of adding to a blank canvas (Western approach), start with a full slab and remove everything that is not the essential art; applied to business, delete every distraction until only the highest-value core remains.

name: One-Thing Forcing Function
definition: A three-step discipline: identify the single most important business objective whose achievement would make all others irrelevant, align all departments behind it, and let lesser fires burn rather than dilute resources.

name: Return on Capital Optimization
definition: Evaluate every business model variant by return on human capital and financial capital, not by absolute revenue or profit, to identify which format to scale.

name: Engineering vs Psychological Solutions
definition: Two distinct classes of solution to any problem: (1) engineering solutions that improve objective metrics (speed, cost, capacity) and (2) psychological solutions that improve subjective experience — both can solve the same problem, but psychological solutions are systematically ignored because they are harder to defend in a spreadsheet.

name: Ergodicity Distinction (Ensemble vs Time-Series)
definition: A system is ergodic only if the average outcome across many people (ensemble) equals the average outcome for one person over time (time-series); most human-welfare situations are non-ergodic, meaning aggregate GDP gains can mask universal individual loss, and variance reduction is more rational than mean maximization.

name: Chesterton's Fence Rule
definition: Before removing any institution or practice that appears purposeless, first determine why it was built; only after establishing the original purpose is no longer valid should you eliminate it, because systems that look pointless often carry non-obvious evolutionary functions.

name: Adaptive Preference Formation
definition: Once people have chosen or been placed in a state, they construct a narrative explaining why their state is preferable; designing systems with genuine trade-offs (rather than a clear winner/loser) allows people in every outcome to form a satisfying narrative, increasing aggregate happiness without changing objective conditions.

name: High-Ticket Local Service Arbitrage
definition: A three-step model: (1) generate inbound leads for high-ticket local service businesses using organic Google My Business ranking, (2) dispatch a third-party contractor to fulfill the job, (3) collect a 40-60% commission on revenue with zero ad spend and no physical presence required.

name: Split-the-Difference Roll-Up Offer
definition: A two-stage multiple structure for DSO consolidation: offer practice owners their solo-sale multiple (4x) plus a share of the uplift to the consolidated multiple (7x), keeping everything above 7x as the consolidator's profit.

name: Coaching Business as the Goose
definition: Retain the educational/coaching business as the permanent demand-generation asset (the goose) while selling the consolidated practice group (the eggs); the coaching book supplies a continual pipeline of willing consolidation targets.

name: Give-to-Ask Ratio
definition: A governance rule for content-based businesses specifying that public content (giving) must outweigh commercial asks (asking) by at least 3:1 to preserve audience goodwill; the optimal target for compounding growth is 30:1.

name: Give Until They Ask Framework
definition: A modified give-ask model where the creator withholds all asks until the audience proactively requests the offer, replacing scheduled asks with audience-initiated demand as the conversion trigger.

name: Integrated vs Intermittent Ask Format
definition: Two distinct commercial placement strategies: integrated asks are embedded naturally within long-form content (books, videos, podcasts); intermittent asks appear between discrete short-form posts (Instagram, TikTok) at a frequency of roughly 1-in-10 posts.

name: Money Model
definition: A deliberately structured sequence of four offer types (attraction, upsell, downsell, continuity) designed to maximize upfront cash collected, total leads converted, and lifetime value per customer, pulling cash forward so the business can outspend competitors on customer acquisition.

name: Four-Bucket Offer Sequence
definition: The four-part offer architecture inside a money model: (1) attraction offers maximize lead-to-customer conversion, (2) upsells maximize gross profit per customer, (3) downsells capture customers who would have said no to the primary offer, and (4) continuity offers generate repeat purchase relationships.

name: First Impression Anchoring Framework
definition: Initial decisions and impressions on a stimulus (like checking into a hotel) anchor all subsequent perceptions of that same stimulus, with evidence-seeking behavior reinforcing the initial judgment.

name: Evolutionary Heuristics vs. Economic Rationality
