definition: Human behavioral heuristics evolved as near-optimal solutions under imperfect information and imperfect trust; labeling them biases misunderstands their adaptive purpose.

name: Satisficing Framework (Herbert Simon)
definition: In real-world decisions with no mathematical optimum, the best attainable outcome is one that is good enough (satisficing), not theoretically perfect (optimizing).

name: Doorman Fallacy
definition: Consultants define a role by its most visible function (opening a door), ignore tacit functions (security, status-signaling, recognition), recommend tech replacement, and destroy value that was never in the model.

name: Explore-Exploit Trade-off
definition: Any decision-making system faces a trade-off between exploiting known-good options and exploring unknown alternatives; ignoring exploration leads to catastrophic failure when conditions change.

name: Fractal Pattern Recognition
definition: Insights from small-scale, low-status domains (chocolate bar promotions, loyalty cards) reveal the same structural patterns as high-status domains (macroeconomics, tax policy) because complex systems are self-similar across scales.

name: Bootstrap-First Retail Entry Sequencing
definition: Sell only through fast-pay channels until sufficient capital cushion is built; only then enter slow-pay retailers (30-90 day terms) to avoid cash-flow insolvency despite profitability.

name: Event-as-Content Frame
definition: Design every in-person event primarily for digital content output rather than live attendance experience; the content artifact outlasts the event and multiplies reach.

name: Eight Business Analysis Equations
definition: A seven-plus-one framework of arithmetic ratios (LTGP:CAC, gross margin, CAC, ROIC, payback period, sales velocity x LTGP, sales velocity / churn, TAM x LTGP / risk) that together determine a business's current health, scalability ceiling, and opportunity size.

name: High-Ticket Local Service Arbitrage
definition: A five-step model: (1) identify a high-ticket local service niche with >400 monthly searches and low Google Maps competition, (2) create and verify a Google Business Profile, (3) optimize the profile for organic ranking, (4) partner with an unmarketed local contractor on a 60/40 revenue split, (5) automate fulfillment with a virtual assistant and scale by adding profiles in new cities.

name: Google Profile Verification Video Protocol
definition: A three-part video sequence for Google Business Profile verification: (1) film the street-sign intersection to establish location, (2) walk to your vehicle and show business signage or a business card, (3) unlock the vehicle and show tools/equipment. Designed to satisfy Google's location, signage, and business-access requirements.

name: Local Market Viability Test
definition: Two-variable screen for entering a local service market: (a) volume threshold: at least 400 monthly searches for clearly intentful keywords via SEMrush, (b) competition threshold: at least two of the top three Google Maps listings have fewer than 100 reviews. Both conditions must hold for the market to qualify.
concept: Market Selection Criteria: Growth + Pain + Targeting

name: Psychophysics of Relative Perception
definition: Human perception of price, pleasure, heat, pain, and volume is entirely relativistic — there are virtually no absolute internal measures; every judgment depends on the comparison context presented.

name: Affirmation Bias First-Impression Lock
definition: The first impression or decision entered into the brain closes it to contradictory evidence, causing every subsequent evaluation to skew toward confirming the initial judgment.

name: Praxeology-First Economics (von Mises)
definition: Ludwig von Mises argued that human action and psychology (praxeology) is a prior science to economics; economics is merely the study of human action under conditions of scarcity, making psychological framing a prerequisite for economic analysis.

name: Two Levels of Employee Effort
definition: Employees operate at one of two effort levels: minimum-to-avoid-punishment (default) or discretionary effort (everything above that floor); only positive reinforcement unlocks the upper level.

name: Punishment vs. Reward Long-Run Dynamics
definition: Punishment produces fast short-term behavior change but must escalate in intensity to stay effective, and its behavioral effects fade when removed; reward produces slower change but persists and is self-sustaining.

name: Circles of Audience Awareness
definition: A four-level concentric model of audience relationship depth: (1) face recognition only, (2) face + positive experience with one piece of content, (3) face + name recognition, (4) regular viewer who watches consistently.

name: State the Facts and Tell the Truth
definition: A two-part content marketing law: (1) state only verifiable facts about yourself and your results, and (2) say what no one else can say and show what no one else can show — using unique proof as the primary differentiator.

name: Proof Hierarchy for Content Credibility
definition: Three descending levels of content credibility: (1) I helped these specific people achieve what you want, (2) I did the thing you also want to do, (3) I did the work you are not willing to do and can show the result.

name: Tweet-First Content Multiplication System
definition: A content production cascade starting from Twitter/X as the lowest-friction proof-of-concept layer: (1) tweet all day, (2) best tweets become Instagram Reels (read to camera), (3) reels become clips, (4) 20 clips strung together become a YouTube long, (5) captions on posts are sourced from other high-performing tweets.

name: Rule of 100
definition: A four-part daily framework: reach out to 100 people, create content requiring 100 minutes, spend $100+ on ads, and spend 100 minutes on ad creation and research.

name: 13 Rules to Win at Anything
definition: A structured set of 13 foundational principles for sustained success across business and personal endeavors, emphasizing instruction-following, persistence, skill development, pain-driven improvement, and long-term thinking.

name: Five Steps to Live the Life You Want
definition: A five-stage decision framework: (1) figure out what you want, (2) ignore others' opinions, (3) do so much work it would be unreasonable to fail, (4) realize it never mattered, (5) help others once you get there.

name: One More Frame (Permission-Based Change)
definition: A mental model that reframes personal changes (relationships, habits, businesses) as temporary one-day commitments rather than permanent decisions, enabling faster action without sunk-cost regret.

name: Seven Pillars of Self-Work
definition: Alex Hormozi's distillation of personal development into seven observable behavioral rules: (1) thoughts aren't true, (2) feelings don't require action, (3) things aren't good or bad—they just are, (4) our greatest enemy is ignorance, (5) to change your life, change your surroundings, (6) our actions not our pasts define who we are.

name: Yeti Can Vacuum Metaphor
definition: A mental model for emotional regulation: imagine a vacuum layer between inner feelings and outer behavior the way a Yeti can has a vacuum between its walls, allowing internal temperature and external temperature to coexist without contaminating each other.

name: The Solomon Paradox
definition: A decision-making framework using internal dialogue between current self and older self to externalize critique and identify real constraints versus perceived limitations.

name: Six M's Constraint Framework
definition: A systematic questioning approach (referenced but not fully detailed in transcript) for identifying binding constraints on business growth by iteratively asking why each constraint exists.

name: Maker vs. Manager Time Blocking
definition: A time-management discipline where founders explicitly declare whether each time block is dedicated to maker mode (deep work) or manager mode (meetings/decisions), then protect each block accordingly.

name: Thought-to-Action Speed Framework
definition: Personal power is proportional to the gap between deciding and executing; shrinking this gap from days to hours to minutes compounds business velocity.

name: Time Perception Acceleration with Age
definition: Subjective time accelerates with age because a fixed duration becomes a smaller percentage of cumulative lifetime; at 37 (male US median midpoint), you are functionally closer to life-end than midpoint when adjusted for time compression.

name: Self-Proliferating Creative Machine
definition: A process where customers generate creative content that acquires more customers, who in turn generate more creative, creating a compounding feedback loop without proportional team scaling.

name: Content-as-Ads Framework
definition: A unified approach where high-performing organic content is automatically tested as paid ads, eliminating the distinction between content creation and ad creation.

name: 10-Stage Revenue Roadmap
definition: A scaling framework that identifies distinct business stages from zero to $100M+, each with specific constraints and transition requirements across eight business functions, applicable across multiple business models.

name: Promote-Convert-Deliver Loop
definition: A simple three-function business loop for sub-$1M businesses: (1) Promote — let people know about the offer via paid ads and content; (2) Convert — an automated or semi-automated page or sales motion; (3) Deliver — a fixed back-end delivery cadence (e.g., one call per week). The only high-leverage variable input is the promotion layer.

name: Home-Life Support as Discretionary Effort Lever
definition: A framework for unlocking employee discretionary effort by systematically ensuring their home environment and relationships are supportive, allowing full cognitive capacity for work.

name: Employee-to-Owner Transition
definition: The shift from employment to self-employment requires understanding that as a solo operator, revenue equals salary (100% of income is personal expenses), and scaling requires hiring to separate ownership from execution.

name: Revenue-First Scaling Path
definition: A structured sequence for building a sustainable business: (1) choose an advertising channel, (2) determine what to sell via offer design, (3) establish delivery systems, (4) specialize labor by decomposing your role into repeatable tasks, (5) hire people to execute those tasks.

name: Progress Accumulation Through Consistent Effort
definition: Small daily progress compounds invisibly until 30-day, 90-day, and beyond checkpoints reveal material improvement; the mechanism bridges hard seasons where individual completion of complex problems is impossible.

name: Mood Recalibration via Moment Magnification
definition: Consciously redefining what counts as a win (coffee with partner, pain-free morning, single positive podcast) to shift the baseline of emotional satisfaction and prevent outcome-dependent happiness.

name: Work Satisfaction Model
definition: A framework for evaluating life satisfaction by distinguishing between work-as-drudgery (driven by external pressure) and work-as-chosen-activity (driven by internal alignment); the critic's frame is projection of their own pain, not objective truth.

name: Bridge to Status Through Mastery
definition: A three-phase framework where early-stage effort on a new skill produces no status, a bridge period requires endurance through social friction, and eventual competence compounds status and intrinsic reinforcement.

name: Seasonal Balance Over Lifetime
definition: Balance and rest are realized over multi-year horizons (seasons) rather than daily or weekly, enabling periods of intense focus without guilt while preserving long-term work-life sustainability.

name: Mentor Selection Criteria
definition: Evaluate advice givers by whether their actual life outcomes match your goals, not by their credentials or charisma.

name: Motivation Source Irrelevance
definition: The origin of drive (pain, shame, purpose) is irrelevant to outcomes; what matters is action despite emotion.

name: Middle-Path Loneliness Framework
definition: The isolated phase between outgrowing old friends and becoming successful enough for new networks requires time investment and skill-building.

name: Approval Self-Sufficiency
definition: Protection against social collapse during upward mobility requires increasing self-approval and decreasing reliance on others' opinions.

name: Time and Money as Zero-Sum Resources
definition: All resources (time, money) are finite; choosing to allocate to one priority requires explicitly pulling from another, making every resource decision a trade-off.

name: Skill Stacking for Compounding Returns
definition: Each additional skill acquired multiplies returns on existing skills, creating non-linear growth as capabilities compound rather than add linearly.

name: Geographic Arbitrage for Relationship Capital
definition: Deliberately relocating to proximity with higher-caliber peers and founders, trading existing relationships for access to better mentors and collaborators.

name: Opportunity Vehicle Assessment
definition: Alex Hormozi's three-factor framework for evaluating a business opportunity: (1) total number of potential units that can be sold, (2) gross margin per unit sold, and (3) supply/demand dynamics for entry — the product of all three determines opportunity quality.

name: Front-End Launch to Legacy Continuity Stack
definition: Sell a fixed-term high-priced front-end program (e.g., 16-week launch at $16k) to liquidate CAC, then downsell into a lower-priced recurring continuity program (e.g., $800/week legacy), framing the continuity as more value for less money.

name: Dual-EFT Revenue Model
definition: Sell a service-based recurring charge (EFT) and a product-based recurring charge (EFT) in the same transaction, creating two independent recurring revenue streams per customer, each with different cost structures.

name: The Obsession Reframing
definition: What others call obsession is actually sane behavior in a finite lifespan; normal people waste their lives while sane people maximize time for meaningful activity.

name: Judgment as Preference Mismatch
definition: All criticism reduces to one statement: 'You do not live your life in a way that I prefer.' Understanding this dissolves defensiveness and enables clarity about whose preferences matter.

name: Jealousy as Desert Belief
definition: When people hate on you, they believe life has unjustly given you benefits they rightfully deserve. The form of jealousy (attention, money, body) varies, but the mechanism is identical.

name: Work-Life Balance as Mediocrity Signal
definition: People obsessed with work-life balance are typically mediocre at both. Excellence requires applying obsession to everything and redefining 'life' to include the work.

name: Smart vs Hard Work Competition
definition: When competing against other smart people, work-smart-not-hard fails. The only differentiator is working both smart and hard.

name: Optionality vs. Commitment Trade-Off
definition: The principle that choosing commitment in any domain (relationships, locations, business strategy) requires eliminating alternative options; maximum optionality is incompatible with the rewards of deep commitment.

name: Zero to 100M Scaling Roadmap
definition: A 10-stage revenue progression (zero to 100M+) with defined constraints and solution steps across eight business functions, validated across software, physical products, services, and brick-and-mortar.

name: One Big Idea + Ten Reasons
definition: Marketing message structure: consolidate multiple product benefits into a single overarching value proposition supported by ten distinct supporting reasons, rather than ten separate claims each with one supporting reason.

name: Copier-as-Follower Frame
definition: A reframe of competitive copying: the copier is structurally second by definition, which means the original creator retains the leader position as long as they keep innovating forward rather than looking backward.

name: Four Elements of Mental Toughness
definition: A model that decomposes mental toughness into four independent dimensions—tolerance (threshold for disruption), fortitude (magnitude of behavioral change), resilience (speed of recovery), and adaptability (ability to improve from adversity)—that vary independently across individuals.

name: Reinforcement-Based Behavioral Causation
definition: Behavior is determined entirely by the consequences (reward or punishment) that follow action; people repeat behaviors that produce favorable outcomes and avoid those that produce negative ones, independent of their origins or circumstances.

name: Scaling Success Framework
definition: Three load-bearing variables for business success: products customers love and repurchase, pricing that generates significant gross profits, and reinvestment velocity to achieve disproportionate growth.

name: Enterprise Value Wealth Progression
definition: A multi-stage business wealth model that progresses from immediate cash needs, through lifestyle fulfillment, to tax-efficient enterprise-value accumulation and capital deployment.

name: Education-First Capital Allocation
definition: A multi-year strategy of investing all available capital into skill-building education until earnings exceed reinvestment capacity, treating each purchased skill as time-value acceleration into future earning potential.

name: Earning Power Compounding Loop
definition: A recursive cycle where invested education increases annual income, excess income funds the next skill tier, and the process repeats until annual learning spend reaches zero percent of income.

name: Scale Zero Framework
definition: The prerequisite stage before location replication in which the founder removes themselves entirely from operations while maintaining or improving business performance.

name: Expansion Readiness Criteria
definition: Two necessary conditions for opening a new location: excess profit beyond current needs and discretionary time available beyond current operations.

name: Nail It Before You Scale It
definition: Optimize a business model fully in existing location(s) before expanding to new locations; premature scaling adds complexity that is difficult to reverse.

name: Rowboat vs Titanic Decision-Making
definition: Early-stage businesses should remain as lean and maneuverable (rowboat) as possible before expanding; additional locations create organizational inertia (Titanic) that slows pivoting and decision velocity.

name: When It Gets Easy, Do More; When It Gets Hard, Do Different
definition: A two-rule heuristic for effort allocation: easy periods are signals to double down on what is working, not to diversify or rest; hard periods are the only time to change tactics.

name: Three-Shift Work Cadence
definition: Alex Hormozi's personal seasonal work structure: two standard daily shifts (6am-noon, noon-6pm) supplemented by a third shift (6pm-sleep) deployed roughly once a year for six to eight week sprints when breakthrough progress is needed.

name: Micro Speed, Macro Patience
definition: A two-level time philosophy: act with maximal urgency on every individual task and compress timelines aggressively (micro), while holding a multi-year horizon for compounding results (macro); the two are not contradictory.

name: Four Levels of Trade-Off Consciousness
definition: A four-stage progression describing how people relate to the price of desired outcomes: Should (zero payment demanded), Too Much (underbidding), Bidding (iterating upward until sufficient), Source (self-setting the standard above market).

name: Pipeline Conditions Model
definition: A model that frames outcomes as requiring all prerequisite conditions to be met simultaneously — like valves in a pipeline — before results can flow; meeting most but not all conditions still produces zero output.

name: Fear vs. Regret Decision Framework
definition: Personal success is determined by which fear is larger: fear of regret or fear of rejection; sustained action requires regret-fear to supersede rejection-fear.

name: Plan B Worst-Case Decomposition
definition: Breaking an amorphous fear into specific concrete steps reveals that downside risk in developed Western contexts is manageable and rarely catastrophic.

name: Skill Decomposition into Observable Behaviors
definition: Decompose any bundled character trait (e.g., charisma, patience) into a numbered checklist of discrete, observable micro-behaviors; train each behavior individually via checklist and repetition.

name: Deprivation-Based Motivation Model
definition: Motivation equals the inverse of deprivation; the more deprived a person perceives themselves relative to a reference group, the higher their drive to close that gap.

name: Behavior-Based Definitions
definition: Define any abstract term (learning, intelligence, love, trust) strictly by the observable behavior required to demonstrate it; circular or vague definitions block clear thinking and prevent improvement.

name: Input-Output Decoupling
definition: Success is a function of continuing input (action, effort, posting) while ignoring output (downloads, views, immediate results) until a threshold is reached; the time lag between input and output is where most people quit.

name: Infinite Game Framing
definition: Life and business operate as infinite games where the only objective is to keep playing and stay in the arena, not to win once.

name: Incremental Path Model
definition: Success builds through laying bricks incrementally and walking forward, fixing failures as they appear, rather than attempting large single jumps.

name: Three-Stage Professional Growth
definition: Progression from awareness of opportunity, through extended isolation/investment, to eventual explosive return once the inflection point is reached.

name: Reference Group Selectivity
definition: Distinguish between mentors/heroes (aspirational) and reference group (actual decision-influencers); listen only to voices aligned with your goals.

name: Expertise Measurement Through Progress Markers
definition: Expertise is the ability to identify multiple intermediate wins and progress markers within a long project; beginners see only binary output (done/not done).

name: Failure Resume Building
definition: A deliberate strategy of accumulating failures and learning from them to build credibility and capability; the more losses a person incurs, the greater their edge in future wins.

name: Long-Tailed Distribution of Returns
definition: In business, unlike baseball, a single success can generate exponentially greater returns than all prior failures combined; bold experimentation pays off when one outcome outweighs the cost of many experiments.

name: Three Archetypes of Effort
definition: A categorization of people by their relationship to effort and completion: the lazy (cannot start), the losers (cannot finish), and the legends (cannot stop).

name: Continuous Cycle of Constraint Resolution
definition: A repeatable loop: find what works, do more of it, identify what prevents more, solve that constraint, return to doing more.

name: Mountain Metaphor for Goal Pursuit
definition: Goals are waypoints, not destinations; reaching a summit reveals another mountain beyond. The value is in the climb, not the peak.

name: 10-Stage Business Roadmap (Zero to $100M+)
definition: A multi-stage progression from zero to $100M+ revenue, broken into eight business functions per stage, with distinct constraints and graduation steps repeated across software, product, service, and brick-and-mortar models.

name: Happiness vs. Satisfaction Framework
definition: A distinction between contentment with present work and action-oriented dissatisfaction; the model requires remaining happy with the process while maintaining strategic dissatisfaction with the outcome to sustain effort.

name: The Solomon Project
definition: A structured dialogue practice in which a founder speaks to their 85-year-old self weekly to gain advice grounded in complete life context and perfectly aligned incentives.

name: Knowledge Gap vs. Execution Gap
definition: A diagnostic framework distinguishing problems stemming from lack of knowledge from problems stemming from failure to execute known solutions, with different remedies for each.

name: E-Commerce Business Model Elements
definition: An e-commerce business is fundamentally composed of two primary levers: product sourcing/arbitrage (cost to markup ratio) and media buying (customer acquisition efficiency); most operators excel at one but not both.

name: Traffic Quality vs. Conversion Rate Optimization
definition: Improving conversion rate through site optimization (CRO) is a secondary lever; the primary constraint is often traffic quality and audience targeting fit, not landing page conversion mechanics.

name: Conference and Outbound Pipeline Alternation
definition: A dual-channel sales motion that alternates between conference-based lead generation (net fishing) and outbound SDR-driven pipeline building, creating a crisscross fill pattern that maintains continuous pipeline velocity.

name: Event Lead and SDR Lead Stacking
definition: A sequential hiring strategy where SDR leads initially supplement event-based leads, and over time SDR leads become the primary stable pipeline while event leads continue to stack incrementally.

name: Three Wheels of Revenue
definition: Service businesses generate revenue from three distinct sources: equipment/core product sales, consumable supplies, and service offerings around the core product.

name: Customer LTV Extension Strategy
definition: A two-step approach to increasing customer lifetime value: first establish high retention on consumables and service (90-95% annual retention), then target higher-tier customers who buy in greater volume.

name: Stone Cutter Perspective Frame
definition: Three stone cutters doing identical work hold three distinct perspectives (complaint, subsistence, cathedral-building); the work itself is the same but meaning varies by frame.

name: Revenue-Per-Square-Foot Service Line Prioritization
definition: Identify the highest-revenue-per-square-foot service line, strip all lower-productivity offerings, and replicate the lean model across locations via franchising or organic growth.

name: Three-Person Franchise Model
definition: Minimal viable team structure: one manager handling morning/evening sales and service, plus two assistants rotating shifts, capable of $500k-$600k annual revenue at 50% margins.

name: Revenue Per Square Foot Analysis
definition: A diagnostic framework that identifies the highest-margin service category within a multi-service location, then extracts and replicates that core model across multiple smaller facilities rather than scaling the entire location.

name: Alloy Semi-Private Training Model
definition: A service-bundling model where three instructors deliver semi-private (1-on-4) training in 1,200 sq ft, generating $560k top-line revenue with 50% net margins, creating a replicable micro-unit that scales across multiple locations.

name: Center of Influence (COI) Acquisition Model
definition: A strategy that identifies gatekeepers and influential intermediaries as the primary customer, then systematically converts them into repeatable referral sources through deliberate customer experience design.

name: Customer Chunking: Upstream vs Downstream
definition: A mental model shift that reframes the business's primary customer from end-users to intermediaries (agencies, brokers, partners), enabling stable retention because intermediaries have structural incentives to stay while end-users are volatile.

name: Broker Acquisition and Farming System
definition: A two-pronged customer acquisition strategy for intermediaries: hunting (outreach to acquire new brokers) and farming (communication cadence and reciprocity-building with existing brokers to increase share of referrals from 10% to 100%).

name: Business Constraint Diagnosis
definition: Systematically distinguish perceived constraints (intellectual curiosity, emotional preferences) from real ones (customer demand, unit economics, time leverage).

name: Niching Decision Matrix
definition: Niche down when operational efficiency improves through narrower delivery; expand avatar when back-end mechanics are identical but messaging differs.

name: Full-Script Pitch Standardization
definition: A training framework where every word and visual of a pitch is pre-scripted on slides (one phrase per slide), reducing speaker training time to delivery mechanics only (pace, volume, gesture).

name: 10-Stage Scaling Roadmap
definition: A structured progression from zero to $100M+ revenue with eight business functions diagnosed per stage, defining constraints and graduation steps across software, physical products, services, and retail.

name: Volatility vs. Risk Distinction
definition: Volatility (predictable monthly fluctuation) is distinct from risk (unpredictable outcomes); a business can be volatile but not risky if the pattern is forecastable.

name: Constrained Scaling in Service Businesses
definition: Service businesses with predictable seasonal demand can scale by increasing supply during peak season proportionally; no business model change is required if the constraint is capacity.

name: Single-Question Scaling Diagnosis
definition: Identify the one question whose answer would unlock the next order-of-magnitude growth; all other questions are distractions until that question is answered.

name: Retail Margin Improvement Framework
definition: A multi-lever approach to fixing low retail margins through staffing optimization, menu pruning, pricing, attachment-rate scripting, hours optimization, and compensation structure changes.

name: Growth Decision Framework
definition: When scaling a retail location business, determine whether the constraint is capital, talent, or margin quality before deciding to expand to new locations.

name: Three-Step Path to Fix a Content Membership Business
definition: A structured approach to optimizing a struggling content membership: understand customer retention patterns, improve annual prepayment incentives, and introduce higher-ticket upsells.

name: Enterprise Lead Generation Architecture
definition: A three-tier system combining cold outbound, event-based acquisition, and affiliate partnerships, where outbound feeds event attendance and events surface both direct deals and affiliate partners.

name: Affiliate Activation Strategy
definition: Treating affiliates as a second customer base requiring dedicated success cadences and data-driven diagnostics to identify and replicate behaviors of high-performing partners.

name: Debt Recombination Model
definition: A strategic framework for choosing which type of business debt (financial, operational, talent, infrastructure, tech) to incur at each stage based on what the founder can most easily repay.

name: Cash Flow Acceleration Variables
definition: A set of four independent levers for improving business cash flow: acquire customers cheaper, get them to pay faster, get them to pay more, and scale execution through hiring.

name: Hunt-Your-Own-Food Closer Model
definition: Closers are responsible for their own outbound lead generation while also receiving inbound leads, keeping them sharp and ensuring they appreciate allocated leads.

name: More, Better, New Scaling
definition: Three-stage decision hierarchy for growth: exhaust more volume on the current thing, then optimize what you have, only then switch to something different (new).

name: ROIC Decision Framework
definition: Evaluating scaling decisions by calculating return on invested capital per new location: investment cost + recruitment cost compared to annual profit generated at payoff timeline.

name: Capital Redeployment Trade-off
definition: The explicit choice between retaining profit for security (no growth) versus redeploying cash for growth (higher risk, higher upside).

name: Lifetime Value to Cost of Acquiring Talent (LTV:CAT)
definition: The ratio of lifetime or annual gross profit per employee to the cost of acquiring that talent, as an analogue to LTV:CAC on the customer side.
concept: Lifetime Value to Customer Acquisition Cost

name: Dual-Constraint Scaling Model
definition: Businesses are constrained on both the demand side (customers) and supply side (talent); scaling requires solving the binding constraint first, typically talent/supply before leads.

name: Economic Arbitrage Core Business Unit
definition: A business at its most basic is the arbitrage between what it costs to acquire customers and what is collected from them, minus the difficulty of repeating that cycle. Optimize for return on human capital and financial capital simultaneously.

name: Direct Response Doom Loop
definition: A named cycle in which paid-media e-commerce businesses scale revenue while margins compress until the operation becomes a high-liability, low-margin treadmill requiring continuous ad spend just to cover overhead.

name: Brand Loop
definition: A virtuous cycle where brand promise attracts customers, product experience reinforces the promise, which deepens brand equity, enabling premium pricing and repeat purchase without incremental ad spend.

name: Multi-Tier Distribution Strategy
definition: A go-to-market approach that targets platform intermediaries (agencies/mentors) rather than end customers directly, increasing CAC efficiency through bulk onboarding and recurring revenue per intermediary.

name: Four-Funnel CRM Architecture
definition: A structured offer approach for online fitness coaches using four distinct funnels: mini-chat automation, link-in-bio lead magnet, application process, and conversion engine.

name: Three Mechanisms for Scaling Service Delivery
definition: When a founder-dependent service business hits capacity limits, scale via one of three levers: charge more (premium positioning), reduce delivery ratio (fewer hours per client), or hire and train replacements (with expected 30% performance decay).

name: Soft Handoff Transition Model
definition: Transfer founder-dependent clients to a replacement practitioner by maintaining perceived founder proximity (via message updates, reduced-frequency check-ins) while gradually shifting execution responsibility, minimizing churn risk and key-person dependency.

name: Cold Sales Motion Architecture
definition: A structured pathway from paid acquisition (cold traffic) to close: lead magnet → application or VSL pre-frame → video consultation close. Warm processes fail on cold traffic; cold processes succeed on warm traffic.

name: Sales Talent Pipeline (Parallel to Demand Pipeline)
definition: A structured internal system for recruiting, nurturing, interviewing, onboarding, and retaining salespeople that mirrors the customer acquisition funnel stage-for-stage.

name: Avatar Clarity Decision Framework
definition: When choosing between multiple customer avatars, evaluate which requires the least change to your day-to-day operations and delivery model; operational burden, not customer size alone, determines viability.

name: Sales Motion ROI Calculation
definition: Estimate close-rate improvement (e.g., 2% to 5% or 10%), multiply by expected volume and average deal size to quantify sales-system impact before investment.

name: Scaling Progression Through Hiring Mastery
definition: A founder scales a business by sequentially learning what each role looks like (SDR, salesperson, sales manager, closer, closer manager, director, VP) through repeated hiring failures until pattern recognition improves, then replicating the pattern.

name: Two-VSL Sales Bridge
definition: Two video sales letters inserted into a multi-step high-ticket service sales process: VSL1 between lead booking and first appointment; VSL2 between first and second appointment (design presentation). Purpose is to build value and prime the close before each in-person touchpoint.

name: Constraint-First Capital Allocation
definition: Always allocate available capital to the current binding constraint rather than aspirational growth levers; the constraint determines ROI ceiling. Once relieved, the next constraint surfaces and receives capital next.

name: Cost of Change Framework
definition: Any business change carries a guaranteed ~20% temporary revenue decrement before gains accrue; changes yielding less than a 2x upside do not justify that guaranteed cost.

name: Growth Path Sequencing: Share-of-Pie Before Expanding-Pie Before Geographic Expansion
definition: A three-stage priority order for service businesses with dominant local market position: (1) increase share of existing market, (2) grow the total addressable market locally, (3) only then expand geographically.
concept: Geographic Expansion Sequence: Dominate Local, Then Expand

name: Law Firm Scaling Constraint Analysis
definition: A diagnostic framework identifying talent acquisition as the binding constraint in high-touch professional services, then solving by multiplying recruiter volume and sophistication rather than business model changes.

name: Distributor-Layer Revenue Architecture
definition: Shifting from direct customer acquisition to acquiring agencies/producers as distribution layers, where each distributor generates multiple recurring customers per year rather than selling episodic customers one at a time.

name: Agency Stacking Model
definition: Acquiring one new distributor (agency or producer) per month, each generating one customer per month, creating a compounding monthly customer base that stacks year-over-year as prior distributors remain active.

name: Distribution Layer Two-Prong Strategy
definition: A framework for building scalable distribution through agencies: first, a launch strategy to acquire initial distributors with immediate value; second, a retention strategy treating agencies as customers with a defined customer journey and usage-based pricing.

name: SMB Pricing Bifurcation
definition: A pricing structure that separates low-tier (low-margin) and high-tier (high-margin) segments, pricing low enough that SMB volatility does not trigger cancellation but high enough to capture premium margin from customers who can afford it.

name: SMB Scaling Bifurcation Model
definition: Service agencies targeting SMBs must choose between two poles—low-cost high-volume with near-zero delivery cost, or premium high-touch serving only businesses with proven models and metrics—with the middle ground as a dead zone.

name: CAC-LTV-Churn Trap
definition: As SMB service businesses scale, SMB churn increases unpredictably, margins compress, CAC rises, and hiring increases to offset churn, creating a negative-feedback loop that stops growth around $100K monthly revenue.

name: Service Business Reinvestment Duality
definition: Service businesses with high cash flow have two primary reinvestment levers—talent and brand plays—each requiring different time horizons and capital allocation frameworks.

name: Performance Marketing vs. Branding Split
definition: Successful national/international businesses allocate 30% to direct-response performance marketing and 70% to brand-building associations, creating 5-20x ROAS over 12 months vs. 30-day direct-response gains.

name: Scale Zero Framework
definition: A founder's role must become entirely optional for growth to compound; any percentage of output tied to founder presence creates a ceiling on scalability.

name: Input-Output Problem Diagnosis
definition: A structured diagnosis of funnel performance that separates three independent variables: absolute volume of leads, percentage qualified (quality), and absolute qualified leads (qualified volume).

name: Friction and Qualification Lever System
definition: A four-stage approach to optimizing funnel quality: measure baseline metrics, add friction filters, evaluate quality improvement vs. volume impact, then scale volume independently to restore absolute qualified throughput.

name: Content-to-Avatar Attribution Framework
definition: A system for identifying which content types attract which avatar segments by tracking customer source data, save-to-engagement ratios, and direct feedback on sales calls.

name: Fix-The-Hole-First Growth Model
definition: Before scaling acquisition spend, eliminate customer churn first; fixing retention yields exponential profit growth without increasing acquisition.

name: Revenue-Stage Health Metrics
definition: At $3M revenue stage, prioritize churn rate and LTV retention impact over acquisition efficiency as the primary lever for compound growth.

name: Time Allocation Diagnosis for Founder Bottleneck
definition: Quantify founder time spent on clinical delivery versus business operations; if delivery work exceeds 50%, hiring a replacement practitioner at the founder's draw salary frees time to address actual constraints.

name: Profit Sufficiency Test for Growth Constraint
definition: Determine whether revenue growth is constrained by cash availability or bandwidth; calculate seller discretionary earnings and test whether additional profit would materially change the founder's life.

name: Owner Empowerment Compensation Structure
definition: A deal structure that combines salary, profit share, and equity-like EBITDA contribution rights to incentivize operator autonomy and ownership thinking without equity dilution.

name: Founder Accountability Role-Play
definition: A hiring conversation technique where the founder explicitly frames the operator's role by describing call-handling scenarios and establishing that 'not calling the founder' is the correct answer, anchoring independent decision-making.

name: Six-Week Onboarding Challenge
definition: A front-end offer structure for membership-based fitness businesses where new clients pay a premium upfront for a defined 6-week outcome program with a money-back or credit guarantee, which filters committed buyers, liquidates CAC via supplement sales, and converts to annual recurring membership via a mid-program upsell.

name: Career Ladder Multiplication
definition: Expand each role level (junior, normal, senior) into nested tiers (junior, junior-plus, normal, normal-plus, senior, senior-plus) with paired title bumps and perks, creating 3-6 months between promotions to sustain engagement.

name: Title and Perks Alternation
definition: Scatter tangible perks (parking, schedule control, vehicle upgrades, weekend exemption) between title promotions to make advancement tangible beyond salary, preventing title-dumping without retention.

name: Progressive Objective Milestones
definition: Anchor promotions to measurable customer outcomes (reviews, delivery metrics) with escalating targets; first milestone set as easy win (six-inch putt) to establish momentum, subsequent milestones expand in steps.

name: Geographic Market Entry Strategy
definition: A framework for scaling a C-suite focused service business into a new geographic market by layering ads as a fast-learning channel while running traditional outreach in parallel.

name: Grand Slam vs Home Run Offer Trade-Off
definition: A grand slam offer (turnkey all-in-one) closes at near-100% but limits volume; a home run offer (core product only) closes at ~75% but frees capacity and multiplies addressable deal flow.

name: Risk Assessment Framework
definition: Evaluating business debt risk through mathematical volatility modeling, seasonal cash flow analysis, and debt covenant coverage ratios rather than emotional fear.

name: Growth vs. Risk Trade-Off
definition: The fundamental choice between faster growth (requiring debt/risk) and slower growth with lower risk; growth rate is constrained by either capital deployment capacity or risk appetite.

name: Grand Opening Playbook for Restaurant Growth
definition: A structured pre-opening validation and post-opening acceleration process combining product-market fit verification with coordinated marketing spend, overstaffing, and promotional giveaways to reach full capacity via word-of-mouth within six months.

name: North Star Metric for Franchising
definition: Unit economics (restaurant profitability per location) is the single core lever that determines franchise sellability and growth speed.

name: Capital Deployment Trade-off Analysis
definition: Comparing return on equity across three paths: scaling corporate locations to 100 (franchise-heavy model), scaling to 20 corporate locations with improved margins, or franchising strategically.

name: Commitment-First Sales Model
definition: Sell the commitment upfront with clear delivery timeline expectations, then execute fulfillment in batches by region, decoupling sales velocity from fulfillment capacity.

name: Five-Part Sales Script Training
definition: A daily group training structure rotating through intro, discovery, offer, objections/looping, and a fifth day dedicated to team-specific hot topics, keeping each script component crisp.
concept: Daily Sales Role-Play as Training Cadence

name: Big Head Long Tail Pricing Model
definition: A pricing structure separating high-value one-time upfront services (head) from low-cost recurring continuity offerings (tail), where the tail becomes a no-brainer continuation after the head.

name: Avatar Segmentation Buckets
definition: Three-part avatar filtering using demographics (what they look like), quantifiables (business size/metrics), and behavioral patterns (activation triggers) to identify high-conversion prospect segments.

name: Skill Extraction and Consumable Separation
definition: Business model separation where one-time skill delivery is priced separately and higher than the recurring consumable services (e.g., creative, ongoing support) that follow mastery.

name: Valuation Risk Layering Framework
definition: A 10x valuation increase is justified when the riskiest assumption (often regulatory or technical de-risking) is proven, reducing overall company assumptions from N to N-1.

name: Founder Control Architecture for Fundraising
definition: Founders can maintain operational control (via voting rights) while accepting minority equity if existing investors trust their execution and understand the capital requirements.

name: Sales God to Sales Training God Identity Shift
definition: A founder who is the top sales performer must transition their identity from personal sales excellence to codifying and replicating that excellence in others in order to scale beyond personal capacity.

name: Headcount-to-Revenue Linear Scaling Model
definition: A simple planning model: divide target revenue by revenue-per-rep to determine required headcount, then build recruiting infrastructure to reach that number.

name: Money Makes You Lazy
definition: Excess capital impairs decision-making by enabling capital-first solutions to problems that require skill, relationships, or focus; conversely, capital constraints force creative problem-solving.

name: The One-Thing Extreme
definition: If only one outcome (the highest-leverage outcome) were guaranteed to occur in the next year, would it solve all business goals? If yes, why are you doing anything else?

name: Influencer-Dependent Scaling
definition: A market-driven transition where all attention and trust flows to creators rather than institutions, making influencer/creator partnerships the primary growth driver despite volatility and dependency risks.

name: Med Spa Margin Recovery Through Founder Extraction
definition: Systematically rebuild unit economics and scale a founder-dependent med spa by fixing sales motion first, then membership model, then talent retention, enabling margin expansion from 15% to 35-40% before opening additional locations.

name: Phantom Stock Structure for Med Spa Provider Retention
definition: Non-dilutive equity program where each location holds phantom stock for its dedicated provider (injector/technician), vesting tied to schedule commitment rather than multi-location oversight, creating brand loyalty instead of provider dependency.

name: Upside-Downside-Livability Filter
definition: A three-question decision filter (What is the upside? What is the downside? Can I live with the downside?) attributed by Alex Hormozi to Keith Cunningham, used to evaluate strategic pivots and major bets.

name: Licensing Readiness Gate
definition: Alex Hormozi's conditional approval framework: a founder earns the right to launch a licensing model only after the business can open a new location per quarter with a team that does not include the founder at all.

name: DSO Consolidation Formula
definition: A multi-practice dental acquisition model that pools 4-5 independent practices into a unified dental support organization (DSO) under shared ownership, enabling higher valuation multiples and improved unit economics through consolidated buying power and operational leverage.

name: Multi-Tier Offer Waterfall
definition: An acquisition offer structure that provides clear tier levels (e.g., 4x multiple for solo practice, 7x for participation in DSO, 10-12x for consolidated platform), with founders keeping equity above the baseline to incentivize participation.

name: IP Carve-Out Strategy
definition: Separating intellectual property (coaching curriculum, AI portal, systems) from the core operational business being sold, with the IP retained as a separate entity and licensed back to the acquirer under defined terms and territories.

name: Operating Under Regulatory Uncertainty Framework
definition: A decision framework for businesses in regulated industries to separate perceived regulatory risk from actual constraint, and to operate aggressively while information is complete, deferring strategy changes only when regulatory headwinds materialize.

name: Software Economics for Distribution Businesses
definition: A three-component framework defining when software multiplies a business: viral growth, high gross margins on incremental customers, and revenue retention (especially net-negative churn).

name: Logic, Evidence, Utility Framework
definition: A three-step diagnostic framework for problem definition: state what the problem is (Logic), quantify how you know it (Evidence), and explain why it matters (Utility).

name: Demand Unlock Constraint Matrix
definition: A four-variable diagnostic for unconstrained growth: messaging clarity, sales motion efficiency, pricing structure, and fast-cash activation capability.

name: Qualification Friction Model
definition: A framework where increased qualification requirements (good friction) improve ROAS and sales efficiency by filtering away low-intent prospects, enabling smaller closing teams.

name: Fast Cash Play Activation
definition: An early engagement strategy where existing business resources (past customers, social lists, content) are mobilized in the first 30 days to generate outcome proof and fund the core engagement.

name: Three-Lever Delivery Redesign
definition: When founder-dependent delivery creates a supply constraint, reduce delivered hours and scope while repositioning the reduction as an integrity move, then reinvest savings in promised-but-underdelivered services.

name: Accessibility Arc
definition: Early-stage founders differentiate via founder accessibility (cell phone, rapid response); at scale, accessibility becomes a liability preventing delegation and growth, requiring repositioning of reduced access as earned confidence rather than loss of service.

name: Sales Discovery Framework
definition: Three-stage sales structure (intro frame + discovery + pitch) where discovery surfaces pain points via questioning, pitch matches those points to solutions, and closing follows naturally from problem-solution alignment.

name: Sales Training As Reinforcement Loop
definition: Sales competence is built through daily script reinforcement and correct-execution feedback, not hiring for natural talent; most businesses do not know how to train sales.

name: Creative-Volume Targeting Framework
definition: A market-selection strategy for service delivery businesses that prioritizes high-volume customer needs (50-100+ units per month) over premium-quality lower-volume offerings, targeting buyers already spending $100k+ monthly in the category.

name: Full-Service Creative Agency Model
definition: A value proposition where the agency handles creative production, fulfillment, and media buying as a unified service, with media buying as the simplest layer and qualified buyer criteria (1+ year profitable advertising, $1M+ annual ad spend) as the gate.

name: Content Creation Motivation Reversal
definition: Identify which content formats the creator personally enjoys, then build sustainable content strategy around those formats rather than algorithmic optimization.

name: Reminder-Based Content Value
definition: Audiences benefit from repeated exposure to core ideas in novel contexts; creators mistakenly believe content must be perpetually novel to the creator when novelty for the audience is the primary requirement.

name: Six-Week Recruitment Sprint
definition: A dedicated time-boxed period where founders and key decision-makers pause operational work to focus exclusively on talent acquisition through interviews and outreach.

name: Cold Headhunt Outreach Message
definition: A low-pressure cold recruitment message that opens with perceived fit and offering opportunity, then segues to 'do you know anyone like you', allowing the prospect to pass without feeling pressured.

name: Tiered Recruitment Approach by Role Expertise
definition: Founders recruit leadership roles within their own expertise network; external headhunter firms handle specialized technical roles (finance, tech, legal) where founder pattern recognition is limited.

name: Supply Chain Deconstraining Path
definition: A three-lever sequence to unlock manufacturing-constrained growth: renegotiate payment terms, leverage influencer demand pull, and execute sell-outs to pull cash forward.

name: Manufacturing Capital Acquisition Strategy
definition: A path to own proprietary manufacturing equipment by achieving the manufacturer's volume capacity first, then purchasing the machine with cash generated by hitting that volume.

name: Supply-First Sequencing in Capacity-Constrained Businesses
definition: When demand exceeds delivery capacity, resolve supply constraints before increasing demand; prioritize hiring and training over sales expansion until fulfillment scales.

name: Price-as-Talent-Signal Framework
definition: Raising prices to the point of margin sufficiency enables recruiting and compensation upgrades to attract top talent, which compounds into a virtuous cycle of quality, reputation, and sustainable growth.

name: Hat Maker Acquisition Model
definition: Direct cold outreach to struggling trade artisans (hat makers, leather workers) offering significantly higher compensation in exchange for relocation and integration into a systemized operation at premium price points.

name: ROAS Doom Loop (Direct Response Doom Loop)
definition: A vicious cycle in performance-marketing-dependent e-commerce where increasing ad spend to maintain growth yields diminishing returns, eventually reaching cash-flow-negative equilibrium despite top-line revenue growth.

name: Brand Levers for Price & Loyalty
definition: Three measurable outcomes of branding: ability to charge higher prices, increase purchase frequency, and reduce customer acquisition cost through premium perception.

name: Association-Based Branding Framework
definition: Positioning a product next to culturally positive associations until the product inherits those associations, then removing the association cue while retaining brand equity.

name: Content Production Workflow
definition: Chunk production into sequential phases (plan, record, edit) rather than end-to-end work per piece; enables 3-5x output increase and consistent cadence.

name: Multi-Platform Content Leverage
definition: A single short-form video multiplies output 21x when repurposed into platform-native posts, transcription posts, and infographic posts across seven distribution channels.

name: Pricing Waterfall Model
definition: A tiered wholesale pricing structure where customers order at different volumes and receive correspondingly discounted rates, with revenue-based advertising requirements that scale with top-line sales.

name: Wholesale vs D2C Margin Analysis
definition: Decomposing profitability across channels to identify which layer of the business waterfall is compressing margins and requires structural fixes (pricing or cost reduction).

name: Three-Lever Business Scaling
definition: A business doubles revenue by increasing customer count, raising average order value (AOV), or increasing repeat purchase frequency; applying all three compounds growth 8x.

name: Brand-Driven E-Commerce Advantage
definition: A strong brand delivers four compounding advantages: cheaper customer acquisition, higher conversion rates at premium pricing, higher repeat-purchase rates, and sustained profitability as ad audiences expand.

name: Multi-Tier Campaign Architecture
definition: Layered email and ad campaigns targeting different audience-awareness segments (cold to warm) improve blended return-on-ad-spend (ROAS) by distributing spend across lower-individual-performance sets that collectively outperform single high-performers.

name: Constraint Cascade for Service Scale
definition: A multi-step sequence where business pricing must increase first to generate cash flow, which enables hiring redundancy, which enables founder offload.

name: Per-Asset Pricing over Tiered Ladders
definition: For ultra-bespoke high-net-worth service businesses, pricing by the asset being worked on (yacht, plane, house) with a small annual continuity retainer outperforms complex multi-tier commitment ladders because it matches client desire for flexibility and speed.

name: Scaling Through Training vs Selection
definition: Two paths to grow a sales organization: scaling through selection (hire many, let weak performers exit) vs. scaling through training (teach anyone off the street to sell at high performance). Scaling through training yields superior margins and competitive advantage.

name: Profit-Driver Identification in Scaling
definition: In a scaling coaching business, the two most profitable customer segments are those acquired for free (organic) and those who renew without paying CAC again. All paid-acquisition customers in the middle serve primarily to unlock scale. Focus compounds on these two drivers.

name: Four Levers for Supply Constraint Resolution
definition: Four operational decisions (price, delivery ratio, productization, hiring) can resolve capacity constraints; the choice depends on team bandwidth and which lever is most efficient to pull first.

name: 60-Second Diagnostic for Scaling Healthcare Services
definition: A rapid diagnosis framework that identifies the binding constraint in a service business by asking: who is the ideal customer, what existing asset can reach them, and where is the gap in the sales execution.

name: Trusted Asset Leverage for Lead Generation
definition: Using an existing credibility asset (podcast appearance, media exposure) as the primary lead magnet, combined with geographic targeting and active sales follow-up to convert awareness into customers.

name: Sales Team Culture as Selectivity
definition: Elite sales teams self-police through narrative of selectivity (brand prestige + peer accountability) where being on the team is framed as an honor and norm violations are policed by peers themselves.

name: Sales Fundamentals Operationalization
definition: Sales excellence is consistency in executing four core steps (follow script, follow up, work the lead, make the offer) for qualified leads, with performance measurement and diagnosis keyed to this checklist.

name: System Design Architecture for Remote Operations
definition: A two-route framework for designing systems in locations where the founder cannot be present: automation that triggers behavior, or a local leader that triggers behavior.

name: Remote Leadership Delegation Pattern
definition: When a founder cannot be on-site consistently, assign a general manager to observe operations, establish standards, and codify them into systems.

name: Three-Market Segmentation for Athletic Training
definition: Athletic training services have three distinct buyer segments with different willingness-to-pay: elite/young athletes (driven by scholarship investment), semi-professional/youth (driven by parental investment in status and skills), and recreational adult athletes (driven by social status and improvement).

name: Domain-Specific Decision Authority
definition: Couples working together assign decision authority by domain expertise—each person owns decisions in areas where they have superior knowledge or relationship—while reserving big strategic decisions for joint agreement.

name: Proactive Relationship Maintenance
definition: Preventing work-relationship degradation requires explicit verbal signaling when imbalance is noticed, with one partner ceding to the other's request rather than letting tension accumulate.

name: Podcast Guest Selection Framework
definition: A three-criterion framework for evaluating podcast invitations: interviewer preparation depth (research demonstrated through question quality), show performance metrics (audience size and episode longevity), and format preference (in-person vs. remote delivery).

name: Action-Based Anxiety Alleviation
definition: Anxiety about the future is reduced through intentional, deliberate action aimed at skill improvement rather than activity for its own sake.

name: Rapid Learning Through Structured Volume + Feedback
definition: Accelerate skill development by generating high volume of work, systematically analyzing outcomes, identifying patterns in top performers, and iterating on those patterns.

name: Skill Stacking as Asset Multiplication
definition: Complementary skills compound disproportionately—mastering two adjacent domains (e.g., sales + finance, code + marketing) generates exponentially greater opportunity than mastery of a single domain.

name: Counsel-Based Feedback Model
definition: A decision-making discipline that filters feedback from crowd sources and prioritizes input only from named, high-credibility advisors and proven successful peers.

name: Collective Bonus Pool Model
definition: A team compensation structure where bonus payouts are tied to collective threshold achievement, aligning individual incentives with group performance.

name: Expert Mapping and Consolidation Method
definition: A rapid learning framework that identifies the smartest people around a problem, maps the neural network of expertise by iterative referral, and consolidates knowledge into actionable buckets.

name: CLOSER Framework
definition: A six-step scripted sales sequence: Clarify why the prospect is there, Label them with a solvable problem, Overview their past experiences, Sell the vacation (dream outcome), Explain away concerns, Reinforce the decision.

name: External Validation Treadmill
definition: A three-stage escalation where seeking approval generates ever-rising targets: make as much as the reference figure, then more, then more than they ever made, with each milestone triggering a reset of the goalpost.

name: Content Creation Workflow
definition: A batched, low-friction system for capturing ideas, structuring them with team input, and executing recording in concentrated sessions to prevent burnout.

name: Burnout Prevention Through Capacity Design
definition: Deliberately building excess capacity into work life to pursue opportunities without overcommitment; burnout stems from capacity exhaustion, not from content creation itself.

name: Marriage as Priority Reversal
definition: Shifting organizational priority from business-first-then-marriage to marriage-first-then-business unlocks relationship satisfaction and improves business outcomes.

name: Three Legs of the Investment Stool
definition: Investment capital allocation across three scalable dimensions: money (capital), time/work (team building), and brand/distribution (limited in how many associations it can sustain before losing potency).

name: Consulting Background to Small Business Bridge
definition: Marrying big business strategy with small business tactics by hiring former big-firm consultants (Bain, McKinsey-type) who want to apply complex problem-solving to scaled small businesses.

name: Three Gym Scaling Models
definition: Progressive business model evolution from owner-operated gym to turnkey consulting to licensing partnership, each offering different leverage and revenue multipliers.

name: Behavioral Deconstruction of Adjectives
definition: A method for operationalizing vague adjectives (energy, confident, lazy) by tracing them back to specific observable behaviors, enabling replication and teaching of those behaviors.

name: Deprivation-Motivation Loop
definition: Motivation is operationalized as the equal-opposite of deprivation: the more deprived a person is of a desired resource, the more motivated they are to obtain it; persuasion works by controlling deprivation and making the desired action the path to relief.

name: Oxygen Mask Priority Framework
definition: Solve immediate survival constraints (ability to pay rent) before attempting long-term vision planning; basic needs security enables strategic thinking.

name: Tweet-to-Content Flywheel
definition: A content system where organic, moment-captured social media posts (tweets) become the seed for higher-quality long-form work (books, courses) through refinement and expansion.

name: Opportunity Prioritization Framework
definition: A three-tier system for selecting which business opportunities to pursue: first, activities requiring no new skills or effort; second, activities requiring effort but no new skills; third, activities requiring new skills with highest leverage payoff.

name: Risk-Adjusted Return Analysis
definition: Comparing opportunities not by eliminating risk, but by normalizing risk across different options using risk-adjusted return metrics to evaluate relative safety rather than absolute safety.

name: Investor Decision Making as Universal Principle
definition: The investor mindset—quantified decision-making with scoreboard-validated track records—applies beyond finance to personal life decisions and provides superior frameworks for evaluating options.

name: Content as Practice Not Game
definition: A mental reframe that treats content creation as rehearsal for future capability rather than the primary competition, reducing stake-anxiety in early-stage production.

name: Multi-Axis Tracking for Micro-Wins
definition: A system that tracks content performance across multiple measurable dimensions (absolute growth, relative growth, impressions, follower count) such that at least one metric shows progress each period, generating reinforcement and sustained motivation.

name: Compound Projection for Long-Term Motivation
definition: A forecasting discipline that calculates the current growth trajectory (e.g. 13% monthly), projects it forward 6-12 months, and surfaces the exciting end-state result to sustain effort over the interim period.

name: Three-Pronged Alcohol Strategy
definition: Three sequential tactics to increase beverage attachment rate: (1) per-meal drink pairing on the menu, (2) a rotating weekly cocktail special the team tastes and endorses, (3) server-delivered natural pairing suggestion at order time.

name: Four Customer Journey Conversations
definition: Four scripted server interactions that must be drilled daily: (1) first-time guest greeting, (2) drink-of-the-week pitch at table arrival, (3) natural drink pairing suggestion per menu item ordered, (4) review-and-return ask post-bill.

name: Grand Reopening Influencer Ambassador Loop
definition: Invite local social-media accounts (10k+ followers or high-hashtag rankers) to a grand reopening framed as a local ambassador program; require review posting plus a video in exchange for the free item; use resulting videos as paid Meta ad creatives.

name: Narrative Anchoring for Commodity Products
definition: Pair a commodity product with a meaningful story or origin narrative to increase perceived value and customer willingness to pay above the base commodity price.

name: Three Levers to Expand Local Business Revenue
definition: A three-part framework for scaling single-location revenue: compress delivery (increase throughput per location), add distribution channels (saturate market across platforms), or replicate the model (open new locations).

name: Expert Rapid Learning Interview Process
definition: A systematic approach to learning an unfamiliar domain by interviewing a cascading chain of experts, capturing their filtered knowledge, categorizing insights, and consolidating into actionable truths.

name: Interview-Based Candidate Evaluation
definition: A hiring framework that evaluates candidates by presenting actual business problems, observing how they break down solutions into specific metrics and behaviors, and assessing the quality and quantity of metrics they track.

name: Goodwill as Positive Reinforcement History
definition: Goodwill is not a vague social surplus but a measurable history of positive reinforcement: each time someone acted on advice and got a good outcome, one unit is deposited; the accumulated balance determines likelihood of future cooperation.

name: Creator Give-to-Ask Ratio Misconception
definition: The common creator belief that selling to an audience withdraws from a goodwill bank is only true if the product is poor; an exceptional product deposits value, making the ask irrelevant, as Steve Jobs demonstrated with Apple product launches that generated demand rather than draining goodwill.

name: Podcast as Email List Model
definition: A podcast audience behaves like an email list: high engagement per subscriber, low subscriber count relative to social platforms, and near-zero organic discoverability without a separate traffic source (YouTube or social). Growth comes from the traffic source, not the podcast itself.

name: Title Defense Model
definition: A competitive framework where winning a position is far harder than defending it; maintaining relevance requires continuously taking on larger challenges.

name: Education-as-Investment Valuation
definition: Frame education spending as a capital investment with a cost and a return (delta between current income and target income), not as a lifestyle expense.

name: Three-Step Skill-Acquisition Process
definition: Execute coaching/education in sequence: (1) follow instructions exactly as given, (2) extract what works and discard the rest, (3) identify and patch knowledge gaps using other resources.

name: Skill Gaps as Bridge Architecture
definition: Education programs build foundational bricks; gaps between your brick-set and the target outcome are due to missing prerequisite knowledge, not program failure.

name: Declarative vs Procedural Content
definition: Communication effectiveness depends on framing content around what is possible or what problems exist (declarative) rather than step-by-step instructions on how to do something (procedural).

name: Pattern Matching Training Model
definition: Teaching people to recognize and apply patterns to standard situations is faster and equally effective as explaining underlying mechanisms, with humans handling exceptions.

name: Continuous Action Model
definition: Consistent work across time horizon creates readiness for all opportunities; timing becomes irrelevant when preparation is continuous.

name: Skill-Opportunity Multiplication Loop
definition: Each skill acquired expands the set of executable opportunities; broader skill portfolio opens exponentially more paths.

name: Inversion as Relationship Due Diligence
definition: Before committing to a long-term relationship, enumerate the most common causes of relationship failure and proactively address each one, rather than hoping they won't arise.

name: Non-Negotiables Disclosure Framework
definition: On one of the first dates, state upfront every non-negotiable behavior or commitment you will not sacrifice, so the other person can self-select out early rather than after years of misalignment.

name: Stable-Trait Partner Selection
definition: Filter a potential partner on the handful of traits that are unlikely to change over a multi-decade horizon (values, behaviors under duress, core dispositions) rather than surface-level interests or current passions, which will change.

name: Short-Term Pain vs. Long-Term Pain Matrix
definition: A four-quadrant model mapping tradeoffs between immediate discomfort and future consequences: short pain/long gain (desired), short gain/long pain (to avoid), with regret and fulfillment as the emotional anchors.

name: 10-Stage Company Roadmap (Zero to $100M+)
definition: A structured progression through predictable business stages as headcount increases, with each stage characterized by a specific constraint (symptom, diagnosis) and a prescribed exit step, applicable across product and service verticals.

name: Five P's Video Content Framework
definition: A five-part video structure (Promise, Pain, Proof, Picture, Plan) that optimizes for retention and viewer engagement by establishing credibility upfront.

name: Messenger-Message Binding
definition: The messenger's credibility is inseparable from message consumption; audiences evaluate education content through the lens of who is delivering it, not the information in isolation.

name: Sales Conversation Framework
definition: A repeatable five-stage structure for consultative sales conversations: (1) understand why they're there and their problem, (2) learn what they've tried and why it failed, (3) explain how the product differs, (4) clarify expected outcomes via analogy, (5) close with permission-based language.

name: Conviction Transfer Model
definition: Trust and conviction are the two prerequisites for sales success; trust is built through expertise and rapport, and conviction is transferred from salesperson to prospect through demonstration of belief.

name: Four Elements of Equity
definition: Equity structure can be decomposed into four independent dimensions—control (decision authority), risk (liability if failure), profits (cash flow distributions), and enterprise value (upside at sale or liquidity event)—each of which can be contracted separately rather than bundled in shares.

name: Investment-Focused Talent Pitch
definition: Recruiting early hires or co-founders is fundamentally a capital-raising pitch, except the investor is deploying time, expertise, and life energy instead of cash; the sales mechanism is identical to investor pitch.

name: Body Composition Achievement Path
definition: A two-phase progression where initial achievement requires substantial effort, then maintenance requires minimal effort once baseline is established.

name: 24-Dollar Daily Budget Allocation
definition: Time allocation framed as a wallet with 24 hourly dollars; every commitment claims a portion, and trade-offs become transparent when visualized this way.

name: Solomon Framework
definition: A self-advice system in which the founder holds a written back-and-forth dialogue with their imagined 85-year-old self (named Solomon), satisfying the three conditions for trustworthy counsel: aligned incentives, complete context, and competence.

name: Four-Point Availability Lever Framework
definition: Four sequential levers that compound show-up rates: time slot density (seven-day/week availability), slot granularity (15-min vs 60-min increments), temporal proximity (same-day or next-day booking preferred), and forward-dragging (moving appointments earlier when possible).

name: Sales Training Progressive Stages
definition: A structured sales onboarding process that moves reps through game-tape study, half-load schedules, call review with Socratic questioning, and scripted drill-down to internalize messaging at the word level.

name: Script Mastery via Repetition
definition: Breaking down complex sales interactions into minute-level script components, drilling each component repeatedly until verbal delivery becomes subconscious, then moving to the next component.

name: Prediction-Control Loop
definition: Mastery is the ability to predict outcomes by understanding all variables affecting a situation; accurate prediction equals controllable behavior.

name: Outcome-First Decision Framework
definition: Before taking action, define the desired outcome, then assess whether the planned behavior increases the likelihood of that outcome occurring.

name: Gap Between Stimulus and Reaction
definition: Victor Frankl's model: there exists a moment of choice between receiving adverse stimulus and choosing one's response; this gap is where human agency and ideals are expressed.

name: Grieving Duration vs. Love Depth
definition: The time spent grieving a loss is independently chosen and not determined by how much someone was loved; short mourning periods do not dishonor relationships.

name: Biological Foundation for Resilience
definition: Sleep quality, nutrition, and recent workload directly modulate stress tolerance and mental toughness; biological optimization improves response capacity to adversity.

name: Three Offer Differentiation Vectors
definition: A commodity offer must win on at least one of three dimensions: speed (faster than competitors), risk-reduction (less risky than competitors), or ease (simpler experience for the customer). Focus on one vector and execute it well rather than mediocre coverage of all three.

name: Three Lead Magnet Types
definition: Lead magnets take one of three forms: (1) Reveal a Problem (e.g., '7 mistakes homeowners make'), (2) Trial of the Solution (give the core deliverable for free and follow up), or (3) One Step of Multi-Step (a splinter offer: give one component of the full offer for free or near-free, then upsell the rest).

name: Attraction Offer Mechanisms
definition: Four wrappings that convert an existing offer into a lead-generation vehicle without changing the core product: giveaway, win-your-money-back, decoy pricing, and buy-X-get-Y-free.

name: Decision-Making Speed Framework
definition: Accelerating decision velocity by reducing deliberation time from weekly to hourly to real-time, enabled by understanding decision reversibility and the speed loss from delayed choice.

name: Decision-Reversal Calculus
definition: Evaluating decisions by the cost delta between forward action and reversal, comparing total time cost (decision delay plus reversal cost) to find the optimal choice moment.

name: Two-Question Decision Razor
definition: A decision-making framework that asks 'What do I want to have happen?' and 'What increases the odds of that happening?' to override initial reactive impulses.

name: $500K Employee Roadmap
definition: A structured path for an employee to increase compensation from $50K to $500K by moving to a larger company, positioning themselves near revenue generation, taking on entrepreneurial risk, and negotiating for a percentage of value created.

name: Value-to-Compensation Negotiation
definition: A framework for employees to articulate measurable business impact they create, propose performance-based upside, and negotiate for a share of that created value.

name: Internal Revenue Attribution
