definition: The discipline of mapping every role's contribution to business revenue generation, from direct (sales) to indirect (customer success, finance, legal), enabling conversations about compensation alignment.

name: Problem-to-Problem Continuity
definition: Products keep customers by positioning the initial problem's solution as creating a new problem that only the product can solve.

name: Consumable Deliverables Model
definition: A community retention model where customers receive education once (black box system) but must repeatedly purchase consumable inputs (supplies, data, updates) to operate the system.

name: Five Creator Monetization Paths
definition: A spectrum of five monetization modes ordered by degree of control: (1) sponsorships, (2) affiliate/performance deals, (3) equity investment with brand+capital contribution, (4) white-label/drop-ship, (5) scratch-built product or service.

name: Three Creator Investment Buckets
definition: The three resources a creator can contribute to a deal: work (time and execution), brand (audience trust and attention), and capital (money); combinations of all three maximize deal leverage.

name: BATNA Framework
definition: Best Alternative to a Negotiated Agreement; a counter-anchor that establishes your walk-away standard and determines leverage in any negotiation.

name: Five Leverage Sources in Negotiation
definition: Five domains where BATNA creates negotiating power: personal purchasing (dating/relationships), inventory sales, employment, vendor relationships, and partnership/business acquisition.

name: Close Rate to Pricing Ladder
definition: A tiered mapping of close rates (sales conversion percentages) to pricing multipliers that determines how much a business is underpriced relative to its market-clearing price point.

name: Daily Sales Training Cadence
definition: A 30-minute daily training block scheduled at the lowest-probability sales hour, covering a rotating weekly script section (intro/discovery/pitch/close Mon-Thu, hot topic Fri), with manager modeling followed by paired role-play.

name: Three-Part One-on-One Structure
definition: Weekly manager-rep one-on-one split into personal check-in, short-term quota and call review, and long-term career development — in that sequence and skipping later sections only when earlier ones reveal critical issues.

name: Bimodal Sales Career Ladder
definition: A six-level career progression (junior setter -> setter -> senior setter -> junior closer -> closer -> senior closer) that gives reps incremental title, pay, and perk milestones tied to gross output rather than tenure.

name: Three-Milestone Sales On-Ramp
definition: New talking-role hires must sequentially pass: (1) full script memorization, (2) recap/labeling skill, and (3) close and objection handling — each gated by a manager test before the next phase unlocks.

name: Blackout Script Memorization Method
definition: Print two copies of the script; say it aloud, black out one word, say it again — repeat until the entire script is blacked out. The number of words equals the number of repetitions.

name: Core Four Advertising Methods
definition: Four fundamental channels for customer acquisition: outreach (direct), paid ads, content, and affiliate outreach.

name: Two Windows of Buyer Readiness
definition: Buyers fall into two distinct windows: immediate-pain buyers ready today, and long-term nurture buyers who become ready over 24-36 months as you stay present.

name: Outbound as Long-Term Nurture Motion
definition: Outbound sales seeds the market initially; most converts into long-term nurture (email, retargeting, content) that keeps the seller top-of-mind when the buyer's pain becomes urgent.

name: Dual-Column Career Pathing
definition: A career progression structure with two parallel advancement tracks—title/perks and compensation—where employees alternate between rank increases and pay raises, creating multiple micro-progressions within a role.

name: Certification-Gated Skill Advancement
definition: In-house mini-certifications gate access to higher-value work; each certification unlocks new procedures or tasks, increases billable rate, and signals progress to the employee.

name: Future-Talk vs. Past-Talk Friend Filter
definition: Distinguish between growth-oriented peers and stagnant relationships by observing whether they discuss only past achievements or also engage with future possibilities.

name: Court-Filter Observable Language
definition: Replace interpretive claims (intentions, motivations, feelings) with only court-admissible facts (what was said, what occurred) to reduce noise and increase clarity in interpersonal navigation.

name: Label-Breaking Identity Loop
definition: Actively resist and contradict labels that others place on you because repeated labeling becomes self-reinforcing behavior, constraining your actual capacity to change.

name: Opportunity Downsides Visualization
definition: A four-stage visual framework for understanding opportunity cost: uninformed optimism, informed pessimism, despair, and upside achievement; most people quit at the despair stage.

name: Declarative vs. Procedural Knowledge
definition: Two distinct knowledge types: knowing about something (declarative) versus knowing how to do it (procedural); watching videos provides declarative knowledge while only doing provides procedural mastery.

name: Difficulty Paradox
definition: Hard situations have only three possible outcomes: you quit, it gets easier, or you get better; difficulty always ends, making persistence mathematically guaranteed to succeed.

name: Proof vs Pudding Framework
definition: The sequence in which trustworthiness is built: proof (demonstrated results and actions) must precede likeability and credibility; most entrepreneurs reverse this order.

name: Visible Output vs Hidden Input Model
definition: The gap between what observers see (a moment of apparent overnight success) and what actually occurred (years of inputs); modeling the output instead of the inputs is why replication fails.

name: CLOSER Framework
definition: A six-step sales conversation acronym (Clarify, Label, Overview, Sell, Explain, Reinforce) guiding a prospect from initial engagement through objection handling to post-purchase reinforcement.

name: Core Four Lead Generation Methods
definition: The four and only four actions a single person can take to generate leads: warm outreach (1-to-1, known contacts), cold outreach (1-to-1, strangers), paid ads (1-to-many, paid), and content posting (1-to-many, organic).

name: Rule of 100
definition: A minimum daily volume standard: 100 minutes of content posting, $100 in ad spend, or 100 outreach contacts per day to generate sufficient data and momentum for consistent sales.

name: Affiliate Activation Framework
definition: Four pillars required for affiliate success: exceptional product quality, low friction, aligned incentive structure, and optimal timing for asking for the referral.

name: Referral-Upsell Timing Decision
definition: A moment-based framework for choosing between asking for a referral or upsell based on whether the customer is satisfied-but-not-deprived (referral moment) or deprived (upsell moment).

name: Value Equation for Affiliate Growth
definition: The framework that models affiliate activation through ease, speed, low risk, and deprivation timing as components of perceived value.

name: Three Vectors of Commoditized Business Differentiation
definition: A diagnostic framework identifying three axes on which any commoditized business can win: risk reduction (brand reputation, guarantees), speed (faster delivery or access), and ease (frictionless client experience). Applied by Alex Hormozi specifically to home services businesses where commoditization is structural.

name: Scale Zero Before Expansion
definition: A sequencing rule requiring a business owner to fully remove themselves from day-to-day operations of a single unit (achieving scale zero) before opening additional locations. Violating this sequence predictably causes revenue decline at the original unit and underperformance at the new one.

name: Five Directions of Market Expansion
definition: Five vectors for growing a business: moving upmarket to larger customers, downmarket to smaller customers, adjacent to related industries, broader into wider categories, or narrower into more specific niches.

name: Puddle-to-Ocean Growth Progression
definition: A staged scaling model where a business progresses from niche mastery (puddle) through expanding market sizes (pond, lake) to open-market competition (ocean), directly correlated with accumulated skill and experience.

name: Elon Algorithm
definition: A five-step operational algorithm: (1) question all requirements, (2) delete unnecessary requirements, (3) optimize what remains, (4) accelerate, (5) automate.

name: Role-Based vs. Workflow-Based Hiring
definition: Replace org-chart role-slot thinking with workflow-first thinking: map the six or seven discrete input-output workflows a position plugs into, then determine which of those workflows can be partially or fully automated before hiring.

name: Roles-to-Workflows Decomposition
definition: Replace role-based hiring decisions with workflow-level automation: decompose every role into its constituent atomic tasks, map them into linear workflows, then assign AI agents to individual task nodes rather than hiring humans into roles.

name: AI Training Parity with Human Onboarding
definition: Train AI agents using the same granular, observable-behavior specification required to onboard a junior employee: break tasks into discrete micro-steps, eliminate vague language, and iterate the prompt the same way you would update a human training document.

name: Video Production Workflow Decomposition
definition: A systematic decomposition of video creation into granular task-level workflows (idea research → ranking → cross-listing → scripting → outlining → packaging) that can be automated or delegated.

name: Directive Specificity as Talent Indicator
definition: A framework for evaluating an employee's capability level by observing the level of specificity required in job directives, from high-level objectives (executive) to granular instructions (individual contributor).

name: Talent Tier Progression
definition: A salary-based framework showing how each incremental hire reveals a new level of capability, with the gap between tiers representing a distinct quality jump.

name: Marathon Winning Framework
definition: Success is only visible at the finish line; the middle (where consistency happens) is invisible to observers and receives no social validation.

name: Capital Redeployment for Constraint Relief
definition: When acquiring a capability is more efficient than building it, deploy capital directly to acquire top talent from that domain rather than acquiring the whole company.

name: Developer Vertical Integration Options
definition: Three pathways to solve land-development bottleneck: hire developer talent away, acquire a developer company outright, or acquire developer and convert to earn-out structure.

name: Front Door Linear Funnel
definition: A straight-line offer architecture with three doors (front-end offer, mid-tier, back-end/ascension) where front-end leads become the lead pool for ascension, handled by two or three top closers.

name: Prune-Then-Scale Sequence
definition: A two-step growth sequence: first eliminate low-margin, low-retention avatars to fix the model; second diagnose and remove what prevents selling 10x more of the single best avatar.

name: Service Business Margin Compression Cycle
definition: As service businesses hire leadership and fulfillment teams to scale beyond founder-dependent operations, profit margins compress despite revenue growth until service focus and pricing tighten around a profitable avatar.

name: Service Business Scaling Path
definition: Service businesses scale by narrowing to an ideal customer profile (ICP), increasing price through reputation and supply constraint, and then automating or templetizing work to expand margin.

name: Perceived Crisis vs. Real Metrics
definition: A diagnostic framework that separates narrative-driven concerns (market disruption, technological threat) from actual operational metrics (churn rate, unit economics).

name: Proof-Promise-Plan-Pain Introduction Framework
definition: A four-element video introduction structure where each of the four Ps (Proof, Promise, Plan, Pain) is addressed with at least one sentence, providing viewers with a visual and verbal roadmap of what they will get.

name: Sales Director Economics
definition: The unit-economics model where each sales director investment is evaluated by acquisition cost versus lifetime gross profit contribution, driving hiring velocity decisions.

name: Multi-Career Risk-Benefit Framework
definition: A decision framework for evaluating the trade-off between a stable, meaningful secondary job and a higher-revenue primary business, balanced against family and personal fulfillment.

name: Hybrid Model (1.0 / 2.0 Transition)
definition: A two-phase transition from in-person to online business: 1.0 keeps in-person sales while shifting delivery to remote; 2.0 makes both acquisition and delivery fully remote.

name: Coal Fire Relationship Model
definition: A relationship anchored in mutual respect and shared decision-making where disagreements surface from information asymmetry rather than conflicting values; initial response to disagreement is curiosity about missing information.

name: Cart Close Sequencing for Membership Launch
definition: A two-phase launch strategy that maximizes annual prepayment by closing the annual tier with exclusive bonuses first, then reopening with monthly-only option at lower value.

name: Physical Product Premium Bundle
definition: Bundling a tangible product (e.g., printer, paper kit) with a digital membership to increase conversion willingness and justify higher price points to end users.

name: Executive Vetting for High-Touch Roles
definition: A multi-stage approach to hiring senior executives that includes pre-employment relationship building, regular dialogue, and assessment across different conditions to evaluate true capability and fit before the role officially begins.

name: 10-Stage Scaling Roadmap
definition: A predictable progression from zero to 100M+ revenue with eight functions per stage, identifying constraints, symptoms, and graduation steps repeated across software, physical products, services, and brick-and-mortar.

name: Talent ROI Framework
definition: Calculate hiring investment by converting annual gross profit per specialized role into lifetime value, then benchmark recruitment spend as a percentage of that lifetime gross profit to determine hiring budget.

name: Talent Acquisition by Seniority
definition: A three-tier framework for hiring based on level: top-tier via headhunting/direct outreach, mid-tier via ads, bottom-tier via ads.

name: Club-Based Tournament Model
definition: A revenue model where tournaments are set up via local soccer-club partnerships; clubs provide fields and marketing, the operator handles everything else including team registration and tournament logistics.

name: National Scalable Tournament Operations
definition: A structure where a single operator runs tournaments at scale (1000+/year) by partnering with clubs in multiple geographies rather than owning fields or operating single locations.

name: Predictive Data Framework
definition: Systematic tracking and analysis of performance metrics across partner products to reduce revenue volatility and improve negotiation leverage.

name: Ambassador Program Model
definition: A two-tier distribution system where micro/nano creators both sell their own branded drops and promote premium licensed IP across multiple weekly releases.

name: Eugene Schwartz Awareness Ladder
definition: A five-level hierarchy of prospect awareness (Unaware, Problem Aware, Solution Aware, Product Aware, Most Aware) that determines what hook and click journey a paid ad must use; colder audiences at higher levels require bridge pages before reaching a sales page.

name: Buy vs. Build Talent Decision
definition: A two-option framework for acquiring skill-intensive talent: buy (hire proven performers at higher cost and speed) or build (recruit raw talent with trainable soft skills at lower cost and longer timeline). Choice depends on capital availability and urgency.

name: Amazon Channel Scaling Decision Tree
definition: Four-phase diagnostic to determine whether a product's scaling constraint is the channel saturation, product quality, or adjacent distribution; distinguishes between buying more impressions vs. entering new channels.

name: Outbound vs. Inbound Sales Team Separation
definition: Structurally separate door-knocking (outbound) and lead-fed (inbound) sales teams to prevent lazy skill atrophy and enable high-velocity close-rate optimization.

name: Sales Career Progression as Graduation Path
definition: High-performing outbound salespeople graduate to inbound lead-fed work as a promotion tier, with higher-volume, lower-commission rates offset by reliability and reduced stress.

name: Expectation-Reality Reframing
definition: A mental model where life satisfaction is anchored to expectations rather than absolute outcomes; shifting expectations downward increases contentment with the same reality.

name: $100 Million Scaling Roadmap
definition: A 10-stage framework mapping business growth milestones and identifying common bottlenecks across portfolio companies, with stage-specific priorities for product, marketing, sales, customer success, recruiting, IT, HR, and finance.

name: Hourly-Rate Purchase Test
definition: Evaluate any purchase by converting its cost into work hours at your post-tax hourly rate, then ask: would I voluntarily work those hours just to acquire this item?

name: Transition Between Groups
definition: Exceptionalism requires leaving the in-group temporarily; reframing this as a transition period rather than permanent rejection reduces shame and enables high output during the lonely chapter.

name: Friendship Filtering by Goal Alignment
definition: Evaluate every relationship by asking whether that person's presence makes goal achievement more or less likely; remove people who accept you as-is in favor of those who force growth.

name: Ten-Stage Scaling Roadmap
definition: A structured progression from zero to $100M+ revenue, broken across eight business functions with identified constraints, symptoms, and graduation steps.

name: Zero-to-$100M Stage Roadmap
definition: A 10-stage roadmap from zero to $100M+ in revenue, broken down by eight business functions per stage, covering symptoms of each constraint and the steps taken to graduate through it, validated across software, physical products, service businesses, and brick-and-mortar.

name: Minority Ownership Investment Model for Service Businesses
definition: An investment structure where the operator takes a minority stake in existing practices to help them grow and sell rather than purchasing majority control.

name: Education vs Recurring Product Distinction
definition: Separate education (one-time, consumable) from community and services (recurring); each has different billing and value durability across time.

name: Consumable vs One-Time Product Segmentation
definition: Products split into consumables (recurring value, lower price, month-over-month) and one-time learnings (higher price upfront, zero repeat value).

name: Tell Them What They Want vs. Tell Them What I Think
definition: A binary advisor-framing choice: assume the questioner's position and advise accordingly, OR give honest assessment regardless of emotional outcome. Hormozi explicitly offers both paths before proceeding with the honest one.

name: Management by Walking Around
definition: A leadership practice of physically moving through the organization to observe operations, feel team energy, and make spontaneous relationship-building interactions.

name: Unstructured Learning in Early Career
definition: Informal knowledge acquisition that occurs through proximity to colleagues in different functions, inaccessible in remote-only environments.

name: Growth-Risk Trade-off Framework
definition: Every percentage point of margin given up to accelerate growth is recaptured through faster revenue growth, but at the cost of increased business risk and reputational vulnerability.

name: Keith Cunningham Risk Filter
definition: A decision framework with three components: what is the upside, what is the downside, and can I live with the downside—proceed only if you can accept the downside.

name: Cash Flow Acceleration Paths
definition: Two primary methods to accelerate cash flow in recurring revenue models: (1) require upfront payment with credit toward service, or (2) raise equity capital to fund faster hiring and onboarding.

name: Transition-to-Group-Delivery Model
definition: A scaling strategy that migrates a service business from 1-on-1 calls through semi-private group formats (6-7 participants) before consolidating into full group delivery while maintaining original price point.

name: Productization Through 1-on-1 Mastery
definition: Using year-long 1-on-1 delivery as the research phase to identify core problems and solutions, then systematizing those learnings into scalable product formats.

name: Rejecting Societal Shoulds
definition: A framework for personal decision-making that dismisses externally-imposed expectations ('shoulds') and replaces them with authentic desire and observable outcomes as decision criteria.

name: Work-as-Reinforcement Model
definition: A framework where continued work effort is justified by ongoing intrinsic reinforcement and cessation occurs naturally when reinforcement diminishes, rather than by external balance prescriptions.

name: Judgment-Casting as Ego Defense
definition: A framework explaining how people who judge others' life choices (as unbalanced, unhealthy, etc.) are often defending against their own perceived inadequacy relative to those outcomes.
concept: Shame vs. Guilt: Navigating Social Signals

name: Work Motivation Volume Map
definition: A framework that segments work into phases: excitement (low work), neutrality-to-stress (work begins), and sustained push past motivation-fade (champions' work).

name: Glass Timeline Model
definition: A mental model visualizing the early phase of entrepreneurial effort as pulling a timeline of life toward you: it starts as glass (painful), gradually becomes less coarse, then neutral, then progressively sweeter — you must get through the glass period to reach the compounding benefits.

name: Performer Archetypes
definition: Three tiers of operator behavior: many who do nothing, optimizers who extract maximum value with minimum input, and maximizers who pursue diminishing returns because the difference between 1st and 2nd place is material.

name: 20-Hour Competence
definition: Most people can achieve functional competence in any skill, including money-making skills, within 20 hours of deliberate practice, provided they delay initial quitting and extend the threshold before declaring something hard.

name: Infinite vs Finite Game Frame
definition: Entrepreneurship is fundamentally an infinite game where persistence and not quitting are the winning conditions, not being the best at any single moment.

name: Work Ethic as Currency
definition: Work ethic is the primary currency of respect across all human societies; respect is earned exclusively through demonstrated action and contribution, not desire, intention, or effort level.

name: Early-Stage Resource Scarcity as Hardship Baseline
definition: The belief that early-stage entrepreneurship is the absolute hardest period because founders have minimal resources (time, money, leverage) and must personally execute every critical function.

name: Skill Accumulation as Implicit Portfolio
definition: Early-stage experiences that appear meaningless accumulate as contextual advantages (hidden arrows in the quiver) that become asymmetric advantages when solving larger problems at scale.

name: Three Levels Before First Dollar
definition: Three prerequisite mental models that must be internalized before earning the first dollar: ownership (it's my fault), resourcefulness (use what you have), and incremental thinking (focus on next step, not 100 steps).

name: Pain-Driven Change Framework
definition: Change occurs when the pain of changing becomes less than the pain of staying the same; future-pacing (vividly imagining future pain) is the mechanism to increase discomfort with the status quo and trigger action.

name: Stone Cutter Parable
definition: A framework for reframing identical work through three different perspectives: pain-focused, family-focused, and purpose-focused — demonstrating that outlook determines bearability.

name: Time Bifurcation Model
definition: Allocating daily time into two blocks: high-intensity focus on one core skill (sales, 8-10 hours), and secondary learning/entrepreneurship (5 a.m.-9 a.m., 5 p.m.-9 p.m.) plus weekends.

name: Ten Stage Revenue Roadmap
definition: A scaling framework outlining predictable stages from zero to $100M+ revenue, broken down by eight business functions and symptoms at each stage.

name: Elon's Algorithm
definition: A five-step process applied at SpaceX to fix any system: (1) question the requirements, (2) delete all unnecessary or dumb rules and requirements, (3) optimize, (4) accelerate timelines, (5) automate. Steps must be executed in order.

name: One-Issue-Per-Week Meeting Cadence
definition: A weekly cadence in which the leader sits with each team member in a 5-15 minute meeting, asks for their single most important issue, and helps them solve it — continuously removing constraints across all levels of the org.

name: Free Training Project Model
definition: A pre-launch proof-accumulation strategy where the founder delivers full service in exchange for a charitable donation (not payment to themselves) and a testimonial/before-after right, building social proof without the awkwardness of early selling.

name: Content Authenticity Hierarchy
definition: Content value axis: edited/AI-generated content (lowest authenticity, controllable) → live streaming (highest authenticity, uneditable, unscalable by automation).

name: Live Stream Content Extraction Strategy
definition: Structure live IRL streams to yield both long-form raw content and extractable short-form clips, multiplying surface area without additional production work.

name: Finite vs Infinite Game Framework
definition: Strategic positioning as either winning a bounded game (known players, rules, endpoint) or keeping an ongoing game alive (no endpoint, infinite players).

name: Three Traits of Hyper-Successful People
definition: Cognitive and personality cluster combining grandiose vision (superiority complex), crippling insecurity (fear of insufficiency), and strong impulse control (focus without distraction).

name: Friend Impact Assessment
definition: A binary framework for evaluating whether a friend increases or decreases your probability of achieving your goal, with no middle ground.

name: Social Consequence Framework
definition: The recognition that social obligations are actually social consequences, and avoiding social punishment often aligns outcomes with your goals.

name: Free-to-Paid Conversion Mechanisms
definition: Three structured pathways to convert free community members into paid offerings: onboarding sales calls, self-serve course progression through a video sales letter structure, and recurring group calls with soft CTAs.

name: 10-Stage Revenue Scaling Roadmap
definition: A structured progression from zero to $100M+ revenue with eight business functions mapped across all stages, including constraint diagnosis, symptom identification, and proven graduation steps applicable across software, physical products, services, and brick-and-mortar.

name: Business Diversification Trade-Off Model
definition: A mental model contrasting the benefits of singular focus (potential to maximize one business) against the breadth benefits of diversification (accumulated knowledge, brand credibility, risk distribution).

name: Investor Regret Loop
definition: The psychological cycle where investors undervalue a company, later see it succeed at higher valuation, experience regret, and then refuse to invest at the higher price to avoid shame, hoping the company fails instead to retroactively justify their earlier decision.

name: Life Game vs. Business Game Framework
definition: Business success is one game within the larger context of the life game; winning at life requires balancing multiple domains (business, health, relationships) rather than optimizing only for business outcomes.

name: Financial Freedom Definition Model
definition: Determining a personal financial freedom number (the point at which incremental money produces no behavioral or life improvement) and recognizing when that threshold is reached, rather than pursuing unlimited wealth.

name: Behavioral Definition Framework
definition: A method for making abstract concepts operationally precise by translating emotional language into observable, measurable behaviors that any external observer could verify.

name: Subjective Well-Being Scaling via Meditation
definition: Sustained meditation practice (4 hours daily) can shift baseline happiness (subjective well-being median) by 3-4 standard deviations, replicating the neurological and psychological baseline of advanced meditation practitioners with 40,000+ hours of practice.

name: Sacrifice Pattern in Goal Pursuit
definition: People sacrifice their primary desired state (happiness) to achieve instrumental goals (success); retrospectively, they realize external achievements alone do not fill the internal void, but cannot know this truth until they have achieved those goals.

name: Hard Work as the Goal
definition: A life thesis in which working hard is the terminal objective, not an instrument to a future state; combined with doing things worth doing, it resolves the destination-driven trap.

name: Days-in-a-Row Happiness Operationalization
definition: A practical method for approximating happiness: identify what a good day looks like and maximize the count of consecutive good days rather than chasing happiness as an abstract state.

name: The Paranoid Survive Principle
definition: A competitive mindset where you assume competitors have unknown capabilities and you are always the underdog, regardless of apparent market position.

name: Volume-Times-Feedback Loop
definition: Skill development rate equals number of repetitions multiplied by the quality of self-correction between repetitions; brute volume without feedback produces stagnation.

name: Patient-Output / Impatient-Input Framework
definition: Patience means finding something productive to do while waiting for lagging outputs; impatience means executing the input actions now. Use action as a coping mechanism for impatience with outcomes.

name: Return on Time Framework
definition: Replace the passive/active income binary with a spectrum measured by return on time (dollars per hour); evaluate activities by their hourly rate relative to personal average.

name: $100 Million Scaling Roadmap
definition: A 10-stage diagnostic framework covering business functions (product, marketing, sales, customer success, recruiting, IT, HR, finance) that identifies where a company is stuck and prescribes next actions.

name: Freedom vs. Optionality Model
definition: The shift from passive freedom (all time back but no engagement) to active optionality (choice to engage in meaningful work), achieved through building capital and systems that create choice rather than forced outsourcing.

name: Wealth Spending Archetypes
definition: Four distinct spending profiles that reveal personal values and trajectory: rich people prioritize time, poor people buy stuff for status, ambitious people buy skills, lazy people buy distraction.

name: Identity-Spending Alignment
definition: Personal identity shifts require congruent spending and calendar allocation; misalignment between stated goals and actual budget/calendar reveals the true identity being formed.

name: Extended Marshmallow Test
definition: A three-variable test of time-horizon and delayed gratification where the threshold window (waiting period for reward) is extended beyond standard 15-30 minute intervals to months or years, revealing true long-term orientation.

name: 10-Stage Business Growth Roadmap
definition: A structured progression from zero to $100M+ revenue with predictable stages defined by headcount increases, business function constraints, and symptom patterns; validated across software, physical products, services, and brick-and-mortar verticals.

name: Learning vs. Earning Trade-Off Decision Matrix
definition: A career-stage decision framework contrasting short-term income maximization against long-term skill-building and optionality, anchored to clarity on long-term goals and market feedback.

name: Owner-Operator vs. Subcontractor Trade-Offs Matrix
definition: A decision framework weighing control/loyalty (owner-operator) against complexity/scaling challenges (subcontractor), anchored to the founder's personal goals and speed-to-scale requirements.

name: 10-Stage Business Growth Roadmap (Zero to $100M+)
definition: A stage-gate model identifying predictable constraint transitions as headcount increases, with 8 functional breakpoints and graduation criteria across software, physical products, service businesses, and brick-and-mortar.

name: Founder Dependency vs. Scalable Ownership
definition: Two business models with identical $10M revenue and $2M profit yield drastically different wealth outcomes: founder-dependent (high hours, slow wealth accumulation) vs. scalable (founder-free, business valued at multiple of profit).

name: Delegation Sequence: Inventory, Process, People
definition: Transform founder dependency through: (1) self-inventory and time study documenting all tasks, (2) classify each task as green/yellow/red (delegable/installable/unfillable), (3) install green tasks first, yellow second, red last.

name: The Suffering Reality vs Motivation Manifesto
definition: Instagram motivation romanticizes hardship as a short, inspiring arc (Rocky's 30-second training montage) when the lived reality is years of unglamorous, grinding suffering—different from the cultural narrative.

name: Commitment to Action Over Outcome
definition: When conviction about winning is absent, the only sustainable commitment is to controllable actions and refusal to quit, not to outcomes or timeline.

name: Market Penetration Math for Content Strategy
definition: A mathematical framework for calculating the addressable audience size at each business-scale threshold, used to set realistic view-count expectations and evaluate content ROI.

name: Social vs Interest Media
definition: A content strategy model where social media primarily displays content to interest-aligned audiences rather than social-graph-based distribution, making content itself the targeting mechanism.

name: Scaling Roadmap Stages
definition: A 10-stage growth model documenting the predictable progression, stall points, and breakthrough solutions across product, marketing, sales, customer success, recruiting, IT, HR, and finance functions.

name: Service vs. Scalable Business Model Selection
definition: A framework for choosing between targeting upmarket with service-based delivery or targeting masses with capital-intensive scalable products, based on founder capital and skill constraints.

name: Decision Under Uncertainty vs. Risk
definition: When facing a major decision, emotional consistency (refusing self-rejection) overrides rational risk calculation; the willingness to accept external rejection rather than self-betrayal is the primary motive force.

name: The Reinforcement Cycle of Identity Through Consistency
definition: Repeated behavioral consistency under adversity creates a reputation for resilience, which others reinforce through labels and expectations, which further hardens the identity through confirmatory behavior.

name: Legacy Framing Through End-of-Life Reversal
definition: Starting decision-making from the end (what people will remember at your funeral) and working backward reveals that only behavior toward others and relational impact matter; material outcomes are forgotten.

name: 10-Stage Roadmap to 100 Million+
definition: A structured 10-stage growth progression from zero to $100M+ revenue, with eight business functions tracked across stages, stage-specific constraint symptoms, and graduation requirements.

name: Behavior-Based Intelligence and Learning
definition: Intelligence is rate of learning; learning is change in behavior under constant conditions; both become measurable and controllable through behavioral definition rather than thought/identity.

name: The Reason Close
definition: A sales and self-persuasion technique where objections become the argument for action: reframe each stated reason as the precise reason the person should proceed.

name: Exploration-to-Exploitation Transition
definition: A two-phase lifecycle where the exploration phase involves broad experimentation across many opportunities (5 years typical), and the exploitation phase involves deep focus on a single proven strength after discovery is complete.

name: Work Before Networking Hierarchy
definition: A decision framework for choosing between execution and relationship-building activities, prioritizing completed work over connection-gathering because work outcomes enable future network access that low-status individuals cannot achieve.

name: Seasonal Friendship Model
definition: A relationship-lifecycle model where close circles are small, relationships are season-specific, and objective-change justifies relationship dissolution without guilt, enabling capital reallocation to higher-alignment relationships.

name: Logic-Evidence-Utility Framework
definition: A three-step diagnostic for unpacking vague self-narratives: (1) Logic — define the claim in observable behavioral terms; (2) Evidence — audit how many times the behavior actually occurred; (3) Utility — ask who cares and why it matters relative to your goals.

name: Framework: The Hard Difficulty Taxonomy
definition: A multi-dimensional categorization of hardship types (sacrifice, effort, risk, uncertainty) rather than treating hardship as a monolithic experience.

name: Foundation Model of Success
definition: Personal responsibility forms the foundational layer on which all other business and personal achievements must rest; without it, all higher-level tactics collapse.

name: Barbell Hiring Strategy
definition: A hiring approach that pairs young, growth-oriented employees with experienced senior talent, explicitly avoiding middle-career employees with conditional commitment.

name: Four Rs Customer Progression
definition: Four sequential milestones that define customer success: retention, review, referral, and resale.

name: Five Stages of Business Scaling
definition: A five-stage model describing the predictable evolution of a business from solo founder through legacy stage: Treadmill → Trailblazer → Pathfinder → legacy, each requiring different operational and strategic approaches.

name: Six Drivers of Business Growth
definition: Six interlocking operational levers (personal growth, purpose, people, profit, planning, and cyclical iteration) that recur across all five scaling stages and must be refined at each stage.

name: On-Time On-Budget Guarantee for Home Builders
definition: A contract structure where the builder guarantees project completion within timeline and budget, with the guarantee enforced by a contingent profit-sharing clause and a constraint that prevents scope creep.

name: ROI Evaluation of Talent Investment
definition: A capital-allocation framework that evaluates hiring decisions by comparing annual gross profit generated per hire to upfront recruitment investment, yielding an ROI ratio that justifies premium recruitment spend.

name: Founder Depth as Talent Magnet
definition: A mechanism where founder mastery in core functions creates organizational brand strength sufficient to attract A-player talent, enabling leverage through delegation rather than constraint.

name: Solomon Framework
definition: A weekly self-advisory practice in which the practitioner simulates conversation with their 85-year-old future self (named Solomon) to obtain advice that satisfies all three criteria for good counsel: competence, context, and alignment.

name: Three Criteria for Good Advice
definition: Any advice source must simultaneously satisfy competence (knowing the domain), context (knowing your specific situation), and alignment (having incentives that match yours); failure on any one criterion compromises the quality of guidance received.

name: Agency Model Opportunity Arc
definition: Agencies have historically been low-stickiness, high-competition commodity businesses; AI automation now enables margin compression and task automation that creates 1-2 year first-mover advantage before commoditization.

name: Four Stickiness Determinants
definition: Business stickiness is determined by switching cost, perceived uniqueness, operational difficulty, and availability of substitutes; agencies fail on all four, making them historically unprofitable despite constant demand.

name: First-Time vs. Third-Time Founder Information Asymmetry
definition: First-time founders withhold information (requiring NDAs) due to idea protection anxiety, while experienced founders share everything transparently, reducing investor perception of risk.

name: Beginner vs. Expert Problem-Solving Framework
definition: Beginners apply binary thinking (this worked or didn't) and pivot ideas entirely; experts break failures into component parts and iterate on specific levers.

name: Heroes vs. Villains Archetype
definition: Both heroes and villains share the same painful backstory; the distinction lies in how they choose to respond to that pain.

name: Documentary Proof Through Struggle
definition: Capturing and retaining documentation of the hardest periods in business and life, because those moments become the evidence of character and resilience that future selves draw upon.

name: The Entrepreneurship Life Cycle
definition: Six-stage emotional and operational arc: uninformed optimism, informed pessimism, crisis of meaning (the split), then either restart the cycle or progress to informed optimism and achievement.

name: Iterative Volume Skill Development
definition: Master any skill by executing high-volume repetitions, extracting the top 10% of attempts, identifying their differentiating factors, and incorporating those factors into the next round of volume.

name: First Principles vs Mastery Illusion
definition: The gap between conceptual understanding and skill mastery; understanding simple addition does not mean you can execute it, and ignoring foundational skills to pursue complex ones ensures failure.

name: Delayed Gratification vs Delayed Pain
definition: Wealthy people trade immediate discomfort for future pleasure; poor people reverse the equation by taking pleasure now and deferring pain to later, then express surprise when the bill comes due.

name: Business Failure Modes by Revenue Trajectory
definition: Categorizes businesses into growth, plateau, and decline modes; each mode has distinct pain profiles and psychological sustainability dynamics that determine founder persistence.

name: Business-as-Vehicle Framework
definition: The business serves as a vehicle toward an external purpose (societal impact, personal development, solving a specific problem) rather than an end in itself; the vehicle must align with intrinsic motivation to sustain effort beyond financial thresholds.

name: Compounding Advantage Stacking
definition: Strategic elimination of habits that create two-day losses (drinking day + recovery day) and substitution with behavioral anchors that compound incrementally across career and life, creating durable competitive advantage through advantage stacking.

name: Humility vs Ego Dynamics in Growth
definition: Framework distinguishing ego-driven self-exaltation (short-term emotional benefit, long-term social liability) from humble self-positioning (short-term ego discomfort, long-term social capital and respect generation).

name: Leader-Driven Performance Diagnosis
definition: When a function underperforms, the leader is always the root cause, though the problem may involve both the leader and the inherited team.
concept: Leadership Sets Culture; Culture Determines Acceptable Effort

name: Leader Replacement vs. Team Recovery
definition: After removing a weak leader, the team's trajectory depends on whether the prior leader selected for low bar (both leader and team must be replaced) or whether the team retained quality (new leader can redirect quality talent).
concept: Leadership Sets Culture; Culture Determines Acceptable Effort

name: Three Levels of Wealth
definition: A three-tier hierarchy of wealth thresholds: (1) basic needs covered, (2) discretionary spending without stress, (3) luxury wealth (~$100k/month), each unlocking qualitatively different life optionality.
concept: Wealth Tiers and Diminishing Marginal Returns

name: Infinite Game Perspective
definition: A mindset that frames competition and business as a game whose only objective is to keep playing; winning is defined as continued participation, not finite endpoint achievement.

name: Keynesian Beauty Contest Social Behavior
definition: People optimize their self-presentation not for what they personally want to say, but for what they believe others want to hear knowing that others are doing the same, producing a recursive loop where nobody expresses their true position.

name: The 10-Year Million-Dollar Contract
definition: A mental commitment device where entrepreneurs visualize a 10-year wealth accumulation goal (adding one to three zeros to net worth), then work backward to identify necessary compound decisions and investments.

name: Entrepreneurial Seasons
definition: Multi-year phases (roughly 3-5 years each) in which a founder focuses on specific business challenges; seasons provide natural beginning-and-end boundaries that reduce decision weight and enable transitions.

name: Mission-Driven Business Purpose
definition: Businesses exist as vehicles to lend credence to books, lessons, and authentic stories that document and share best practices; the business itself is secondary to the knowledge transfer mission.

name: Three Types of Debt
definition: A classification of debt including financial debt, ignorance debt (knowledge and skills), and the cost of not learning.

name: Expert Definition Through Mistakes
definition: An expert is someone who has made all the mistakes possible in a narrow field; expertise is built by learning to lose first.

name: Content Friction Removal Model
definition: Content creates purchase intent when it removes friction from a person's life by identifying problems they face and providing depth—people save content they intend to use but cannot immediately execute.

name: 10-Stage Roadmap to $100M+
definition: A systematic progression through 10 growth stages with defined constraints, symptoms, and graduation steps, broken down by eight business functions (applicable across software, product, service, and retail).

name: On-Time On-Budget Guarantee Offer
definition: A home service pricing and closing strategy that raises prices 20% while guaranteeing delivery on time and under budget, contingent on no scope changes, and refunds the margin if guarantees are missed.

name: No-Change Contingency Protective Clause
definition: A pricing guarantee protection mechanism that explicitly conditions the offer on scope immutability, allowing the seller to renegotiate if the buyer modifies requirements mid-project.

name: Maintenance Plan Upsell with Review Incentive
definition: A continuity upsell strategy that bundles annual maintenance coverage at a fixed cost, covers repairs up to 2x the plan cost, and waives the fee in exchange for a five-star review and operator spiff.

name: Action-Leverage Inverse Relationship
definition: Early-stage founders must maximize volume of attempts to compensate for zero leverage; advanced operators minimize volume and rely on high-leverage decisions.

name: Deprivation-Motivation Model
definition: Motivation is directly proportional to perceived deprivation; changing behavior requires changing environment to create comparative deprivation and social feedback loops.

name: Patent Reality Framework
definition: Patents require continuous legal defense infrastructure and business success to be meaningful; a patent alone has no value without active enforcement and profitable underlying business.

name: 10-Stage Roadmap to 100M+
definition: A structured progression through ten predictable growth stages for scaling businesses, characterized by headcount transitions and changing constraints across eight business functions.

name: Quit Decision Framework
definition: A structured decision model for evaluating when to leave a job or quit a business based on financial readiness and goal alignment rather than difficulty.

name: Fear Specificity Model
definition: A mental model that resolves vague, amygdala-driven fears by decomposing them into specific, verifiable outcomes, engaging prefrontal cortex reasoning.

name: 20 Hour Competence
definition: Base competence in any skill, including money-making skills, is achievable in approximately 20 hours of deliberate practice; the delay before beginning is the primary obstacle most people face.

name: Habituation for Fear Mastery
definition: Systematic exposure to fear-inducing stimuli until the nervous system adapts and the stimulus no longer triggers an aversive response; the endpoint is practiced indifference, not belief-based confidence.

name: The Ladder Rung Model
definition: Focus requires consolidating all available effort into a single endeavor until critical mass is achieved; spreading effort across multiple projects prevents any from reaching the threshold for success.

name: The 10-Stage Roadmap (Zero to $100M+)
definition: A predictable progression of business stages indexed by headcount, with each stage carrying distinct constraints and symptoms; graduation requires removing the constraint via documented steps.

name: Hook Optimization Framework
definition: A three-layer content structure that leads with the widest emotional hook, followed by specific business application, then philosophical principle to maximize initial retention and downstream conversion.

name: Stoic Response to Insult
definition: A two-step framework for neutralizing insults: first determine if the insult contains truth; if yes, agree and one-up; if no, the agreement itself extinguishes the conflict by nullifying the attacker's intent.

name: Authenticity Through Secrets Elimination
definition: Reduce the gap between internal reality and external presentation by minimizing secrets; fewer back rooms mean more people see the true self, enabling genuine hate or like rather than reaction to a curated persona.

name: Free Trial Conversion Architecture
definition: A multi-stage analysis comparing free trial vs paid-first models across three vectors: landing page conversion, paid conversion rate, and post-trial churn.

name: Earnings-Per-Click Model
definition: A decision framework that factors clicks, conversion rate, customer LTV, and churn into a single unit-economics calculation to compare acquisition models.

name: Four Acquisition Targets Framework
definition: Acquisition.com targets four categories of high-cash-flow service businesses: e-learning businesses in niches, brick-and-mortar chains with multiple existing locations, tech-enabled services (SaaS or software-adjacent), and consumer experience businesses.

name: Photographer Studio Expansion Model
definition: A capital-deployment model where the parent company funds the opening of new studio locations while the founder focuses on replication of a proven experiential service delivery model, converting B2B coaching revenue into high-margin B2C location expansion.

name: Document-Demonstrate-Duplicate
definition: A three-step training method for transferring procedural knowledge: document the exact steps of a process while performing it, demonstrate the process by executing steps with explanation, then have the learner duplicate the process under observation until mastery.

name: Declarative vs. Procedural Knowledge
definition: Two distinct types of learnable knowledge: declarative knowledge (knowing that something exists, the unknown unknowns) versus procedural knowledge (knowing how to execute a task step-by-step).

name: Finite vs. Infinite Game Frame
definition: Two fundamentally different ways to approach endeavors: finite games have known players, agreed rules, and a defined win condition; infinite games have known and unknown players, no agreed rules, and the goal is continuation.

name: Character as the Only Keepable Asset
definition: The sole asset one retains across all endeavors is personal character; making character development the win condition enables perpetual success by decoupling from external validation.

name: Three Strategic Buckets
definition: Every business allocates resources into three categories: acquiring more customers, increasing customer lifetime value, and decreasing operational risk.

name: Five Levels of Friendship
definition: A hierarchy of friendship depth ranked by conversation topic: (1) past reminiscing, (2) gossip about others, (3) idea-sharing, (4) collaborative action, (5) making, losing, and spending money together.

name: Reactive Discounting Trap
definition: When a competitor undercuts on price or offer, a reactive price reduction to match them often fails to reduce churn or improve retention because the decision point has already passed.

name: Close Rate Pricing Guide
definition: A framework correlating observed close rates to price elasticity, using close rate as a proxy for whether pricing is below market-clearing and how much room for increase exists.

name: Tiered Pricing with Decreasing Marginal Rate
definition: A pricing structure with fixed base fee and watermarked tiers (e.g., $6k base, +5% above $20k spend, +2.5% above $100k) where higher tiers apply only incrementally, not retroactively.

name: Shame vs Guilt Model
definition: A two-part distinction where guilt is internal (breaking your own rules) and shame is external (breaking others' rules), with the power to choose whose rules to follow as the key lever.

name: Asymmetric Risk-Reward of Action
definition: When attempting any outcome with no downside below the current state, every attempt produces either a win (sale) or learning (experience), creating upside-only dynamics.

name: Fog Visibility Model
definition: Movement through uncertainty is only visible one step at a time; additional steps reveal as you walk, not before, eliminating the need to see the entire path in advance.

name: Culture as Rules and Reinforcement
definition: A system of spoken and unspoken conditional rules (if-then statements) that govern what behaviors are rewarded, punished, or ignored within an organization.

name: Values as Chunked Rules
definition: Condensing hundreds of behavioral rules into 3-5 value statements; each value, when unpacked, maps to a coherent set of conditionals that reinforce aligned behavior.

name: Context-Specific Rule Definition
definition: Identifying and codifying all behavioral rules within specific interaction contexts (meetings, client calls, decision-making) before generalizing to org-wide values.

name: Three Foundations for Escaping Poverty
definition: The foundational mindset pillars required to build wealth from zero: accept accountability (not external blame), spend less than you make, and reinvest all excess into income-generating activities.

name: Experience Points Model for Skill Building
definition: A mental model that reframes failed business experiments not as losses but as experience points accumulating toward the next skill level, with sufficient points enabling level-up to the next income tier.

name: Income Reinvestment Loop for Compounding
definition: A strategy of treating monthly income as potential energy rather than stored energy, reinvesting surplus back into income-generating activities to compound growth month-over-month.

name: Life Meaning as Learning Output
definition: The meaning of life is the aggregate output of experience—learning and behavioral change—which accumulates over time and constitutes the substance of a lived life.

name: Business Purpose as Output Mirror
definition: A business's meaning is equivalent to its output, which reflects its stated mission; Elon's Mars mission means the output is Mars-bound people.

name: Reinforcement-Based Culture Governance
definition: Culture is the sum of spoken and unspoken rules that govern organizational behavior through rewards and consequences; standardizing reinforcement across departments ensures culture scales consistently.

name: Continuous Talent Elevation
definition: Recruiting standards rise predictably with organizational revenue scale; as new tiers are reached, previously tolerable mediocrity becomes unacceptable, requiring continuous skill upgrade in recruiting itself.

name: Natural Skill as Unconscious Observational Learning
definition: A natural is someone who acquired skill not through deliberate study but through passive observation of rewarded behaviors in their environment, often in early childhood, without conscious intent to model.

name: Brand as Curated Garden
definition: Building brand by deliberately including only content and associations that reinforce a core identity, treating all non-aligned elements as weeds regardless of their intrinsic quality.

name: Compounding Customer Acquisition Through Product Delivery
definition: Creating a self-sustaining growth loop by prioritizing product delivery and reputation over constant customer acquisition, enabling repeat purchases and referrals.

name: Conditional Love Framework
definition: A relationship model grounded in explicit agreements around shared mission, values, and interests rather than unconditional commitment, with revisable terms when conditions change.

name: Calendar-Sync Reconnection Protocol
definition: A structured daily ritual where partners review their separate calendars for 45 minutes to exchange independent experiences and create surface area for conversation, avoiding over-togetherness.

name: Human-in-Loop LTV:CAC Scaling Ladder
definition: A four-rung target ratio framework (3:1, 6:1, 9:1, 12:1) that sets the required LTV-to-CAC minimum based on how many of three business stages (attraction, conversion, delivery) involve humans versus automated/scalable systems.

name: Attraction-Conversion-Delivery Scalability Spectrum
definition: A three-axis diagnostic that rates each of a business's three core stages (attraction, conversion, delivery) on a 0-to-1 scale of human involvement, where 0 = fully automated/scalable and 1 = fully human-dependent.

name: Four Components of Mental Toughness
definition: A structured model of mental toughness comprising power management, momentum control, fortitude, and adaptability as learnable behavioral skills rather than innate traits.

name: Decade Sustainability Test
definition: A heuristic for evaluating any diet or training protocol: if you cannot sustain it for ten years, it is not worth starting for a day.

name: Physics-First Nutrition Model
definition: Hormozi's simplification of nutrition to thermodynamic laws: calorie intake versus calorie expenditure determines body composition; macros (especially protein) and progressive overload determine muscle mass; everything else is preference.

name: Deal Variable Multiplication Framework
definition: A negotiation approach that breaks an offer into multiple independent dimensions (price, speed, ease, risk) to expand trading leverage while maintaining reciprocity.

name: Value Equation Framework
definition: A model organizing all variables in a transaction into four axes: speed (timeline), risk (who bears responsibility), ease (friction), and price, enabling flexible concessions without eroding value.

name: ROI Framing vs. Cost Framing
definition: A persuasion technique that repositions an expenditure from a cost center (overhead, expense) to an investment center (return-generating asset), increasing buyer conviction.

name: Value Equation
definition: A five-component model of value: latency (speed), ease (friction removal), consistency (perceived reliability), impact (customer meaningfulness), and risk (likelihood of achievement).

name: Skill Development Through Repetition and Feedback
definition: Skills compound through deliberate repetition with external feedback; the work changes the person (building skill) more than the person's output changes until sufficient skill is developed.

name: 10-Stage Roadmap to $100M+
definition: A structured progression through ten predictable stages of business growth (zero to $100M+), differentiated by headcount thresholds, with eight functional dimensions per stage showing constraint symptoms and graduation steps.

name: Four Pillars of Successful Entrepreneurship
definition: Four foundational qualities determine whether an entrepreneur succeeds: power to influence others, significant drive or motivation, impulse control to say no, and knowledge of input-output relationships.

name: The Quality Amplification Loop
definition: Superior product quality (achieved through deep time investment) generates organic referrals and word-of-mouth that compound over time, eliminating the need for future marketing spend.

name: Product Quality Effort Curve
definition: Each incremental quality improvement requires exponentially more effort; moving from 8.0 to 9.0 requires 10x the work, and 9.0 to 9.5 requires another 10x.

name: Special Projects Incubator (Shark Tank Model)
definition: A dedicated cross-functional team at Ramsey Solutions that handles two types of work: (1) broken existing business units that are missing budget/revenue targets, and (2) orphaned new ideas without a home, nurturing them from beta to either a standalone profit center or integration into an existing unit.

name: Beta-Then-Double-Down New Initiative Process
definition: Dave Ramsey's framework for evaluating new product ideas: run a beta test, measure ROAS, conversion rates, and margins, iterate the concept five to ten degrees before killing it, and only kill it when hope for scale or commensurate margins is lost. Ideas that survive are doubled down on.

name: 10-Stage Revenue Roadmap
definition: A progression from zero to $100M+ revenue with eight business functions tracked across each stage; each stage has distinct constraints and required changes to graduate.

name: Value Equation Framework
definition: A four-component model defining value as dream outcome minus time delay, effort burden, and probability of success.

name: Blame-Control Inversion
definition: What you blame external forces for is what you give them power over; shifting from blame to self-accountability transfers control to yourself.

name: Excuses as Power Transfer
definition: Using an excuse ("I can't do X because of Y") makes Y the entity controlling your life outcomes.

name: Four Dimensions of Equity
definition: Equity comprises four independent levers: risk (downside loss participation), decision-making power (control), profit sharing (cash flow participation), and sale value (exit proceeds). Decoupling these dimensions enables custom incentive structures without diluting ownership.

name: Profits Interest Structure
definition: A tax-efficient alternative to traditional equity that grants employees a percentage of company profits and/or sale proceeds, structured as a sale bonus rather than stock ownership, eliminating the need for employee cash outlay and avoiding immediate income taxation.

name: High-Frequency Low-Duration Training Protocol
definition: Six short training sessions per day (10 minutes each, spaced 45 minutes apart) distributed across a longer timeframe instead of consolidated volume, paired with high-carbohydrate low-fat nutrition to minimize fat storage during caloric surplus.

name: Logic-Evidence-Utility Framework
definition: A decision-filtering model: logic (what does it mean?), evidence (how do I know that?), utility (why should I care?). Only pursue questions or stressors that change behavior or outcomes.

name: Idea-First Content Strategy
definition: Content success prioritizes exceptional idea and personal interest (20% inspired moments) above production quality, headlines, and algorithmic optimization.

name: Depth-Over-Surface Framework
definition: Content expertise demonstrates by peeling back 2-3 layers to reveal ground-truth insights; surface-level understanding produces mediocre service-grade content, while deep thinking compounds through sustained problem time.

name: Creator Capacity and Creative Conditions
definition: Creative insights require excess capacity, sleep quality, eliminated friction, and unscheduled exploration time; structured posting cadences conflict with genuine interest-driven content moments.

name: Maker Mode Time Protection
definition: Protect 4-5 days per week with zero meetings to enable deep thinking; insights emerge from unstructured exploration and follow-through on sparks, not from scheduled meetings.

name: Founder Handoff Readiness
definition: A decision framework for determining when a founder should exit day-to-day operations based on profit available to absorb management salary and founder's alternative ROI on freed time.

name: Push vs Pivot Decision Framework
definition: Continue pushing on a business opportunity until a fundamental original assumption is proven false; if no core assumption is invalidated, the apparent losses are the cost of learning, not a signal to quit.

name: Earning vs Learning Framework
definition: Career decisions should be evaluated on two axes: are you earning sufficient income for your goal, and are you learning valuable skills that compound your earning potential?

name: Risk Ladder by Goal Size
definition: The acceptable personal risk ratio scales with goal magnitude; $1M goals can be achieved with minimal risk through known paths, while $100M+ goals require higher personal risk because fewer validated paths exist.

name: Give First, Get Later Content Flywheel
definition: Publish all business knowledge free and without paywalls to pre-deliver value before any commercial relationship begins, creating inbound pull from companies seeking help.

name: Two-Question Business Clarity
definition: Reduce any growth problem to two questions: (1) how do I get more customers? and (2) how do I make each customer worth more? Then map the eight acquisition methods to the first question.
concept: Undefined Words Create Mythology and Prevent Clear Thinking

name: The Impossible Choices Framework
definition: At each revenue stage, entrepreneurs face trade-offs between two painful paths (e.g., sacrifice profit for hiring or overwork to avoid the hire), both of which are necessary to break through constraints.

name: The Swamp Stage ($1-3M ARR)
definition: A predictable plateau where profit margins cannot sustain A-player hires, forcing founders to either sacrifice 100% of annual profit or work 6+ additional hours daily, creating perceived impossibility.

name: The Glass-Chewing Model
definition: A framework naming the non-obvious hardship of entrepreneurship: founders become filters for unsolvable problems, facing new sacrifices at every scale (risk, difficult conversations, legal issues, channel shifts).

name: Four Elements of Influence
definition: A four-component model explaining what drives audience compliance with creator directives: Likeness (demographic/values similarity), Credibility (say-do correspondence proven by results), Power (follower acts on a directive and gets a positive consequence), and Status (control over scarce reinforcers).
concept: Influence Measurement: Engagement Over Follower Count

name: Woman in the Red Dress Metaphor
definition: As one progresses, distractions become more attractive proportionally; distinguishing between genuine opportunities and seductive distractions requires clarity of vision to resist increasingly tempting deviations.

name: Work Periodization Framework
definition: Structuring work cycles (like athletic training) with alternating phases of maximum effort, preparation, and specialization, rather than maintaining constant intensity across all projects.

name: Hidden Shoulds Framework
definition: Unexamined beliefs we never think to question—the demands we place on the universe (life should be meaningful, I should be happy) that create internal gaps we can never close.

name: Goodwill Deposits vs. Right Hooks
definition: A content strategy that measures audience trust by the ratio of value-giving (deposits) to monetization asks (right hooks); sustained deposits enable outsized media revenue because the audience has accumulated goodwill to spend.

name: Book-as-Incentive Funnel
definition: A distribution mechanism where high-leverage entrepreneurs (with email lists) donate books in bulk, enabling free distribution to entrepreneurs without capital, while aggregating the audience and monetizing through subsequent sales.

name: $100 Million Scaling Roadmap
definition: A portfolio-derived diagnostic quiz spanning 10 growth stages with prescriptive guidance across 8 business functions (product, marketing, sales, customer success, recruiting, IT, HR, finance) to identify stage-specific constraints and solutions.

name: The 100 Golden BBs Framework
definition: Great products are built from hundreds of tiny improvements (golden BBs) rather than a single silver bullet; each detail compounds to create products people love.

name: Repetition Path to Masterpiece
definition: Mastery requires exponential repetition: 5 reps shows improvement, but 95 additional reps elevate work from great to masterpiece-level; the second 95 reps is where world-class emerges.

name: Making for Yourself vs Making for Everyone
definition: Best work comes from making something for yourself as the primary audience; thousands of people with identical problems discover and love it, whereas making for a generic audience produces mediocre work that solves no one's problems.

name: Luxury Allocation Framework
definition: Intentional spending on a high-value personal practice that requires no optimization or guilt, justified by accumulated wealth and its role as a daily anchor.

name: Reverse Role Model Framework
definition: Identify who you don't want to become, extract specific counterexamples from their behaviors, and use those negative way-markers to navigate toward your desired life.

name: Directional vs. Absolute Correctness
definition: When facing uncertainty and lacking perspective, bias toward taking action in roughly the right direction rather than waiting to identify the perfect path.

name: Cheese and Cat Metaphor
definition: Life presents rewards (cheese) and threats (cat); when uncertain about the target, move away from pain as a reliable initial direction-setter toward unknown rewards.

name: Two-Bucket Venture Investment Framework
definition: ACQ Ventures categorizes early-stage investment targets into two buckets: existing-round companies already familiar with the founder's methodology seeking capital partnership, and bootstrapped operators seeking funding without requiring active management involvement.

name: Founder Dependency Test
definition: A diagnostic framework distinguishing revenue businesses (work without founder) from founder-dependent income sources; wealth creation requires the former.

name: Creator Type Taxonomy
definition: Creators fall into distinct categories: words guys (audio/written content), video guys (visual content), and crossovers; each category has different conversion and audience dynamics.

name: Private Equity Plus Creator Model
definition: Combining traditional private equity value-creation (operational systems improvement) with creator/influencer leverage (attention and distribution) to scale portfolio companies.

name: Face-Driven to Faceless System Transition
definition: The operational challenge of converting a business that depends on the founder's personal presence into a system that runs independently; required for scaling beyond the founder's time capacity.

name: Happiness Paradox Framework
definition: Chasing happiness as a goal creates a distance between current and desired state, ensuring perpetual unhappiness; relinquishing the pursuit of happiness as a precondition allows enjoyment to emerge as a surprise.

name: Purpose vs Passion Model
definition: Purpose is intrinsic, stable, and independent of external validation; passion is fickle, external-dependent, and unreliable for sustaining long-term effort.

name: Memory Dividend Framework
definition: Short-term sacrifices compound into long-term joy through retrospective meaning-making; the momentary cost is exceeded many times over by the memory dividend of the accomplished outcome.

name: Business Overhead Cycle
definition: Recurring pattern where operational overhead (legal, admin, non-core work) grows disproportionately until deliberately restructured; each revenue stage triggers a new overhead expansion.

name: Gratitude as Recalibration
definition: Using negative experiences to recalibrate baseline expectations and increase genuine appreciation for existing conditions.

name: SPCL Framework
definition: A four-element content framework (Status, Proof, Credibility, Likability) that drives prospect compliance and outcome likelihood; raw, unscripted content (live streaming) maximizes SPCL delivery.

name: Being-Doing-Having Model
definition: A causal chain where being (identity) flows from doing (actions) rather than preceding it; having (results) follows from doing, making doing the primary lever for outcome control.

name: Offer Lifecycle and Market Saturation
definition: When an offer stops converting, the root cause is not market saturation but failure to deliver the promised value; the solution is execution excellence, not new product innovation.

name: AI Integration Strategy Choice
definition: Two distinct paths exist for AI adoption: augmenting an existing business model (AI-enhanced plumbing, AI-augmented coaching) versus building a pure-AI business; the latter carries higher risk because major AI vendors can commoditize pure-AI solutions within 6 months.

name: Information-Based Buyer Spectrum
definition: Buyers exist on a spectrum from low to high information rather than categorical emotional vs. logical types; all buyers move in one direction only (toward more information) and require enough data points to commit.

name: Advertising as Information Provision
definition: Advertising and outbound communication exist to provide enough information for a buyer to make a decision; the volume of information required is inversely proportional to brand strength.

name: Market Awareness Underestimation
definition: Founders systematically underestimate the effort and spending required to achieve meaningful market awareness, confusing advertising saturation with market saturation.

name: The Subconscious Voice Framework
definition: Decision paralysis stems from internalized external voices (not your own) that subconsciously control your choices; identifying and dismissing these voices unlocks decision-making velocity.

name: The Cost-of-Delay Analysis
definition: If you believe you will take an action sooner or later, the rational decision is to take it now to begin capturing benefits immediately rather than postponing.

name: Conquer City Before Country
definition: A sequential market expansion model: dominate the local city before pursuing national scale; early national expansion collapses like an overextended army.

name: Done-With-You vs Turnkey Tiering
definition: A two-tier offer structure for coaching or education businesses: a done-with-you tier (~$15k-$25k) for guided execution and a total-turnkey tier (~$100k) for full-service delivery; each tier targets a different buyer segment by budget and desired involvement.

name: Work = Volume × Leverage
definition: Output is the product of repetition volume and per-instance return; volume drives skill acquisition, which then increases leverage per instance, creating a compounding cycle.

name: Requisites-for-Focus Framework
definition: Only activities that sustain direct focus on the primary goal (sleep, food, basic needs) are productive; all other activities are distractions. Rest becomes requisite and therefore productive when it enables continued output on the core mission.

name: Three Types of Business Debt
definition: Every business always incurs debt at inception; the three forms are financial debt, management debt (underskilled hires), and technical debt (inadequate infrastructure). The strategic choice is which type to take on first based on ease of repayment.

name: Units x LTV Growth Formula
definition: Business growth reduces to two levers: sell more units or increase lifetime value per unit. Everything else is complexity layered on top of this identity.

name: Business Model Difficulty Curves
definition: Each major business model (Info, SaaS, E-commerce, Service) has a characteristic shape: startup speed, scalability trajectory, and the dominant constraint (people, cash flow, retention, talent) that emerges at each stage.

name: Demand vs. Supply Constraint Framework
definition: Businesses face either demand constraints (can acquire more customers than can be served) or supply constraints (cannot hire talent fast enough to serve existing demand); this industry-level pattern predicts difficulty and hiring challenge severity.

name: Volume Multiplication Through Skill Leverage
definition: Output scales via volume times skill: beginners must triple effort to match experienced operators, but sustained volume eventually generates superior skill and disproportionate returns.

name: The Rocky Cutscene Frame
definition: The movie montage of sustained grinding effort (two minutes on screen) spans years in reality; expectation-setting on duration is critical for motivation preservation.

name: 10-Stage Roadmap from Zero to 100 Million Plus
definition: A predictable progression through 10 distinct organizational stages as headcount and complexity increase, with specific constraints, symptoms, and graduation steps per stage, replicated across software, physical products, service businesses, and brick-and-mortar operations.

name: Focus vs. Portfolio Ownership
definition: Distinction between owning a portfolio of companies (passive wealth-generation) and being a CEO of one company (active scaling requirement); early-stage operators conflate these roles and apply portfolio logic prematurely.

name: 10-Stage Business Roadmap
definition: A ten-stage progression from zero to $100M+ revenue that applies across software, physical products, service businesses, and brick-and-mortar; each stage has distinct constraint symptoms and graduation requirements across eight business functions.

name: Three-to-Five Year Horizon Planning
