definition: A decision framework in which individuals plan for outcomes 3–5 years forward, anchored to personal financial stability (resolution of immediate bills and personal constraints) before extending vision further.

name: Wealth Progression Milestones and Vision Expansion
definition: As revenue crosses capability thresholds ($100k → $300k → $1M), founder skill inventory and market clarity increase, reframing the competitive landscape and revealing previously invisible opportunities.

name: Four Wealth Acquisition Groups
definition: A typology distinguishing how different groups use money and time: the rich buy time, the poor buy stuff, ambitious people buy skills, lazy people buy distractions.

name: Generational Wealth Transfer Through Skills
definition: Wealth compounds across generations only when transferred as skills and education, not as accumulated assets; a son without skills renders inherited wealth irrelevant.

name: Focus as Constraint
definition: Focus is operationally measurable by the count of things you say no to; maximum focus is saying yes to one thing and saying no to everything else.

name: How Your Role Makes The Company Money
definition: A diagnostic framework for mapping any employee's impact to revenue by identifying the cost consequences of poor performance and translating those into measurable operational standards.

name: Personality vs. Identity Model
definition: Personality is the observable set of behaviors you exhibit in specific conditions; identity is the label you place on top of those behaviors that then coordinates future behavior.

name: Authenticity Through Apparent Contradictions
definition: Interesting people display non-obvious pairings or contradictions (e.g., intellectual brute, wealthy broke-looking person) that violate expected patterns, making them memorable and attractive.

name: 10-Stage Revenue Growth Roadmap
definition: A 10-stage progression from zero to $100M+ revenue, with documented constraints, symptoms, and execution steps across eight business functions; less than 1% of companies complete the full progression.

name: Seven Systems to Remove Founder from Marketing
definition: A structured process hierarchy that replaces founder-led marketing with seven repeatable systems: testimonial screenshots, incentivized customer testimonials, lifecycle ads, client deliverable moments, customer support testimonials, review mining, and affiliate programs.

name: Time Study Measurement System
definition: A 15-minute interval time-tracking system using a kitchen timer and single-sheet logging to identify how a founder allocates their week and expose high-ROI delegation opportunities.

name: Founder-to-Owner Transition Model
definition: A conceptual framework where an entrepreneur systematically hires replacements for each time allocation, converting from founder-dependent service delivery to owner-level profit distribution.

name: Unicorn Decomposition Strategy
definition: Rejecting the search for a single all-capable hire (the "unicorn") and instead partitioning the founder's role into discrete sub-roles (white horse + rhino horn + fireflies) that can be hired separately and executed in parallel.

name: Volume-Output Scaling Progression
definition: A three-stage growth model where initial founder-driven output scales through hiring identical roles (2x), then through strategic innovation (new channels), then through reinvestment into building infrastructure.

name: Party Analogy Framework
definition: A commitment framework using a party metaphor: starting one well-resourced party (business) always outperforms attempting four simultaneous parties (businesses) with the same limited resources.

name: Need-to-Believe Test
definition: A framework for evaluating major business decisions by identifying the minimal set of assumptions that must be true for success, then assessing conviction and risk tolerance on those assumptions.

name: Strong Conviction Loosely Held
definition: The dual capacity to maintain deep conviction in a reasoning-based position while remaining ready to revise entirely when presented with sound evidence that a core pillar was wrong.

name: Management Diamond
definition: A framework identifying four reasons why people don't execute: they don't know they need to do it, they don't know how to do it, they don't know when to do it, or something is blocking them; the fourth category is motivation.

name: Activity Rank-Ordering via Time Study
definition: A time-tracking system where the founder logs activities every 15 minutes over one week, then ranks them by revenue impact to identify which tasks are highest-leverage and unique vs. delegatable.

name: Three-Element Daily Excellence
definition: A personal operating system anchored on three observable daily behaviors—workout with liked people, meal with liked people, write something down—that predicts subjective well-being and composable life quality.

name: Life Stage and Organizational Focus Progression
definition: A three-phase model where founder priorities shift from destination (20s) to journey (30s) to company and people (40s), driving decision architecture at each stage.

name: Three-Layer Market Opportunity Framework
definition: A visual model showing that a business operating on one platform captures an infinitesimal slice of the total available market; the full market expands across channels (platforms), ad formats (creative variations), and outreach methods (direct contact), each with unrealized capacity.

name: Free-Client Leverage Ladder
definition: A two-batch acquisition sequence: acquire 10 free clients to generate proof, then use that proof to close the next 10 paying clients — each batch funds credibility for the next.

name: Four Types of Leverage
definition: A stack of four distinct leverage mechanisms (labor, media, capital, technology) that compound when combined; each type multiplies return on input effort.

name: Order of Magnitude Income Transitions
definition: Progressive shifts in business structure (employee > self-employed > small team > licensed model > capital deployment) that correspond to $10M+ cumulative income milestones.

name: Work Exponentially to Compound Returns
definition: Absolute work shows diminishing returns, but relative excellence (being #1 vs #2) produces exponential payoff gains; 10x work input yields outsized returns in competitive markets.

name: Counting in Hundreds Framework
definition: Measure work effort in hundreds of hours per project to achieve genuine depth of understanding and quality; work expands to fill time allowed, but quality threshold is reached only at extreme hour counts.

name: Three Things to Win
definition: Success requires only three prerequisites: the courage to start (balls), the discipline to learn (brains), and the commitment to persist (heart).

name: 20 Hour Competence Rule
definition: Base competence in any skill (including money-making skills) requires only 20 hours of focused effort; the binding constraint is starting, not capability.

name: Three Things to Win Framework
definition: Success requires three elements: the courage to start, the intelligence to learn continuously, and the heart to persist—all of which you already possess.

name: Information Paralysis vs. Action Gap
definition: Most people know what to do but delay action by seeking a perfect plan; the real world rewards starting imperfectly and learning via feedback rather than pre-planning.

name: School vs. Real World Learning Model
definition: School provides clear directions, single correct answers, and immediate feedback; the real world offers many right paths, only one wrong path (inaction), and delayed feedback—requiring a behavioral reorientation.

name: $100 Million Scaling Roadmap
definition: A 10-stage growth framework that identifies where businesses get stuck and prescribes functional strategies (product, marketing, sales, customer success, recruiting, IT, HR, finance) at each stage.

name: Identity-Action Loop
definition: The mechanism that identity follows from repeated action, not vice versa; what you do publicly becomes how others describe you, making identity 100% controllable through deliberate behavioral choices.

name: Growth-Certainty Paradox
definition: Growth and certainty are mutually exclusive; pursuing one requires accepting the absence of the other.

name: Credibility-Results Equivalence
definition: Credibility derives from visible results, not from stated knowledge; evidence always overrides argument.

name: Cost-Outcome Binding
definition: Every outcome has a required cost; accepting the outcome means accepting its price without reservation.

name: 99% Right, 100% Wrong
definition: A pattern where repeated validation of short-term correctness (being right) obscures long-term failure (being wrong on the extended time horizon).

name: Powerless Frame (Victim Mentality)
definition: A psychological stance where one surrenders agency and gains the short-term reward of rightness while guaranteeing long-term loss.

name: Short-Term Risk vs Long-Term Guarantee
definition: The tradeoff between taking small risks today for compounding gains later versus accepting comfort today that becomes pain tomorrow.

name: Ignorance Debt Payment Framework
definition: The metaphor of personal growth as paying down accumulated ignorance through action and skill investment; the rate of debt repayment compounds based on years invested.

name: Three-Tier Drop-Servicing Niche Framework
definition: Categorizes drop-servicing niches into three tiers by average ticket price (high-ticket: construction/roofing/pools; mid-ticket: plumbing/HVAC/electrical; low-ticket: auto detailing/cleaning/window cleaning), each with distinct trade-offs in sales cycle length, close rate, lead volume, upsell potential, and setup difficulty.

name: Whisper-Tease-Shout Launch Sequence
definition: A three-phase promotional cadence for any product launch: Whisper (6+ weeks out, build anticipation with no details), Tease (6 weeks to 7 days out, reveal partial content), Shout (final 7 days, direct reminders). Each phase has distinct content strategy and contact frequency.

name: Two-Tier Affiliate Architecture
definition: A structure distinguishing super-affiliates (large audiences, status-motivated, rewarded with scarce-access prizes tied to audience benefit) from regular affiliates (small audiences, rewarded with low-bar achievable bonuses). Incentive design differs for each tier.

name: Triple Aligned Incentive Test
definition: A validation gate for any affiliate promotion: the affiliate's incentive, the creator's incentive, and the audience's incentive must all point toward the same action (the click or signup). Any misalignment reduces outcome.

name: SPCL Influence Framework
definition: A four-component model for building influence: Status (control of scarce resources), Power (say-do correspondence that produces reinforcing outcomes), Credibility (third-party verified proof), and Likeness (shared identity or values). All four stack multiplicatively.

name: Ghost Product Trust Architecture
definition: A sales framework that recommends alternative products at lower margins (or free alternatives) to establish buyer trust, then upsells higher-margin products based on that trust foundation.

name: Prescriptive Close with Habit Stacking
definition: A closing method that prescribes exact usage instructions before the ask, pairs products with existing daily habits (toothbrushing, morning routine) to reduce new habit friction, and closes via a simplified one-click decision.

name: Consultative Objection Reframe
definition: When a buyer claims budget constraints, reframe the removed product in terms of the new behavior it enabled (e.g., 'you'll eat broccoli instead'), shifting the frame from price negotiation to outcome preservation.

name: Acquisition Triangle
definition: A three-part framework for guaranteeing employee non-compliance or, inverted, ensuring compliance: (1) Expectation Setting (communication, recording, frequency, metrics), (2) Training (task methodology, prioritization, preferences), (3) Motivation (compensation, purpose, values alignment, self-interest).

name: Platform Evaluation Framework
definition: A four-axis scoring system (Who, Volume, Growth, Depth, Conversion) applied to each content platform to rank money-making potential by audience wealth, market share, discoverability, engagement duration, and downstream conversion rate.
concept: Platform Choice and Backup Channel Resilience

name: Money Models
definition: Offering the right thing at the right time in the right way to the right customer; the monetization structure governing how a business collects and charges for value.

name: Cash-Forward Launch Model
definition: Structuring a product launch so that pre-orders and advertising spend are offset by launch revenue, enabling the launch itself to demonstrate the money model principle of pulling cash forward.

name: Reverse Weakness Training Order
definition: Train body parts in reverse order of weakness (worst to best), starting each session with the lagging muscle group so it receives the most energy and volume.

name: Compress-Until-Nothing-Remains Editing
definition: A prose compression method: write a full draft, then repeatedly cut every sentence that can be removed without losing meaning, iterating until every remaining sentence carries unique load.

name: Best-Day Replication Framework
definition: Identify the specific days on which you do your best work, then design your life to repeat those days as often as possible rather than optimizing for abstract goals.

name: Criticism vs. Insult Distinction
definition: Criticism identifies a discrepancy (she is bigger than me in this way — why?) which drives improvement; an insult renders a judgment (therefore I am bad) which only produces shame without actionable signal.

name: Logic-Evidence-Utility Problem Definition
definition: A three-question framework for defining business problems: What does it mean? How do you know that? Why do you care? Forces quantitative grounding of vague claims.

name: Fast Cash Play via Existing Resources
definition: A structured approach to generating immediate client revenue by mobilizing the client's existing dead contacts, old customers, or social media audience before new acquisition begins, making the product self-funding within 30 days.

name: Win Your Money Back Dual-Conversion Frame
definition: A $500 front-end offer where the customer earns a 100% store credit by completing daily habits (activation) and submitting multi-platform testimonials (referral), with the store credit rolling into a full-year upsell at $5,000; combines results guarantee with social proof harvest in one mechanism.

name: Court Filter for Observable Language
definition: A translation discipline requiring all marketing and sales copy to describe only observable, court-admissible behaviors — physical actions, visible states, measurable outputs — removing interpretive or amorphous language that cannot be verified by a third party.

name: Evolution as Advertising-Driven Process
definition: Much of evolutionary progress is driven by the need to attract mates through costly signals; these signals function as natural advertising campaigns that drive behavioral selection.

name: Four Components of Equity Framework
definition: A decomposition of what real equity provides into four distinct elements — cash flow, sale bonus, risk, and control — used to identify which elements a prospective equity recipient actually wants, then substitute non-dilutive instruments for those elements only.

name: Profit Share Pool Structure
definition: A fixed percentage of annual profit (typically 10–20%) set aside as a leadership incentive pool; individual leaders receive slices of that pool rather than ownership stakes, capping total incentive spend while creating owner-like thinking.

name: Return on Time Framework
definition: Reframes all income as dollars-per-hour by dividing annual earnings by hours worked (2,000 for 40-hr weeks, 8,000 for all waking hours), enabling a single comparable metric to evaluate every income-generating activity.

name: Ten-Year Million Dollar Contract
definition: A commitment device in which a person agrees to act as if they have signed a contract to add one or two zeros to their net worth over ten years, converting long-run compounding from abstraction into a binding behavioral frame.

name: Declarative vs. Procedural Knowledge Framework
definition: Two distinct types of knowledge: declarative (knowing something exists) and procedural (knowing how to do it). Each requires a different investment vehicle and produces a different learning outcome.

name: Wealth Creation Equation
definition: Total lifetime earnings = (Value created for others) x (Negotiating power to capture that value) x (1 / Number of others who can create the same value). All three variables must be optimized simultaneously.

name: 12 by 30 Work Sprint
definition: Work 12 hours a day for 30 consecutive days with no weekends to discover your capacity ceiling, compress progress, and install the belief that you can sustain extreme output.

name: Trade-Off Levels Framework
definition: Four-level model of how people respond to a required cost: should (expects it free), too much (under-bids), bidding (keeps raising offer), source (sets own standard above the market).

name: Work = Volume x Leverage
definition: Productive output is defined as the product of how many times you do something (volume) and how much you receive per unit of effort (leverage); both dimensions must grow over time.

name: SCALE Loop
definition: A five-step loop for growing any system or department: Start (begin), Compound (do more volume), Augment (do better), Leverage (automate for consistency), Expand (move to next channel or territory).

name: Question-Delete-Optimize-Timelines-Automate (Turnaround Sequence)
definition: A five-step optimization sequence for fixing an existing broken system: question every requirement, delete everything non-essential, optimize remaining work by output-per-resource, pull up timelines, then automate.

name: Six Horsemen of Business Stagnation
definition: Six structural reasons businesses get stuck: (1) underpriced, (2) overcompensation of employees, (3) serving too many avatars, (4) overextension into multiple locations or businesses, (5) running more than one business without focus, (6) no data collection.

name: B2B Brand Building Buckets
definition: Three approaches for building a B2B brand without celebrity endorsements: (1) help your audience accomplish their goals for free (content), (2) demonstrate success for people like them (case studies/proof), (3) accomplish an aspirational outcome yourself.

name: Friendship Transactionalism
definition: A framework for evaluating friendships based on mutual return on investment rather than emotional obligation or duration, with explicit criteria for inclusion and removal.

name: Seasonal Friendships
definition: A model treating friendships as time-bound relationships aligned with shared goals; when trajectories diverge, the relationship ends without resentment or obligation.

name: Competitive Status Threat Mechanism
definition: The dynamic wherein a friend's rising status creates relative status loss for peer group members, incentivizing sabotage through gossip, distraction, and guilt-framing rather than celebration.

name: Scientific Attribution Model
definition: A blended attribution rule: if a conversion occurs within 30 days of a touchpoint, assign credit to the last touch; if the gap exceeds 30 days, assign credit to the first touch. This prevents both the short-termism of pure last-touch and the brand-inflation of pure first-touch.

name: Sales Hire Pattern Recognition Ladder
definition: Founders must fail-and-learn through each successive sales hire type (SDR, salesperson, manager, closer, director, VP) in sequence; pattern recognition for what good looks like only comes after multiple failures at each level.

name: Kano Attribute Hierarchy
definition: Products are perceived on three dimensions: threshold attributes (must-have, no delight if present), performance attributes (linear satisfaction curve), and excitement attributes (irrelevant to core function yet disproportionately drive purchase and loyalty).
concept: Brand Effect on Customer Behavior and WTP

name: Rider-Elephant Model (Haidt)
definition: The conscious mind (rider) believes it controls behavior but is actually a press office generating post-hoc rationalizations for decisions made by the unconscious (elephant); the monkey brain drives action through emotion, not through deliberate reasoning.

name: McNamara Fallacy
definition: Decision-makers optimize exclusively for whatever is easily measurable (SI units: time, weight, distance), systematically discarding psychological variables that resist measurement, producing solutions that score well on metrics but poorly on human experience.

name: Costly Signaling Theory
definition: Communications or investments that impose a genuine cost on the sender (money, talent, bravery, humor) are trusted as authentic; cost-free signals are discounted because they are cheap to fake.

name: Ergodicity Distinction
definition: Under multiplicative dynamics, what is a positive-expected-value bet for an aggregate population is simultaneously a losing bet for any given individual traced through time; economics uses ensemble averages and therefore systematically misjudges individual risk.

name: Forced-Growth Constraint Framework
definition: Deliberately engineering an uncomfortable financial situation (moving out, making a large investment) to eliminate optionality and activate non-negotiable effort.

name: Innovation-as-Behavior-Change Definition
definition: Stuart Butterfield's criterion that the only useful definition of innovation is the extent to which it changes human behavior; novelty without adoption is invention, not innovation.

name: Technology-Psychology Innovation Spectrum
definition: All innovations sit on a spectrum from purely technological to purely psychological; the decisive value-creating insight is often psychological rather than technical, even when delivered by technology.

name: Dr. Pepper vs. Coke Reframing Test
definition: A mental model for diagnosing whether an option is perceived as normal (Coke) or socially risky (Dr. Pepper); shifting a behavior from Dr. Pepper to Coke status dramatically increases adoption without changing the underlying option.

name: Fish Restaurant Problem
definition: The pattern of preferring instrumentalist (economic/logistical) explanations for success over psychological ones, even when the psychological explanation better predicts the data; named after the clustering of fish restaurants at the coast.

name: Investor Risk Ladder
definition: Investors pay down assumptions, not ideas; each funding round represents a specific assumption that was de-risked, and the valuation step-up must be justified by naming which assumption was proved true.

name: Three-Step GMB Ranking Formula
definition: A three-stage process for ranking first on Google Maps without a website: (1) market research to select cities by search volume and competition, (2) on-page GMB SEO optimization combined with review-count parity, (3) ongoing maintenance to preserve rank.
concept: Geographic Expansion Sequence: Dominate Local, Then Expand

name: Three-Factor Google Maps Ranking Model
definition: Google Maps ranking for local service businesses is determined by three factors in descending importance: (1) physical address verification in the target city, (2) review count competitive with the local top-three, and (3) keyword presence in the business title. All other SEO is secondary.

name: Google Business Profile Three-Phase Optimization
definition: A three-stage framework: (1) pre-listing considerations for location and name, (2) live listing optimization via reviews, keywords, and profile completeness, (3) post-rank conversion maximization via photos, ratings, and profile presentation.

name: Blackhat GBP Ranking Blueprint
definition: A four-part counter-conventional system for ranking Google Business Profiles into the three-pack within one week: (1) keyword-stuff the business name with service + city, (2) verify via video on a physical address, (3) pump reviews immediately at volume from local real accounts, (4) replicate into additional low-competition service areas.

name: Remote Drop-Service Model
definition: A local-service arbitrage framework: create multiple Google Business Profile listings across a city, capture inbound calls from people searching for a service, then route jobs to a subcontractor who performs the work for a 40-50% share of revenue, keeping the remainder without performing manual labor.

name: Small TAM Entry to Mass Market Expansion
definition: Enter the smallest defensible niche first, validate product-market fit, then expand outward to broader segments over a multi-year horizon.

name: Speed-to-Market Priority
definition: Ship a proof-of-concept product with adequate packaging before perfecting it; iteration replaces planning as the primary product development method.

name: Find-Sell-Deliver Sequence
definition: When launching a new product or service, identify a customer first, sell them on a meaningful outcome you will deliver, and commit to staying until they are satisfied — before building a detailed plan or process.

name: Clear-Mind-First Framework
definition: A three-step prerequisite sequence before executing on an online business: (1) eliminate all cognitive distractions (social media, relationships, social obligations), (2) put financial or lifestyle stakes on the line to create an inescapable forcing function, (3) then allocate 95%+ of work time to customer acquisition exclusively.

name: Evidence-Over-Emotion Self-Assessment
definition: Apply the same evidence standard you use to judge others when evaluating your own character traits; a trait is possessed if observable behavior demonstrates it, regardless of whether you feel you have it.

name: Penny-on-the-Scale Accumulation
definition: Build a character trait by accumulating undeniable behavioral proof one action at a time; each act consistent with the trait adds a penny to the scale until the weight of evidence makes the self-attribution credible.

name: 5-Step Remote Service Business Launch
definition: Sequenced launch system: (1) choose city/market, (2) set up organic Google Business Profile lead generation, (3) grow and multiply profiles, (4) operations (quoting, booking), (5) fulfillment via subcontracted cleaners.

name: Low-Competition High-Demand Area Selection Framework
definition: A two-variable market-entry filter that selects a service area by cross-referencing keyword search volume (demand proxy) against the review count of existing top-3 Google Business Profile competitors (competition proxy), targeting zones where top competitors hold fewer reviews than is feasible to overcome.

name: Remote Service Arbitrage Business Model
definition: A three-role structure where a business-profile operator generates inbound leads via Google Maps listings, answers calls and books appointments, then routes jobs to a subcontractor at a negotiated revenue split (typically 60/40 in the operator's favor), keeping 40% of each job without performing the physical work.

name: Give-Then-Ask Brand Investment Framework
definition: Brands accumulate goodwill through sustained value-giving (content, partnerships, community) before making asks during high-purchase-intent moments like Black Friday; the depth of prior giving is directly proportional to conversion when asking.

name: Focused Offer Architecture for Peak Buying Events
definition: During peak buying windows, narrow the navigation and offer set to three to four items so consumer attention is concentrated on the highest-converting products, rather than paralyzed by breadth.

name: Advent Calendar as Product Test Vehicle
definition: Package existing bestsellers alongside unreleased prototype products in a collectible advent calendar; sell exclusively to hardcore fans under scarcity conditions, generating both revenue and statistically useful demand signal data for next-year product decisions.

name: Death Wish Mechanic
definition: A product feature allowing life insurance customers to record specific intentions (financial, experiential, emotional) for what happens after their death, serving dual purposes: emotional personalization of the policy and a calculation tool for determining appropriate coverage amounts.

name: Tackling vs. Ducking the Negative
definition: A brand strategy framework where a product's inherent negative (uncomfortable subject matter, slow service, minority status) is addressed head-on rather than avoided, converting the liability into a salient differentiator. Rory Sutherland cites Avis (We Try Harder), Guinness (Good Things Come to Those Who Wait), and Dead Happy (humor around death) as canonical examples.

name: Purchase-Longevity Payment Matching
definition: Match payment duration to expected product enjoyment horizon: durable goods warrant deferred or split payment; consumables warrant immediate payment.

name: Incentive Alignment Differentiation
definition: BNPL lenders profit only when consumers repay, creating shared upside with consumers; credit card revolving models profit when consumers do NOT fully repay, creating adversarial incentive structures.

name: Marketing as Opportunity Cost Avoidance
definition: Reframes marketing spend from a cost-center to a mechanism that avoids opportunity cost; the correct mental model is not cost minimization but loss prevention.

name: Reverse Marketing (Consumer-Appointed AI Agency)
definition: A speculative future model in which consumers deploy AI-powered agents to actively seek out relevant products and services on their behalf, reversing the direction of marketing from push to pull.

name: Kano Model
definition: A framework mapping how product/service features translate into customer satisfaction, identifying four zones: negative features (add functionality but reduce satisfaction), table-stakes (absence destroys trust, presence is neutral), indifferent (investment with no noticed effect), one-dimensional (proportionate satisfaction), and delight attributes (tangential features that deliver outsized loyalty).

name: SCARF Model
definition: David Rock's neuroscience framework identifying five dimensions that people deeply care about but that are unmeasurable in SI units: Status, Certainty, Autonomy, Relatedness, and Fairness. Loyalty programs and service design can play to all five.

name: Explore-Exploit Trade-off
definition: Dynamic systems must allocate a fixed percentage (roughly 20%) of capacity to random exploration rather than exploiting known-good options, or they become over-optimized on the past and miss newly emerging opportunities.

name: Five Unmeasured Human Motivators
definition: Status, Certainty, Autonomy, Relatedness, and Fairness are deeply embedded human motivators that conventional economic and engineering models lack numerical metrics for, yet they dominate real-world behavior in travel and product decisions.

name: Psychological Arbitrage
definition: The discovery and exploitation of psychological value in a place where conventional analysis would declare it nonexistent; the mechanism by which Red Bull, Nespresso, Dyson, and Uber created outsized returns without matching competitors on conventional product metrics.

name: Proactive Libertarianism
definition: A stance that goes beyond protecting existing choices to actively creating new choices people did not know they had, treating invisible or unnamed options as a design failure.

name: System One vs System Two Design
definition: A two-mode behavioral model in which System One is automatic, instinctive, and heuristic-driven while System Two is deliberate and rational; Rory Sutherland argues most policy and product design optimises for System Two while actual behavior runs on System One.

name: Deferred Prescription Choice Architecture
definition: A three-option antibiotic prescription model (immediate, deferred, none) that reveals how the binary framing of a choice can encode implicit bias toward one option, and that a third path reduces over-prescription from ~80% to ~16%.

name: Tony's Open Chain Five Sourcing Principles
definition: A five-part supply-chain standard — 100% traceability, living income reference price, professionalised farmer cooperatives, long-term partnerships (minimum five years), and yield/quality improvement support — that Tony's Chocolonely requires of itself and recruits mission allies to adopt.

name: Sequential Distribution-as-Marketing Strategy
definition: A staged retail distribution sequence — independent image accounts first, then premium grocery, then mass-market grocery — designed so each tier builds brand credibility and consumer inference before the next tier is entered.

name: Arithmocracy
definition: Rory Sutherland's term for the class of people who rule organizational decision-making by controlling access to numerical measures, regardless of the quality or relevance of those numbers.

name: Clocks vs. Clouds Spectrum (Karl Popper)
definition: A spectrum from deterministic, mathematically solvable systems (clocks) to irreducibly complex, unpredictable systems (clouds / weather / human behavior); the error is applying clock-science tools to cloud-problems.

name: Goodhart's Law
definition: Any metric that becomes a target loses its value as a metric, because once people optimize for it directly the measurement is automatically distorted and ceases to track the underlying reality.

name: Ratchet Effect
definition: A class of products and technologies where adoption is very slow until a threshold of experience is crossed, after which reversion is near-zero; the value of the product is only revealed through use, not through prior reasoning.
concept: Brand Effect on Customer Behavior and WTP

name: EAST Behavioral Adoption Framework
definition: A four-lever framework for accelerating behavior adoption: make the target behavior Easy, Attractive, Social, and Timely. Rory Sutherland applies it specifically to recycling and sustainable product adoption.

name: Map vs. Territory (Korzybski Applied to Economics)
definition: Economics provides a map of human behavior; reality is the territory. What the economic map omits (context, packaging, psychological association) is often more important than what the map contains. Coined by Alfred Korzybski; applied here to consumer valuation by Rory Sutherland.
concept: Undefined Words Create Mythology and Prevent Clear Thinking

name: Operational vs. Psychological Value Creation
definition: Two distinct value-creation modes: operational (process efficiency, cost reduction, widely pursued, subject to diminishing returns) and psychological (context, packaging, association, perception — largely ignored by CEOs/CFOs because it is non-numerical and uncertain). Rory Sutherland argues the second mode has orders-of-magnitude greater untapped potential.

name: BAMFAM (Book a Meeting from a Meeting)
definition: A commitment rule that every sales call must end with the next scheduled touchpoint booked before hanging up, so no prospect falls into an untracked follow-up gap.

name: On-Call / Off-Call SOP Dual Checklist
definition: Two separate operating procedures for salespeople: the on-call SOP governs what to say during prospect conversations; the off-call SOP governs activity between calls (following up, pulling up appointments, rescheduling no-shows, prospecting for referrals).

name: Obstacles vs. Objections Distinction
definition: Obstacles are concerns raised before price is mentioned; objections are concerns raised after price is revealed. Obstacles are defused proactively (kill zombies up front); objections are handled reactively under time pressure.

name: Three-Category Obstacle Framework
definition: All pre-close obstacles fall into three buckets: (1) Circumstances (time, money, program fit); (2) Other people (spouse, business partner, decision-maker); (3) Self-doubt (the prospect doubts their own ability to succeed). Each category has a distinct rhetorical strategy.

name: Dogs / Horses / Tigers Sales Archetype
definition: Three salesperson archetypes by intrinsic drive: Dogs require constant attention and die without hand-holding; Horses gallop only while whipped and stop when whipping stops; Tigers hunt for sport even when full. High-performance teams require Tigers.

name: Best Leads to Best Closers Lead Distribution
definition: A lead routing system that scores leads by close probability, assigns highest-probability leads to top closers, and trains new reps on the lowest-probability leads, maximizing total revenue while developing skill at the bottom.

name: Three-Lever Scaling Sequence
definition: Fix sales motion first, then raise prices, then use increased profit to improve talent retention — each lever unlocks the next.

name: Mass-GMB Proximity Arbitrage
definition: Create large quantities of Google My Business profiles at physical addresses distributed across every target service area; proximity to the searcher is the dominant ranking signal, so quantity of correctly-placed listings beats quality or review count on any single listing.

name: VA-Dispatch-Subcontractor Fulfillment Stack
definition: A three-layer fulfillment model: virtual assistants handle all inbound calls and calendar booking; a pre-vetted subcontractor roster receives text-blast job assignments; the founder handles none of the operational loop.

name: Expanded Career Ladder Framework
definition: Transform a 3-rung career path into 9-18 rungs by subdividing each existing title into junior, normal, and senior tiers, alternating title upgrades with tangible perks so employees are always 3-6 months from the next promotion.

name: Debt Risk Quantification Framework
definition: A three-variable coverage-ratio analysis (seasonal volatility, cash flow vs. debt covenants, and coverage buffer) that converts emotional debt fear into a tractable math problem.

name: College vs Career Scorecard
definition: A point-by-point comparison framework that tallies arguments for and against attending college across dimensions: debt burden, lifetime earnings, probability of outperforming, network access, and social experience.

name: Warren Buffett Investment Question Applied to Education
definition: Evaluate any education decision by the gap between what you pay (tuition + opportunity cost + interest) and what you get (lifetime earnings differential), not by the gross earnings figure alone.

name: Service Area vs. Physical Address GMB Decision Framework
definition: A two-option decision tree for Google Business Profile setup: service area pages (easier to verify, lower suspension risk, require more SEO work) versus physical address pages (proximity search advantage, faster early results, harder to verify, higher suspension risk and policy compliance burden).

name: Niche Depth Over Audience Width
definition: A content strategy that maximizes revenue-per-follower by targeting an ultra-specific audience with problem-specific content, trading vanity metrics (views, likes) for business metrics (opt-ins, sales).

name: 1,000 True Fans Revenue Model
definition: A monetization framework asserting that 1,000 deeply loyal fans who pay even $10/month generate $100k/year, making mass reach unnecessary for profitable audience-based businesses.

name: Partnership Justification Test
definition: A partnership only creates value if the partner supplies something the other party genuinely lacks: money, time, skills, or network/distribution. Absence of at least one gap means one partner is redundant.

name: Real Business Behind the Business
definition: Every business has an obvious surface activity (fitness, product quality, sales) and a hidden primary constraint that actually limits scale; identifying the hidden constraint is the prerequisite to enterprise-value growth.

name: Car Analogy for Business Components
definition: All business functions (marketing, product, ops) are like car components — all necessary, but the question is which component is the binding limiter for a specific business at a specific stage.

name: Woman in the Red Dress
definition: Any shiny new opportunity that appears when a founder encounters the real hard problem inside their current business; its perceived attractiveness scales with the founder's skill level, making it progressively harder to resist.

name: Leads-First Agency Model (Reordered Agency)
definition: Generate leads for an in-person service business first using organic Google My Business ranking, then recruit a fulfillment partner to execute the work, collecting 40-60% of job revenue — reversing the traditional agency sequence of client-first, leads-second.

name: Website-as-Converter Framework
definition: A website's sole purpose in a local-service drop servicing business is to convert inbound traffic from external sources (Google Business Profile, ads); it is not a traffic-generation tool and should not be optimized for SEO or traffic volume.

name: Drop Low or Go High
definition: Digital marketing agencies serving SMBs must choose between two viable poles: ultra-cheap automated delivery (≤$400/month) or high-touch services for sophisticated business owners with proven metrics; the middle band ($1,500–$3,000/month) is a structural dead zone.

name: Launch and Integrate Affiliate Strategy
definition: Two-step process for activating affiliate partners: a launch (get a batch of referrals fast to create an internal case study) followed by integration (embedding your service into the affiliate's standard onboarding so every new client they bring on automatically becomes your client).

name: Remote Service Business Speedrun
definition: A four-step organic launch sequence for a local-search-dependent service business: (1) map target areas and plan GMB profile locations, (2) verify and list Google Business Profiles, (3) optimize profiles and acquire reviews to rank, (4) fulfill jobs via subcontracted labor at 50-60% margin.

name: Remote Service Arbitrage Model
definition: Create keyword-optimized Google Business Profile listings in high-demand, low-competition service markets; collect inbound leads; dispatch pre-sourced contractors at a 20% markup; pocket the spread without doing any physical labor.

name: GBP Ranking Formula
definition: Three inputs determine Google Business Profile rank: (1) exact-match keywords in the business name, (2) total review count exceeding the current top-ranked competitor, and (3) geographic specificity of service area targeting.

name: Data as Rationality Signaling
definition: In modern business culture, the display of numerical data serves as a social signal of rationality and credibility, regardless of data quality.

name: Three-Level AI Service Delivery Stack
definition: A progression from websites (level 1) to individual automations (level 2) to full integrated AI systems (level 3), where each level requires more skill and commands higher prices.

name: Doctor Sales Approach
definition: A consultative sales structure where the seller talks 20% of the time and asks diagnostic questions that lead the prospect to identify their own pain, then positions the seller's service as the solution.

name: Five-Step AI Business Roadmap
definition: A sequenced roadmap from (1) learn a skill, (2) work for free to build proof, (3) sustain yourself ($2-3k/month), (4) charge more and filter clients, to (5) identify and solve bottlenecks continuously.

name: Result-Based vs Upfront-Plus-Recurring Pricing
definition: Two primary pricing structures for AI services: (1) result-based at 20% of gross profit generated, which pays more when work is excellent but requires trackability; (2) upfront setup fee plus monthly recurring, used when results are hard to attribute, combined with a satisfaction guarantee.

name: Hook-Meat-CTA Ad Structure
definition: Every paid ad has three mandatory parts: a hook (call-out that makes the viewer think 'this is for me'), meat (value = more good stuff or less bad stuff), and a call to action (offer + clear next step).

name: Value Equation Reversal
definition: Frame ad value by maximizing four good-stuff vectors (fast, easy, risk-free, likely) and minimizing four bad-stuff mirrors (slow, hard, risky, unlikely); each vector can also be sold as 'what you lose by not buying' to create a second set of copy angles.

name: Levels of Awareness Ad Targeting
definition: Eugene Schwartz's five-level model (unaware, problem-aware, solution-aware, product-aware, most-aware) determines hook style: colder audiences need curiosity hooks with no solution reference; warmest audiences need only an offer restatement.

name: Same Bundle Different Wrapper
definition: Once an offer is proven to convert, keep the bundle identical but cycle through seasonal or event-based wrappers (holiday, Super Bowl, spring, back-to-school) to create perceived novelty without rebuilding the offer.

name: Organic Drop-Servicing System
definition: A three-stage local-service arbitrage model: (1) create multiple Google Business Profiles in target cities, (2) build review volume to surface in near-me search, (3) answer inbound calls, book jobs, and outsource execution to cheap contractors while keeping the spread.

name: 10-Profile Geographic Coverage Map
definition: Distribute 10 Google Business Profile locations across a single city spaced roughly 15 minutes apart so that each profile captures near-me searches without profiles overlapping each other.
concept: Geographic Expansion Sequence: Dominate Local, Then Expand

name: Sales-to-Fulfillment Continuum
definition: A spectrum where ease of selling and difficulty of fulfillment are inversely correlated: done-for-you is easy to sell and hard to fulfill; do-it-yourself is hard to sell and easy to fulfill.

name: Done-For-You to Do-It-Yourself Pyramid (Tesla Model)
definition: A top-down product sequencing strategy: start at the premium done-for-you tier (highest price, hardest to fulfill), build SOPs, then release done-with-you at one-third to one-fifth the price, then do-it-yourself at the lowest price; each layer productizes the layer above.

name: One-on-One to Group Delivery Scaling Sequence
definition: A progressive output-multiplication pattern for service delivery: one-on-one -> one-on-six -> one-on-twenty -> one-on-thirty -> train others to deliver; each step multiplies throughput while preserving most of the personalization value.

name: Two Magic Customer Questions
definition: Two inverted feature-priority questions: (1) If forced to keep only one feature, which would it be? (2) If forced to eliminate one feature with no consequence, which would it be? Together they produce a power ranking of value and waste.

name: Face-Saving Re-Entry Frame
definition: A negotiation tactic for allowing a previously resistant partner to accept new terms without humiliation by reframing their earlier refusal as contextually reasonable and shifting blame to external demand pressure.
concept: Partnership Equity Must Be Codified Upfront

name: Extinction Curve of Determination
definition: A behavioral model defining determination as the length of the extinction curve: how many times a person continues acting without seeing results. Each successive attempt (knock, shout, try the window, go around back) is attempted by an exponentially smaller fraction of people, making extreme persistence statistically rare and therefore a durable competitive advantage.

name: Intelligence vs. Determination Character Allocation (Paul Graham)
definition: A two-axis model where a person has 100 points to allocate between intelligence and determination. Reducing determination toward zero produces a smart, paralyzed person. Reducing intelligence toward zero while keeping determination at 100 still produces successful outcomes. Conclusion: determination is a stronger determinant of success than intelligence.

name: Replace-Six Strategy
definition: Rather than scaling headcount of low-quality clients, replace current clients one-for-one with higher-quality, compliant clients over a 12-month horizon, then go deep on the single best performer.

name: Sell to the Rich, Not From Your Own Wallet
definition: A pricing mindset framework asserting that entrepreneurs should price for the top 10% wealth tier (net worth $1M+), not for the 50th-percentile buyer who is never their customer.

name: LTV-Conversion Rate Model Selection Test
definition: Compare two business models by asking three questions: (1) Does more of the target market want it (conversion rate)? (2) Is the lifetime gross profit per customer higher? (3) Is the CAC comparable or lower? The model that wins on all three is mathematically superior.

name: Negative Motivation Stack
definition: A three-element cognitive structure that drives achievement: (1) a large meaningful goal, (2) massive fears about inadequacy/failure, (3) impulse control anchored to pain-avoidance rather than pleasure-pursuit.

name: Pain-as-Fuel Framework
definition: Deliberately harnessing negative emotional states (anger, disgust, shame, pain) as the primary fuel for action, instead of waiting for purpose or passion to materialize.

name: Build for Cold, Works Everywhere
definition: A sales process designed for cold (unwarmed) leads will function on warm leads too; a warm-only process underconverts cold traffic by a large margin.
concept: Warm vs. Cold Sales Process Mismatch

name: Cold-Lead Sales Architecture (VSL + Qualification + Training Cadence)
definition: Three-component system for cold traffic: (1) video sales letter pre-frames and filters before the call, (2) structured qualification gates separate genuinely qualified prospects, (3) ongoing sales training cadence ensures reps follow the process consistently.

name: Dawn to Dusk Portfolio
definition: A brand portfolio organized to cover every meal occasion from morning to evening, enabling cross-category household penetration without a single brand bearing all positioning weight.

name: Become a Friend Programme (Ella's Kitchen)
definition: A post-purchase loyalty and education programme for parents of Ella's Kitchen customers, combining weaning guides, feeding resources, and direct customer care contact to function as a trusted advisor rather than a brand.

name: Drop Servicing Setup Sequence
definition: A step-by-step launch sequence for remote service businesses: select a niche, map out an exact to-do list, set up business profiles, complete verifications, acquire first contractors, then close initial sales — all executable in 1-2 hours/day.

name: Platform Brand Architecture
definition: A brand designed from launch to expand across product categories under a single umbrella name, rather than being named after a product, ingredient, or founder, enabling acquirer confidence and category expansion.

name: Meme Page Arbitrage Model
definition: Early-stage community growth tactic of purchasing ad slots on high-follower meme pages to grow a founder-anchored social community rather than to directly sell a product, functioning as an early form of influencer marketing.

name: Scale Before Optimizing
definition: Build for growth first; defer financial and operational optimization until the business is at meaningful scale, because optimization at small scale trades mind-share for marginal gains on a tiny base.

name: No Winning Lottery Ticket Numbers Principle
definition: Business success formulas cannot be replicated because they embed timing, personality, obsession, and risk tolerance that are unique to the original founder's context; copying a playbook is structurally equivalent to replaying lottery numbers.

name: Data vs. Culture Decision Framework
definition: Data reveals what people already did (backward-looking); cultural reading reveals what people are going to do (forward-looking). Decisions based only on data compete on yesterday's information; elite entrepreneurs read culture to get ahead of the data.

name: Today Constraint vs. Horizon Constraint
definition: Distinguish the constraint blocking growth right now (sales/marketing) from the constraint that will become existential at a future date (facility/supply); address today's constraint first unless the horizon constraint's timeline forces earlier action.

name: Launch Then Integrate B2B Partnership Model
definition: Enter a B2B partner relationship with a one-time co-webinar launch to build goodwill, then transition to permanent integration into the partner's sales motion so the partner sells the complementary service as a standard add-on.

name: Competition-First Ranking Framework
definition: Before optimizing any Google Business Profile signal, audit the current top-three local competitors across every ranking factor and beat them in as many dimensions as possible; winning enough dimensions guarantees top-three placement.

name: Three Ways to 10x Income
definition: A three-part framework for income multiplication: (1) arbitrage — exploit price differentials between markets; (2) giveaways — give away outsized value to generate demand then monetize a back-end product; (3) price anchoring — raise perceived value of existing offers by placing a premium anchor tier above them.

name: Lead Magnet Types
definition: Three structural forms for free-value giveaways: (a) reveal a problem — surface a gap the prospect didn't know they had; (b) free trial — let them sample the core product; (c) one-step solution to a multi-step problem — solve step one for free so the prospect naturally needs the remaining steps.

name: Give Free, Monetize Differently
definition: Hormozi's preferred business model: identify what competitors sell, make a better version free, then monetize via a separate back-end product that the free offer naturally leads to — reversing the conventional paid-then-deliver sequence.

name: Three Content Buckets
definition: A taxonomy dividing all content into entertainment (goal: get people to watch), education (goal: change behavior), and edutainment (goal: both simultaneously); the prevailing outcome across viewers determines the bucket.

name: Proof-Promise-Plan Introduction Framework
definition: A three-element intro structure for educational videos: Proof (evidence you can deliver on the promise), Promise (what the viewer will gain), and Plan (the steps that will get them there); order is flexible — lead with whichever element is most important for the content.

name: Four Paths to Mega Money
definition: A 2x2 framework combining your money vs. other people's money with your business vs. other people's businesses to produce four distinct wealth-building paths: bootstrapping, raising capital, investing, and fund management.

name: The Going Pro Decision
definition: A binary internal commitment to pursue a skill or goal at a professional standard, triggered by a deliberate choice rather than external circumstances, with the understanding that effort will never receive credit and that the work must be done purely for the doer.

name: Six Levels of Making Money
definition: A ranked hierarchy of six compensation structures ordered by leverage and risk transfer: (1) work then get paid, (2) pay as you go, (3) pay then work, (4) when X happens you pay me, (5) sell/buy risk itself (insurance model), (6) no-matter-what you pay me (government/monopoly model).

name: Behavioral Trauma Framework
definition: A two-axis diagnostic: (1) was there a permanent behavior change from an aversive stimulus? — determines whether trauma occurred; (2) does the behavior change move toward or away from long-term goals? — determines whether the outcome was positive or negative.

name: Three-Option Hate Response Framework
definition: A three-level response menu for handling public attacks: (1) Ignore — lowest effort, lets the attacker advertise you for free; (2) Agree — defuse conflict by stepping to the attacker's side; (3) Agree-plus-one — out-insult the attacker by escalating the self-critique beyond what they said.

name: Ignore-and-Amplify Strategy
definition: When a lie or reputational attack cannot be ignored in silence, combine disciplined non-response with a 10x increase in message volume, drowning the attack via audience share rather than direct rebuttal.

name: Performance-Based Zero-Capital Business Selection
definition: Two criteria for selecting a business when starting with zero capital: (1) pay-for-performance compensation structure so no capital is required to start earning, and (2) no upfront cost to operate, meaning the business runs on the founder's time and skill rather than inventory or ad spend.

name: Vendor Discount Arbitrage Model
definition: Negotiate a discounted bulk rate from a business owner (the delivery cost floor), then sell to end customers at a higher market price; the spread between the two prices is the founder's margin, requiring zero capital if the business owner absorbs delivery cost.

name: Three Reality Distortions (Ellis-Hormozi)
definition: Adapted from Albert Ellis's CBT framework: the three irrational beliefs that cause people to cast power away from themselves — Circumstances (I must get what I want when I want it), Others (people must treat me fairly or be condemned), and Self (I must do well or I am no good) — which manifest in sales as time, money, fit, authority, and avoidance objections.

name: Five Objection Categories (Hormozi)
definition: The five surface manifestations of the three reality distortions in a sales context: Time (busy, bad timing), Value/Price (too expensive, can't afford), Fit (not for me, wrong vehicle), Authority (need spouse/partner approval), and Avoidance/Stall (need to think about it). Ordered from surface-level to core self.

name: Three Closing Questions (Hormozi)
definition: The core close after all external objections are exhausted: (1) Do you believe this product will help you achieve your goal? (2) Do you trust me to fulfill my word? (3) Do you believe it will work for you specifically? When all three are yes, close on access to money.

name: Obstacle vs. Objection Distinction
definition: Obstacles are disagreements that surface before asking for the sale; objections arise after the sale is solicited. Obstacles are easier to handle because no stake has been presented yet; they should be fully resolved before entering closing mode.

name: Behavioral vs. Attitudinal Data Hierarchy
definition: Behavioral data (what people actually do) is more valuable and revealing than attitudinal data (what people claim they do), because self-reported intentions systematically diverge from revealed preferences.

name: Ergodicity Fallacy in Aggregate Statistics
definition: The false assumption that what is good on average for a population doing something once is also good for a single individual doing the same thing repeatedly; this misapplication of ensemble averages to time-series decisions produces fatally wrong conclusions in economics, policy, and risk.

name: Features vs. Bugs Framework
definition: Every business has permanent structural characteristics (features) that require ongoing management rather than one-time fixes, and temporary fixable problems (bugs); the founder's error is misclassifying features as bugs and breaking working systems to eliminate them.

name: Business Scalability Spectrum
definition: A three-point spectrum ordering business types by ease-of-start vs. scalability ceiling: service businesses (easy start, hardest to scale quickly) in the middle e-commerce (moderate start cost, moderate scalability), and SaaS/software (hardest to start, easiest to scale at maturity).

name: Core Four Customer Acquisition Methods
definition: Four sequenced channels for getting customers: (1) warm outreach one-to-one, (2) free content posting, (3) cold outreach one-to-one, (4) paid ads one-to-many.

name: Hook-Retain-Reward Content Framework
definition: Three-part content structure: hook (first 3 seconds to stop the scroll), retain (list, steps, or story to hold attention), reward (funny moment, call-to-action, or shareable payoff at the end).

name: Four Returns From Free Work
definition: Every free service recipient can generate value in four ways: (1) they become a paying customer, (2) they leave a review, (3) they refer a friend, (4) they give feedback that improves the offering.

name: Scale Zero Framework
definition: A principle requiring the founder to reduce their personal operational contribution to zero before a business can scale without ceiling; any function requiring founder involvement caps total scale.

name: Two Service Business Reinvestment Paths
definition: Service businesses should direct end-of-year profit into exactly two categories: A-player talent acquisition or brand-building plays (high-visibility associations), not physical capital or general overhead.

name: Explore-Exploit Trade-off
definition: Every surviving organization must balance exploiting known information (reliable, short-term return) with exploring for unknown or new information (costly in the short term but essential for adaptation and survival). The ratio between the two is a strategic choice with survival consequences.

name: Waggle Dance Incentive Model
definition: Rory Sutherland's framing of how bee colonies solve information-sharing incentives: explore-bees share new discoveries with the hive; the length of the waggle dance is proportionate to the significance of the find, creating a natural reward signal for information sharing that most human organizations lack.

name: Ergodicity Framework
definition: The distinction between ensemble average (many people taking a bet once) and time average (one person taking the same bet repeatedly). A bet that is profitable on average for a group can still be ruinous for individuals because the majority can end up poorer than their starting position even while the group average rises.

name: Innovation Adoption Gap
definition: The gap between technological invention and market adoption is a function of perception and marketing, not product quality; historical hindsight compresses this gap into apparent instantaneity.

name: Marketing Moonshot Framework
definition: A two-category model separating standard-optimization activity (80% of bees following the waggle dance) from exploratory high-variance bets (20% rogue bees) where failure is frequent but rare successes pay back 10,000-fold; applied to marketing as changing perception rather than physical reality to achieve order-of-magnitude improvements at relatively low cost.

name: Satisficing vs. Optimizing Decision Model
definition: Herbert Simon's distinction between archery-style optimization (aim for the single best outcome) and darts-style satisficing (aim for the southwestern quadrant to avoid catastrophic low scores); in evolutionary and business contexts, satisficing considers both average outcome and worst-case variance, not only the maximum.

name: Costly Signaling / Handicap Theory
definition: Amotz Zahavi's principle that meaningful signals require genuine cost (financial, effort, time, creativity) because cheap signals are unreliable; applied to marketing, advertising spend, gift-giving, and brand behavior as mechanisms that signal long-term commitment and trustworthiness to observers.

name: Five AI Workers System
definition: A bundled agency offer of five AI-driven automation roles — outreach specialist (database reactivation), reputation manager (reviews and referrals), website lead nurturing, AI receptionist (missed call text-back), and marketing director (paid ads with AI lead nurturing) — sold together to local businesses as an inseparable department rather than individual point solutions.

name: Niche Research Rubric
definition: A four-criteria filter for selecting an agency niche: proof of concept (other agencies succeeding), total addressable market over 10,000 businesses, high-ticket recurring pricing, and a growing market; evaluated via Claude prompt.
concept: Market Selection Criteria: Growth + Pain + Targeting

name: The Lonely Chapter
definition: The early phase of an exceptional path during which the founder operates without peer support, social validation, or external cheering — positioned as a diagnostic signal that you are on the right path rather than a problem to solve.

name: Protect Your Passion
definition: A discipline of actively preserving enthusiasm for one's work during the low-reward early phase, because passion destroyed before compounding kicks in inverts the effort-reward relationship at precisely the time when effort has the highest return.

name: Epic Story Razor
definition: A personal decision heuristic: when choosing between paths, default to whichever option produces the most compelling long-arc narrative, on the reasoning that the most epic story is almost never the shortest path to victory.

name: Map-Territory Distinction
definition: Economic models (maps) abstract from reality (territory); the information omitted from the model is often more important than what the model contains.

name: Close Rate to Price Multiple Ladder
definition: A tiered rule-of-thumb mapping sales close rates to implied pricing multiples, used to diagnose whether a business is underpriced relative to demand.

name: LTV:CAC Human-in-Loop Multiplier
definition: A framework for setting minimum LTV-to-CAC ratio targets based on how many of three business functions (attraction, conversion, delivery) involve a human, scaling from 3:1 (all automated) to 12:1 (all human).

name: 30-Day Cash Collected Rule
definition: A cash-flow rule requiring that gross profit collected within the first 30 days of a new customer relationship exceeds the sum of CAC plus COGS, enabling a self-funding acquisition loop.

name: Darwinian Costly Signalling Framework
definition: Signalling only carries information when it is costly (in resources or difficulty); low-cost signals are ignored or discounted by receivers because they cannot distinguish fit from unfit.

name: Guppy Three-Stage Mate-Selection Heuristic
definition: Female guppies apply a three-stage decision tree: (1) choose the 50%-larger male by size; (2) if sizes are close, choose the more-orange male; (3) if coloring is similar, apply social proof and choose the male observed mating with a peer.

name: Clouds-and-Clocks Spectrum
definition: Karl Popper's taxonomy positioning phenomena on a spectrum from clouds (complex, emergent, unpredictable: markets, ecosystems) to clocks (mechanistic, mathematically modelable: bridges, engines); the gravest intellectual error is treating clouds as clocks.

name: School Bias Toward False Rationality
definition: Educational systems teach two apparently distinct subject categories—exact sciences (maths, physics, chemistry) with apparent single answers, and arts with inherent ambiguity—creating a false perception that rationality requires mathematical models with provably single answers.

name: Creator Risk Continuum
definition: A spectrum from low-risk to high-risk creator types (entertainer -> B2C educator -> B2B prosumer -> B2B expert) where risk is defined by the potential downside to the consumer of acting on the advice; AI disrupts low-risk types first and high-risk types last.

name: Self-Linking Business Loop
definition: An engineered business motion in which the delivery of the core product or service generates marketing proof automatically, which in turn acquires more customers, creating a compounding self-reinforcing cycle.

name: Always Invert Framework
definition: A decision discipline attributed by Rory Sutherland to Charlie Munger: for any dominant assumption, actively construct and test the opposite hypothesis before accepting the consensus view.
concept: Contrarian Conviction as Outsized Return Driver

name: Physical Fallacy
definition: A cognitive bias named by Steven Pinker in which people systematically assign lower value to intangible goods and services than to physical ones, even when the intangible creates equivalent or greater utility.

name: Anti-Fragility Economic Model
definition: Nassim Taleb's framework arguing that complex systems including economies are strengthened by frequent mild stressors; suppressing those stressors creates fragility and eventual catastrophic failure.

name: Discount Plus One-Time Fee Structure
definition: A two-part offer that charges a deeply discounted first term to lower acquisition friction, then adds one or more separately named one-time fees to fund commissions and reduce churn.

name: Four-Step One-Time Fee Creation
definition: A four-step process to create any made-up fee: (1) pick fee name, (2) pick fee price, (3) pick reason why, (4) start charging, discounting, or waiving it.

name: Desire-Reason Framework
definition: Sustainable achievement requires both a strong desire for the outcome and a deep, compelling reason why that outcome matters; desire alone without reason causes quitting; reason alone without desire lacks motivation.

name: Newtonian Physics vs. Human Perception Frame
definition: The erroneous assumption that humans respond to objective, measurable reality causes a monumental misdirection of effort in design and marketing; the correct frame is that humans respond to perceived, contextual, and emotional reality — not physical metrics.

name: Sonic Identity as Brand Property
definition: A named musical or jingle identity functions as a superpower brand property with measurable recognition, familiarity, and reassurance value — distinct from and often outperforming verbal or visual brand assets.

name: Occasion-Driven Price Perception
definition: The value customers perceive in a purchase depends on the significance of the occasion, not the product's intrinsic properties; occasion context justifies premium pricing that would appear unreasonable in ordinary contexts.

name: Pareto Pricing Tier Framework
definition: Four price tiers with 5-10x gaps between each level; expect approximately 20% of customers at each tier to take the next step up; top tiers generate the majority of profit despite minority of customers.
concept: Pareto Pricing: Four-Tier Structure at 5-10x Gaps

name: Rider and Elephant (Haidt)
definition: Jonathan Haidt's metaphor: the elephant is System 1 (instinctive, habitual, non-verbal), the rider is System 2 (conscious, rational, verbal). The rider believes he controls the elephant but mostly post-rationalizes what the elephant has already decided; the rider is the Press Office, not the Oval Office.

name: Acquisition Utility vs Transaction Utility (Thaler)
definition: Richard Thaler's two-component model of purchase psychology: acquisition utility is the subjective value of owning or consuming the thing; transaction utility is the emotional quality of the purchase act itself (fairness, guilt, pleasure). A product can have high acquisition utility but low transaction utility, explaining why people want things they feel unable to buy.

name: Defensive Decision-Making (Minimax)
definition: A decision bias in which individuals unconsciously choose options that minimize worst-case personal embarrassment rather than maximize expected value. The operative question is not 'what is the best outcome?' but 'in the worst case, to what extent will I look like an idiot?' Leads to systematic over-reliance on defaults.

name: Replace-Not-Scale Partner Sequencing
definition: When a partner portfolio has low-quality or legally gray clients, the path to growth is replacing the six existing clients with six higher-quality ones before attempting volume expansion.

name: R&D Distribution Model
definition: A monthly R&D process where the operator selects 10-20 representative accounts from the distribution base, assigns a fixed budget to test one pressing problem, and releases results to the full base monthly regardless of outcome.

name: Must Be Easy Diagnostic
definition: The phrase 'it must be easy' is a reliable surface signal of victim-mindset; its presence indicates the speaker is externalizing inadequacy onto circumstances rather than accepting agency.

name: Four Buyer Screening Criteria
definition: Four non-negotiable attributes of a market before entry: audience is in pain, easy to identify, has money to spend, and the market is growing.

name: Marketing Method-Platform-Media-Volume Hierarchy
definition: Four-layer decomposition of customer acquisition: method (paid ads, content, outreach, affiliates), platform (Facebook, email, YouTube, Google), media type within platform (stories, posts, reels, DMs), and volume executed within media.

name: Pyramid of Markets Expansion
definition: Five directional vectors for market expansion: up-market (fewer, higher-spend customers), down-market (more volume customers), adjacent (similar business characteristics), broader (entire psychographic), or narrower (hyper-specific niches).

name: Problems vs. Missed Opportunities Classification
definition: A two-bucket classification system separating threats to business survival (problems) from growth-positive additions (missed opportunities); problems must be solved before pursuing opportunities.

name: Four-Step Hypothesis Testing Loop
definition: A four-step business problem-solving loop: (1) define current state vs. desired state, (2) state hypothesis action, (3) track before/after data, (4) evaluate whether expected outcome occurred.

name: Signal vs. Noise Data Filter
definition: A filter for business data: any metric that, when it changes, does not trigger a change in behavior is noise and should be removed from dashboards and meetings.

name: The Season of No Framework
definition: A defined time period of extreme focus where the founder says no to nearly all discretionary commitments (social events, side projects, family obligations) in order to concentrate all energy on the single most important business goal, enabling rapid compounding without distraction.

name: Warren Buffett's Goal Prioritization Method
definition: Write 25 goals in ranked order, circle the top five, throw away everything else; during a season of no, execute solely against the single most critical of those five goals while maintaining minimum non-regression effort on the others.

name: The Opportunity-Cost Frame
definition: Reframe yeses to other people as withdrawals from a personal energy account and nos as deposits into a goal account, making the zero-sum trade-off explicit and emotionally tangible.

name: Eleven Rules of Profitable Irrationality
definition: A structured set of eleven principles (with invited extension) for generating competitive advantage by being less logical than competitors, covering contrarian logic, system complexity, psychological reframing, and empirical experimentation.

name: Adaptive Preference Formation
definition: A psychological mechanism by which people forced to choose option A over B construct a narrative in which they prefer A anyway, minimizing regret — exploitable in product and choice architecture design to manufacture net utility from nothing.

name: Triangle Framework for Non-Performance
definition: A three-vertex diagnostic tool (adapted from Andy Grove and Layla Hormozi) that isolates the root cause of any employee non-performance: (1) they don't know the expectation was set, (2) they don't know how to perform it, or (3) they are not motivated to perform it.

name: Three Macro Opportunity Waves
definition: A sequence of three platform-level macro opportunities — Internet, Web 2.0 (social), and AI — each spawning sub-layer micro opportunities (e.g., Google Search, Facebook Ads, TikTok Shop) with outsized early-mover returns before market stabilization.

name: Big Hairy Problem Framework
definition: A method for identifying and valuing the single constraint blocking a business from its next revenue tier, then framing its enterprise-value unlock as motivation to solve it despite uncertainty.

name: Good Hard vs. Bad Hard Distinction
definition: A decision rule: push when underlying assumptions remain valid and only execution is lacking (good hard); pivot when a core assumption is proven false by evidence (bad hard).

name: Business You Are Really In
definition: A diagnostic exercise in which a founder identifies the true economic mechanism of their business (e.g., sales vs. fitness, brand vs. product quality) by studying what operators who are 100 steps ahead actually optimize for.

name: Need-to-Believe Assumptions Test
definition: Before a major investment, list the minimum assumptions that must be true for the investment to produce the desired outcome; continue if assumptions hold, pivot if any is disproved by data.

name: Entrepreneurship Video-Game Level Model
definition: A progression model in which each stage of business growth requires a distinct skill set; entrepreneurs who skip levels or switch businesses before mastering a level carry that unsolved level into the next venture.

name: Blended ROI Channel Evaluation
definition: Evaluating marketing channels by blended return rather than transaction-proximity ROI: a channel ranks high when it captures new attention AND nurtures existing audience, not merely when it sits closest to purchase.

name: Shorts as Ads to Longs
definition: Short-form content functions as top-of-funnel advertising whose goal is to drive audiences into longer-form content with greater total time-on-brand, not to serve as the primary engagement vehicle.

name: CLOSER Framework
definition: A six-step sales call structure: Clarify why they are here, Label them with their problem, Overview past pain, Sell the vacation (dream outcome), Explain away concerns (objections), Reinforce the decision post-purchase.

name: AAA Objection Method
definition: Three-step objection response: Acknowledge what the prospect said (builds rapport, buys time), Associate with something positive or a foil success story, Ask the next question to advance the sale.

name: BANT Qualification
definition: IBM-originated lead qualification framework requiring four conditions before a lead reaches a closer: Budget (funds available), Authority (decision-making power), Need (problem to solve), Timing (ready to start soon).

name: Three-Pillar Pitch
definition: A product pitch structured around exactly three load-bearing value pillars, each illustrated with a metaphor or analogy, designed to diagnose which pillar previous solutions lacked and position the seller as the complete solution.

name: Proof Promise Plan Opener
definition: A 15-20 second sales call opener that establishes social proof (we have done this for people like you), states the promise (what outcome we will work toward), and lays out the plan (what the call will look like), mirroring content hook structure.

name: Four Wealth Accumulation Strategies (V1-V4)
definition: Four progressively more leveraged paths to a target net worth: V1 pure income, V2 income plus public equity reinvestment, V3 income plus private business sale, V4 income plus retained ownership with liquidity via ESOP, dividend recap, or public stock loans.

name: Three Fallacies of Warren Buffett
definition: Three conditions that made Warren Buffett's compounding strategy unreplicable: buying his first stock at age 7 during the Pearl Harbor crash, living through the greatest growth era in American history, and survivorship luck among equally skilled investors.

name: Measuring Sticks Mental Model
