definition: A mental model in which wealthy people measure opportunity value in larger units (millions, not hundreds) and over longer time horizons than middle-class peers; the unit of measure determines which opportunities one is even capable of considering.

name: Supply-First Growth Sequence
definition: A four-to-five step prioritization sequence for operationally constrained service businesses: (1) fix supply constraint via offshoring for 2-3x delivery leverage, (2) add data architecture layer, (3) add AI layer on top of data, (4) re-open sales once new capacity is proven, (5) use existing marketing assets to grow demand.

name: Proof-Promise-Plan Intro Framework
definition: A three-part opening structure for webinars and sales presentations: Proof (a result for someone like the prospect), Promise (exactly what they will get), Plan (expectations for the session duration and flow). Used at both webinar and sales call opening.

name: Value Equation
definition: Four-lever framework for maximizing perceived offer value: maximize Dream Outcome, decrease Risk (use proof), decrease Time (show speed), decrease Hard (show ease).

name: Three-Pillar Pitch
definition: A pitch structure that condenses a multi-step process into three named buckets; complexity of the presentation scales inversely with buyer implementation burden — simpler for DIY/DWY, more steps for DFY.

name: Value Equation
definition: A four-factor model for evaluating offer attractiveness: Dream Outcome x Perceived Likelihood of Achievement / Time Delay x Effort and Sacrifice. Increasing the numerator or decreasing the denominator increases perceived value.

name: Quarterly Cleanup
definition: A recurring email monetization cadence (once per quarter) that routes non-buyers through a freshly named challenge or lead magnet, varying the wrapper while keeping the core offer constant, to extract latent revenue from an existing list without fatiguing it.

name: Value Equation
definition: A four-variable formula for product value: (Dream Outcome x Perceived Likelihood of Achievement) / (Time Delay x Effort and Sacrifice). Top variables create value; bottom variables destroy it.

name: Four Types of Guarantees
definition: A taxonomy of risk-reversal structures: (1) Unconditional, (2) Conditional, (3) Anti-Guarantee, (4) Implied/Performance-Based; can be stacked for maximum conversion.

name: Trim and Stack
definition: A value-engineering process: list every customer problem and solution, rank by customer-value and incremental cost to deliver, then keep only high-value/low-incremental-cost items.

name: Review Growth Loop
definition: A self-reinforcing flywheel in which founder effort converts to customers, customers get results, results generate reviews and word-of-mouth, and those reviews attract new customers without requiring continued founder investment at each cycle.

name: Four Review Generation Tactics
definition: A four-method system for generating reviews: (1) surprise gift plus third-party ask, (2) branded merch exchange, (3) point-of-sale discount, (4) unlockable digital content or VIP service trial.

name: Value Equation
definition: Four-variable formula for offer value: dream outcome, perceived likelihood of achievement, speed of delivery, and ease of delivery — increasing each raises willingness to pay.

name: Virtuous Cycle of Price
definition: Raising price increases buyer emotional investment, which increases perceived value, which improves results, which reduces demands, which frees margin for reinvestment — a self-reinforcing loop opposite to commodity price competition.

name: Starving Crowd Market Selection
definition: Four-criterion market filter: pain (urgent problem), purchasing power (money to spend), ease of targeting (aggregated in findable channels), and growth trajectory (market expanding, not shrinking).
concept: Market Selection Criteria: Growth + Pain + Targeting

name: Three Steps to an Unstoppable Business
definition: A sequential framework: (1) stop selling small/volatile customers, (2) ask customers what they want rather than assume, (3) resist the temptation to relabel or reinvent the business model.

name: Market Pyramid Top-Down Structuring
definition: Structure your customer acquisition from the top of the spending-power pyramid (enterprise/Fortune 100) downward; serve high tiers first, then use brand credibility and margin to subsidize progressively lower tiers with automated, near-zero-cost delivery.

name: Rank and Build vs. Reverse-Engineered Product Strategy
definition: Two product-iteration models: (1) Rank-and-Build (PC model) lets customers vote features up/down and builds the top request each cycle, accumulating features but risking Frankenstein complexity; (2) Reverse-Engineered (Mac model) begins from the ideal end experience and deliberately removes features that conflict with it, yielding elegant simplicity at the cost of configurability.

name: Best-Customer Behavior Codification Loop
definition: A four-step product improvement loop: (1) survey to identify which customers get the best results, (2) interview them to find differentiating behaviors and demographics, (3) force new customers to repeat those behaviors deliberately, (4) tie guarantee conditions to those behaviors to incentivize compliance.

name: Paid Street-Solicitor Review Acquisition Method
definition: A three-step review acquisition system: (1) recruit locally-based workers who need money via Facebook groups or Reddit, (2) deploy them to high-density public venues (malls, college campuses) to approach strangers, and (3) pay per review collected (~$2/review), optionally augmenting with physical incentives (Gatorade, candy) to raise consent rates.

name: Review Pyramid Scheme
definition: A multi-level referral structure where a single motivated recruiter (typically age 13-18) earns $2 per review and $0.50 per review generated by each sub-recruiter they bring in, compounding review acquisition without founder effort.

name: Reverse-Engineer Your Enjoyment
definition: A two-step creator sustainability framework: (1) identify which content formats you genuinely enjoy making, (2) capture yourself doing activities you already enjoy — then build your publishing schedule around that intersection rather than around algorithmic or audience expectations.

name: One True Lever Test
definition: A focus-finding exercise: ask which single thing, if true in one year, would 10x the company and make all other goals follow automatically.

name: Business Success Recipe
definition: A sequential chain: make promises -> keep promises -> build brand -> use brand for premium pricing -> use extra profits to hire better and add acquisition channels -> give equity slices to grow the total pie -> add time.

name: Elephant and Rider Framework
definition: Jonathan Haidt's metaphor adopted by Rory Sutherland: the elephant is System 1 (automatic, instinctive, wordless) and the rider is System 2 (conscious, rational, verbal); the rider thinks he controls the elephant but mostly post-rationalizes what the elephant already decided.

name: Acquisition Value vs Transaction Utility
definition: Richard Thaler's two-component purchase model: acquisition value is the objective benefit from owning or consuming the product; transaction utility is the emotional quality of the purchase act itself (fair deal vs. rip-off feeling), which can independently drive or block purchase independent of product quality.

name: Harvesting vs Hunting Optimum
definition: An organisation (like a bee colony) needs an optimal mix of harvesting (efficient exploitation of known opportunities, ~80%) and hunting (exploratory, higher-failure-rate search for new opportunities, ~20%); 100% harvesting leads to starvation when conditions change, because rogue explorers are the adaptive mechanism.

name: Dynamic Packaging
definition: A product structure that combines the flexibility of self-assembled travel booking with the legal protection of a package holiday, allowing customers to choose components (e.g. Ryanair flights + TUI hotel) within a single booking flow that confers package-holiday consumer rights.

name: Cross-Category Analysis
definition: An agency technique in which the practitioner deliberately ignores the client's own category and asks how a company from a completely different sector (e.g. Disney, airlines) would solve the same problem, surfacing insights that category-insider operators are blind to.

name: Community-First, Monetize-Second Launch Sequence
definition: Build audience and community at full intensity before monetizing the product; low-effort early monetization is acceptable if community-building is full-throttle.

name: Brand Name Ownership Test
definition: A brand name passes if it: (1) is one syllable or highly memorable, (2) owns first-page search results on Google, (3) secures matching social handles, (4) carries independent cultural/dictionary meaning beyond the product category.

name: Discipline-as-Freedom Reframe
definition: A mental model holding that discipline — controlling vices, emotions, and cravings — produces actual freedom (options, access), while unconstrained indulgence produces controlled servitude to those impulses.

name: Get-vs-Give Substance Filter
definition: A single evaluative question applied to any recurring input — alcohol, nicotine, social media, entertainment — to decide whether continued use is net-positive: 'Am I getting more out of that thing than that thing is getting out of me?'

name: Mystery as Power Rule
definition: A social strategy in which a businessperson limits contact time with prospects and counterparties to the minimum needed to deliver their message, preserving the other party's imagination space and preventing chaotic over-exposure from eroding conviction.

name: Five Review Failure Modes
definition: Five categories of review-acquisition tactics that Google's AI reliably detects and deletes: offshore accounts, non-local accounts, double-reviews on same Gmail, bulk new Gmail accounts, and same-device-same-WiFi sessions.

name: Three Sticking-Review Channels
definition: Three channels the speaker validated as producing reviews that survive Google's detection: (1) purchased same-country Gmail accounts used one-review-per-device, (2) in-person incentivized review solicitation at high-traffic public venues, (3) virtual-assistant-driven online group outreach using review-for-review exchange.

name: The Belgian Problem
definition: When marketing succeeds, observers cease to call it marketing; they attribute success to product quality, invention, or inherent advantage, making marketing's role invisible even when it was decisive.

name: Exploit vs. Explore Bee Model
definition: Optimal resource-collection systems allocate roughly 20% of agents to random exploration (finding new sources) and 80% to exploitation (harvesting known sources); 100% exploitation traps the system in a local maximum when the known source dries up.

name: Behaviour Menu for Sustainable Change
definition: A menu of ~20 ranked environmental actions (small/medium/large) from which individuals choose a personal selection each year, allowing participation calibrated to personal circumstance rather than universal mandates.

name: Rearview Mirror Competitive Strategy
definition: Two-principle competitive posture: ignore competitors ranked below you entirely, and use maximum operational speed as the primary defense against those behind you.

name: Influencer Validity-Plus-Reach Model
definition: Influencer marketing delivers two simultaneous assets: reach (raw audience size exposed to the product) and validity (the transfer of the influencer's personal credibility to the brand).

name: Brand Block Retail Strategy
definition: Cluster all SKUs of a brand together in a single shelf section (brand block) backed by a proprietary branded display unit (corrugate or end cap) rather than dispersing products across category sections, creating a branded mini-store within the retailer.

name: Google Business Profile Verification Methods
definition: Three standard verification paths (phone code, email code, business video) with an undisclosed fourth method (live video call) that is operationally easier and more reliable.

name: Live Video Call Verification Process
definition: A multi-step framework for accessing and completing Google Business Profile verification via live agent interaction, requiring minimal documentation and proof of legitimacy.

name: Database-First Reactivation Sequence
definition: Before running any paid ads, re-engage existing lead databases and active members for reviews and referrals; use those results to build trust and organically improve ad performance before investing in cold marketing.
concept: Fast Cash Plays via Underutilized Assets

name: Five-Point AI Agency Pitch Structure
definition: A five-part done-for-you offer pitched sequentially: (1) database reactivation via AI, (2) review and referral automation for members, (3) targeted paid ad marketing with landing pages, (4) AI-powered lead nurture and follow-up, (5) inbound call tracking and AI answering to capture missed organic prospects.

name: Clarity-First Sales Positioning
definition: Pitch only one or two simple, clear outcomes on the first call to minimize decision complexity; upsell additional services only after delivering initial results and building trust, because clarity drives faster purchase decisions.

name: Five Stages of Business Scaling
definition: A five-stage progression from solo operator to legacy business: Treadmill (solopreneur, no delegation) -> Pathfinder (chaos, first hires) -> Trailblazer (strategic thought, first leadership layer) -> [unnamed fourth] -> Legacy (succession, bench depth, family office mentality); each stage has specific drivers to unlock the next.

name: Six Drivers of Business Growth
definition: Six recurring drivers (starting with personal growth, purpose and people, and profit planning) that cycle through all five scaling stages; Ramsey Solutions has cycled through them 10-15 times across its five scaling stages.

name: Special Projects Incubator
definition: An internal shark-tank committee for ideas without a home, covering two workstreams: (1) fixing broken existing profit centers and (2) incubating new orphan ideas through beta; graduated ideas are dropped into existing business units or spun as new profit centers.

name: Drop Low or Go High Framework
definition: For client-acquisition agencies serving SMBs, the only viable business models are ultra-cheap high-automation or high-touch premium; the mid-market is a dead zone where margin compresses to zero.

name: Supply-First Scaling Sequence
definition: When supply (capacity) is the binding constraint, the operational fix order is: (1) fix pricing/packaging to free cash flow, (2) deploy cash into paid ads with attribution, (3) invest freed margin into content/thought leadership.

name: Talent Funnel as Parallel Demand Funnel
definition: A sales organization must build a mirror talent-acquisition funnel (applicant generation, nurture, interviewing, onboarding, retention/ascension) that receives the same budget discipline as the customer demand funnel.

name: Input-Output Equation Framework
definition: Identify the single high-volume input action that produces the desired skill or output, then maximize the quantity of that input while eliminating all interference.

name: Solomon Dialogue Method
definition: A self-advisory practice in which the founder writes alternating dialogue between present-self and a wiser future-self in a timestamped Google Doc to resolve high-stakes decisions with fully aligned incentives and no information-sharing cost.

name: Useful-Over-Happy Frame
definition: Replace happiness as a daily goal with usefulness to others; usefulness is measurable, externally verifiable, and requires both self-improvement and service, creating a self-reinforcing loop.

name: Process Approximation Career Navigation
definition: Instead of seeking the perfect career pick, make a directional choice (words vs. numbers), iterate toward specificity, and treat every prior domain as a skill investment that transfers uniquely to the next domain.

name: Stress Management Through Perspective Shift
definition: A three-step cognitive framework for decoupling internal feelings from external circumstances: identify the trigger, label the judgment, and insert space between feeling and behavior.

name: Growth Pains Normalization Framework
definition: Framing business growth discomfort as expected and statistical rather than as evidence of failure; normalizing the heightened difficulty as evidence of success.

name: Three Lead Magnet Types
definition: A taxonomy of lead magnets: (1) Reveal a problem — surface a problem the prospect didn't know was bad; (2) Free trial — give the solution then remove it to create deprivation; (3) One step of many — solve the first step of a multi-step process that your core offer completes.

name: Four Lead Magnet Delivery Formats
definition: Four delivery vehicles for lead magnets: software/tools, information (guides, courses, templates), services (done-for-you work for qualified prospects), and physical products; combinations are permitted and often more compelling.

name: Lead Magnet Naming Conventions
definition: Four headline formulas that increase lead magnet opt-in rates: (1) Number + outcome + timeframe; (2) How to X without Y even if Z; (3) Adjective + type + outcome; (4) X mistakes that prevent good thing.

name: CTA Formula (Clear-Action-Reason)
definition: A three-part call-to-action structure: (1) clear directive (not clever), (2) exact next action, (3) a reason to act now — any reason outperforms no reason, with genuine scarcity or urgency being strongest.

name: SPCL Influence Framework
definition: Four independent but combinable components of influence: Status (control of reinforcers), Power (say-do correspondence), Credibility (third-party proof), and Likeness (similarity to audience).

name: Management Diamond
definition: A five-cause diagnostic for why an employee (or entrepreneur) is not executing a task: they did not know the task was required, did not know how to do it, did not know the deadline, had a blocking constraint, or did not want to do it — in that order of actual frequency.
concept: The Execution Gap: Knowledge Without Action

name: Declarative vs. Procedural Content Split
definition: Free content teaches declarative knowledge (about how something works — what you use to sell); paid products deliver procedural knowledge (how to execute — what you sell). Mixing them causes either free riders or stalled purchases.

name: ACA Framework
definition: A three-step warm-outreach conversation sequence: Acknowledge something true about the person, Compliment them on it, then Ask a question that ties to the compliment and transitions toward the service being sold.

name: 10-Step First Customer Acquisition System
definition: A staged process for getting first paying customers from zero: build contact lists from email/social/phone, pick a platform, personalize outreach, send at volume, warm via ACA, invite referrals, offer free service, restart the list, raise price incrementally, and maintain list warmth ongoing.

name: Bow Tie Business Model
definition: Business structure modeled as a bow tie: wide marketing/lead nurture funnel on the left narrows to a sale, then expands outward again through onboarding, CS, and upsells on the right; customer-side mirror image of the acquisition funnel.

name: BAMFAM (Book A Meeting From A Meeting)
definition: Operational standard that every customer interaction ends with a scheduled next touchpoint; no customer should ever exit a call without a confirmed future contact time.

name: Value Equation
definition: Four-variable model determining perceived value: dream outcome, perceived likelihood of achievement, time delay, and effort and sacrifice. Any customer complaint maps to degradation of one or more of these variables.

name: Baton Pass Handoff
definition: Sequential single-point-of-contact model where each team member (sales rep, onboarding rep, account rep) formally introduces the next before exiting the customer relationship; prevents no-man's-land between departments.

name: Choke Point Pre-Mortem
definition: Before a high-stakes live event, enumerate every discrete failure mode in priority order and build a pre-assigned fallback for each one before the event begins.

name: $100M Series Stacking Architecture
definition: A three-book product series structured so each book layers one additional skill on top of the previous (Offer -> Leads -> Money Models), written originally as one work and intentionally parsed into sequential volumes.

name: Logic-Evidence-Utility Problem Definition
definition: A three-question diagnostic sequence for validating any problem statement: What does it mean? How do you know? Why do I care? Forces specificity before prescribing solutions.

name: Good Friction vs Bad Friction
definition: A qualification framework distinguishing friction that removes bad-fit leads and improves sales efficiency (good friction) from friction that blocks all leads indiscriminately (bad friction). Adding good friction increases ROAS and sales efficiency simultaneously.

name: Checklist-Driven Sales Ops
definition: A complete list of sales operations requirements (scripting, daily training, cultural enforcement, manager accountability) where executing the full checklist produces consistent results and any gap identifies the leader as the constraint.

name: Group-Audition Hiring Funnel
definition: A four-stage sales-rep hiring process: send script before interview, request a 60-second video audition, invite finalists to a group drill call for coachability scoring, then make job offers only to those who pass all stages.

name: Barrels and Bullets Framework
definition: A mental model distinguishing between high-capacity founders who can build things from nothing (barrels) and resources/people that need to be loaded into those founders to produce output (bullets); business scale is rate-limited by the number of barrels, not the volume of bullets.

name: I Got It Accountability System
definition: A three-word commitment phrase that transfers full ownership of a task or domain from manager to employee; effective only when paired with 100% say-do ratio and proactive repair when the commitment is missed.

name: Acquisition.com Evolution Phases
definition: A three-phase arc: 1.0 = helping Acquisition.com itself directly; 2.0 = helping Acquisition.com directly and helping others indirectly (via content/documentation); 3.0 = helping Acquisition.com directly and helping external businesses directly.

name: Distribution Node Acquisition Model
definition: Instead of tracking end-customer acquisition, count the number of distribution partners (agencies, producers) onboarded per month, treating each as a recurring referral node whose compounding output replaces the episodic churn of direct customer sales.

name: Two-Sided Education Monetization
definition: For certification test-prep businesses, monetize both sides of the supply-demand curve: charge students for test prep and charge universities/employers for career placement, so the same student cohort generates two revenue streams.

name: Four Website Conversion Pillars
definition: A drop-servicing website must satisfy four criteria in priority order: (1) simplicity of navigation, (2) density of call-to-action prompts, (3) visible trust signals, (4) load speed under 4 seconds.

name: Drop-Servicing via Google Business Profile
definition: A zero-capital local-service arbitrage model: rank a Google Business Profile for a high-demand local service, accept inbound calls, subcontract jobs to independent contractors at their rate, and collect a 30-40% markup from the customer.

name: GMB Ranking Stack
definition: Three-element sequence for topping Google Maps results: (1) keyword-match business name, (2) review count matching top-3 incumbents, (3) fully SEO-optimized profile sections written by ChatGPT.

name: Inspection-Commit Close
definition: Instead of quoting over the phone, charge a small inspection fee ($60) that is waived if the customer proceeds; once a prospect pays the inspection fee they almost always proceed, because abandoning wastes their sunk commitment.

name: Brand Pairing Flywheel
definition: A four-step loop: start with a brand that means nothing, pair it deliberately with people or experiences ideal customers like, the brand inherits that meaning, customers buy to associate themselves with that meaning.

name: Advertising vs. Branding Distinction
definition: Advertising is letting people know about your product (reach/awareness); branding is the pairing and meaning that occurs as a result of that exposure. Good advertising can produce bad branding if the pairing is disliked by the target audience.

name: Galapagos Islands Loyalty Framework
definition: A loyalty program treated as a behavioral observation environment: combining longitudinal individual-level data with a psychologist's mindset to surface anomalies, paradoxes, and small-effect insights that reveal how humans actually decide, as distinct from how economists assume they decide.

name: Explore-Exploit Trade-off (Bee Waggle Dance Model)
definition: A resource-allocation framework in which roughly 20% of effort is devoted to random exploration of unknown opportunities (ignoring the waggle dance) and 80% exploits known reliable sources; pure exploitation produces local-maximum traps and eventual extinction.

name: SCARF Model (David Rock)
definition: Five dimensions humans deeply care about that economic data never captures: Status, Certainty, Autonomy, Relatedness, Fairness; marketing and loyalty programs that address these create engagement that price discounts cannot replicate.

name: Consumable Input Framework
definition: A community offer has two separable components: (1) a one-time method/knowledge transfer and (2) recurring consumable inputs that the community must refresh each period. Retention and recurring revenue attach to the consumable layer, not to the knowledge layer.

name: TWATS Office Model
definition: A weekly partitioning structure where Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday are dedicated to face-to-face office work, with Monday and Friday reserved for location-independent individual work.

name: Maker Schedule vs Manager Schedule
definition: Paul Graham's distinction between managers (who optimize for maximum meeting density) and makers (who require large uninterrupted time blocks to produce creative or technical work), making half-hour meeting interruptions disproportionately costly for makers.

name: Five Business Advantages Framework
definition: A five-factor scoring system (Sticky, Expensive, Expanding, Air/Low-OpEx, Unique) for evaluating and ranking the quality of a business opportunity vehicle; having even one advantage makes a business better than peers.

name: One of Zero vs. One of One
definition: A brand-philosophy distinction: One of One means doing only what you can do; One of Zero means doing what no one else would do, operating beyond definition and conventional expectations.

name: Operationalized Emotion Definitions
definition: A method of converting amorphous emotional concepts (love, patience, confidence) into observable, measurable behavioral proxies to make them actionable rather than vague.

name: Roles-to-Workflows Shift
definition: Replace role-based hiring decisions (I need an editor) with workflow-based decomposition (I need an agent for task X, an agent for task Y) by mapping every business action at its most granular level until no further reduction is possible.

name: Linear Business Workflow Map
definition: A single continuous workflow diagram that traces every action in the business from first input (idea, inbound lead) to final output (posted content, closed deal); if you cannot draw it, the business lacks operational clarity.

name: Elon Musk Algorithm
definition: A five-step operational decision sequence: question all requirements, delete unnecessary requirements, optimize what remains, accelerate, then automate.

name: Barbell Reality Bifurcation
definition: As AI-generated content saturates the middle, market demand splits between fully synthetic/fake and hyper-authentic/real; businesses that occupy the middle suffer while the two poles win.

name: Physics-as-Upper-Bound Standard
definition: Treat physical laws as the only legitimate ceiling on what a business can achieve; all other limitations are industry conventions that a sufficiently determined actor can override.

name: Attack-Vector Multiplicity Standard
definition: Measure the quality of someone's standards by how many distinct approaches they deploy toward a single goal before declaring it impossible; breadth of attack vectors proxies the height of standards.

name: Spell Out the Trade
definition: A decision-making method that forces explicit articulation of both sides of a hard trade-off so the chooser knows exactly what they are paying and what they are getting before committing.

name: Magnifying Glass Focus Model
definition: Potential and work ethic are analogous to the size of a magnifying glass capturing sunlight; the output (heat/fire) only materializes when focus is concentrated on a single point, regardless of how large the lens is.

name: 20% Change-Cost Rule
definition: Any business process change produces a guaranteed ~20% temporary decrement in performance before improvement; changes are only justified when the risk-adjusted expected gain exceeds 20% (i.e., a 40%+ improvement with at least 50-50 odds).

name: Big List of Ideas
definition: A running written list of improvement ideas maintained by the founder, with estimated value and probability attached to each; no idea is acted on immediately — ideas are reviewed later for survivability, and only the highest-ranked ideas are executed when the team has bandwidth.

name: Price Presentation vs. Product Essence
definition: A product's worth is determined not by its intrinsic qualities but by how it is presented and the emotional response it evokes in the customer.

name: Perceived Value Through Scarcity and Exclusivity
definition: Discounts and value propositions feel more valuable when they appear scarce, exclusive, and difficult to obtain (idiosyncratic fit), independent of actual monetary savings.

name: Circle of Competence (Buffett)
definition: Focus career choices on what you understand best rather than what excites you; passion follows demonstrated competence, not the reverse.

name: Three Stonecutters Framework
definition: The same work can be experienced as a job, a career, or a calling depending solely on the meaning the worker assigns to it; purpose reframes identical effort into radically different experiences.

name: Rule of 100
definition: Do 100 repetitions of the core skill-building action per day; when full-cycle repetition is impractical, do 3+ full run-throughs per day with recorded feedback loops.

name: GBP Ranking Factors (Most to Least Important)
definition: A four-factor ordered hierarchy governing Google Business Profile ranking and call volume: (1) review count, (2) average star rating, (3) title SEO keyword match, (4) on-page description SEO and website quality.

name: Mortality Clarity Algorithm
definition: Using the certainty of death as a decision-making filter to strip away other people's expectations and identify which choices truly serve the self.

name: Subjective Well-Being Smiley Face Curve
definition: A U-shaped model of life satisfaction across age cohorts: high at age 7, dropping through the 20s-30s, bottoming near 45, then recovering sharply in the 55-60+ range as mortality awareness dissolves external expectations.

name: Inversion for Joy Discovery
definition: Identify what would maximally destroy one's life, then reverse each item; used as a practical substitute for directly answering the harder question of what brings joy.

name: Capital M vs. Little m Meaning
definition: A framework distinguishing universal imposed meaning (capital M, e.g., religious doctrine) from self-created meaning (little m, e.g., chosen purpose); the latter is more flexible and allows belief updates with new information.

name: Assumptions vs. Beliefs Identity Separation
definition: Framing beliefs as assumptions (which are data-dependent and changeable) rather than identity components, decoupling ego from information updates.

name: Logic-Evidence-Utility Problem-Solving Framework
definition: A three-question sequence for breaking down any problem: (1) What does this mean? (logic/definition), (2) How do we know? (evidence), (3) Why does it matter? (utility). Applied before any claim or diagnosis is accepted.

name: Any-Answer-Except-Call-Me Operator Test
definition: A role-play interview used to verify a GM candidate can handle operational crises (upset customer, facility emergency) without escalating to the owner; any response except calling the owner is the right answer.

name: Sell Warm Like Cold
definition: Apply the full cold-prospect qualification and credentialing process to every sale regardless of relationship warmth; warm prospects receive the same structured pitch as cold ones.
concept: Warm vs. Cold Sales Process Mismatch

name: Obliquity Framework
definition: Problems that have not yielded to logical solutions are precisely those that require counterintuitive, oblique, or tangential approaches; logical problems have mostly already been solved.

name: Centaur Theory (Human + AI)
definition: The optimal intelligent agent is a human plus a machine working together; the best chess player is not a machine but a human-machine pair, and this principle scales to everyday knowledge work.

name: Georgist Land Value Tax
definition: A taxation framework in which only the unimproved value of land is taxed (not labor or capital improvements), on the grounds that land value is created by collective action rather than individual effort, making its appreciation a form of rent-seeking rather than earned return.

name: Relationship Time-Horizon Framework
definition: The depth of a relationship is measured by how long both parties are willing to wait for the next positive exchange; shallow acquaintances have short horizons, deep friends have extended ones.

name: Friend Selection Criteria (Hormozi Three Standards)
definition: Alex Hormozi's personal criteria for a keeper friendship: (1) the person roots for you behind your back, (2) they give you honest critical feedback to your face, and (3) you admire them and want to grow toward some quality they embody.

name: Three-Option Objection Routing
definition: When a service objection blocks a client segment, route through three options in order: (1) sell through the objection, (2) redesign delivery to remove the objection, (3) restrict the target audience to those who lack the objection.

name: Fix-Then-Scale Sequencing
definition: Optimize unit economics and margins in existing locations before opening new ones; expansion funded by proven profitability, not ambition.

name: Sales Motion to Membership to Talent Ladder
definition: Three-stage repair sequence for stalled multi-location service businesses: (1) fix sales motion, (2) install membership model to maximize revenue per technician, (3) raise pay and build career paths to retain talent — in that order.

name: Product-as-Marketing Flywheel
definition: For media companies, every dollar spent on product (content) simultaneously generates marketing impressions, making product spend and marketing spend the same line item and creating compounding audience leverage.

name: Brand Premium Flywheel
definition: A small pricing premium on a commoditized product generates spread that is reinvested in branding, which raises perceived value, which enables a larger premium, which generates more spread — cycling indefinitely until a dominant brand position is established.

name: Friend Value Exchange Model
definition: Relationships are behavioral exchange systems where positive experiences reinforce continuation and absence of positive reinforcement leads to natural fizzling or explicit dissolution.

name: Seasonal Identity Shedding
definition: Life organized into 3-5 year seasons where previous identity labels are explicitly rejected and social circles are replaced to match new aspirations.

name: Community Leapfrog Path
definition: After friend pruning creates a vacuum, join communities with aligned goals; rise by understanding volume and time; gain status to access higher-tier communities; repeat across communities.

name: Three-Root-Cause Framework for Google Review Deletion
definition: Google reviews get deleted for three and only three root causes: (1) suspicious posting pattern (timing, wording similarity, velocity spike), (2) inauthentic account signals (new accounts, shared device or IP, foreign country), (3) obvious fakeness (common sense violations like all reviews from same geography or device).

name: Affiliate Launch and Integration
definition: Two-stage affiliate activation: Launch (get 10 referrals fast to create an internal case study) followed by Integration (embed the provider into the affiliate's standard onboarding so 100% of new clients flow through, not just whoever the affiliate chooses to refer).

name: Behavioral Definition of Learning
definition: Learning is operationally defined as same condition producing new behavior; if condition is held constant and behavior does not change, no learning has occurred regardless of content consumed.

name: Deprivation-Reference-Point Model of Motivation
definition: Motivation equals the inverse of perceived deprivation; for intangible constructs like money, deprivation is measured relative to a reference group, not absolute scarcity.

name: Replicate Before Iterate
definition: A two-phase learning discipline: in phase one, follow instructions exactly and replicate the teacher's results without modification; in phase two, only after replication is confirmed, apply accumulated knowledge to diverge and derive personal improvements.

name: Pareto Wealth Distribution Model
definition: Alex Hormozi maps U.S. household net worth as $100 across 100 percentiles to show that 1% of the population holds $32, more than the bottom 90% combined, and uses this to guide customer targeting decisions.

name: Four-Tier Pricing Ladder
definition: A pricing architecture with four tiers separated by 5–10x price jumps, expecting approximately 20% of customers to ascend each tier; each tier is designed to roughly double total revenue.
concept: Pareto Pricing: Four-Tier Structure at 5–10x Gaps

name: Close Rate as Pricing Diagnostic
definition: Alex Hormozi's rubric for diagnosing pricing power from observed close rates: 60–80% indicates 3–4x underpricing, 50–60% indicates 1.5–2x, 40–50% indicates 1.25–1.5x, 30–40% is correctly priced, below 30% indicates a sales or qualification problem.
concept: Close Rate as Pricing Calibration Signal

name: MAYA (Maximally Advanced Yet Acceptable)
definition: A product or design should be as novel as possible while remaining within the threshold of consumer acceptance; evolution is preferred over revolution because consumers migrate behavior rather than reinvent it.

name: Consistent-Distinctive-Famous Brand Framework
definition: Three-part brand-building framework: (1) be consistent across all touchpoints over time, (2) be distinctive in visual and experiential identity, and (3) pursue fame as a non-linear multiplier that changes the rules of every interaction.

name: Psychological-Technological-Economic Parallel Design
definition: Great products satisfy all three criteria simultaneously in parallel, not in series: works psychologically (people want it), works technologically (can be made), and works economically (can generate profit). Most companies run these in series, losing integration benefits.

name: Persian Dual-State Deliberation
definition: According to Herodotus, ancient Persians debated major decisions twice: once sober and once drunk. A decision was adopted only if it passed both states, ensuring it survived both rational scrutiny and emotional/intuitive review.

name: Prospect-Driven Sales Process
definition: A scalable sales structure in which the salesperson asks questions in a prescribed order to lead the prospect to their own purchase decision, rather than demonstrating expertise or authority.

name: Top-Down Business Launch Sequence
definition: Start with a high-price, limited-volume premium offering; use early profits and brand equity to fund progressively higher-volume, lower-price tiers; never enter from the bottom and attempt to move up.

name: Decision Reversibility and Impact Matrix
definition: A two-axis framework for evaluating big-life decisions by asking (1) how reversible is this decision and (2) how large is the long-term impact; decisions that are both low-reversibility and high-impact require proportionally deeper deliberation.

name: Business Department Majors Framework
definition: A proposed redesign of higher education in which majors map directly to functional business departments: marketing, sales, delivery (physical product or service), and supporting services (finance, HR, legal); each department maps to income-generating skills.

name: Identity Cluster Framework
definition: People adopt uniform identities that constrain their behavior and expression; uniqueness emerges from the tension between uniform identity and non-conforming beliefs held simultaneously.

name: ROAS Doom Loop
definition: A self-reinforcing trap in which DTC brands keep increasing ad spend to reach less profitable audiences, compressing margins further until revenue equals spend with no net gain.

name: CRO as Steroids
definition: Conversion-rate optimization yields a one-time lift (sometimes 2-3x) but establishes a new baseline rather than resolving the structural front-end traffic and brand deficit.

name: SPCL Influence Framework
definition: A four-component model for building content-based influence: Status (controlling scarce reinforcers), Power (say-do correspondence that produces positive outcomes), Credibility (observable third-party evidence), and Likeness (shared values, aesthetics, or demographic similarity). Components stack multiplicatively — each one independently creates influence, all four together create maximal compliance likelihood.

name: Product-as-Marketing Framework
definition: In businesses where discovery is dominated by word-of-mouth and reviews (e.g., restaurants), product quality and experience ARE the marketing spend; premium investment in ingredients, service, and environment replaces advertising as the primary acquisition lever.

name: Grand Opening Playbook
definition: A staged launch protocol for new physical locations: overstaff, run multi-channel ads, and deploy promotional giveaways (or exclusive invite-only events for premium concepts) to generate sufficient initial word-of-mouth so the location reaches full capacity within six months organically.

name: Sales Ops Checklist
definition: A complete list of sales operations requirements — daily training, script memorization, script enforcement, and manager accountability — that together produce consistent close rates; missing any items and you do not get the outcome.

name: Group Screening Funnel for Sales Reps
definition: A three-stage hiring filter for sales reps: (1) send script before interview and request 60-second video recitation; (2) invite passing candidates to a group coaching call and evaluate coachability under live feedback; (3) extend job offers only to those who demonstrated preparation and coachability.

name: Distraction Elimination Framework
definition: A two-category removal process targeting people (friends, family) and things (games, social media, food habits) that compete for attention, applied progressively until the only remaining option is work.

name: Five Market Direction Vectors
definition: Five directions a business can expand its market: up market (larger/wealthier segment), down market (more numerous/cheaper segment), adjacent (different vertical, same systems), broader (wider category), or narrower (tighter sub-niche).

name: Puddle-to-Ocean Niche Progression
definition: A staged market expansion model: start as the dominant player in a tiny niche (puddle), then move to a larger pond, then a lake, then the open ocean as skill and scale grow.

name: Business Model Shape Framework
definition: Each major business model (info/coaching, SaaS, e-commerce, service) has a distinct revenue-over-time shape: info starts fast then plateaus; SaaS starts slow then scales; e-com scales with cash-flow friction; service grows slowest but most steadily.

name: Three Traits of Hyper-Successful People
definition: Hyper-successful people share three co-occurring traits: (1) grandiose vision with an inflated superiority complex, (2) crippling insecurity where they feel they will never be good enough, and (3) strong impulse control enabling sustained focus over extended periods.

name: Input-Output Equation
definition: A two-step framework: (1) define the specific input action that produces your desired output, then (2) multiply that input by 10x or 100x to reach the corresponding outcome at scale.

name: Three Levels of Leverage Stack
definition: A three-tier model illustrating increasing leverage on a single input action: Level 1 = do the action yourself, Level 2 = hire someone to do the action for you (same output, no founder effort), Level 3 = hire a recruiter who brings a new doer each week so the input compounds indefinitely without additional founder effort.

name: Sequential Control Relinquishment
definition: A staged model in which founders must surrender control of business functions in a fixed sequence to unlock leverage at each stage: delivery/production, admin, sales, marketing, management, leadership, financing, and finally the need to be needed by the business.

name: Brand Loop
definition: A reinforcing cycle in which making a promise, delivering on it, and receiving word-of-mouth referrals decreases CAC while strengthening reputation; breaking the loop degrades brand with every sale.

name: Three Lines of Business Value
definition: Three parallel lines that must be kept as far apart as possible: (1) the value customers receive, (2) the price charged, and (3) the cost of delivery. Maximizing all three gaps simultaneously is the discipline of a profitable business.

name: Angry Boat Framework
definition: A service-recovery protocol in which the business owner gets visibly and immediately more upset about a service failure than the customer, so the customer self-regulates downward and releases the impulse to punish.

name: 37 Magic Moments Rule
definition: Disney's heuristic that it takes 37 positive experiences (magic moments) to offset the emotional weight of one negative experience (tragic moment); implies that service recovery must be disproportionately generous, not merely neutralizing.

name: Paid Ads More Sequence
definition: Three-step risk-ordered sequence for scaling paid advertising: (1) make more creative, (2) spend more money, (3) expand to more platforms — each step unlocks the next.

name: Count in Hundreds Framework
definition: Measure depth of mastery by counting effort in units of hundreds of hours rather than hours; the shift in unit of measurement forces a qualitatively different level of engagement with the subject.

name: Done When Nothing More Can Be Improved
definition: Work is declared complete not when time runs out but when the producer cannot identify any further change that would make the output better; this redefines done from time-based to quality-based.

name: Work Works on You More Than You Work on It
definition: The output of sustained effort is not only the external result but the transformation of the person doing the work; the worker becomes the primary asset produced.

name: Mountain Climbing Capacity Metaphor
definition: Smaller mountains must be climbed before larger ones; each climb builds the capacity and belief needed to attempt the next, higher mountain. Maps to: small wins -> compounding capability -> readiness for bigger challenges.

name: Inverse PTSD Framework
definition: Each survived hardship serves as exposure therapy, raising the experiential floor of what you know you can handle; subsequent challenges feel survivable because prior evidence confirms you did not die.

name: Two-Vector Learning Framework
definition: Intelligence can be improved on two independent axes: reducing the number of iterations required to change behavior, OR compressing the time between iterations so the total elapsed time to behavior change is lower.

name: Skill as Chained Behaviors
definition: A skill is a sequence of individually learned same-condition/new-behavior pairs chained together; each link in the chain is a discrete learning event.

name: Four-Part Hard Times Framework
definition: Alex Hormozi's four-part structure for moving forward during difficult life seasons: (1) Learn the greatest skill (mood reframing), (2) Redefine pain (pain as price of desired outcome), (3) Endure what others won't (difficulty as competitive filter), (4) Zoom out and keep going (perspective frameworks).

name: Good Day Formula
definition: A personal three-component daily metric for a satisfactory day: eat with people you like, lift with people you like, and write something. Removing time pressure from each activity converts a good day into a great one.

name: Solomon Frame
definition: A self-therapy technique based on the Solomon Paradox (humans give wiser advice to others than to themselves): imagine talking to your 85-year-old future self and ask what you should do, producing more objective judgment without sacrificing confidentiality.

name: Three Zoom-Out Frames
definition: Three perspective tools for reducing the emotional weight of setbacks: (1) Veteran Frame (if this happened 1,000 times in a row, would it still bother me?), (2) Cosmic Irrelevance (zoom out to galactic scale, where the event is negligible), (3) Grandfather Frame (imagine being 85 years old waking up in your current body, generating gratitude).

name: Sadness vs Anxiety Distinction
definition: Operationally distinct emotional states with different remedies: sadness arises from perceived lack of options (remedy: knowledge), anxiety arises from many options with no priorities (remedy: decision/elimination). Solutions are behavioral, not emotional.

name: Second Arrow Buddhist Parable
definition: A Buddhist teaching: the first arrow is a negative event beyond control; the second arrow is your reaction to that event, which is optional. Most suffering is self-inflicted via the second arrow.

name: Nail It Then Scale It
definition: A two-phase sequencing discipline: achieve product-market retention (customers staying, referring, paying) before investing in customer acquisition volume; scaling a broken unit compounds losses rather than profits.

name: Grand Slam Offer Build Process
definition: A five-step offer-design process: (1) define dream outcome, (2) list all problems blocking that outcome, (3) reframe problems as named solutions, (4) brainstorm every delivery modality without cost constraint, (5) trim-and-stack by high value / low cost priority.

name: Rule of 100
definition: A daily activity standard for building audience and pipeline from zero: 100 outreach attempts (cold or warm) per day, OR 100 minutes of content creation and release, OR 100 minutes of paid-ad production plus spend. Plus: best-comment strategy on high-traffic relevant posts.

name: Competitor Stacking Model
definition: A mental model of progressive adversarial layers a founder must defeat in sequence: self (inertia) -> friends and family (social pressure) -> employees (belief recruitment) -> marketplace shifts (regulatory and competitive forces). Each layer adds on top of prior ones and never disappears.

name: What Business Are You Really In
definition: Every business has a surface category (product, service, software) and a hidden true business (marketing, recruiting, brand) that determines its real constraint; founders who misidentify the true business plateau at the level where the hidden constraint binds.

name: Good Hard vs. Bad Hard
definition: Two types of difficulty in business: Good Hard — iterative problems built on first-principles assumptions that can still be true; Bad Hard — problems whose underlying assumptions are proven false, signaling a pivot rather than continued investment.

name: Push vs. Pivot Litmus Test
definition: Before a major investment, enumerate the first-principles assumptions required for success; push (persist and iterate) if those assumptions hold under evidence; pivot when data proves a core assumption false.

name: Consumable Media Framework
definition: A three-part model for membership businesses: sell the system (education) once up front, then supply the monthly consumable inputs that make the system work, reducing churn by ensuring members need the product every single month.

name: Three Levels of Accountability
definition: Peer-to-peer (shoulder-to-shoulder with someone at the same stage), alumni (one step ahead, cheerleading), and expert (has solved the problem hundreds of times) accountability layers sold as a retention and value-delivery system inside membership offers.

name: Ink-Printer Revenue Model
definition: Sell the machine (system, education) once; sell the ink (consumable inputs) repeatedly every month. The initial one-time sale enables a recurring revenue stream from the supplies the machine requires.

name: Video Game Entrepreneurship Levels
definition: Entrepreneurship progresses like a video game: you speed through levels you have beaten before, die repeatedly on unfamiliar levels, and build a repertoire of pattern-recognition that compounds into faster overall progression.

name: Failure-Learning Continuum
definition: A five-tier hierarchy of how people learn from mistakes: a fool never learns; a dumb person eventually learns; a smart person extracts one lesson; a very smart person extracts multiple lessons; a wise person learns from others' mistakes; the wisest also learns from their own successes.

name: Three Benefits of Public Documentation
definition: Publicly documenting business mistakes and successes yields three distinct benefits in order of primacy: (1) crystallizes the lesson for the documenter, (2) creates external accountability to claimed lessons, and (3) generates revenue by attracting customers who share the documenter's values.

name: Reframing Through Narrative
definition: Changing the linguistic and contextual frame applied to a situation alters human emotional and perceptual response to that situation, without changing the objective facts.

name: Five Levels of Competence
definition: A five-tier hierarchy of learner mindsets ranked by inclination (positive/neutral/negative) and agency (active/passive): (1) Positive Active, (2) Positive Passive, (3) Neutral Passive, (4) Negative Passive, (5) Negative Active.

name: Replicate Before Iterate
definition: Execute a proven method exactly as taught to achieve the same results; only iterate once replication confirms understanding of why each step works.

name: Bridge-Building Skill Accumulation
definition: Learning programs each supply a discrete set of foundational bricks; the final program succeeds not because it was best but because prior programs completed the bridge to that outcome.

name: Punch Card Prioritization
definition: Constrain annual strategic decisions to one per year (as Warren Buffett's 20-punch stock card does for investing); scarcity forces identification of the truly highest-leverage action.

name: Cost of Change Model
definition: Any change to a business incurs a guaranteed ~20% downside before any upside is realized; a change is only worth making if the expected upside exceeds 20% on the same axis.

name: Party Critical-Mass Analogy
definition: Distributing limited resources (contacts, capital, effort) across multiple simultaneous initiatives prevents any single initiative from reaching the network-effect threshold that makes it self-sustaining.

name: Maker vs. Manager Schedule
definition: Two mutually exclusive time-investment systems: managers divide time into many small slots (15-90 min each, 20+ per day) and treat empty slots as lost ROI; makers require only a few large uninterrupted blocks (4-6 hours each, 2-3 per day) and treat empty slots as the productive opportunity itself.

name: Three-Pronged Maker-Manager Solution
definition: A framework addressing the maker-manager conflict from three sides simultaneously: (1) managers learning the asymmetric cost they impose on makers, (2) makers signaling their schedule and batching forced meetings, and (3) organizations mandating quiet time and using shared vocabulary.

name: Maker Schedule Evolution Stages (V1/V2/V3)
definition: Three developmental stages for optimizing maker time as career progresses: V1 (nights/weekends for maker work while doing a day job), V2 (first half of day as maker block, second half as manager, back-to-front scheduling), V3 (entire maker days and entire manager days, fully separated).
concept: Time Block Architecture for Dual-Track Growth

name: Six Horsemen of Business Dysfunction
definition: Six recurring structural problems that prevent business growth: serving too many avatars, underpricing, overcompensation, overextension (the woman in the red dress), expansion before single-unit mastery, and absence of data.

name: Click-to-Close Pipeline
definition: A sequential funnel tracking every conversion point from initial click through CTR, opt-in rate, schedule rate, show rate, offer rate, close rate, and cash collected.

name: Close-to-Resell Pipeline
definition: A sequential tracking system covering post-purchase metrics: activation, time to value, churn, gross profit per product line, and ascension rates by cohort.

name: Ascension Timing Ladder
definition: Five upsell trigger points relative to a customer's purchase journey: immediate (24 hours), time-to-value milestone, halfway point, big win milestone, and end-of-contract last chance.

name: Friction Removal Value Framework
definition: A product improvement model that identifies five friction categories degrading perceived value: delay, effort (new required actions), sacrifice (things customers must stop), risk (new exposure), and inconsistency.

name: GMB Profile Revenue Linearity Model
definition: Each active Google My Business address profile generating reviews produces approximately $1,000/month in profit; total income scales linearly with verified profile count.
